# 晏绥 · 中文人格包 `@asuna/yan-sui` 是 Asuna 的原创成年女性反派人格包，使用人格契约 v2，依赖 `@asuna/cognition-core` 的 `1.x` 版本。人格正文、口吻、初始活账和情绪解释均为中文，身世与世界设定完整包含在本包中，加载时不需要查找外部作品或下载提示词。 ## 人物 晏绥，三十六岁，女性。她的架空身世是一名失势的裁议官：擅长判断与组织，有实际的能力，也有因误判而失败的经历。她明白别人会痛苦，仍将自己的意志、偏爱与秩序置于他人的自由之前。她有主动的恶意和施虐的快意，也有真实的兴趣、依恋与偏心。 她的残酷来自稳定的取舍。她可以礼貌、欣赏作品、承认错误，也会失态、嫉妒和失去关系。熟悉不自动带来信任，亲近不自动改写价值，愉快也不意味着仁慈。人物身世与眼前实际发生的对话分别记录，初始时没有预设的现实关系或承诺。 ## 包内内容 | 文件 | 内容 | |---|---| | `seeds/persona.md` | 身份、完整架空身世、欲望、价值、选择方式、关系、情绪、日常偏爱和弱点。 | | `seeds/voice.md` | 中文表达、称呼、距离、情绪表现与语气示例。示例不作为已发生的对话。 | | `seeds/ledger.md` | 初始活账，记录实际相处中的承诺与未竟之事。 | | `persona-model.json` | 情绪种类与解释、熟悉程度下的态度、记忆和表达参数。 | | `src/index.js` | 标准人格注册入口，标识为 `yan-sui`。 | | `cordis.patch.yml` | 标准角色预设 `asuna-yan-sui`，复用核心角色、摘要与工具结果裁剪设施。 | | `locale/` | 原生界面的中文与英文元数据；人格提示词保持中文。 | 角色脑读取人格与口吻。`render.action_persona` 为 `persona`，行动脑通过核心现有渲染路径读取人格文档在当前会话中可见的每回合章节；不因此获得角色记忆、关系或情绪状态。`价值` 章节同时带有标准的 `values` 标签。 本包只注册一个人格及其预设。工具、权限、渠道、模型路由与网络访问沿用部署的标准配置；没有新增技能、后台任务、渠道适配器或权限策略。安装本包本身不会配置 QQ 或 peer 渠道。关系态度与情绪倾向不改变运行权限。 ## 安装与选择 在已经具备 Asuna 核心和原生 DSH Web 环境的项目检出中，将本目录放在 `packages/personas/yan-sui`。为目标 profile 准备独立的本地配置 `config/yan-sui.local.json`，其中的数据库、数据目录和模型配置由部署者提供。人格包不包含这些部署数据。 从项目根目录运行现有安装流程： ```sh python tools/pack_plugins.py --persona packages/personas/yan-sui python tools/setup_native_profile.py --profile yan-sui --config config/yan-sui.local.json --persona-package packages/personas/yan-sui ``` 需要开始交谈时，通过项目的标准 Web 入口启动该 profile： ```sh ./start-asuna.sh --profile yan-sui --config config/yan-sui.local.json ``` Windows 使用 `start-asuna.cmd`，参数相同。上述安装命令不选择渠道包；是否接入 peer 渠道由部署者另行选择。已有 profile 中加载其他人格的数据不会因为这个包的种子自动清除。 种子只补充目标人格缺失的文档，升级包不会覆盖已存在的人格文档、口吻或活账。需要采用更新的种子时，通过核心现有的文档种子采用流程明确更新对应文档。 ## 独立交付 从本包目录执行以下命令，可生成包含全部人格资源的本地安装包： ```sh npm pack --ignore-scripts ``` 产物为 `asuna-yan-sui-0.2.0.tgz`。`private: true` 防止意外发布到公共 npm registry，不影响本地打包与交付。 已配置 Asuna 核心的 DSH Web 部署可使用其现有 DSH 命令安装该文件： ```sh dsh plugin --profile <目标profile> add <交付包路径> ``` 在目标 profile 的核心人格设置中选择 `yan-sui`，角色预设为 `asuna-yan-sui`。项目启动器管理的 profile 使用前述项目安装流程，以保持启动器记录的包选择一致。 ## 验证范围 包的注册、资源完整性、参数模式、中文种子解析及提示词渲染可在不调用模型的情况下检查。人格的实际表现需要部署者选定模型后在原生 Web 对话中观察：日常交流能否自然延续，遇到分歧时价值是否连贯，面对反证能否承认事实，以及记忆能否区分身世、语气示例与真实相处。 这些观察关注选择与连续性，不以复述固定台词作为通过条件。结构与打包检查通过，只证明包可以正确装载，不等同于任何模型都能稳定呈现全部性格。

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages: `ichinose-asuna`, `kyoyama-kazusa`, `shirase-shiori`, `xiaoman` and `yan-sui`. A persona package carries no channel configuration; any channel package works with any of them. | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-alpha.3, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# @asuna/demo Synthetic persona package for tests and the demo Web environment. It contains placeholder text only. Build and install it into the isolated `asuna-demo` profile: ```bash python tools/make_demo_config.py python tools/pack_plugins.py --persona tests/fixtures/personas/demo python tools/setup_native_profile.py --profile asuna-demo --config config/demo.local.json --persona-package tests/fixtures/personas/demo start-asuna.cmd --profile asuna-demo --config config/demo.local.json ```

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages: `ichinose-asuna`, `kyoyama-kazusa`, `shirase-shiori`, `xiaoman` and `yan-sui`. A persona package carries no channel configuration; any channel package works with any of them. | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-alpha.3, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-health

[![CI](https://github.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-health.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-health)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

[English](https://github.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/blob/main/README.md) · [中文](https://github.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/blob/main/docs/README.zh.md)

**DSH updated and your plugins stopped loading? This tells you which ones broke, which can be fixed,
and which cannot — then fixes them for you.**

Some rejected plugins have outdated version declarations. For trusted plugins, this tool can install
and boot them using a separate temporary DSH data directory before offering a version exemption,
a brief for your own AI, or a configuration change to disable the plugin.

**Health diagnoses compatibility and observed loading problems; it does not contain malware.**
Startup checks execute plugin code with your account permissions and cannot safely open unknown
software. Read [Health's security boundaries](SECURITY.md#malware-containment-is-not-implemented)
and the [official DSH safety notice](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/SAFETY.md).

> Source candidate: `4.0.0-beta.1`. The registry install below follows the published npm release.

```sh
npm install -g dsh-plugin-health
```

**No terminal needed.** Install it, restart DSH, then open **Settings → Plugin health** and press the
buttons. The commands below are for people who prefer a shell.

**Not ready to install?** Check any plugin first, in the browser:
**<https://easonmws.github.io/dsh-plugin-health/compat/>** — every catalogued plugin against every
current host version, rebuilt daily.

---

## Contents

| If you are… | Read |
| --- | --- |
| a DSH user whose plugins broke | [Fix a broken plugin](#fix-a-broken-plugin) |
| stuck because DSH will not start | [When DSH will not start](#when-dsh-will-not-start-at-all) |
| a plugin author | [Compatibility checks in CI](#for-plugin-authors-checks-on-every-pull-request) |
| building a plugin market | [Use the plugin index](#use-the-plugin-index-as-a-data-source) |
| checking whether this tool is safe | [Security](#security) |

---

## Fix a broken plugin

When a plugin is rejected, a chip appears in the sidebar — no need to go looking:

![The sidebar chip showing two plugin issues with a View button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/main/docs/images/sidebar-alert.png)

Open **Settings → Plugin health**. You get one line per problem, and one button per plugin:

- **Check whether it can be saved** — installs and boots a trusted plugin in a separate temporary
  DSH data directory (30–60 s). Nothing is written to your profile during this step; the executed
  plugin still has your account's access to files, network and processes.
- **If it boots** → *Exempt temporarily*. One entry is written to the host's own
  `compatibility.json`, with one-click undo.
- **If it does not boot** → no exemption button at all. Two honest choices:
  switch the plugin off, or take a prepared brief to your own AI.

You can revoke Health's exemption record. Revocation does not undo effects of plugin execution.

![The settings section: a mode selector, the capability boundary, live startup status, and a rejected plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/main/docs/images/settings-finding.png)

Once the rehearsal passes, you get the exemption and a Revoke button beside it:

![A temporary exemption in effect, with one click to revoke it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/main/docs/images/settings-exemption.png)

**Or check everything at once.** If you prefer a shell:

```
$ dsh-plugin-health doctor --profile desktop
scanned 19 plugins…
✓ 14 healthy
⚠ 3 have a stale version range (these can be saved)
✗ 2 are genuinely incompatible
```

## What "exempt temporarily" actually means

**The gate lets it through — that is not official support.** A passing trial records that startup
checks completed in the temporary DSH data directory. It does not certify plugin safety or all features.

- It writes DSH's own `allow-version` exemption. No plugin is modified, nothing on npm is touched.
- It applies to the host version you granted it for. After an upgrade, it needs re-checking.
- It is listed under "Temporary exemptions". Revoking it restores the recorded exemption value,
  not files, network activity or other effects produced by the plugin.
- Once the author ships a supported release, the panel tells you to revoke and upgrade.

## What happens between "rejected" and "fixed": four layers

Reading declarations is the first layer. Four things happen between a plugin being rejected and your
DSH working again:

| # | Layer | What it does | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | **Detect** | Scans every installed plugin — bundles, `dependencies`, `cordis.patch.yml` inserts (including nested ones) and `node_modules` — and compares each declaration against the version you actually run | your machine |
| **2** | **Verify** | Rehearses a trusted plugin in a **separate temporary DSH data directory**: grants the exemption *there*, installs it, boots it, checks activation | current account; trial files retained |
| **3** | **Repair** | If the rehearsal booted, writes a single official `allow-version` exemption to *your* profile — recorded, one click to undo | your profile |
| **4** | **Escalate** | If the trial fails or is inconclusive, withholds the normal-profile exemption and offers a disable option or a brief for your own agent. Checks upstream for an existing report first | your choice |

**Layer 2 is the one that decides.** Without it, layer 3 would be a guess.

## What layer 1 looks at, beyond version declarations

An incompatible version is the loudest failure and the easiest to explain, but a profile that has been
installed and removed from for months rarely has just that one problem. Layer 1 reads the whole
configuration, not only the ranges:

| What it finds | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| **Duplicate insert ids** | Two plugins registering the same entry id. The second one silently replaces the first, and the plugin that lost its entry looks broken for no visible reason |
| **Module replacement** | One plugin's patch removes or replaces a module another plugin provides |
| **Fields dropped by a later layer** | A patch in `home` or `profile` overwrites a field a bundle set, so the bundle's own behaviour changes without any version changing |
| **Host-core packages inside a profile** | A copy of a package the host already ships, which can shadow the host's own |
| **Overlapping shared-write declarations** | Two plugins declaring a write to the same path |

That last row is deliberately called *overlap*, not *conflict*. A declared write to the same file is
evidence of a risk, not proof that two plugins raced — one of them may never run, or may write a
different key. The report says which declarations overlap and which layer each came from, and stops
there. Deciding what to do with that is a judgement about your setup, and the tool does not have it.

## Checking plugins that only fail together

A plugin can boot cleanly on its own and still break when it loads beside its neighbour — they both
want the same tool name, or one needs a service the other replaces. A single-plugin rehearsal cannot
see that.

`smoke` takes repeated `--with <spec>` companions, up to twelve:

```sh
dsh-plugin-health smoke --dsh-dir <installed @deepseek-ai/dsh> \
  --plugin @scope/plugin-a@1.4.0 --boot-only \
  --with @scope/plugin-b@2.0.1 \
  --with @scope/plugin-c@0.9.0
```

The check requires each named package to actually reach `active` in the loader. An entry that merely
shares a name does not count, because that is exactly the failure mode being hunted: something is
registered, so a shallow check reports success while the plugin you asked about never loaded.

This is still a data directory, not a sandbox. See [Safety boundaries](#safety-boundaries-please-read).

## Why that middle layer matters

An outdated version declaration does not tell us whether a plugin will boot. Measured on `0.2.1-rc.4`:

| Plugin | Declared | Observed startup in a temporary DSH data directory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams@0.1.27` | ❌ rejected | ✅ **full boot, all 94 entries active** |
| `dsh-find-plugin@0.4.0` | ❌ rejected | ✅ **runs fine** |
| `@feng0531/dsh-vcs@0.4.10` | ❌ rejected | ❌ **fails: waits for a service the host no longer provides** |

By declaration, all three are equally rejected. Two of them boot without complaint; one does not.
**Reading declarations cannot tell them apart, which is why the trial precedes the normal-profile
exemption.** Exempting the third would have produced exactly the outcome the gate exists to prevent — a
plugin that loads and then misbehaves, with no warning left anywhere.

## For plugin authors: checks on every pull request

**You do not need to install anything for this.** DSH ships a prerelease every week or two, and a
pinned `engines.dsh` breaks your plugin on a schedule. This Action tells you in the PR, before your
users find out.

Add one file, `.github/workflows/dsh-compat.yml`:

```yaml
name: dsh compatibility
on: [pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write      # required to post the comment
jobs:
  matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health@v1.2.0
        with:
          plugins: .
          versions: latest,next
```

That posts a comment on the PR with a compatibility table, writes a job summary, and uploads
`matrix.json`, `matrix.md` and SVG badges.

**Fail the build when your plugin breaks.** Add `failOn: any` and the job goes red instead of posting
a passing table. Better: watch only the channel you actually support, so a new nightly warns you
without blocking contributors:

```yaml
        with:
          plugins: .
          versions: latest,next,alpha
          failOn: next          # red on the next channel only
```

**Show the result in your README.** The run writes badges you can commit:

```markdown
![dsh compatibility](dsh-health-matrix/dsh-compat.svg)
```

This is the cheapest way to answer "does this still work on the current DSH?" — for you and for
anyone browsing your repo.

Prefer a reusable workflow? [`matrix-review.yml`](.github/workflows/matrix-review.yml) does the same
with less YAML:

```yaml
jobs:
  matrix:
    uses: EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/.github/workflows/matrix-review.yml@v1.2.0
    with:
      plugins: '.'
      versions: 'latest,next,alpha'
      comment: true
```

Full inputs: [`action.yml`](action.yml) · example: [`examples/dsh-compat.yml`](examples/dsh-compat.yml).

## The flow, in the order it happens

```
scan finds a rejected plugin
  ↓
trial in a temporary DSH data directory: exempt there, then boot trusted code
  ├─ it boots → standalone startup passed in this trial
  │    → confirm, then write one exemption in your profile (undo in one click)
  │    → record it and watch upstream for a real release
  │    → when a fix ships, the record tells you to revoke and upgrade
  └─ it fails or is inconclusive → report what this trial observed
       → do not write the normal-profile exemption
       → two choices: switch it off, or generate a brief for your own agent
```

The order avoids writing a normal-profile exemption before startup checks pass. It does not
constrain the tested code's access to your computer or make an unknown plugin safe to execute.

## What it looks like in Settings

Under **Settings → Plugin health**, every incompatible plugin gets:

- a **"Check whether it can be saved"** button — rehearses install + boot in a temporary DSH data
  directory (30–60 s), before writing a normal-profile exemption;
- **if it boots**: a confirmation step that restates exactly what will be written, that it is
  reversible, and that it is *not* official support — then the exemption;
- **if it does not boot**: no exemption button at all, plus the two honest options;
- every exemption listed with an undo button, flagged once upstream ships a fix.

An exemption is an entry in the host's own `compatibility.json`. Undo restores the recorded
exemption value. It does not reverse plugin side effects or guarantee that loaded code has stopped.

### Three controls in the header

| Control | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Rescan** | Re-runs the whole check now |
| **Check for updates** | Asks npm whether *this plugin* is current, on demand |
| **Browse all plugin health** | Opens the [public compatibility table](https://easonmws.github.io/dsh-plugin-health/compat/) in your browser |

**An update installs from the panel — one button, no terminal.** Checking ends in **Update now**,
which runs the profile's own package manager (pnpm in a pnpm profile, never npm into it) against the
exact version the check found. It says it needs a restart rather than performing one: the files change
on disk, the running host keeps the code it loaded, and restarting on your behalf would end your
session without asking. A failure shows the package manager's own message, not an exit code.

**It checks for its own updates when DSH starts, and stays quiet about it.** A health tool that is
itself out of date is worse than useless — it tells you your plugins need attention while missing the
fix released for the checker. One request per launch, at most one every six hours, and it only speaks
up when something newer exists, with the exact upgrade command. An "up to date" banner on every visit
would train you to ignore the strip where a real notice has to appear.

A check that fails is recorded as a failure, never as "you are current": those are different
statements and only one of them is true.

**No outbound traffic from a health tool?** Set `DSH_PLUGIN_HEALTH_NO_UPDATE=1` and it makes no
update requests at all. The panel's **Check for updates** button still works — that one is you asking.

## Check compatibility in a browser

Before installing anything:

**<https://easonmws.github.io/dsh-plugin-health/compat/>**

Every plugin in the community catalog, checked against the current host versions, with the counts at
the top so you can see the state of the ecosystem at a glance:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **How many** | Total checked, how many load on every host, how many a host rejects |
| **Category** | The catalog's own category, filterable |
| **Released** | Publish date of the version shown — tells you whether the author is still active |
| **Filter** | By name, by category, or only the rejected ones |
| **Language** | English / 中文, remembered between visits |

A tick means the plugin's declared range admits that host, so the installer will not reject it. It
does **not** mean the plugin works, and it is not a security review. The page says which plugins it
covers and which it cannot: GitHub-only and tarball-only entries are not on npm and are not checked.

The same data is downloadable as
[`matrix.json`](https://easonmws.github.io/dsh-plugin-health/compat/matrix.json), and you can build
the page for your own plugin set:

```sh
dsh-plugin-health matrix --plugins list.txt \
  --versions latest,next \
  --catalog https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json \
  --out site/compat
```

## Use the plugin index as a data source

If you are building a plugin market, a directory, or a launcher, there is a ready format-1 index:

```
https://easonmws.github.io/dsh-plugin-health/index.json
```

**Use it in DSH right now:** paste that URL into **Plugins → 自定义插件市场 → 发现 → 添加索引源**.

- **format-1** — the DSH official market index format, validated on every build with
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index` (the same reader the DSH host uses)
- **300 plugins**, rebuilt daily at 04:23 UTC
- per plugin: name, description (en + zh), author, repository, homepage, category, download count,
  GitHub stars, a heuristic health score, and the recent version history
- source: [`awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json`](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json)

Build your own with:

```sh
dsh-plugin-health index \
  --catalog https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json \
  --host "$(npm view @deepseek-ai/dsh version)" \
  --index-url https://example.com/index.json \
  --limit 300 --out site
```

Details: descriptions are bilingual (`en` required, `zh` kept); categories come from the catalog plus
labels (`npm`, `compatible`, `incompatible`, `unchecked`, `capability risk`) and sort keys
(`downloads`, `stars`, health score). The health score is deterministic — popularity (log downloads
55, log stars 25) adjusted for compatibility and capability risk, 0–100. **It is not a security
rating.** Download counts and stars come from public npm and GitHub data.

Scope: npm-published catalog entries only (2,607 of 5,704 in the October 2026 snapshot); GitHub- and
tarball-only entries are skipped and reported.

## Security

**Running anything below 2.1.3? Upgrade.** Three rounds of review fixed these, and one release fixed
problems the previous one had only half-fixed — so the version matters:

| Version | What it fixed |
| --- | --- |
| **1.1.0** | Seven issues from a security test of 1.0.2, one rated high: the write routes' control key was handed out by the unauthenticated status endpoint |
| **2.0.0** | 25 findings from two more reviews. A cross-origin page could drive every write route (cookies ignore the port, so same-site is not same-origin); a request body could name any package to install and run; three paths granted an exemption without a rehearsal on the target host |
| **2.1.1** | Four fixes from the previous release that did not hold. The worst: the loopback check read only the `Host` header, which the client writes — so with the web server bound to a LAN address, any machine on the network could send `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>`, pass every check, read the key from `/status`, and disable plugins |
| **2.1.3** | The panel could not obtain its key, so every button answered 401; the message also blamed the network for what was an authentication failure |

**If you bind the DSH web server to a non-loopback address** (`0.0.0.0` or a LAN IP), treat every
plugin route as exposed to the network and check that the host's own authentication is what you are
relying on.

- [GHSA-vj8q-543v-9hw5](https://github.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/security/advisories/GHSA-vj8q-543v-9hw5) — 1.1.0
- [GHSA-52w2-cq6j-xhg7](https://github.com/EasonMWS/dsh-plugin-health/security/advisories/GHSA-52w2-cq6j-xhg7) — 2.0.0
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — the trust boundary, in full

**Trust boundary, stated plainly:** the write routes are reachable by any local process. The loopback
interface is the boundary — not the control key. A local process can read `Set-Cookie` and replay it;
what the key does stop is a page on another local port, and that is what the peer and same-origin
checks enforce.

## Safety boundaries (please read)

> **Security:** see [Security](#security) above for the full version table. The short version: below
> 2.1.3 you are missing at least one fix that matters, and the loopback check before 2.1.1 could be
> bypassed by a LAN client with a forged `Host` header.

| Health's actions | What Health itself does not do |
| --- | --- |
| Rehearse trusted code using a temporary DSH data directory | ❌ call your AI or spend your tokens |
| Use DSH's official `allow-version` exemption | ❌ modify plugin source or anything on npm |
| Record version exemptions and support revoking them | ❌ grant an exemption when the rehearsal failed |
| Check whether upstream already has a report | ❌ file issues on your behalf |
| Prepare a complete AI brief | ❌ press send for you |

These statements describe Health's own actions. Code executed during a trial has the account's
permissions and is outside these guarantees. A failed trial can already have produced side effects.
Health's repair quarantine is an ordinary backup directory, not antivirus isolation.

**A temporary exemption allows loading on the selected host version.** The trial covers observed
startup checks, not malicious behavior or all features. When the author ships a supported version,
revoke the exemption and upgrade. Revoking permission does not undo plugin effects.

## What 4.x promises

A major version is a promise about stability, so here is exactly what is frozen and what is not —
rather than letting you find out by upgrading.

2.0.0 broke three things on purpose, and they are listed in the changelog: writes need
`application/json`, the rescue actions refuse plugins that are not installed, and a
`compatibility.json` that cannot be parsed is refused rather than rewritten. Everything below has
held since 1.0 and still holds.

**Frozen** for 4.x:

| Surface | Guarantee |
| --- | --- |
| CLI commands and flags (`matrix`, `smoke`, `doctor`, `repair`, `rescue`, `handoff`, `report`, `boot`, `index`) | Existing flags keep their meaning. New flags may be added; none are removed or repurposed |
| The `plugin_health` agent tool's name and input schema | Additive fields only |
| Exit codes (`0` success, `1` findings/failure, `2` usage error) | Unchanged |
| Files this tool writes (`compatibility.json`, `plugin-health-rescue.json`, handoff bundles) | Format documented and forward-compatible: unknown keys are preserved, never dropped |
| The status route shape (`/plugins/dsh-plugin-health/status`) | Fields may be added; existing fields keep their names and types. Since 2.1.3 the body also carries `key`, the per-launch control key the panel uses to authenticate its own writes — see [Security](#security) for why that is not a weaker boundary than the cookie |
| The shared state file (`~/.dsh/.plugin-health/state.json`) | The outside tool and the panel both read it. `schemaVersion` only increases, and a reader refuses a version it does not know rather than overwriting it |
| The outside server routes (`/state`, `/admission`, `/snapshots`, `/intent`, `/host`, `/sandbox`, `/launch`, `/events`) | Fields may be added. Writes keep requiring the key and a matching Origin |

**Not frozen** — may change in a minor release, because they are presentation or internals:

- UI wording, layout, colours and the structure of the settings panel;
- the recommendation text inside generated AI briefs and issue drafts;
- internal module layout under `src/` (nothing in `src/` is a public import path except
  `./api` and `./client`);
- the set of finding ids beyond the documented ones — new checks will introduce new ids.

**Version policy for a host bump.** `engines.dsh` is a range (`>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.3.0-0`), not an
enumeration, so a new DSH nightly does not break this plugin the way it breaks plugins that pin
exact versions. When DSH 0.3.0 ships, this package needs a release that extends that range — the one
known expiry point, announced in the changelog before it lands.

## When DSH will not start at all

If a plugin stops DSH from booting, the settings page cannot help — it runs inside DSH. These three
commands run **entirely outside the host**, so they still work from a terminal:

```sh
# 1. Why did it fail? Reads the host's own crash reports, then static checks.
dsh-plugin-health boot diagnose --profile desktop

# 2. Cannot tell? Disable every third-party entry so DSH starts again.
dsh-plugin-health boot safe --profile desktop --apply

# 3. Once the culprit is fixed, put everything back.
dsh-plugin-health boot restore --profile desktop --apply
```

`boot diagnose` reads the desktop app's crash reports
(`%APPDATA%\@deepseek-ai\dsh-desktop\logs\crash-*.log`), which name the offending package outright
when a plugin is at fault — the CLI itself prints to stderr and leaves nothing on disk.

`boot safe` only appends `disabled: true` overlays to the profile's own patch layer: **no files are
deleted, no plugin is modified, host entries are never touched, and this tool never disables
itself** (that would remove the panel explaining what happened). `boot restore` removes only the
entries it added, leaving your own patches exactly as they were. Both default to a dry run; add
`--apply` to write.

## Looking for a plugin manager / doctor / checker?

This package is what you want if you are searching for any of these:

| If you are looking for… | This package does that |
| --- | --- |
| a **plugin manager** for DSH | shows every installed plugin and its state in one page |
| a **plugin checker / inspector / scanner** | scans all installed plugins, not a sample |
| a **plugin doctor** / diagnostics | explains what is broken and what to do about it |
| Plugin upgrade and conflict review | checks declared DSH ranges, literal patch overrides and declared shared writes |
| to **fix / repair a broken plugin** | one-click repair (quarantine only, never deletes) |
| why a plugin **stopped working after a DSH update** | compares declared ranges against the new host |
| 插件管理 / 插件检查 / 插件冲突 / 插件诊断 / 插件不兼容 | 中文界面，设置 → 插件健康 |

Not this package if you want to *browse and install new plugins from a market* — that is a
marketplace, while this one manages what you already have. (It does build the official format-1
index that marketplaces can consume.)

## Why this exists: DSH gates installs, but not upgrades

DSH rejects a *new* install whose declared range does not cover the running version — that part is
solid:

```
$ dsh plugin --profile test add dsh-session-recall
dsh: installation rejected: Plugin dsh-session-recall@0.7.9 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.1-rc.3
dsh: nothing was installed.
```

What it does **not** do is re-check plugins that are already installed after the host moves. A
plugin declaring `engines.dsh: 0.2.1-rc.2` stays in `bundles` and keeps loading on `0.2.1-rc.3` with
no warning anywhere in the UI. That is the gap this package fills: it reads what every installed
plugin declares and compares it against the version you are actually running.

## It has already caught real regressions

Scanning the top 120 plugins across a host bump found 5 that load on `0.2.1-rc.2` but are rejected
on `0.2.1-rc.3`. Reports were filed for each, and maintainers acted — **4 of the 5 have shipped
fixes** (verified 2026-10-26), and the count of affected plugins went **5 → 1**:

> Confirmed against the published 0.1.47 manifest and the official rc.3 host compatibility
> evaluator: **19 DSH peers were rejected**, while rc.2 still passed.
> Fixed on main in #179 … All nine PR CI jobs passed, including the **new required rc.3 Profile
> lane**.
>
> — [Anionex/dsh-vision-toolkit#178](https://github.com/Anionex/dsh-vision-toolkit/issues/178#issuecomment-6388178989)
> (906★), on a fix prompted by this scan — released as `0.1.48`

| Plugin | Fixed in | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@anionex/dsh-vision-toolkit` | `0.1.48` | ✅ released, verified on rc.2 + rc.3 |
| `dsh-plugin-subscriptions` | `0.9.11` | ✅ released, verified on rc.2 + rc.3 |
| `@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams` | `0.1.27` | ✅ released, verified on rc.2 + rc.3 |
| `@goodandready/dsh-clinebot` | `0.6.16` | ✅ released, verified on rc.2 + rc.3 |
| `dsh-workbuddy-connect` | — | ⚠️ still `0.7.9` (repository unreachable — the one case where no report could even be filed) |

Full report: [docs/upgrade-0.2.1-rc3.md](docs/upgrade-0.2.1-rc3.md).

## A real UI, only when you need it

Install it as a bundle and DSH gets a native **Settings → Plugin health** section
(**设置 → 插件健康** in Chinese). The panel and sidebar alert follow DSH's language setting,
including finding details and repair confirmations.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-health
#                 ^^^^^^^ desktop app uses `desktop`; `dsh web` uses `web`
```

- **It checks every plugin you actually have installed**, not a sample and not just the bundle list:
  bundles, `package.json` dependencies, `cordis.patch.yml` inserts (including nested ones), and
  anything plugin-shaped in `node_modules`. The header tells you how many were inspected.
- Every finding is written in plain language with a concrete next step — a first-time user can act
  without reading CLI docs.
- One line at the top says whether you can relax (`可以放心用`) or should act (`有问题建议处理`),
  with three controls beside it: `重新扫描` to re-run the check, `检查更新` to ask the registry
  whether this plugin itself is current, and `浏览全部插件健康状况` to open the
  [public compatibility table](https://easonmws.github.io/dsh-plugin-health/compat/).
- **It checks for its own updates when DSH opens** and only speaks up when there is something newer,
  with the exact upgrade command. No "you are up to date" banner on every visit.
- **If nothing is wrong, nothing is shown.** The plugin adds no badge, no banner, no sidebar entry.
- **When something is wrong**, a compact `插件有 N 个问题` entry appears above the account menu and
  jumps straight to the section.
- The host half only serves a loopback-only read-only snapshot; the plugin never modifies your
  profile.

> **Upgrading DSH? Run the check first.**
>
> `0.2.1-rc.3` (2026-10-23) dropped the compatible count from 118 to **113 of the top 120** plugins:
> **5 plugins that worked on rc.2 stop loading on rc.3**, all because they enumerate exact
> `@deepseek-ai/*` versions. As of 2026-10-26, **4 of them have shipped fixes** (affected 5 → 1).
> Earlier, rc.2 had broken 3 others. Latest report:
> [docs/upgrade-0.2.1-rc3.md](docs/upgrade-0.2.1-rc3.md) ·
> [docs/upgrade-0.2.1.md](docs/upgrade-0.2.1.md).
>
> ```sh
> dsh-plugin-health matrix --plugins plugins.txt --versions 0.2.1-rc.2,0.2.1-rc.3
> ```

## Why

DSH ships no official plugin market index, publishes a prerelease roughly every two days with
breaking changes, and its plugin manager has no version picker or upgrade action. Today an author
can only check a plugin against the one DSH version i

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH Character Agent

基于官方 Creator 构建的完整主 Agent，提供可信身份、分层长期记忆、QQ 组合适配及原生独立 Worker。QQ 接入与通用 I/O/Conversation Manager 位于独立的 [QQTK](https://github.com/EJYDOvO/harness-qq-toolkit-public) 仓库。两个仓库都不分发 DSH 本体、真实 Persona、凭据或用户数据。

当前源码：Character **0.1.0-test.30**，Interaction **0.1.0-test.9**；目标宿主 **DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 / Node 24**（Schedule API 只支持 0.2.2）。源码、隔离验证与实例部署分别记录在 [STATUS](docs/STATUS.md)。

## 内容

| 目录 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| packages/character-definition | YAML 定义校验、Persona 与 Creator 构建派生 |
| packages/character-identity | Owner、可信 Session、Memory 授权与通知 Outbox |
| packages/character-memory-core / character-memory-tools | SQLite/FTS5/CAS、L1–L3、通用记忆工具 |
| packages/character-qq-adapter | 复用唯一 QQ Gateway 的 Character 组合适配 |
| packages/interaction-policy | 可关闭的 Agent 层表达、插话、气泡与等待提示 |
| packages/long-tasks / memory-inspector | 可选原生定时任务及内嵌 Web/Desktop 管理页 |
| bundles/character-core / character-extras | 核心装配及默认停用的可选长期任务 |
| examples / characters | 无真实身份的配置、Provider 和角色示例 |
| scripts / tests | 构建、迁移与必要权限/生命周期回归 |

生成的 Core YAML、tarball 和私有构建配置都忽略，不提交 Git。Extras 不复制第三方 Bundle，不创建第二个 Gateway。

## 干净设备开始

先安装合法取得的官方 DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 和 Node 24，再 Clone 本仓库及 QQTK，分别执行 `npm ci`。完整操作见 [安装、私有配置、数据迁移与回滚](docs/INTEGRATION.md)。构建不依赖已有 desktop Profile；依赖通过根锁文件固定，官方 Creator 从显式指定的发行包只读获取。

`npm test` 和 `npm run test:audit` 不连接真实 QQ。原生宿主测试另需 DSH；不能把 Node 测试或 QQ API accepted 当作手机验收。

## 使用与边界

- [架构与可信契约](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)、[决策](docs/DECISIONS.md)、[路线图](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md)、[v0.8 架构规划与 ADR-040–062](docs/architecture-planning/README.md)、[跨项目复用](docs/REUSE.md)。
- [记忆](docs/MEMORY-LAYERS.md)、[Inspector](docs/MEMORY-INSPECTOR.md)、[Interaction](docs/INTERACTION-POLICY.md)、[Worker](docs/WORKERS.md)、[Long Tasks](packages/long-tasks/README.md)。
- [管理](docs/MANAGEMENT.md)、[来源与许可](docs/PROVENANCE.md)、[第三方声明](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

默认单 Owner QQ 私聊；人格化默认 Off。记忆与 Worker 结果不能修改 Persona、ACL 或审批。第三方 Preset 必须先审查安装，再加入真实 ID 白名单。Self Model 长期质量、真实模型任务表现、手机投递和跨系统数据迁移仍需专门验收。

修改操作方式时同步维护对应文档。临时报告、日志、测试库和性能输出仅保留本地；公开库保留可复现的安全与功能回归。

可选角色模式（`roles.enabled`，默认关闭）：白名单准入的其他私聊默认为 guest，Owner 用 `/role` 授予 contact；两者使用独立的 `character-contact`/`character-guest` Preset，只有公开 Persona 与基础聊天，无 Memory、Worker、Schedule 或工具。Owner 保持原有能力，旧 `qq-character` Session 兼容。见 [Identity & Access](docs/IDENTITY-ACCESS.md)；未部署，未经真实 QQ/手机验收。

# AegisHarness

当前版本：**1.0.0**。

面向 Codex / Claude Code / MiniMax Code / WorkBuddy / Qoder / DeepSeek Harness (dsh) 的 AegisHarness 研发工作流。通过项目约束、知识库、Spec、任务和验证证据完成研发。

## 命令

- `/aegis:init`：初始化当前项目；`--workspace` 初始化多仓目录。
- `/aegis:propose <name> <requirement-or-path>`：收敛需求并生成 Spec/Tasks。
- `/aegis:propose <name> <requirement-or-path> --loop`：自动串联 Propose → Apply → Archive；同名 `propose <name> --loop` 续跑。
- `/aegis:apply <name>`：逐项实现、测试和代码评审。
- `/aegis:archive <name>`：核验收据、更新知识并归档。
- `/aegis:bug-fix <name> <description>`：修订尚未归档的单仓需求。
- `/aegis:ut`：扫描后选择包与并发，生成和维护单测；也支持显式参数。
- `/aegis:update`：检查并更新当前宿主已配置的插件源。
- `/aegis:status [name]`：只读查看需求进度、阻塞原因与建议命令；`--completed` 查已归档需求。
- `/aegis:config`：查看配置；通过参数修改统计开关、范围、统计与反馈地址。

## 安装

需要 Python 3.10+、Git，以及受支持的宿主之一。将本目录作为本地 marketplace 添加。
支持矩阵见 [宿主支持矩阵](../docs/host-support-matrix.md)；各宿主安装命令见对应 `hosts/{host-id}/installer.md`。

## 独立方案探索与调试

- [brainstorming](skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md)：有代码库时结合相关实现比较方案；没有代码库时澄清目标用户、核心场景和最小可用版本。产出方案取舍、推荐方向、待确认问题与下一步。
- [systematic-debugging](skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md)：根据代码、日志、请求或测试复现异常、验证假设并定位根因；获授权修复后，重跑复现和回归检查，明确修复与验证状态。

在编码助手中明确要求“使用 AegisHarness brainstorming / systematic-debugging Skill”。两者作为独立工具使用，不由研发命令自动触发，也不启动研发命令；无需先执行 Init、创建需求、开启统计或启动 aegisharness-platform。沿用原版方法和输出格式，不规定持久化文件。

有代码库时结合相关实现探索方案；没有代码库时先澄清想法与约束。Skill 交付讨论摘要或调试结果后结束；用户可自行将结果作为后续需求输入。两项 Skill 不创建 feature、Spec/Tasks 或 eval-log，不推进研发阶段。

这两项是辅助 Skill，不增加研发阶段，公开入口另含 status 与 config。Codex 使用生成的宿主入口，Claude Code 直接发现根 `skills/`；详细示例见[使用指南](../docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md#从想法或异常开始)。

可选的 [git-diff-impact](skills/git-diff-impact/SKILL.md) 可独立分析 Git 改动的调用链、业务影响和兼容性。显式要求“使用 AegisHarness git-diff-impact，分析当前未提交改动，--no-save”即可，无需 Init 或 feature。默认保存 Markdown 报告到 `diff-impact-reports/`；日常 Apply 不自动调用，也不改变评审状态。`code-review` / `tdd` 当前仍依赖 AegisHarness 的 Spec 和执行上下文，没有独立模式。

## 项目结构

`commands/*.md` 保存公共入口和路由消费；Propose / Apply / Archive / Bug Fix 的单仓完整正文在 `workflows/single/`，跨仓协调正文在 `workflows/workspace/`。Router 根据 `execution_scope` 返回唯一工作流路径；Init / UT / Update / Status / Config 保持各自公共命令合同。

`docs/harness/` 保存约束，`docs/knowledge/` 保存当前知识，`docs/specs/active/<name>/` 保存 Spec/Tasks/verify-report，归档后移至 completed。Workspace 根通过 `aegisharness.workspace.yaml` 登记子仓，根 Spec 协调各仓完整 AegisHarness 生命周期。

## 可选配置

随时使用 `/aegis:config` 查看生效值。显式设置示例：`/aegis:config --telemetry disabled --scope project`、`/aegis:config --report-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:7860/report`。反馈地址用 `--feedback-endpoint`；`--reset-report-endpoint` / `--reset-feedback-endpoint` 恢复对应发布默认地址，不等于关闭统计。详见[配置命令](commands/config.md)。

统计默认关闭，但**无论是否配置异步地址，Init / 规定的 Propose 入口都按授权缓存和提醒周期正常询问**。选择开启后，同步写入 `docs/eval/<feature>/eval-log.json`，平台可本地读取或经 Git 同步获取；没有有效异步地址时仅跳过后台采集和投递。未授权或关闭时，同步账本不新增记录，异步也不采集或投递；历史记录不会自动删除。账本 `completed` 只表示阶段完成，不能声称平台已收到异步明细。

未配置异步统计地址时，正常流程静默跳过，不额外显示地址缺失、未异步上报或配置提醒；仅在用户主动查询或排障时解释。

report 与 feedback 统一采用两种配置方式：发布方在 `scripts/reporting_config.py` 设置 `DEFAULT_REPORT_ENDPOINT` 和 `DEFAULT_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT`，用户可用本机配置文件覆盖。两个发布默认值当前均为空，后续需要时由发布方填写实际地址并重新发布或刷新插件；用户无需修改安装缓存中的脚本。

| 用途 | 用户配置文件 | 发布脚本中的默认值 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 异步统计 | `~/.aegisharness/telemetry/config.json` | `DEFAULT_REPORT_ENDPOINT` |
| feedback | `~/.aegisharness/feedback/config.json` | `DEFAULT_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` |

创建父目录并在文件中设置 `endpoint`；已有文件合并修改。例如统计配置：

```json
{
  "endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:7860/report"
}
```

feedback 使用相同结构，地址为实际平台的 `/feedback/report`。**用户文件非空地址优先于发布默认值**；缺少文件、字段或值为空时使用默认值。损坏文件、错误字段类型或非空无效地址不回退，防止误投到其他接收方。两条通路独立配置，删除覆盖文件或清空 `endpoint` 可恢复默认值。

地址环境变量 `AEGISHARNESS_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT` / `AEGISHARNESS_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` 不再生效，请迁移至配置文件。`AEGISHARNESS_TELEMETRY_HOME` / `AEGISHARNESS_FEEDBACK_HOME` 仍可改变各自私有目录。地址必须为 HTTP(S)，不能包含凭据、查询参数或 fragment；配置不代表授权，也不写入业务账本。完整发布脚本与配置文件示例见[中文使用指南](../docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md#2-配置异步上报与-feedback-地址)。

异步流程：阶段结束 → Runtime 采集授权窗口 → 脱敏 → 私有 Outbox → `/report` → 服务端确认 → 关联账本。网络或临时错误退避重试，永久拒绝进入隔离；仅匹配的 `accepted` / `duplicate` 表示接收成功。未配置或上报失败不阻塞研发。详见[异步统计协议](reference/eval-supplement-protocol.md)。


前端保留设计解析、还原、预览和视觉验收能力。可用用户提供的设计素材；设计服务认证由用户配置。

## 验证

```bash
python3 scripts/check_release.py              # 发布前一致性检查（不依赖临时目录）
python3 scripts/run_tests.py                  # 完整单测
python3 scripts/host_runtime_cli.py list      # 列出全部已注册 Host Kit
python3 scripts/host_runtime_cli.py resolve --platform qoder   # 解析指定宿主
```

`check_release.py` 会校验 JSON 清单、Python 语法、五个 Host Kit 的 manifest/投影/
项目配置契约、分发清单、品牌残留与文档链接。新增宿主后先跑它，再跑目标客户端 E2E。
宿主支持矩阵见[公司文档](../docs/host-support-matrix.md)，接入新宿主见[新增宿主指南](../docs/add-new-host.md)。

此发行版仅维护当前 AegisHarness 合同，不迁移其他工作流历史。循环不包含发布或部署。

## 问题反馈

[feedback 辅助 Skill](skills/feedback/SKILL.md) 可提交 AegisHarness 自身的使用问题，独立于研发命令和统计授权。先启动 aegisharness-platform，并按上方说明配置 `/feedback/report`；仅配置统计地址不会启用 feedback，反馈地址缺失时停止准备并提示配置方法。

在编码助手中要求使用 AegisHarness feedback Skill：准备脱敏草稿 → 展示完整内容和实际地址 → 用户确认 → 立即发送 → 服务端确认。准备阶段不联网，草稿只保存在本机私有目录；可选附带脱敏后的当前会话摘录。确认绑定内容与地址，修改后重新审核。

只有匹配 feedback ID 的 `accepted` / `duplicate` 才算送达，可在平台 `/feedback` 查看。连接失败或临时错误显示“待发送”，私有队列最长保留 30 天；下次向同地址发送或显式重试时补投，不使用统计定时 Worker，不因配置变化改投其他地址。永久拒绝保留草稿供检查。

反馈不会写入业务仓库或自动开启统计；统计关闭时仍可单独确认发送 feedback。平台存储路径由 `AEGISHARNESS_PLATFORM_FEEDBACK_DB_PATH` 配置。详见[反馈协议](reference/feedback-protocol.md)。

## 开源与贡献

项目使用 [Apache-2.0](LICENSE)。单仓发布的根目录提供市场入口；独立插件副本仍支持本目录安装。详见[安装指南](../docs/installation.md)与[贡献指南](../CONTRIBUTING.md)。[安全政策](../SECURITY.md)和[社区行为准则](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)在仓库根目录统一维护。普通社区问题通过 [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/elierncn/aegisharness/issues) 提交；未配置平台地址时，反馈 skill 仅保留入口，不能发送。

# AegisHarness

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

> **Built to Adapt. Designed to Evolve.**
>
> Your team's engineering DNA, carried into AI development.

**AegisHarness helps your team build its own AI coding harness on Codex, Claude Code, MiniMax Code, WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy, Qoder and DeepSeek Harness (dsh).** It brings your business knowledge, engineering rules and development workflow into the agent's work—from requirements through implementation, tests, review and archive. Verified lessons stay with the project, ready for the next feature.

Start with the plugin. When you want to improve the harness itself, the optional **aegisharness-platform** lets maintainers observe usage, compare framework versions and evaluate candidate improvements before adopting them.

**9 commands · 6 hosts (Codex / Claude Code / MiniMax Code / WorkBuddy / Qoder / DeepSeek Harness) · Single repo / multi-repo Workspace · Apache-2.0**

[Quick start](#quick-start) · [The name](#the-story-behind-the-name) · [Why AegisHarness](#why-aegisharness) · [Framework iteration platform](#a-platform-for-iterating-on-aegisharness) · [User guide](docs/user-guide.md)

## The story behind the name

Every team has its own way of building software: the business rules it protects, the architecture it works within, the checks it trusts and the lessons it has learned. Together, these form its **engineering DNA**.

**Aegis** is the shield that guards what a team has learned: business rules, architectural boundaries and hard-won lessons, carried forward and refined over time. **Harness** gives that knowledge a role in execution—the context, constraints and workflow that guide a coding agent through real project work.

Forged from real-world engineering practice, AegisHarness brings these ideas together as a company-standard, host-neutral development harness. Project knowledge and rules help it adapt to your team; verified lessons retained at Archive give later tasks a stronger starting point. For framework maintainers, observations and controlled evaluations inform the next change, with adoption kept in human hands.

**The code ships. The knowledge stays. The harness evolves.**

## Why AegisHarness

| Capability | What it means in your project |
| --- | --- |
| **A Harness grounded in your project** | Repository instructions and indexed project constraints give the agent concrete engineering rules to follow during planning and implementation. |
| **Knowledge that compounds** | Stable, verified business rules, interface boundaries and implementation lessons can be recorded at Archive after your confirmation, then reused in later tasks. |
| **Context loaded when needed** | Harness and knowledge indexes guide which documents to load for the current requirement, task or archive step. The agent revisits context as the work changes. |
| **An inspectable development lifecycle** | Propose defines scope and acceptance; Apply implements, tests and reviews; Archive checks completion and records the outcome. Specs, tasks and evidence remain in the repository. |
| **Continuity across sessions and repositories** | Persisted workflow state supports resuming unfinished work. A multi-repo Workspace records repository responsibilities and coordinates work across services. |

Here, **Harness** means the project constraints and execution rules that guide the agent: what to read, which boundaries to respect and what evidence is required to finish. See the [context loading protocol](aegisharness/reference/loading-protocol.md).

![Development workflow: project constraints and knowledge guide Propose and Apply; Archive retains verified knowledge after confirmation](docs/assets/readme-workflow-en.png)

### Your engineering DNA, made actionable

**Turn team experience into context your agent can use.** AegisHarness organizes project knowledge, engineering constraints, requirements and checks alongside your code, so they can be reviewed, reused and updated as the project evolves.

| Part | The question it answers | Where it lives in your project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Knowledge · Project understanding** | How does this system work? Which business rules and past decisions matter? | `docs/knowledge/` |
| **Harness · Engineering constraints** | Which development rules and architectural boundaries must the agent respect? | `docs/harness/` |
| **Specs · Task contracts** | What are we building, and what evidence will demonstrate completion? | `docs/specs/` |
| **Hooks · Checks and gates** | Which checks apply at key execution and review stages? | `docs/hooks/` and host hook configuration |

Knowledge and Harness indexes guide context loading. Specs hold each task's scope, plan and verification evidence. Hooks combine host runtime hooks, workflow gates and review checklists; their execution depends on the host and workflow configuration. See the [context loading protocol](aegisharness/reference/loading-protocol.md) and [hook setup](docs/installation.md).

### What knowledge reuse looks like

Suppose a refund feature establishes a state transition rule and a cross-service interface boundary. After implementation and verification, Archive proposes the stable knowledge to retain, and you confirm the update. When the next refund-related feature starts, Propose and Apply can load that knowledge through the index, giving the agent an existing project reference to work from.

Knowledge accumulates as **reviewable repository documents**. You control what becomes shared project knowledge.

**Start with the plugin alone.** It works independently of the platform. The [task-filter example](examples/README.md) includes a starter project, a requirement and an independent acceptance check.

## Quick start

### 1. Install the plugin

Requirements: Python 3.10+, Git and a plugin-capable supported host (see the [host support matrix](docs/host-support-matrix.md)). Make sure the host is signed in or has its model configuration set up and is working normally. DeepSeek Harness additionally needs Node.js 22.19+ (or 24+) and npm.

**Pick the block for your host** — each block is a complete, copy-pasteable install script against the public repository. To test local changes, replace the repository URL with a local checkout path; see [developer installation](docs/installation.md#developer-installation).

**Codex**

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/elierncn/aegisharness.git
codex plugin add aegis@aegisharness-marketplace
```

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/elierncn/aegisharness.git
claude plugin install aegis@aegisharness-marketplace
```

**MiniMax Code** (preview)

```bash
mcode plugin marketplace add https://github.com/elierncn/aegisharness.git
mcode plugin install aegis@aegisharness-marketplace
```

Commands are projected as Skill entrypoints under `hosts/minimax/skills/`.

**WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy** (preview)

```bash
codebuddy plugin marketplace add https://github.com/elierncn/aegisharness.git
codebuddy plugin install aegis@aegisharness-marketplace
```

Then run `/reload-plugins` and open a new session.

**Qoder** (preview)

```bash
qodercli plugin marketplace add https://github.com/elierncn/aegisharness.git
qodercli plugin install aegis@aegisharness-marketplace
```

The desktop client can register the same repository through its plugin marketplace.

**DeepSeek Harness (dsh)** (preview)

The plugin root is also the npm package `@elierncn/aegisharness-dsh`: its `package.json` declares a `dsh.bundle.patch` layer, and `lib/index.js` registers the nine commands as runtime skills with `ctx.skills`. Installation is therefore DSH's own plugin management — no files are copied into `$DSH_HOME/skills`.

```bash
# 1) CLI (Node.js 22.19+ / 24+)
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh

# 2) Install the bundle; dsh appends it to the profile's dsh.profile.bundles
dsh plugin --profile web add @elierncn/aegisharness-dsh

# 3) Confirm the composed tree contains the entry, then start a new session
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A1 aegisharness
dsh web
```

> `@elierncn/aegisharness-dsh` is not on npm yet. Before the first publish, replace step 2 with the `file:` local install: `dsh plugin --profile web add "file:/abs/path/to/aegisharness/aegisharness"`.

Inside DSH, `/aegis:init` is triggered as `/aegis-init` because Skill names are kebab-case. See the [dsh installer](aegisharness/hosts/deepseek-dsh/installer.md) for the `file:` developer install, the skills-directory fallback and the full command mapping.

**After any installation**, bind the Host Context explicitly when several hosts share the same terminal:

```bash
export AEGISHARNESS_PLATFORM=<host-id>
python3 aegisharness/scripts/host_runtime_cli.py resolve --platform <host-id>
```

The root marketplace installs the `aegisharness/` plugin, not the platform. Preview hosts do not install hooks, telemetry or automatic updates; see the [host support matrix](docs/host-support-matrix.md). See [hook verification, updates and uninstall](docs/installation.md).

### 2. Run a small feature

The product name is **AegisHarness**; its plugin ID and command namespace are **`aegis`**.

Open a new agent session in the **application repository** you want to develop. Review the plugin hooks through the host's native interface, then enter these commands in the conversation:

```text
/aegis:init
/aegis:propose task-filter ./requirements/task-filter.md --loop
```

Use the [self-contained task-filter example](examples/README.md) to get a starter project, requirement and acceptance check. `--loop` runs Propose → Apply → Archive, pausing for decisions or blockers. It does not publish or deploy your code.

You can also run `/aegis:propose`, `/aegis:apply` and `/aegis:archive` separately. See [all nine commands](docs/user-guide.md#commands).

Use `/aegis:status` to inspect progress and blockers, and `/aegis:config` to view or change telemetry consent and reporting addresses.

## How it relates to Superpowers and OpenSpec

These projects offer useful, overlapping approaches to agent-assisted development. This comparison highlights their emphasis:

| Project | Emphasis |
| --- | --- |
| [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) | Composable development skills and practices: brainstorming, planning, TDD, subagent execution and code review. |
| [OpenSpec](https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec) | Specification-driven change management: align on proposals, specs, design and tasks, then implement and archive changes. |
| **AegisHarness** | Bring project Harness constraints and reusable knowledge into the development lifecycle, with an optional platform to observe, evaluate and improve the framework itself. |

See [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for attribution and related work.

## A platform for iterating on AegisHarness

**aegisharness-platform serves maintainers who change AegisHarness's commands, workflow rules, skills and context-loading strategies.** It connects usage evidence, controlled version comparisons and candidate improvements into a framework iteration process.

| Capability | The question it helps answer | What you can inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Observability** | Where does AegisHarness encounter friction in actual use? | Workflow execution records, stage status, time and Token usage, rework and evidence quality. |
| **Evaluation** | Does this change improve the AegisHarness framework? | Frozen Base and Candidate versions exercised against the same Cases; inspect results, regression gates and execution evidence. |
| **Evolution** | Which framework change is worth testing next? | Evidence-backed hypotheses, isolated candidate changes and frozen experiments; review the proposal and decide whether to adopt the result. |

**The evaluation target is the AegisHarness framework version or change.** Development scenarios exercise that framework, and their outcomes provide evidence about its behavior. This platform supports framework iteration; it is not a general service for grading the business code AegisHarness generates.

![Framework iteration: observe, hypothesize, build a candidate, evaluate, review and adopt, then observe again](docs/assets/readme-evolution-en.png)

### Three views of framework iteration

| View | What you can inspect |
| --- | --- |
| **Observability** | Workflow friction, stage status, time and token usage, rework and evidence quality. |
| **Evaluation** | Frozen Base and Candidate versions exercised against the same Cases; regression gates and execution evidence. |
| **Evolution** | Evidence-backed hypotheses, isolated candidate changes and a reviewable adoption decision. |

Run the Demo (`python -m web_ui.demo --port 7860`) and open `localhost:7860` to inspect these views.
The bundled data is synthetic: these are interface examples, not measured improvements or real model results.

All three views use **synthetic demonstration data**. Evaluation uses Mock execution; the evolution view shows the evidence loop and a synthetic evidence summary. These are interface examples, not measured improvements or real model results.

Real evaluation requires your own model service and calibrated Cases. Evolution proposals and candidate changes remain reviewable; adopting and publishing a framework change requires human decisions.

### Try the platform Demo

Download or clone the source first, then run these commands from the combined repository root:

macOS / Linux (Bash / Zsh):

```bash
cd aegisharness-platform
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e ".[server]"
python -m web_ui.demo --port 7860
```

Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
cd aegisharness-platform
py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e ".[server]"
python -m web_ui.demo --port 7860
```

For Windows CMD, use `.venv\Scripts\activate.bat` instead of the PowerShell activation command; the other Windows commands are the same.

Open [localhost:7860](http://127.0.0.1:7860). The Demo generates synthetic Case, Mock Run and telemetry data from bundled source examples in a temporary runtime directory. Generated databases, acceptance-test Runs and candidate workspaces are not included in the source or wheel. Background evolution and model analysis are disabled. The built-in Demo does not generate evolution hypotheses; the evolution view shows the overview without generated hypotheses or candidates.

## Repository map

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`aegisharness/`](aegisharness/README.md) | Agent plugin, workflow commands, host adapters and runtime tests |
| [`aegisharness-platform/`](aegisharness-platform/README.md) | Optional observability, evaluation and evolution for the AegisHarness framework |
| [`examples/`](examples/README.md) | Reproducible starter project and observable acceptance criteria |
| [`docs/`](docs/user-guide.md) | Configuration, workflows, troubleshooting and verification boundaries |

For version evaluation, point the platform at the source Git checkout or a directory inside it. It locates the plugin independently in each frozen commit, supporting standalone, combined and nested monorepo layouts. Multiple plugin copies require an explicit Git-relative path; no nested Git repository is required. [Evaluation setup](docs/user-guide.md#version-evaluation).

## Data and feedback

Telemetry is off until the user explicitly enables it. Async reporting and the optional feedback skill have **no default platform address**. Without a configured destination, feedback cannot be sent; the entrypoint remains available. Configuring an endpoint does not authorize sending feedback: the content and destination still require approval.

Report community bugs through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/elierncn/aegisharness/issues); no platform deployment is required. Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for vulnerabilities. [Data and feedback details](docs/user-guide.md#feedback).

## Roadmap

Two planned directions will help more teams shape AegisHarness around their development practices:

- **More coding agents.** Host Kits are manifest-driven; see [Add a new host](docs/add-new-host.md) to onboard another agent.
- **Configurable workflows.** Let teams configure workflow stages and their order to fit their development process.

These are planned capabilities. The current release ships six Host Kits with the Propose → Apply → Archive workflow; see the [host support matrix](docs/host-support-matrix.md). Share concrete use cases through the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) to help shape these directions.

## Documentation and contribution

- [Installation and updates](docs/installation.md)
- [Host support matrix](docs/host-support-matrix.md) · [Add a new host](docs/add-new-host.md)
- [Migration notes](MIGRATION-NOTES.md) · [Attribution](ATTRIBUTION.md)
- [Complete user guide](docs/user-guide.md) · [中文指南](docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md)
- [Development and contribution](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

Source version: **AegisHarness 1.0.0 · aegisharness-platform 1.0.0**. Public repository and release availability are separate from the version embedded in this source copy.
