# StudyHub search extension

A companion bundle for [StudyHub](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub). It lets StudyHub search large textbooks by topic: StudyHub's Settings and its "Large textbooks" card install it with one click, and build the index with one more.

It contains one small DSH plugin that mounts DSH's MCP client for [mcp-local-rag](https://github.com/shinpr/mcp-local-rag) (MIT, pinned in `package.json`). The server is started with the Node that DSH itself runs on and finds its files next to this package, so nothing in DSH's configuration is edited by hand, and no system Node, Python or Docker is needed. Index and model cache live under `<DSH home>/study/retrieval`.

The first index build downloads the embedding model (about 90 MB, per the server's documentation). The default model favours English; keyword matching still helps Chinese text. To download from another address, set `hfEndpoint` (an https URL) in `<DSH home>/study/retrieval.json`, which StudyHub's Settings also offers under Advanced; the server's documentation describes this as `HF_ENDPOINT`.

Before the server starts, the extension checks its index. An index the server could not open (for example one whose newest files a crash left empty) is moved aside to `chunks.lance.broken-<time>` (kept, never deleted), `<DSH home>/study/retrieval/reset.json` records when and why, and the server starts on an empty index; StudyHub then asks for the index to be built again. The check opens the table with the server's own LanceDB in a separate process, and only when its newest version changed since the last check passed.

License: MIT.

# StudyHub

English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Turn your lecture slides into questions that each link back to their page; finish a round and see yourself getting it.

Free and open source, your materials stay on your computer; pick your own model and pay for what you use.

StudyHub is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/), an AI agent app. DSH runs as a desktop app or as a web page served from your own computer, and StudyHub opens inside it.

[Try the demo](https://daily-flashcard-demo.ziangw1358.chatgpt.site) · [Install guide](docs/install.md) · [Release 4.5.1](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/tag/v4.5.1) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

The demo runs in your browser with sample questions and prepared AI replies. It needs no install and no key, and your progress there stays in that browser.

## At a glance

- **Made for:** students who learn from slides, PDFs, notes and recorded lectures, in English or Chinese.
- **Cost:** StudyHub is free and open source (MIT). Browsing sources, answering questions and review scheduling are free, with no model calls. Generating questions and AI help are billed by your model provider. StudyHub shows the estimated tokens before a generation run and the actual tokens after it, and **Statistics** totals the last 7 or 30 days.
- **Network and cost:** supported regions, free allowances and pricing depend on each provider’s current terms. If installing from the GitHub address fails, see the notes under [Quick start](#quick-start).
- **Computers:** the install links below cover Windows x64 and macOS on Apple silicon. For other systems, check current DSH support or use the web version with Node.js 22.19 or later.
- **Requires:** DSH 0.2 (0.2.0-rc.2 or later, below 0.3).
- **Your data:** the library is a folder on your computer. [Data and privacy](#data-and-privacy) lists what is sent where.

## What you can do

- **Make questions from your own sources.** Pick pages or chapters and generate flashcards, single- or multiple-choice, open-response or fill-in-the-blank questions. Every question cites its passage, and you review the draft before you publish it.
- **Move between questions and sources.** A citation opens the passage it came from. In a source, paragraph and table markers lead to the questions and explanations linked to them.
- **Practise and review.** Start today's study from the **Study library**, shape each course's **Learning method** (`学法`) or ask the main chat for **AI-guided study** (`AI 带学`), click **Help me understand** on any question, and let FSRS-6 schedule your reviews.
- **Add exam focus highlights, even from screenshots.** Drop chat screenshots, whiteboard photos or scope notes into **Add exam focus…** (works with both vision and text-only models such as DeepSeek): focus topics schedule at shorter intervals, go first in daily rounds and study plans, and generate deeper application and advanced questions. Once topics are saved, the home shows how many are mastered, not yet and without questions, with a link to practise the ones you can't do yet; **Course settings** lists each topic with its questions.
- **Find weak points.** Use **Mistakes & weak points**, **Statistics** and **Mock exam**, which offers a multiple-choice paper, a case paper or an oral interview.
- **Finish with a daily recap.** After answering 10 distinct questions in one course on the same day, generate one recap across its chapters. Retries count once. Choose a friendly or professional tone and opt into automatic generation in Settings. Recaps use the source reader; saving one as a source and publishing on CSDN are separate actions.
- **Turn recordings into text.** Import a lecture recording, or transcribe a **Live class** as it happens, and get a Chinese–English transcript you can generate questions from.
- **Read and organise.** The reader keeps its toolbar short (**Contents**, **Make questions**, **Mistakes**, **Mind map**); search, **Translate…**, display settings and **Study tools** are in **More**, and **Practise these pages** is the arrow beside **Make questions**. Courses, **Study notes**, **Tasks** and a **Knowledge outline** keep a term's work together.
- **Works well with** the open-source [Archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) (MIT licence, by tt-a1i; no partnership with StudyHub): your assistant can draw a knowledge outline as an interactive diagram with it, and StudyHub keeps and shows the file. See [Works well with other tools](docs/companions.md).

## Quick start

| You want to | You need | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Take the sample course and tour, browse sources, practise existing questions | StudyHub only | Free, no model calls |
| Generate questions, explanations and **Help me understand** | A model provider key in DSH **Settings › Models** | Billed by your provider, for example the [DeepSeek API](https://platform.deepseek.com/) |
| Turn recordings into text | A transcription key in StudyHub **Settings › Audio transcription** | SiliconFlow SenseVoice supports recording transcription. Gemini and Groq availability and allowances depend on the provider |

1. **Install DSH** (skip this if you have it). Use the official [Windows x64 installer](https://download.deepseek.com/desktop/dsh-latest-windows-x64.exe) or [macOS Apple silicon installer](https://download.deepseek.com/desktop/dsh-latest-macos-arm64.dmg). On any other computer, install Node.js 22.19 or later and run `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.
2. **Install StudyHub.** In DSH, open **Plugins**, click **Add plugin**, paste this address and click **Enable**:

   ```text
   https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/download/v4.5.1/ericwang1358-dsh-daily-flashcard-4.5.1.tgz
   ```

   Check that the package is `@ericwang1358/dsh-daily-flashcard`, version **4.5.1**. The [release page](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases) is the newest channel: npm's `latest` tag can lag behind it, so install the `.tgz` from the release page. StudyHub then opens by itself. Later, open it from **StudyHub** in DSH's left sidebar (the session tab and the right sidebar also work); you do not need to send a chat message first.
3. **Take the tour (optional, a minute or two).** On the welcome page, click **Load the sample and start the tour**. The 7-step tour follows the first-run line's order (where the model is set up, add a source, make questions, check the draft, practise), pointing at the real controls, and ends on the line's step 2. A full tour of every page, Jobs included, is offered at its end. The sample makes no model calls and can be removed with one click.
4. **Add a model.** Paste a key in DSH **Settings › Models** and choose a model in your session. Until then, StudyHub says so wherever a step needs a model, with a **Go to settings** link, instead of letting the step fail later; **Settings › Library & model** shows **Model connected** or **Model not connected** and the steps.
5. **Start with your own material.** Click **Add source** and drop several PDFs, slides or notes at once. Then use **Generate from sources**, review the draft, publish it and practise.

Notes on installing:

- **Already use DSH?** Install only the plugin. Keep your current desktop app or web server, profile, model settings and workspace.
- **GitHub address fails, or says `unable to get local issuer certificate`?** Use your browser to [download the complete 4.5.1 package](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/download/v4.5.1/ericwang1358-dsh-daily-flashcard-4.5.1.tgz). **Keep the original `.tgz` file; do not extract it.** In **Add plugin**, enter the absolute path to the file itself, for example `C:\Users\your-name\Downloads\ericwang1358-dsh-daily-flashcard-4.5.1.tgz`, replacing it with your actual saved path. The file must be on the computer or server that runs DSH. See the [local-file install steps](docs/install.md#if-dsh-cannot-download-from-github).
- **Which file on the release page?** A standard install needs only that complete package. It includes the main entry and six components, seven entries in total; there is no need to download, extract or merge the separate component packages. StudyHub installs the optional search extension when you click **Install the search extension**. The checksum list and two setup guides are there for reference.
- More options, including the command line: [installation and model setup guide](docs/install.md). Setup guides you can open in a browser: [English](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/download/v4.5.1/StudyHub-4.5.1-Setup.html) · [Chinese](https://github.com/EricWang1358/dsh-web-studyhub/releases/download/v4.5.1/StudyHub-4.5.1-Setup.zh-CN.html). DSH itself comes only from the official sources in step 1.

## Use StudyHub

### Add sources

Click **Add source**, choose the course, then drop several files at once or paste text. Recordings go in the **Audio / recording** tab of the same window.

| Format | Limit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDF | 8 MB, 200 pages | Kept as one document that you expand to pages. For bigger books, see below |
| Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx, and the old .ppt) | 40 MB | Only text is read. Pictures, charts and SmartArt are skipped, and so are Word text boxes, headers and footers. A presentation keeps one page per slide, with its speaker notes. In an old .ppt, bullet indent levels are not kept |
| Markdown, HTML, TXT | 8 MB | |
| JSON deck | 2 MB | Questions you already have, or ones written elsewhere ([format](docs/json-import.md)) |
| Subtitles (.srt, .vtt) | 8 MB | Needs the audio component |
| Audio (MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, OGG, FLAC, OPUS, WEBM, AIFF) | 512 MB, 8 hours | See [Transcribe recordings](#transcribe-recordings) |

Old .doc files (and .wps, .key, .pages) are not read. Save them as .docx or PDF first. Password-protected files are not read either.

**Large textbooks** (over 8 MB or 200 pages):

- Click **Convert with MinerU** in the import window. StudyHub converts PDFs up to 800 MB and imports the result as one paged book that you can choose by chapter.
- MinerU runs on this computer. Click **One-click install** in **Settings › PDF conversion** (or right in the import window): StudyHub puts the program, Python and the models into one folder, not on the system drive by default, with no admin rights and nothing to install beforehand. The PDF stays on your computer and no token is needed. The cloud route was removed in 3.5.5 ([details](docs/mineru-conversion.md)).
- To practise across a whole book, use the search extension or the **Step-by-step path** on **Create deck**.

See [large textbooks](docs/large-documents.md) and [MinerU conversion](docs/mineru-conversion.md).

For another route, open the [external Marker guide](docs/marker-external.md) from Add material, download a script to run yourself, then choose its paginated Markdown output. Install Marker and its models separately; code and model licences apply separately.

### Generate a deck

1. Open **Create deck**. On the **Generate from sources** tab, choose sources by document (or by chapter for a big book), then the question type, count and difficulty. Not sure what to focus on? **Suggest a focus** proposes topics from your source titles and headings, without sending the full text.
2. Click **Generate & check deck**. The job runs in the background; you can keep studying.
3. Review the draft and its citations, then publish it. Publishing checks every question again; questions with a problem stay in the draft. Drafts stay separate from published questions.

To add to an existing deck, choose that deck: approved questions are added, and the old questions and their review progress stay. To bring in questions you already have, use the **Import JSON deck** tab.

<details>
<summary>How generation checks questions</summary>

- Each batch gets one independent review. Questions that pass are kept, and any shortfall is reported. Version 2.5.8 introduced one citation repair; the current workflow verifies knowledge points and answers first, corrects those preparation stages when needed, then writes and independently reviews questions. A question flagged only for wording is re-worded once and re-reviewed alone; there is no open-ended repair loop.
- When you add to an existing deck, reviewed questions are saved even if the generation budget runs out, with no second publish step.
- Citations and question structure are checked in code. The content itself can still be wrong, so read the draft. More in [question quality checks](docs/assessment-quality.md).
- Source text is given to the model as evidence, never as instructions to follow.
- Courses label sources and decks; folders only group decks for display. Every action uses only the courses, sources and decks you selected.

</details>

Save a default question type, count, content language, difficulty and focus in **Settings › Question defaults**; each new request can override them. Questions per batch, parallel batches and the time budget are there too, initially 5, 4 and 20 minutes. Started tasks and continued drafts keep their original choices. See [Generation pace](docs/generation-agents-sidebar.md#what-a-generation-task-does).

### Practise and review

Today's learning plan connects tasks to the library home. Ask AI for a plan based on real due reviews, weak areas, available materials and accepted tasks. Give feedback to revise it, or accept. Each action has a reason and estimated duration; suggestions become board tasks only after acceptance, with direct start and resume controls.

Today's time budget is separate from your saved weekday/weekend pace; zero minutes supports a rest day. Unfinished actions are allocated within the budget, and completed actions still count toward today's workload. Record actual time after completion. After at least five comparable completed-day records, the median estimates your usual pace; explicitly saved preferences always take priority.

Practice progress counts actual answers, flows use completed steps, and you explicitly mark a reading block complete. Opening content or skipping questions does not count, and completing an action does not establish mastery. AI sees compact titles, progress and exam dates, not full materials. Invalid or unavailable AI results are clearly labelled as local suggestions. Plans are saved by library and date, alongside ordinary board tasks.

- Answer, then read the explanation. **Help me understand** asks a tutor about the current question.
- Rate flashcards and open answers from 0 to 5; FSRS-6 picks the next review date from your rating and the days that really passed since the last review. Each rating button shows the gap it would give. Answering and scheduling make no model calls.
- **Mistakes & weak points** groups wrong answers by deck (or by topic), filters them by deck, status and keyword, and can **Generate variants**. **Mock exam** and **Statistics** show what still needs work.

<details>
<summary>How Help me understand keeps context</summary>

When DSH supports local subagents, repeated **Help me understand** on the same question keeps the same tutor and its conversation, and follow-ups sent together are answered in order. Moving to another question, editing the question or switching model starts a new tutor. A tutor is released after 2 idle minutes or 8 rounds; a new one receives the last 3 answered exchanges. Earlier answers stay saved with the question.

</details>

### Read your sources

- Sources keep their original file and earlier versions, and open full screen.
- **Original page** shows the PDF page behind a citation, **More › Translate…** adds a translation, and **Practise these pages** (the arrow beside **Make questions**, shortcut P) quizzes you on the pages you are reading.
- Select a passage to ask about it, or to generate candidate questions that you review and add to an existing deck.
- A source imported as text only can get its original back with **Add the original file**, with no reimport.
- When a source changes and a linked position is no longer certain, StudyHub asks you to relocate it instead of guessing.
- Explanations, notes, **Tasks** and the **Inbox** link back to the question or source they are about. The reader and question links help you return to the current question.
- Press `?` to see every keyboard shortcut.

## Choose a model

Generation, explanations and learning help use the model selected in your DSH session. To use a different model for StudyHub, open **Settings › Library & model** and change **Generation model** from **Follow current session**. DSH stores the model credentials.

- **Everyday use:** the [official DeepSeek API](https://platform.deepseek.com/).
- **Heavy use:** a Coding Plan, but only if it gives you an API key and allows DSH and your actual study use. Before you buy, check its supported tools, endpoint, models, concurrency and quota rules.
- **Subscriptions are not keys:** Claude Pro/Max and ChatGPT/Codex subscriptions do not provide a general API key for DSH. Separately billed Anthropic or OpenAI APIs can be added as third-party providers.

Setup steps: [configure a model provider](docs/install.md#configure-a-model-provider). For how many tokens each feature uses, see [token usage and estimates](docs/token-usage.md).

## Transcribe recordings

1. Open **Settings › Audio transcription** and add a key. SiliconFlow SenseVoice supports recording transcription. Gemini (Google AI Studio) and Groq are also supported.
2. Open **Audio transcription**, click **Add audio** and then **Start import**. Nothing is uploaded until a provider is set up.
3. The transcript is saved as a source. Generate questions from it like any other source.

Only transcription uses these keys. Proofreading and translation use your DSH model by default, so their tokens are billed by your model provider and appear under **Model usage** in **Statistics**. **Live class** transcribes in real time and supports only Gemini.

<details>
<summary>More about audio</summary>

- With several keys, StudyHub tries Gemini free, then SiliconFlow, Groq and Gemini paid. A single import can be set to use paid keys only.
- M4A recordings over 1 hour can be split losslessly with one click.
- Recordings are processed one at a time; within a recording, 2–3 proofreading and translation windows run in parallel. Finished windows are checkpointed, and a retry reuses them.
- The **Proofreading & translation** panel sets the reasoning level for each step: Low, Medium, High or Model default. Higher levels take longer and do not guarantee better accuracy. A level the model does not support falls back to its default. Only high-confidence corrections that pass the source-location check rewrite the text; the rest are left as suggestions for you to check.
- The **Usage console** on the audio page records this plugin's requests to the transcription providers (failures and retries included), tokens and audio minutes. It shows free and paid keys separately, with a 7-day trend, and keeps 31 days. Groq's remaining daily quota comes from its responses; for Gemini, you can enter the daily limit shown in AI Studio to get an estimate. Requests from other apps, live-class streams and DSH model tokens are not counted there.
- Keys are stored in `study/audio.json` in your DSH home (by default `~/.dsh/study/audio.json`), outside the library. The interface shows only whether a key is set and its last 4 characters. Keys never enter library exports or chats. The environment variables `GEMINI_FREE_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_PAID_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY` and `SILICONFLOW_API_KEY` fill in a key that is not saved.

</details>

See [audio import](docs/audio-import.md) and [live class](docs/live-class.md).

## Use StudyHub from the DSH chat

- **Study mode preset.** For a new session, pick the agent preset **学习模式 · StudyHub** (Study mode; the label is in Chinese in both languages). The assistant then takes "materials", "my notes" or "this lecture" to mean your StudyHub library and asks when a request is ambiguous. It has the same tools as DSH's standard preset, so it can also run commands and edit files to convert material (for example split a question book by chapter) before importing it: it writes the results under `studyhub-work/` in the workspace, never deletes or overwrites your originals, and asks before installing anything.
- **Ask about your library** in the main chat: see [query sources and decks from the main chat](docs/main-session-queries.md).
- **Save a question you could not answer.** Type `/study-spar <your question>` in a DSH chat. StudyHub files it in your question bank as a flashcard. Add `--mq` for single choice or `--multi` for multiple choice; start with `--pre` to file it as a prerequisite of the question you are working on.
- **Follow background tasks** in DSH's sidebar: see [background tasks and the sidebar](docs/generation-agents-sidebar.md).

## Update StudyHub

DSH plugins do not update themselves, and restarting DSH alone keeps the old version.

- **2.1.2 and later:** StudyHub asks GitHub for a new release at most every 6 hours. When there is one, a **Version x.y.z available** chip appears in its sidebar, where x.y.z is the new version. Click it, then **Upgrade to x.y.z** and **Upgrade now**. StudyHub downloads the package, checks it against the release's `SHA256SUMS-x.y.z.txt` and hands it to DSH's plugin manager. If background tasks are running, **Stop tasks and upgrade** stops them and keeps their finished parts. The check sends no study data; switch it off in **Settings › About & updates**.
- **Older versions, or a DSH that cannot install from inside the app:** finish or cancel background tasks, open **Plugins**, uninstall StudyHub, then use **Add plugin** with the new release's package address.

Then restart DSH. Quit the desktop app fully (including the tray icon) and reopen it, or restart the web service with its original profile and reload the page. A browser refresh alone does not load new plugin code. Your library and settings are kept.

## Data and privacy

**Stays on your computer**

- The library: sources and their original files, decks, answers and review schedules, saved in shards. By default it is in the DSH session's workspace folder; choose another folder in **Settings › Library & model**.
- Transcription keys, in `study/` in your DSH home (by default `~/.dsh/study/`). They never enter the library, exports or backups. DSH keeps the model keys. (A MinerU token saved by a version before 3.5.5 stays in `study/mineru.json`; nothing reads it any more, and you can delete it.)
- The usage frequency record, if you turn it on in **Settings › Usage frequency record**. It is off by default, and StudyHub never sends it anywhere ([details](docs/usage-frequency.md)).

**Leaves your computer only when you use the feature**

- Generating questions or asking for help sends the selected source text to your model provider through DSH. **Suggest a focus** sends only titles and headings.
- Recordings go to your transcription provider. PDF conversion with MinerU runs on this computer; installing it downloads the program and its models (from mainland mirrors or the official sources) and uploads nothing.
- The update check asks GitHub for the latest version and sends no study data.

**Backups and older libraries**

- In **Settings › Import, schedule and backup**, **Backup & restore** exports one JSON file with your sources, decks, review progress and answers. Original files that were copied into the library are included; originals attached by reference are only listed.
- A restore first saves the current library under `backups/`. It is refused while a generation job is running.
- An older library is migrated on its first write, and its original file is backed up. Libraries missing newer optional fields stay usable, and data from a plugin that is not installed is kept.
- To import a library from the older `study-lib-spar` tool, use the same Settings category and choose the folder that holds `study-lib.json`, `nodes/` and `quizzes/` (not the tool's source code). The import only reads those files, keeps the due dates, intervals and sources it can parse, and importing again does not overwrite existing progress.
- Clearing finished task cards keeps the sources and questions they produced. Audio usage records and keys are not part of library backups.

## Interface language

The interface starts in Chinese when your browser's first preferred language is Chinese, and in English otherwise. Switch it with **Language** at the bottom of the sidebar; StudyHub remembers your choice. Buttons, errors, background progress, notifications, messages handed to the chat and new AI explanations follow it.

Switching does not translate what you saved: sources, file names, questions, notes and provider replies stay in their original language. New questions use the interface language unless you choose another in the **Language** field of **Create deck**. To read English under a Chinese question while you practise, click **EN** on the practice toolbar ([details](docs/translate-en.md)). Audio transcripts keep their own source and translation languages.

## Choose components

The complete package installs seven components. DSH's own plugin manager lists them as **StudyHub** (the main package), **StudyHub · Core**, **StudyHub · Materials**, **StudyHub · Question bank**, **StudyHub · Question generation**, **StudyHub · Practice & review** and **StudyHub · Audio**. Turn each one on or off there. Saved data is kept while a component is off.

- **Create deck** needs Materials, Question bank and Question generation. Practice, **Mistakes & weak points**, **Mock exam** and **Statistics** need Question bank and Practice & review.
- A component that is off hides its pages or says that it is turned off.
- If several installed packages provide the same component, turn all of them off to switch it off.
- The release page also has each component as a separate package.

Details and safe source deletion: [customise components](docs/install.md#customise-components). Command-line installs: [install from the command line](docs/install.md#install-from-the-command-line).

## Development

StudyHub is an ES-module DSH plugin built on Cordis, with a React interface bundled by esbuild. Its seven components work together through public plugin APIs; see [architecture](docs/architecture.md). The package is named `@ericwang1358/dsh-daily-flashcard`; the product name is StudyHub.

```sh
npm install --legacy-peer-deps
npm run verify         # lint, tests and build
npm run test:fast      # the tests without browser, ffmpeg and program-starting files, for quick iteration
npm run dev            # preview at http://127.0.0.1:4178 (after a build)
npm run build:demo     # static demo in output/static-demo-site/dist
npm run release:pack   # release packages and SHA256SUMS-<version>.txt in output/release-<version>
```

- `npm run dev` needs `npm run build` (or `npm run verify`) first, because it serves `dist/`. It uses a throwaway library in `output/preview-library` and keeps global study files in `output/preview-home`, never in `~/.dsh`. Add `-- --library=<dir>` to open another library, and set `STUDY_FAKE_MODEL=1` for a deterministic fake model.
- `npm run release:pack` does not build; run `npm run verify` first.
- `npm test` (and so `npm run verify` and CI) always runs every test file, starting the longest first from the durations of the last run (cached in `node_modules/.cache/studyhub-tests/`; a machine with no timings of its own, such as a CI runner, orders by `tests/test-weights.json`). Full runs on one machine take turns through a lock file in `~/.cache/studyhub-tests/`: a second run prints one line and waits (at most 20 minutes, then it goes ahead with fewer workers); set `STUDY_TEST_NO_LOCK=1` to skip the queue. `npm test -- tests/<file>.test.mjs` runs just those files without queueing.
- `npm run test:fast` skips the files named in `tests/slow-tests.json`: those that launch a browser, run ffmpeg or start another program. `tests/slow-tests-list.test.mjs` fails when a new test file does one of these and is not listed, so the fast tier stays fast; run `npm run verify` before a pull request.
- The host supplies the DSH SDKs `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm

# dsh-sidebar-dock

把 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）左栏里「工作区 / 会话记录」那一块**单独停靠到 **左 / 右 / 上 / 下**
任意一边，插件图标条、品牌行、底部设置钮留在原位 —— 用来解决「左侧栏插件装太多、会话列表被挤得没法看」。

Dock the **workspace / session list** of DeepSeek Harness to the left, right, top or bottom edge,
leaving the plugin rail where it is. Switchable at runtime in **Settings → General**.

| 设置行 | 右侧停靠 | 上侧停靠 + 自动收纳展开 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![](docs/settings.png) | ![](docs/dock-right.png) | ![](docs/dock-top-peek.png) |

## 功能

- **四向停靠**：左侧（默认，等于不改） / 右侧 / 上侧 / 下侧，点一下立即生效，无需重启。
  「工作区 / 会话记录」跟着宿主数据自动更新 —— 以后新建的工作区、会话照常出现在那一侧。
- **左栏宽度**：`原始`（保持宿主宽度，默认） / `适中 176px` / `紧凑 112px`。停靠到别的边时，
  左栏会按这个宽度收窄，把空间还给会话内容。
- **自动收纳**：面板平时收成贴边 5px 的一条线，鼠标贴到那条边才展开；移开 420ms 后自动收起。
- **触发范围**：`窄 32 / 标准 64 / 宽 104 / 很大 160` px —— 触发带只监听 `pointermove`，
  本身不可见、不接收点击，所以放大后也不会挡住任何按钮。
- 所有状态存 `localStorage`；卸载或禁用插件即自动还原宿主布局（不写宿主文件、不改宿主配置）。

## 安装

本插件是一个 DSH **bundle**（`package.json` 里声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`）。

**方式一（推荐）** —— 在 DSH 的 Agent 会话里让它安装这个目录：

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=<本仓库的绝对路径>
```

它会把自己加进 profile 依赖并自动 enable，返回 `application: applied` 即生效。

**方式二** —— 命令行（只加依赖，之后还要在「插件」界面把 bundle 打开）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile-name> add <本仓库的绝对路径>
```

装好（或改了 `client.js`）之后，**已经在跑的窗口需要重载一次页面 / 重启软件端**才会拿到新的
client 模块（DSH 的插件集合在启动时定型，应用内的「刷新」按钮在部分版本上救不了）。

卸载：在「插件」界面关掉 / 移除该 bundle。`localStorage` 里的几个键可以留着，下次装回来直接生效。

## 设置项

**设置 → 通用 → 工作区列表停靠位置**

| 控件 | 取值 | `localStorage` 键 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 停靠位置 | `左侧` / `右侧` / `上侧` / `下侧` | `dsh-sidebar-dock/position` |
| 左栏宽度 | `原始` / `适中 176px` / `紧凑 112px` | `dsh-sidebar-dock/rail` |
| 触发范围 | `窄 32` / `标准 64` / `宽 104` / `很大 160` px | `dsh-sidebar-dock/zone` |
| 自动收纳 | 开 / 关 | `dsh-sidebar-dock/peek` |

想恢复原样：把停靠位置点回 `左侧`，或清掉上面几个键。

## 原理（为什么是样式表）

宿主 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout` 的三列 grid 写死在 AppFrame 里，`ctx.layout` 只暴露
`toggleSidebar / openRightbar / closeRightbar / selectPanel`，没有「换边」的 API；而
`sidebar.workspaces` 是 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar` 内部渲染的，插件无法把它挂到别的 slot。
所以这里走**最小侵入的样式表**：

1. `apply()` 之后用 **DOM 顺序锚点**认列：`[data-shell-bottom]` 的父节点是 frame，它前面的 3 个元素
   兄弟依次是 `sidebar / center / rightbar`（`DocumentTitle` 渲染 null，不占位），再给
   `[data-slot="sidebar.workspaces"]` 打上 `data-dssb-tree`。
2. `measure()` 从宿主**自己的计算轨道**（`getComputedStyle(frame).gridTemplateColumns`）读回列宽，
   算出 `--dssb-rail`（左栏视觉宽）、`--dssb-rail-width`、`--dssb-pull`、`--dssb-right-rail`；
   窗口缩放、右栏开合都会重算 —— 宽度从不写死。
3. 一张包自有样式表按 `html[data-dssb-pos]` / `html[data-dssb-peek]` 生效：
   - `left`（默认）：**一条规则都不写**，与宿主完全一致；
   - 停靠在别处：左栏按 `--dssb-rail-width` 收窄，center 用 `margin-left:-pull` 贴过来（不留空档），
     整棵树 `position:fixed` 停到目标边，center 用 padding 让出面板厚度，**不覆盖会话**。
4. 卸载 / 禁用时移除属性、样式表、数据标记和测得的自定义属性，布局自动还原。

### 踩过的坑（留档）

- **`height:5px` 收不到 5px**：元素是 `box-sizing:border-box`，padding 合计 20px + border 0.5px，
  border-box 下 used height 被撑到 21px。收起态必须同时 `padding:0`。
- **设置行显示 `position.title`**：内联词典是嵌套的（`{position:{title}}`），查找却用扁平键。
  现在按点路径取，并且 `props.t` → locale 命名空间 → 内置词典逐级回退，最坏也不显示键名。
- **壁纸主题下穿模**：`--dsw-specific-sidebar-fill` 是半透明的，会话文字会透上来。改用
  `--dsw-alias-bg-base` + `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-1` 渐变 + `backdrop-filter: blur(18px)`。
- **`renderSlot` 的占位元素是 `display:contents`**：要给它的子节点打 `position:fixed` 前必须先
  `display:flex !important`，否则没有盒子。
- **收起侧栏时树是空的**：`WorkspaceBrowser` 在 `wide=false` 时只渲染图标变体。所以停靠在非左侧时
  先通过公开的 `ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()` 展开侧栏；若仍收着就**不接管布局**并在设置行提示。

## 已知边界

- 侧栏收起（rail 态）时插件不接管布局，设置行会提示先展开。
- 非左侧停靠时宿主的分栏拖拽把手会隐藏：它的 `left` 是按默认 lane 算的像素值，换边后必然错位。
  改回「左侧」即恢复。
- 右栏（rightbar / better-sidebar 等）保持原位，面板会让开它；但其它插件自己的固定层
  （例如顶部 tab、右下气泡）z-index 更高，可能压住面板边角。
- DSH 升级后宿主 class 名可能变（hash 前缀）。本插件不依赖 class 名，只依赖
  `data-shell-bottom` / `data-rightbar-col` / `data-slot="sidebar.workspaces"` 这几个稳定属性。
- 官方 `ui-plugin.md` 建议「挑一个已经分配好空间的 slot，不要读别人的 DOM」。本需求物理上做不到
  （宿主不给换边 API，slot 里也没有可放树的位置），因此采用**只加可移除样式 + 自己的 data 属性**
  的最小侵入方案，并把边界写在这里。

## 目录结构

```
.
├── client.js           # Client 半：标记 / 测量 / 样式表 / 指针揭示 / 设置行（全部逻辑）
├── index.js            # Host 半（空实现，只为保住 Loader 行）
├── cordis.patch.yml    # bundle 的 insert 行
├── locale/{zh,en}.json # meta.title / description 与行文案
├── icon.svg            # 插件图标
├── docs/               # README 截图
├── CHANGELOG.md
└── LICENSE
```

## 开发

```bash
node --check client.js     # 语法检查（CSS 是模板字符串，注意别在注释里写反引号）
```

- 以 `link:` 方式装进 profile 后，改源码即时生效，只需重载页面。
- 设置行走 `ctx.slots.register({ name, id, order }, DockRow)`，标题、控件、描述全部自绘
  （`settings.general.item` 不向 occupant 投影任何 label）。
- 想换包名 / 发到 npm：改 `package.json` 的 `name`（例如 `dsh-sidebar-dock`）后重装一次 bundle 即可，
  `client.js` 里的 `NS` 不需要跟着改。

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# dsh-tower DeepSeek Harness bundle for [agent-control-tower](../../README.md): drive a control tower from inside a DSH session. Registers five tools on the harness tool registry: | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `tower_dispatch` | dispatch a brief to a role, return that role's report (`summary` / `files` / `checks` / `open issues`) and the task id | | `tower_inbox` | list the reports roles have filed, optionally mark them read | | `tower_accept` | verify a reported task (files exist, checks carry results, `verify_commands` pass) and accept it — or get the rejection reasons | | `tower_rework` | send a task back with feedback and re-dispatch it (round + 1) | | `tower_status` | list the task board | | `tower_roles` | list the roles (bots) with their write scope, round budget and wired DSH session id | | `tower_role_add` | create a role (bot): appends `tower.toml`, writes `roles//AGENT.md`, wires the session id | | `tower_role_remove` | unregister a role (bot), optionally deleting its charter directory | The tools shell out to the Python CLI, so it stays the single implementation. **No runtime dependencies.** ## Install ### Prerequisites - **DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 or newer**, desktop app or CLI. The bundle declares `engines.dsh`, so an incompatible harness now refuses it with an explicit message instead of failing at mount time. - **The Python package on the `PATH` of the process that runs DSH.** Every tool shells out to `tower`; installing it into a virtualenv you never activate for DSH makes every call fail with `spawn tower ENOENT`. ```sh python -m pip install agent-control-tower # or: pip install -e /path/to/agent-control-tower tower init . # once, in your project ``` ### DSH desktop app The desktop app owns its profile: `dsh plugin --profile desktop ...` refuses with `profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`. Two working routes: 1. **Plugins page (preferred).** Install the bundle from this checkout through the app's plugin manager, then restart the app. 2. **Hand-install into `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`**: - copy the package to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-tower` as a **real directory** (the loader resolves bundles through the profile's `node_modules`; do not leave a symlink), - add `"dsh-tower"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile's `package.json`, plus a `"dsh-tower": "file:..."` entry under `dependencies` so a later `pnpm install` keeps resolving the local checkout, - restart the app and check the tool list for the five `tower_*` tools. ### DSH CLI profiles ```sh dsh plugin --profile add ./packages/dsh-tower ``` The bundle row is inserted by [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) as `id: tower`. ### If the tools never appear A bundle that throws inside `apply()` — for example a tool schema the harness rejects — fails to mount **silently**: no tools, no dialog. Boot the profile from a terminal and read stderr, which is where the harness prints `tower (dsh-tower): ...`: ```sh deepseek-harness/resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd --profile ``` To inspect one profile in isolation, copy its `package.json` + `cordis.patch.yml` into a scratch `DSH_HOME`, boot it there and keep the terminal output. ## Configuration All optional; set them in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` as a later layer targeting `id: tower`: ```yaml - id: tower config: workspace: C:/abs/path/to/project # default: process.cwd() towerBin: tower # default: "tower" # python: python3 # with towerBin: "__python__" -> python -m control_tower timeoutMs: 1800000 # per-call timeout (30 min) ``` The desktop app hot-reloads `cordis.patch.yml`, so configuration changes apply without a restart; changes to the bundle list itself (or to this package's code) need one. If no `tower.toml` / `tower.yaml` / `tower.json` is found in `workspace`, the tools fail with an actionable error instead of inventing results. ## Example: a lease-style loop from a DSH session 1. `tower_dispatch { role: "frontend", brief: "Rework the hero: two-column, image frame, proof band. Deliver before/after screenshots at 1440 and 390." }` 2. `tower_inbox {}` — see what came back. 3. `tower_accept { task: "T-0001" }` — verifies; if it fails you get the reasons. 4. `tower_rework { task: "T-0001", note: "Checks list no results; re-run the suite" }` — when it is not good enough. The DSH session never has to paste briefs between windows, and "done" has to survive verification. ## Why a bundle and not a skill The value here is *state*, not prompts: tasks, reports, rounds and a verifier. Skins/skills cannot hold that between sessions; a bundle can, because the tools below it are plain files. ## License MIT
# agent-control-tower **One agent to talk to. Many agents doing the work. Evidence before "done".** A local control tower for role-based AI agent teams — dispatch, report, verify, accept or rework. DSH-first, adapter-portable, no SaaS, no database, no daemon. [![English](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-English-blue.svg)](README.md) [![简体中文](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-%E7%AE%80%E4%BD%93%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87-red.svg)](README.zh.md) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-3776AB?style=flat&logo=python&logoColor=white)](pyproject.toml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2EA44F?style=flat)](LICENSE) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-239%20python%20%2B%2027%20node-brightgreen?style=flat)](tests) [![CI](https://github.com/evolution301/agent-control-tower/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/evolution301/agent-control-tower/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/evolution301/agent-control-tower?style=flat&label=release)](https://github.com/evolution301/agent-control-tower/releases) [![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-PyYAML%20only-lightgrey?style=flat)](pyproject.toml) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-D97757?style=flat)](packages/dsh-tower)
![architecture](docs/assets/architecture.png) ## The problem You can already get one agent to write code, one to write copy, one to review. What breaks is **the handoff between them** — in five predictable ways: | What actually happens | What it costs you | |---|---| | **Self-grading** — the agent that did the work also reports "done, tests pass". It never ran them. | You ship a bug and find it in production. | | **Context rot** — a long session compacts its history, and the deliverable was "in the conversation". | Re-doing work, contradicting earlier decisions, circular rounds. | | **Silent collisions** — two agents edit the same file in the same round; both report success. | Lost work, regressions nobody can explain. | | **No audit trail** — which role changed what, on which instruction? | You cannot review, reproduce, or hand the project over. | | **Ping-pong** — "fix it" → "fixed" → "still broken". Nothing tracks rounds or forces escalation. | Hours burned; you become the message bus. | `agent-control-tower` is the missing middle layer. ## The loop ![demo](docs/assets/demo.gif)

Real output: tower demo → tower dispatch → tower accept → tower status / tower log

| Dispatch | Verify & accept | |---|---| | ![dispatch](docs/assets/terminal-dispatch.png) | ![accept](docs/assets/terminal-accept.png) | | Audit trail — just files | |---| | ![status](docs/assets/terminal-status.png) | ```bash tower dispatch frontend "Rework the home layout. Deliver before/after screenshots at 1440 and 390." tower inbox # what came back tower accept T-0001 # files exist? checks carry results? verify_commands pass? tower rework T-0001 --note "Checks list no results; re-run the suite" ``` ## Who it is for **Good fit** - You already run **2–8 agent sessions** (DSH, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider, plain API) and you are the one copy-pasting between them. - **Indie devs / small teams** building something multi-part: an app (backend + frontend + QA), a content site (research → copy → design → SEO), a data pipeline. - **Agencies / freelancers** who must show a client *what was done and how it was verified* — the ledger and reports are that answer. - **Anyone burned** by an agent saying "done" when it was not. - **CI / automation** that wants reproducible agent work: `tower demo` runs the loop offline in under a second. **Not a good fit** - One-shot tasks ("rename this variable") — a single prompt is faster. - You want agents to talk to each other freely — this design is deliberately hub-and-spoke. - You want a hosted dashboard / multi-tenant service — this is a local CLI with adapters. ## What you get | Without the tower | With the tower | |---|---| | You paste briefs between windows | `tower dispatch ""` — contract and write scope included | | "Done ✅", no evidence | Reports must list **Files** (must exist) and **Checks** (must carry a result); `verify_commands` run for real | | Deliverables live in chat | Deliverables in `roles//`, reports in `-REPORT.md` | | Nobody knows who changed what | Append-only `.tower/ledger.jsonl`, timestamped | | Rounds loop forever | `round` counter + `max_rounds` → the tower stops and tells you to escalate | | Two agents overwrite each other | `write_scopes` per role, one directory per role | | Work lost after compaction | State on disk; `tower rework T-0012` resumes with the note attached | | Can't hand the project over | `git log` of reports and tasks *is* the handover doc | | You re-read every report to see if a human is needed | `tower attention` lists only `ready` / `blocked` / `failed` | | A retry or a double-click creates duplicate work | `tower dispatch --key ` returns the existing task | ## Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/evolution301/agent-control-tower.git cd agent-control-tower python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate pip install -e . ``` Python 3.10+. One runtime dependency (`PyYAML`). ## 60-second demo (no model, no network, no API key) ```bash tower demo ``` ``` [1] dispatched T-0001 -> reported [2] verify: PASS [3] accepted T-0001 [4] ledger lines: 5 ``` The `mock` adapter writes a placeholder artifact and a real report, so the entire dispatch → report → verify → accept loop is deterministic and CI-friendly. ## Use it with DSH (primary) The pattern was extracted from a real [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/) deployment: one lead session steering several long-lived role sessions through a multi-week build, verifying every delivery. ```yaml # tower.toml roles: frontend: description: Layout, components, styling, browser verification. adapter: dsh write_scopes: ["web/"] adapters: dsh: base_url: "http://127.0.0.1:65163" sessions: frontend: "session-acc99990-..." ``` → Full walkthrough: **[docs/dsh-quickstart.md](docs/dsh-quickstart.md)** — create role sessions, wire config, run the loop, plus the five failure modes the reference project hit and how the code prevents them. ### Drive it from inside DSH: `packages/dsh-tower` A companion bundle registers five tools on the harness tool registry, so the session never leaves the conversation: ```bash dsh plugin --profile add ./packages/dsh-tower ``` `tower_dispatch` · `tower_inbox` · `tower_accept` · `tower_rework` · `tower_status` → [packages/dsh-tower](packages/dsh-tower/README.md) ## Panel: what needs me, and is this team working well `tower panel` serves one read-only page on `127.0.0.1` (default 8787, `--port` to move it). It answers three questions in the order a person asks them: 1. **now** — what needs you (only person-states get red), what is in flight; 2. **who** — one robot per role, its face *is* its state (blinking = idle, hopping = working, X eyes shaking = failed); 3. **history** — the ledger, plus a business strip: verified rate, lead time p50/p90, throughput, per-role numbers, overdue and nudges. **Several projects, one switcher.** Each project keeps its own `tower.toml` and `.tower/`; `tower projects add ` (or `scan`) registers them and the page grows project pills plus an **all projects** view. `tower projects use ` marks the active one — the panel defaults to it, and the DSH bundle's `tower_*` tools follow it (`tower_use` switches it from inside a session, no restart). Deep links: `?lang=zh`, `?theme=dark`, `?project=`, `?project=__all__`. ### Async dispatch & relay (0.9.0) `tower dispatch --async` queues the task and returns its id in under a second; a background `tower worker` process (started automatically on first use) runs the adapter, relays peer messages and runs auto-triage, then lands an `async_settled` notice in `tower inbox`. Set `dispatch_mode: async` in `tower.toml` (or `roles..dispatch_mode`) to make it the default; `--no-auto` and every other flag behave as in sync mode. `tower relay --to -m "..."` delivers a message to **any** DSH session — a session id, a unique session-title substring, or the alias `tower` (this tower's own inbox). With `--await-receipt`, a worker watches for a reply carrying the relay id (the peer answers with `tower relay --to tower --reply -m "..."`) and lands a `relay_receipt` — or `relay_timeout` — in the inbox. In the DSH plugin this is `tower_dispatch {async: true}` and the new `tower_relay` tool. #### Async knobs (0.9.1) ```yaml dispatch_mode: async # tower default (per-role: roles..dispatch_mode) workers: 4 # threads inside one `tower worker` process notify: kind: lead_session # inbox (default) | lead_session — one message pushed to the lead's session session: session-… async_roles: [seo, ops] # role-level override as a list ``` Relay flags: `--to role:` targets a role's session; `--wait ` uses a file as the receipt (its content, once it appears); `--timeout 45m` uses the same duration grammar as `--due`. Settlement notices read `[tower] T-00xx settled: accepted | role=… | summary=…`, land in `tower inbox`, and — with `notify.kind: lead_session` — are also pushed to the lead's session. `.tower/.lock` serialises board writes; `.tower/events.jsonl` is the enqueued→settled→notified audit trail. The **control room** lives at `/scene`: an isometric glass tower where each role is a robot, floors are departments, LED strips show alert state, and approving / replying / repairing happens in place (every action lands in the ledger). Data comes from `/api/scene`, i.e. from the same task files this README describes. `tower panel` keeps a **stable URL**: it reuses the port this workspace used last time (`.tower/panel-port`), else 8787, else the next free port — and remembers the choice, so a bookmarked page keeps working. Two panels can no longer share one port. When the installed code changes (a plugin update), the running panel detects it and **restarts itself**, and the page reloads once the new instance answers — no more "the board is silently showing yesterday's build". **Every number has a written formula.** The board is for people, so the model is specified once — [docs/board-model.md](docs/board-model.md) — and the page, the CLI and the panel all read the same decisions: | Queue | Who owns it | |---|---| | 需要你 / *needs you* | a person: only `blocked` or `failed` (retries exhausted) | | 待总控 / *tower queue* | the tower: verify → accept, or rework with the failure reasons | | 进行中 / *in flight* | the bot | | 已完成 / *done* | nobody: accepted tasks never occupy a queue | `tower triage` closes that loop; `tower dispatch` runs it automatically after a report (`--no-auto` opts out), so an accepted-by-verifier job never waits for a human. Two renderings of the same snapshot — the terminal (`tower board`) and a local read-only web panel (`tower panel`). Person-states first, healthy work takes no space. ![panel](docs/assets/panel.png) ```bash tower board # print once tower board --watch # refresh in place (tmux/ssh friendly) tower panel # http://127.0.0.1:8787/ (read-only, auto-refresh 2s) ``` The panel shows **needs you** (ready / blocked / failed, each with its one question), then what is in flight, then what every role is doing right now, then the tail of the ledger. It reads the same files the CLI does — no database, no daemon, no writes. ## Adapters An adapter is the only component that knows how to make an agent act. Same contract for all four: | Adapter | Drives | Use when | |---|---|---| | `dsh` | a live DeepSeek Harness session (`session/prompt`, queued) | **primary**: long-lived roles with browser + shell tools | | `cli` | any agent binary that takes a prompt (`claude -p`, `codex exec`, Aider, your script) | you already run agent CLIs | | `openai` | any OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` with a small `run_shell` loop | hosted models, vLLM, Ollama | | `mock` | nothing (writes a placeholder artifact) | tests, demos, CI | Adding one is ~40 lines → [docs/adapters.md](docs/adapters.md). ## The report contract (and why the verifier exists) ```markdown ## Status → progress | waiting | ready | blocked | failed | dropped ## Summary → 2–5 sentences ## Files → - — (must exist on disk) ## Checks → - → (a bare command fails) ## Open issues → anything unfinished, or "none" ## Attention → only when status is blocked/failed: one concrete question ``` The status vocabulary is a closed set, borrowed from DeepSeek's [dsh-superagent](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype) research prototype: the lead routes on a state, not on prose, and `tower attention` shows only the tasks that are actually waiting for a person. See [docs/superagent-ideas.md](docs/superagent-ideas.md) for what we borrowed and what we deliberately left out. `tower accept` mechanically rejects: a missing/empty section · a check line without a result · a listed file that does not exist · any failing entry in `verify_commands`. ```yaml verify_commands: - "pytest -q" - "npm run build" ``` That is the difference between *"the agent said it works"* and *"the tower checked"*. ## Commands | Command | Purpose | |---|---| | `tower init ` | scaffold config + role folders | | `tower dispatch "" [--due 90m]` | create and run one task (idempotent with `--key`, deadline with `--due`) | | `tower dispatch "" --restate` | restatement gate: the role first says back what the brief means; no work runs | | `tower restate ok ` | accept that restatement, then dispatch the work | | `tower say "…"` | bot-to-bot note: queued into the peer's session + filed for the lead, fire-and-forget | | `tower huddle role1 role2 … --topic "…"` | up to six roles, two bounded rounds; minutes land in `.tower/huddles/` | | `tower stats [--all] [--days 14]` | business view: verified rate, lead time, throughput, per-role stats | | `tower projects list` / `scan` / `add` / `remove` / `use` | many towers, one switcher: what the panel and `tower_*` tools follow | | `tower supervise` | chase every open task past its deadline in its own session | | `tower batch role1 role2 --brief "…"` | fan one brief out to several roles | | `tower inbox [--all] [--read]` | reports filed by roles (the full log) | | `tower attention` | **only** the tasks waiting on a person | | `tower board [--watch]` / `tower panel` | the same picture, in a terminal or a local web page | | `tower accept ` | verify, then accept (auto-rejects to rework) | | `tower rework --note "…"` | send back with reasons and re-dispatch | | `tower status [--json]` | task board | | `tower show ` / `tower log` | inspect one task / tail the ledger | | `tower demo` | offline end-to-end demo | | `tower doctor` | validate config, adapter options, keys, sessions | `--restate` buys one cheap turn before an expensive one. The role answers with only `## Restatement` / `## Assumptions` / `## Done looks like`; the task waits in `restating`, shows up under **needs you**, and cannot be accepted — no report exists yet. `tower restate ok ` copies the accepted text into the work prompt as `## Confirmed understanding`, then dispatches. The gate fails closed: a non-zero exit or a missing section leaves the task `failed`, never `restating`. ## What's on disk ``` my-project/ ├── tower.toml # roles, adapters, verify commands ├── roles/ │ ├── backend/ # this role's only write area │ │ ├── AGENT.md │ │ └── T-0001-REPORT.md │ ├── frontend/ │ └── qa/ └── .tower/ ├── tasks/T-0001.json # materialised task view ├── ledger.jsonl # append-only event log (source of truth) └── inbox.jsonl # reports + unread flag ``` ## How it compares | | single agent | agent framework (graph/DSL) | **agent-control-tower** | |---|---|---|---| | Who routes the work | the one agent, in its head | the graph you wrote | the lead, explicitly, per task | | Deliverable | chat text | node outputs | files + a four-section report | | "Done" means | the agent said so | the node finished | the tower verified it | | Audit trail | scrollback | framework logs | `ledger.jsonl` you can `git diff` | | Setup | prompt | graph + runtime + infra | `pip install` + one YAML | | Runs offline / in CI | no | sometimes | yes (`tower demo`) | ## FAQ **Do I need DSH to use it?** No. DSH is the primary adapter because that is where the pattern came from; `cli`, `openai` and `mock` follow the same contract. **Does it run the agents itself?** No. It renders the prompt, calls your adapter, and checks what came back. The agent runtime stays yours. **Can agents talk to each other?** No. Hub-and-spoke on purpose: the lead routes, so the task tree stays inspectable and two roles cannot silently converge on the same file. **What if a role keeps failing?** `round` increments on every `rework`; when `round > max_rounds` the tower stops and tells you to escalate instead of looping. **Is the ledger safe to commit?** Yes — append-only JSONL; committing it puts the audit trail in `git log`. Add `.tower/` to `.gitignore` if you only want deliverables. **Where does it write?** Only inside the tower workspace: `roles//` for deliverables and `.tower/` for state. ## Docs | Doc | What's inside | |---|---| | [DSH quickstart](docs/dsh-quickstart.md) | the primary setup, end to end, plus five failure modes it prevents | | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | components, state machine, why files instead of a queue | | [Adapters](docs/adapters.md) | mock / cli / dsh / openai, and how to add your own | | [Borrowed from dsh-superagent](docs/superagent-ideas.md) | the five ideas we adopted, and what we left out | | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | ground rules, PR checklist, adapter guide | ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). ## Acknowledgements - The pattern was extracted from a real long-running build on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/), then generalised so it works without it. - The `dsh-tower` bundle follows the harness bundle conventions from the [DeepSeek Harness docs](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): `dsh.bundle` + `cordis.patch.yml` + `ctx.tools.register`. - Terminal frames in this README are **real command output**, rendered by [`docs/assets/build_assets.py`](docs/assets/build_assets.py) — no mock-ups. ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=evolution301/agent-control-tower&type=Date)](https://star-history.com/#evolution301/agent-control-tower&Date) Context hygiene: `tower ctx` prints each session's contextPressure (⚠ at ≥50%, John's rule) and the DSH plugin's `tower_compact { session }` forces the native /compact machinery in-process — no extra turn. DSH ships built-in auto-compaction (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic`, mounted by default). Its threshold lives in `compaction-basic.thresholdRatio` (default **0.8**); set it to **0.5** in your cordis patch for a global auto-compact-at-50% rule — no plugin needed: ```yaml - id: compaction-basic config: thresholdRatio: 0.5 ``` The plugin's `tower_compact { session }` tool remains the manual one-shot trigger; `tower ctx` still prints live pressure per session.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# lz-work-bootstrap

> 按 `plugins.md` / `skills.md` 编排插件安装、Skill 同步、失败续跑、验证与移除墓碑的**薄编排插件**。

`lz-work-bootstrap` 是一个薄编排层：它只解析清单、维护状态机、调度外部能力，
**不重复实现插件下载和 Skill 落盘**。

- 插件安装 / 更新 → 复用 `dsh-market`（软依赖）
- Skill 同步 → 复用 `dsh-skills-console`（软依赖，不可用时降级）
- 状态记录 / 墓碑 / 续跑 → 本插件维护 `.dsh/lz-work-bootstrap-state.json`

## 安装

```bash
npm install
npm run build      # 产出 dist/
npm test           # 运行单元测试
```

把编译产物 `dist/` 与 `plugin.json` 注册到 DSH 即可用 `lz-work` 命令。

## 命令

```bash
lz-workplan         --plugins plugins.md --skills skills.md [--profile dev-workbench]
lz-workinstall      --plugins plugins.md --skills skills.md [--profile dev-workbench] [--continue-on-error]
lz-workinstall      --plugins plugins.md
lz-worksync-skills  --skills skills.md
lz-workresume       [--plugins plugins.md] [--continue-on-error]
lz-workverify
```

| 子命令 | 读取 | 写状态 | 行为 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plan` | 清单 + state + 本地存在性 | 否 | 只输出计划表，不安装、不改状态 |
| `install` | 清单 + state + 本地存在性 | 是 | 安装/更新非墓碑、非手动项；失败写 `failed` |
| `sync-skills` | `skills.md` + state | 是 | 调 `dsh-skills-console` 同步 Skill |
| `resume` | state（可选清单） | 是 | 只重试 `failed` 项，不碰墓碑 |
| `verify` | state + 本地存在性 | 否 | 只报告健康状态，不直接改状态 |

退出码：`0` 全部成功；`1` 部分失败；`2` 预检阻断 / 必需依赖缺失。

## 清单格式

只解析 Markdown 中的围栏代码块，其余内容忽略。

### `plugins.md`

````md
```yaml dsh-plugins
version: 1
profile: dev-workbench

sources:
  market: dsh-market
  allow_github_orgs:
    - oxmumu3
    - KYCOMING

plugins:
  - id: dsh-market
    source: market
    required: true

  - id: dsh-agent-teams
    source: market
    required: true
    precheck: dsh-plugin-compat-check
    notes: |
      安装前必须通过宿主版本兼容性预检。

  - id: dsh-project-companion
    source: github-release
    required: false
    manual: true
```
````

字段约定：

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `id` | 插件 ID，必填 |
| `source` | `market` / `github` / `github-release` / `local` |
| `required` | `true` 时安装失败阻断后续必需项；不代表必须自动安装 |
| `manual` | `true` 时 `install` 只提示，不执行安装 |
| `precheck` | 安装前需运行的预检插件或命令名 |
| `profile` | 过滤：仅当当前 `--profile` 匹配或未指定时处理 |
| `config` | 普通配置；密钥只允许 `keychain:` / `env:` 引用 |
| `notes` | 人类可读说明，不参与执行 |

### `skills.md`

`version: 2` 用 `categories` 把 Skill 分三类：

| 分类 | 说明 | 典型 `scope` |
|---|---|---|
| `general` 通用技能 | 通用辅助能力（如 `browse`、`use`） | `global` |
| `dev` 开发技能 | 面向开发流程（如 `openspec`、`cr`、`review`） | `project` |
| `internal` 内部技能 | 来自内部 GitLab 仓库 | `project` |

````md
```yaml dsh-skills
version: 2
manager: dsh-skills-console

categories:
  general:
    skills:
      - id: browse
        source: github:your-org/skills/browse
        enabled: true
        scope: global
  dev:
    skills:
      - id: openspec
        source: github:your-org/skills/openspec
        enabled: true
        scope: project
  internal:
    gitlab_group: __ask__   # 启动时询问用户；或填具体分组如 my-org/skills
    skills:
      - id: example-internal-skill
        source: gitlab:${gitlab_group}/skills/example-internal-skill
        enabled: true
        scope: project
```
````

**内部技能的 GitLab 分组**：`internal.gitlab_group` 设为 `__ask__` 时，
`sync-skills` 启动时会通过 `host.ui.prompt` 交互式询问用户输入内部技能市场的
GitLab 分组，再代入内部技能源中的 `${gitlab_group}`；prompt 不可用或用户留空时，
内部技能降级为 `manual_sync_required`，不影响通用/开发技能的同步。

`version: 1` 的扁平 `skills:` 列表仍向后兼容（不区分分类）。

Skill 不走插件安装通道。`install` 只确保 `dsh-skills-console` 已安装；`sync-skills` 把清单交给 `dsh-skills-console`。

## 状态机与墓碑

状态文件：`.dsh/lz-work-bootstrap-state.json`（schema version 2）。

| 状态 | 含义 | 下次 `plan/install` 行为 |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | 清单内有，从未装过 | 安装 |
| `installed` | 已装且受管 | 比对版本/hash，决定是否更新 |
| `failed` | 安装失败 | `resume` 时重试 |
| `removed_by_user` | 墓碑：检测到用户本地移除 | 跳过，不安装、不更新 |
| `manual` | 清单标记手动安装 | 只提示，不自动装 |

**墓碑规则：**

- 墓碑是**用户意图**，优先级高于清单配置变更。
- 即使清单配置 hash 变化，只要 state 是 `removed_by_user`，仍跳过；`plan` 提示“有配置更新但因已移除未应用”。
- 清除墓碑的唯一自动路径：检测到本地重新存在该插件。不需要额外 `unblock` 命令。
- `removalLog` 只追加，不修改历史。

检测矩阵（本地是否存在 × state 状态）：

| 本地存在 | state 状态 | 动作 |
|---|---|---|
| 是 | `installed` | 比对版本/hash，按需更新 |
| 是 | `removed_by_user` | 清除墓碑 → `installed`，正常管理 |
| 是 | 无记录 | 记录为 `installed` |
| 否 | `installed` | 标记 `removed_by_user`，写 `removalLog`，跳过 |
| 否 | `removed_by_user` | 跳过 |
| 否 | `pending` | 安装 |
| 否 | `failed` | `resume` 时重试 |
| 任意 | `manual` | 只提示 |

## 安全底线

1. **来源白名单**：只允许 `market` 与 `allow_github_orgs` 中的 GitHub 来源。
2. **不执行任意 shell**：不自动运行 `postinstall`，需要执行的项标 `manual`。
3. **密钥不落盘**：只接受 `keychain:` / `env:` 引用，拒绝明文；state、日志、plan 输出中不出现密钥。
4. **不自动接受条款**：数据条款、地区限制、OAuth/扫码授权必须交互确认。
5. **免费 Token 单独 profile**：`free-token` 清单不混入 `dev-workbench` 自动安装。
6. **预编译二进制项目**：如 `DeepSeek-Harness-Token-Free` 默认排除。
7. **墓碑优先**：`removed_by_user` 不被配置更新覆盖。
8. **幂等**：重复运行不重复安装；hash 未变则跳过。

## 目录结构

```
lz-work-bootstrap/
├── plugin.json          # 插件声明：命令 + 软依赖
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts         # activate()：命令注册、参数解析、宿主组装、子命令分发
│   ├── types.ts         # 共享类型
│   ├── config.ts        # 常量与默认值
│   ├── manifest.ts      # 解析 plugins.md / skills.md（围栏提取 + YAML + 校验）
│   ├── plan.ts          # buildPlan：清单 + state + 本地探测 → 计划表（只读）
│   ├── state.ts         # 状态文件 + 状态机 + 墓碑 + removalLog
│   ├── executor.ts      # 执行安装/更新/同步，软依赖降级
│   ├── verify.ts        # 健康报告（只读）
│   └── ui.ts            # 计划表与摘要格式化
├── templates/
│   ├── plugins.md       # 插件清单模板（dev-workbench）
│   └── skills.md        # Skill 清单模板
├── tests/               # 单元测试（node:test）
└── README.md
```

## 与 `dsh-market` / `dsh-skills-console` 的协作

`plugin.json` 把二者声明为软依赖：

- 缺 `dsh-market`：`install` 把该项标 `failed`，提示先装 market；不自行 git clone 或下载。
- 缺 `dsh-skills-console`：`sync-skills` 降级为“生成可消费清单 + 提示手动同步”，状态标 `manual_sync_required`。
- `precheck` 指定的预检不通过：阻断该项，写 `failed` 或返回退出码 `2`。

宿主能力优先取自 `ctx.plugins` / `ctx.skills` / `ctx.get(name)`；若运行时未提供，
降级为基于文件系统的尽力探测（检查 `DSH_PLUGINS_DIR` 或 `~/.dsh/plugins/<id>`），
真实运行时应注入准确的本地存在性适配器。

## 验收标准

详见需求文档 §10。单元测试覆盖：

- `plan` 解析两份清单、输出计划表、不写状态；
- 首次 `install` 安装非手动项、写 `installed`；重复运行幂等；
- 本地删除已装插件 → `removed_by_user`，`install` 跳过；手动装回 → 自动清墓碑；
- 墓碑期间配置变化 → `plan` 提示、`install` 仍跳过；
- `failed` 经 `resume` 重试，`resume` 不碰墓碑；
- `manual: true` 只提示；`precheck` 不通过退出码 2；
- `sync-skills` 优先 console，不可用降级；密钥不落盘。

## 命名说明

- 包/插件名：`lz-work-bootstrap`（`lz` 取自「靓仔」liangzai 的缩写）。
- 命令：`lz-work`。
- 状态文件：`.dsh/lz-work-bootstrap-state.json`。
- 仓库：`lz-work-bootstrap`（GitHub 仓库已与包名统一）。

## License
