# dsh-session-remover

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@jamolpe88/dsh-session-remover?style=flat-square&logo=npm&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jamolpe88/dsh-session-remover)
[![GitHub release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/JaMoLpE88/dsh-session-remover?style=flat-square&logo=github&label=release)](https://github.com/JaMoLpE88/dsh-session-remover/releases)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%3E%3D0.2.1--rc.3-4B8BBE?style=flat-square)](#compatibility)
[![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2011-0078D6?style=flat-square)](#compatibility)
[![dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/jamolpe88/dsh-session-remover)

**Delete a DeepSeek Harness session for good, straight from its `⋯` menu.** One red row, one confirmation, and the conversation is gone from DSH *and* from the disk: its JSONL log, its projection cache and its place in the workspace registry.

No settings page, no archive manager, no agent tools. English-only interface. Nothing else is added.

**Español** → [README.es.md](README.es.md)

![Delete session in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar session menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JaMoLpE88/dsh-session-remover/main/assets/session-menu.png)

*The session `⋯` menu: **Delete session** sits in red after the shipped rows (pin, rename, fork, archive, copy Session ID). Workspace and session names are blurred.*

![Confirmation dialog for permanent session deletion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JaMoLpE88/dsh-session-remover/main/assets/confirm-dialog.png)

*The confirmation: the session to delete is named in the dialog (blurred here), **Cancel** has the initial focus, and nothing is sent to the Host until you confirm.*

## What it does

- Adds **Delete session** to the `⋯` menu of every session row, in red, ordered after the shipped rows.
- Opens a DSH-styled confirmation that names the exact session; **Cancel** takes the initial focus and **Escape** closes the dialog without doing anything.
- Closes the session before touching storage. If it is open, the plugin runs the same ordered teardown DSH uses for its own agents (stop, drain, release the writer, detach) and waits for it to finish.
- Removes the session's own directory `<session store>/<project>/<session-id>/`, including its `.v4.jsonl.zstd` log.
- Removes the derived cache record `storages/session_projcache/sessions/<session-id>.json`, so no cached title or message text survives.
- Cleans the workspace registry: detaches the session from every workspace that lists it, unpins it and clears its archive marker.
- Refreshes the sidebar, and clears the main panel if the deleted session was the one on screen.

## What it does not do

- **Does not delete attachments.** Images and files live in a content-addressed shared store (`attachments/v1/objects/<hash>`) that other sessions may reference, so they are left alone. See [What stays on disk](#what-stays-on-disk).
- Does not touch other sessions, the files of your workspace, DSH logs, backups or any cloud copy.
- Does not add a settings page, an archive browser or a history search.
- Does not add an agent tool or a slash command: deletion is user-only and confirmed in the UI.
- Does not make any network request.

## Why there are no settings

The only decision is which session to delete, and that is already an argument of the action. There is no threshold to tune, no interval, no key, no scope. A config page would be a second place to explain the same single behaviour.

## Requirements

- **DSH Desktop** `>= 0.2.1-rc.3`, profile `desktop` (tested on `0.2.1-rc.3`, Windows 11).
- The default per-session **JSONL** session store. A non-JSONL backend is refused at load time.
- Node 22+ (DSH ships its own runtime).
- **One restart after installing or updating the plugin.** The Host half intercepts the agent lifecycle, so it can only close sessions that were opened *after* it loaded. Sessions opened before that are refused, not half-deleted.

## Install

From npm:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @jamolpe88/dsh-session-remover
```

From the repository:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:JaMoLpE88/dsh-session-remover
```

From a local checkout, while developing:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add C:\path\to\dsh-session-remover
```

Fully quit and reopen DSH after installing, then refresh the window.

## Usage

1. Hover a session in the sidebar and open its `⋯` menu.
2. Choose **Delete session** (red, last row).
3. Check the session name in the dialog and confirm with **Delete permanently**, or cancel.

An archived session has no sidebar row: unarchive it first from DSH's own archive page, then delete it from its menu. Deletion clears the archive marker and the pin on the way out, so nothing stale is left in the registry.

## What gets deleted

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `<session store>/<project>/<session-id>/` | The session's own directory: its versioned `.jsonl.zstd` log and anything beside it |
| `storages/session_projcache/sessions/<session-id>.json` | Cached projections: title, message-derived values |
| `storages/workspace.json` | Only the references: the session is detached, unpinned and unarchived |

Nothing else is removed. The session is not moved to a recycle bin: the files are deleted, so the space is returned immediately.

## What stays on disk

**Attachments.** Images and files are stored once per content hash under `attachments/v1/objects/`. A forked session inherits references to the same hashes, so deleting the objects would break the fork's images. DSH keeps no reference count, so the plugin leaves them alone rather than guessing.

For a text-only conversation this is nothing at all. If your goal is reclaiming disk space, images are what dominates — that cleanup needs a scan of the remaining logs and is deliberately out of scope for now.

Also untouched: DSH's own logs, your workspace files, backups you made yourself and any copy that already left the machine.

## How it works

The **Host** half registers one route, `POST /plugins/session-remover/delete`:

1. The request must pass the Host's own request fence and carry the `x-session-remover-confirmation: delete-session` header. A link, an HTML form or a cross-site request cannot produce that header.
2. The session id is validated (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,127}$`) before it can name a path.
3. A live agent is closed through the `AgentHandle` that `ctx.agents.create`/`resume` returned. DSH exposes no dispose on the registry itself, so the plugin keeps those handles as they are created and refuses to delete when it has none.
4. The storage directory is resolved from `sessionPersistence.stat` + `locate` and cross-checked by scanning the store root, then required to be exactly `<root>/<one project segment>/<session id>`, a real directory, containing a session log file.
5. Workspace references are cleaned, the directory is removed, and the projection-cache record is dropped through its table API (or its file, when the API is absent).
6. A cheap search reconciles the SQLite search index, which otherwise only drops removed sessions on its next search. Every step after the directory check is best-effort and reported, never assumed.

The **Client** half is one plain `client.js` with no build step: it registers a row in `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` and a dialog in `shell.overlay`, requires only `react`, and styles with `--dsw-alias-*` tokens. It does not load Harness Client packages, so a DSH update that renames a primitive cannot blank the entry.

## Compatibility

| | |
|---|---|
| DSH | `>= 0.2.1-rc.3` (tested on `0.2.1-rc.3`) |
| Node | `>= 22` |
| OS | Windows 11 (tested); macOS and Linux untested |
| Profile | `desktop` (tested); `web` untested |
| Session store | per-session JSONL backend (the default) |
| Catalog | [listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/jamolpe88/dsh-session-remover) |

Validation status: **tested on Windows 11 with DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3** (2026-10-26). The menu row and the confirmation were used through the interface; a real session (a fork) was deleted and its directory, its projection-cache record and its workspace references were verified gone afterwards, with a sibling session left intact.

Not validated: macOS, Linux, the web profile and other DSH versions.

## Limits

- **One DSH version is tested.** The deletion path depends on the JSONL store's on-disk layout and on the `AgentHandle` returned by the agent registry; a future DSH release may change either.
- **Sessions opened before the plugin loaded cannot be closed.** Restart DSH once after installing or updating.
- **A corrupt or unexpected store is refused, not forced.** Symlinked directories, a session directory without a log file, or an ambiguous match in two project directories end in an error and no deletion.
- **Archived sessions** need unarchiving first, because DSH gives them no sidebar row.
- **Attachments are kept** (see above).
- **One deletion at a time per session.** A second request while the first is running is rejected.

## Privacy

- No network access, no telemetry, no external service.
- No cookies, no tokens, no credentials read.
- The confirmation dialog sends only the session id.
- The interface text is English only, by design.
- The screenshots above come from a real session; workspace and session names are blurred.

## Troubleshooting

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `This session was opened before Session Remover was loaded…` | The agent existed before the plugin loaded. Restart DSH and try again; nothing was deleted. |
| `DeepSeek Harness did not finish closing this session; nothing was deleted.` | The teardown did not settle in time. Retry; nothing was deleted. |
| `The session directory does not contain a session log; nothing was deleted.` | The directory does not look like this session's storage. Nothing was deleted. |
| `This session matches more than one storage directory; nothing was deleted.` | The same id exists in two project directories. Resolve it by hand; nothing was deleted. |
| `The session files could not be removed (…)` | The operating system refused the removal; the dialog reports the code. |
| `The delete request did not pass the origin and confirmation checks.` | The request did not come from the app window. Reload DSH. |

When something fails, the rule is the same: **nothing is deleted unless the whole validated path succeeds**, and the error says so.

## Development

```bash
npm run check   # syntax checks plus the path-validation self-check
npm test        # end-to-end Host deletion against a throwaway tree
```

`check.mjs` covers the containment rules (invalid ids, `..`, wrong depth, foreign directories) and that the Client module id, the package name and the patch row agree — a mismatch crashes web boot. `test-host.mjs` drives the real handler with stubbed Harness services: request gating, invalid id, cold deletion with a surviving sibling, live-agent teardown, the cache-file fallback and the refusal to treat a log-less directory as storage.

Local install:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add C:\path\to\dsh-session-remover
```

No build step: `client.js` is the shipped artifact.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 JaMoLpE88

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # doubao-image — generate images with the local Doubao app > 面向：使用者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20 Registers one tool, `generate_image`, that drives the **locally installed and logged-in Doubao (豆包) desktop app** to produce a picture, saves the full-resolution file, and sends it into the conversation. ``` plugins/doubao-image/ ├── package.json # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch, exports ├── cordis.patch.yml # bundle patch: the loader row ├── lib/ │ ├── index.js # cordis plugin: the generate_image tool │ ├── doubao.mjs # app launch, prompt submission, result harvest │ ├── cdp.mjs # dependency-free Chrome DevTools Protocol client │ ├── watermark.mjs # removes Doubao's own overlay, with a self-check │ ├── image.mjs # minimal PNG codec + raster helpers │ └── generate.mjs # CLI driver, for testing without spending a model turn └── test/ # node --test (no DSH, no app, no network) ``` ## Install ```bash # from npm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-doubao-image # or from the repository root — the leading ./ matters: DSH anchors relative specs # against your current directory, otherwise pnpm would resolve it inside the profile dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/doubao-image ``` Then restart DSH (or reload the profile). The tool appears as `generate_image`. ## Use ```bash # exercise the whole path without going through the model node plugins/doubao-image/lib/generate.mjs \ --prompt "一只戴黄铜护目镜的橘猫，坐在双翼飞机驾驶舱里" \ --style "黏土质感 C4D 渲染，暖色夕阳光" \ --out ~/Pictures/doubao ``` The tool takes `prompt` (required) plus `style`, `composition`, `aspect`, `negative`, `count`, `dir`, and `reuseCurrentChat`. ## How it works, and why it is built this way Doubao ships a **full Chromium** (`Contents/Helpers/Doubao Browser.app`), and its launcher forwards unknown flags, so starting it with `--remote-debugging-port` yields a real CDP endpoint. That is the whole reason this works without the macOS Accessibility permission that `osascript` would need — which matters, because that permission is not granted on this machine. The findings each step depends on, all established by probing the running app: | Step | What is actually true | | --- | --- | | Launch | Doubao holds a **singleton lock**. A normally-launched instance never opens the debug port, and launching again just forwards to it. The app must therefore be quit and restarted — the first call costs ~10–40 s. | | Attach | `doubao-chat` is the real 1200×800 window. `doubao-launcher` is a 400×600 **sidebar that also accepts prompts** and renders results at 90 px, and `doubao-chat` is *additionally* served as an empty `hello` shell. Identification uses live window size plus the presence of the editor, never the URL alone. | | Type | The box is `div.tiptap.ProseMirror[contenteditable=true]`. `execCommand('insertText')` goes through the same `beforeinput` path a keystroke does, so the app's own state and send button update. Assigning `innerText` would not. | | Detect | The status sentence 「已生成 N 张候选图」 is the completion signal, not the image count — the grid mounts placeholders before the renders arrive. | | Harvest | The picture in the grid is a `cpreview_wm1` render behind an overlay, and its full-size sibling `` is a bare `data:image/svg+xml` **placeholder with no pixels**, so the bytes cannot be read from the grid. Instead the tool clicks each thumbnail to open the image viewer and uses the app's own `[data-testid=edit_image_download_button]`, which writes the file to `~/Downloads`; the tool then moves it to `dir`. | `dsh-doctor`-style checks live in the unit tests: the output schema must stay in sync with `execute`, because a tool that returns a value without a declared schema is refused at registration and takes the **whole plugin tree — and every DSH boot, the desktop app included — down with it**. ## The watermark Doubao stamps 「豆包AI生成」 into the bottom-right of every saved picture. It is an overlay the app composites on, not part of the artwork, which is what makes removal a solved problem instead of an inpainting guess. All of this was measured, not assumed: | Property | Measurement | | --- | --- | | Position | Anchored to the bottom-right corner; a glyph mask from one image correlates with an unrelated image's corner at **NCC 0.949** (inverse control −0.949, exactly symmetric) | | Scale | Proportional to the image's **short side**, not its width: 2048²→321×69 box, 1365×2048→214×46 box, both giving width/short ≈ 0.1567. Verified on a second sample per shape | | Blend | Plain alpha composite `C = a·W + (1−a)·B`, fitted at **a = 0.638**, W = 234.4, RMS residual 6.3/255 | | Soft edge | Glyph interiors measure a = 0.63 while the antialiased rim ramps to 0 — which is why a hard 0/1 mask left a visible outline | Removal inverts the composite per pixel, and estimates the artwork behind the mark by coarse-grid interpolation that excludes masked pixels. The output PNG is encoded losslessly (round-trip delta verified 0). **Self-check.** The `verifyOnFlat` helper turns "does it look clean?" into a number: on a flat-background sample the artwork behind the mark is a constant, so any residual offset inside the glyph area *is* the watermark that survived. Measured on a flat 2048² sample: **residual 46.3 → 0.0 (100% removed)**. On a photograph the same metric would be meaningless, so it detects a non-flat frame (background IQR > 8) and says so instead of printing a flattering zero. **Scope.** This targets this one overlay, at this one anchor, with this one calibrated blend. It is not a general watermark remover. It exists for internal reference material — animation reference, storyboards, internal review. Doubao's official API (Volcengine Ark) returns images with no watermark at all, and that is the right channel for anything published or commercial. **Stripping is off by default** (owner's decision, 2026-09-25): an image comes back with Doubao's own 「豆包AI生成」 badge unless the caller explicitly asks for `stripWatermark: true`. Keeping the badge is the safe default — it is what makes a picture traceable to the tool that made it — and the capability stays here for the internal-reference case described above. ## Known limitations - **Generation consumes the user's Doubao quota** (the app reports 「本次生成将 消耗每日免费额度」). Exactly one generation is issued per call; if the plugin cannot confirm a submission it stops rather than retrying, because a blind retry is what once produced duplicate generations. - **The app window is closed and reopened** on the first call, and Doubao must stay running-and-instrumented for the harvest to complete. - The harvest depends on Doubao's own UI markup (`image-box-grid`, `edit_image_download_button`). A Doubao redesign breaks it; the selector surface is deliberately kept to those two names. - The watermark pass only re-encodes PNG. Other formats are saved exactly as downloaded rather than silently recompressed. # DSH Mobile **中文** · [English](README.en.md) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [![listed in awesome-deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--deepseek--harness-4D6BFE?logo=awesomelists&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness) [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness) [![iOS 17+](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-17%2B-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](docs/VERSIONING.md) [![TestFlight](https://img.shields.io/badge/TestFlight-join-0D96F6?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk) [![connector on npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-mobile-link?label=connector)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-mobile-link) [![CI](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) 把电脑上的 [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 会话接到 iPhone 与 iPad：原生 iOS 客户端、电脑侧连接器、可自建的公网中转。手机经中转连接电脑上的 DSH host，会话与消息流与电脑端 一致；任务在电脑锁屏后继续运行，挂起的提问可在手机上作答。电脑无需公网 IP，也无需 VPN。 ![DSH Mobile 演示：电脑端登记、手机扫码配对，查看会话、远程文件、git 改动与提交历史](docs/artifacts/demo/dsh-mobile-demo.gif) ## 状态与兼容性 连接器与 iOS App 请保持最新版本：两者按同一份协议演进，跨版本的兼容窗口有限。版本组合与 兼容性约束见 [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](docs/VERSIONING.md)。 ## 前提 - 电脑已安装并可运行 DSH（`dsh web`）；连接器需要 Node.js ≥ 22。 - 自建中转需一台有公网 IP 的主机（macOS 或 Linux）与 Caddy。 - 从源码构建 App 需 macOS + Xcode 16 以上；日常使用不需要。 ## 快速开始 ### A. 使用公共中转 1. 安装 App：加入 [TestFlight 公开测试](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk)（需先安装 TestFlight）。 2. 安装连接器，装进实际在用的宿主档案（装错不会报错，但连接器不会被加载）： - 命令行 web 版：`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mobile-link` - 官方桌面版：用应用内插件页，或应用自带的 `dsh` 命令装进 `desktop` 档案（普通 npm 版 `dsh` 会拒绝该档案）。两种宿主的识别判据见 [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。 3. 登记：DSH 左下角「移动端连接」→ 确认中转地址 →「登记」。开放登记，无需邀请码，按来源限流； 无头环境用 `dsh-mobile-link enroll --relay wss://<中转地址>/dsh-link`。 4. 生效：安装插件与面板登记均无需重启；仅命令行登记且宿主正在运行时需重启一次。 5. 配对：App「扫码配对」扫描面板中的二维码与配对码；配对码点「重新生成」才会更换。 顶部显示「已连接」即为成功；完整步骤与故障排查见 [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。 ### B. 自建中转 自建使用仓库内 Go 实现（`relay-go/`）。构建与安装见 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md) §2–§4；Caddy 路由用 [`Caddyfile.snippet`](relay-go/deploy/Caddyfile.snippet) 配合 [`caddy_splice.py`](relay-go/deploy/caddy_splice.py) 插入站点块。 ```bash sudo systemctl enable --now dsh-relay-go ``` 实时负载与每设备用量：`curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/stats`（仅监听回环）。限额与运维细节见 [`relay-go/README.md`](relay-go/README.md) 与 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md)。 ## 组件与数据流 ``` ┌──────────────┐ WSS ┌────────────────────┐ WSS ┌───────────────────┐ │ iOS App ├─────────►│ Relay（公网主机） │◄─────────┤ 电脑侧连接器 │ │ SwiftUI │ │ 鉴权 + 转发 │ │ (DSH 插件) │ └──────────────┘ └────────────────────┘ └─────────┬─────────┘ │ HTTP + WS ┌─────────▼─────────┐ │ dsh web │ │ 127.0.0.1: │ └───────────────────┘ ``` | 组件 | 位置 | 职责 | |---|---|---| | iOS App | 手机 | 会话列表、转写、图片与文件、配对与设备管理 | | 连接器 | 电脑（DSH 插件） | 以 `127.0.0.1` 访问本机 DSH，转成中转帧 | | 中转 | 公网主机 | 鉴权与按 `agentId` 转发；**不解析会话内容** | | DSH host | 电脑 | 会话、agent 与工具的真实执行方 | 产品上只提供经中转这一条连接方式；`dsh://direct` 是 DEBUG-only 的测试通道。选型与边界见 [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) 与 [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md)。 ## 配置 仓库中的 `relay.example.com` 一律为占位符：中转地址由部署方决定，不属于仓库。真值只存在于本机并被 gitignore： | 位置 | 用途 | 提供方式 | |---|---|---| | `.env.local` | 发布脚本、开发探针 | `cp .env.example .env.local`，按模板填站点与中转地址 | | `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | 连接器的中转地址与身份 | 面板「登记」，或 `dsh-mobile-link enroll --relay <地址>` | | `ios/DSHMobile/Config.local.xcconfig` | App 内预填的中转地址与更新源 | 从 `Config.xcconfig` 复制后填写 | 直接 clone 构建的 App 不含中转地址，属有意设计。 ## 开发 ```bash cd ios/DSHMobile/DSHKit && swift test # 协议层 cd plugins/mobile-link && npm test # 连接器 cd relay-go && make test # 中转（Go，生产实现） cd mail && ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q # 信件服务 npm run check:secrets # 本机真值没有进跟踪文件 npm run check:docs # 文档规范（结构、口吻、链接） cd ios/DSHMobile && xcodebuild -scheme DSHMobile \ -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=DSH-Test' build ``` 上述单测与一次不带本机配置的 Release 构建由 GitHub Actions 执行。需要仿真器、真实中转或开发者团队 ID 的验证不在 CI 内；CI 通过不等于可以发布。 界面测试为独立测试台：`./test/run.sh prepare` → `run <用例>` → `report --verdict …`；口径见 [`test/RULES.md`](test/RULES.md)，模板见 [`test/examples/`](test/examples)。 ## 文档 | 文档 | 内容 | |---|---| | [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md) | 两种部署路径的选择、操作步骤、故障排查 | | [`docs/GLOSSARY.md`](docs/GLOSSARY.md) | 术语表（DSH、host、连接器、中转、DLP 等） | | [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | 架构与关键决策 | | [`docs/DSH-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/DSH-PROTOCOL.md) | DSH 原生协议参考（权威、面向实现） | | [`docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md) | DLP v1 中转协议规范 | | [`docs/CONNECTOR-NOTES.md`](docs/CONNECTOR-NOTES.md) / [`docs/RELAY-NOTES.md`](docs/RELAY-NOTES.md) | 实现与规范的偏差记录 | | [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md) | 连接方式与配对设计 | | [`docs/IMAGES.md`](docs/IMAGES.md) | 图片能力的设计约束与实现 | | [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](docs/VERSIONING.md) | 三处部署的版本与发布策略 | | [`docs/PRIVACY.md`](docs/PRIVACY.md) | 隐私说明：App 不收集数据，中转只做转发 | | [`docs/dsh-rpc-catalog.json`](docs/dsh-rpc-catalog.json) | 某次快照：机器可读的 RPC 目录（不是持续校验的契约） | | [`docs/artifacts/samples/`](docs/artifacts/samples) | 从真实 DSH 抓取的响应样例（已脱敏） | 开发约定见 [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md)，安全问题见 [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md)，版本变化见 [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md)。 ## 已知限制 - **后台通知**：App 退到后台后，任务完成与待答提问仍推送至手机；无任务、无提问时不推送。 - **不覆盖**：电脑端新开始的会话无法唤起 App（需 APNs，尚未实现）；长时间未答的提问可能丢失。 - 文件发送仅在经中转时可用。 ## 许可 MIT，见 [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)。

# dsh-plugin-mobile-link

[![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![listed in awesome-deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--deepseek--harness-4D6BFE?logo=awesomelists&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-mobile-link)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-mobile-link)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](../../LICENSE)

> 面向：使用者与实现者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20

**The computer half of [DSH Mobile](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile): it
dials a relay over WSS, so the native iOS client reaches this DSH instance even
though the computer has no public IP.**

```
iPhone App ──WSS──▶ Relay（公网，只鉴权与转发）──WSS──▶ this plugin ──HTTP+WS──▶ 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

The connector always talks to the local DSH as `127.0.0.1:<port>`, so the host's
authority and its trust fence are unaffected: no `--trusted-host`, no rewritten
`Host`, no new listening port on this machine.

```
plugins/mobile-link/
├── package.json          # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch, bin: dsh-mobile-link
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle patch: the loader row + config reference
├── lib/
│   ├── index.js          # cordis plugin: starts the agent, registers 5 routes
│   ├── link.js           # the DLP agent transport: identity, socket, heartbeat, reconnect
│   ├── router.js         # frames ⇄ local DSH mux streams, per-device `$events`
│   ├── dlp.js            # DLP v1 frame codec (shared with the relay)
│   ├── files.js          # phone → computer file transfers (`_link/file*` methods)
│   ├── enroll.js         # open enrollment (no invite code), writes ~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json
│   ├── journal.js        # lifecycle journal: why a relay link was dropped, after the fact
│   ├── routes.js         # status, enroll, pair-code, pair-code/regenerate, devices/revoke
│   ├── qr.js             # dependency-free QR SVG
│   └── cli.js            # dsh-mobile-link: enroll / mint-pair-code
└── test/                 # node --test, 100+ tests (no DSH, no network)
```

## Install

The connector runs in whichever host runs your DSH. There are two supported hosts today —
**the official desktop app** and **the command-line web host** — and each keeps its own
profile, so you install the plugin into the one you actually use. The connector discovers
the local DSH by itself in both (the host hands it the authenticated loopback address);
you never type an address or a token.

**Command-line web host**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mobile-link
```

**Official desktop app** — install through the app's own plugin page, or with the CLI that
the app ships (`…/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh`, installable from its settings). The npm
`dsh` refuses this profile on purpose (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the
Electron application`). Two prerequisites matter in practice: let the app start once so it
initializes its profile, and **quit it completely** before installing — otherwise the
profile is locked.

```bash
# quoting the app's bundled CLI; see docs/ONBOARDING.md for the section titles
"<DeepSeek Harness.app>/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh" \
  plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-mobile-link
```

Then restart the host (or reload the profile). From a checkout the same command takes
a path — the leading `./` matters, because DSH anchors a relative spec against
your current directory instead of resolving it inside the profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/mobile-link
```

## Use

1. Register this computer with a relay (once). Open the **移动端连接** panel at the
   bottom of the DSH sidebar: the relay address is prefilled (editable) from the
   installation default; click **登记**. The connector derives the computer name
   automatically, writes `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` and reconnects in place —
   no terminal and no DSH restart. Open enrollment is the default; the relay
   rate-limits by source. If an installation has no panel (headless, CI), the CLI
   still works:

   ```bash
   dsh-mobile-link enroll --relay wss://<你的站点>/dsh-link
   ```

   …or register it on the relay host with `dsh-relay admin agent-register
   --write-config ~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json`.

2. The same panel shows the pairing code and its QR once the relay link is up.
   The CLI can still mint one directly:

   ```bash
   dsh-mobile-link --mint-pair-code        # prints JSON: code + relay + agentId
   ```

   The code is persistent: it stays valid until you click 重新生成. Each paired device
   has a quiet 撤销 action; revoking one device leaves the code and other devices alone.

3. Scan it in the iOS app. The code can be claimed again for another phone, a reinstall
   or a new device; only 重新生成 revokes it (already-paired devices stay connected).
   After that the phone reconnects on its own — nothing else has to be run by hand.

`GET /mobile-link/status` reports whether the link is up, which devices are
attached, and whether this computer is registered yet. Its `enroll` block also
carries `panel` (this connector can enroll from the DSH panel), `relayPrefill`
and `relayLocked` (the address to prefill and whether it came from config).
`POST /mobile-link/enroll` performs that enrollment (open enrollment; no invite code); it returns the agent id and
name, never `agentSecret`, and is behind the same DSH request fence as pairing. `GET /mobile-link/devices` lists the full paired roster (including offline) for the panel, and
`POST /mobile-link/devices/revoke` revokes one paired device by `deviceId` through the relay; both are behind
the fence and authenticated with the agent secret. Its `journal` block carries
the current process's newest lifecycle events (link opened/closed with the reason,
device attached/detached); the counters in it reset when the plugin hot-reloads, so
the full history — across restarts — is the JSONL file at `journal.path`.

## Configuration

All optional; the defaults are what a stock deployment needs. Set them in the
plugin's config block (`cordis.patch.yml`), not by editing this file.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` stops the outbound link without uninstalling |
| `relayUrl` | from `agent.json` | Relay base URL; a bare deployment dials `<relay>/link/agent`. Pinning a real value here outranks the enrolled identity and makes the panel field read-only |
| `defaultRelayUrl` | empty | Form-only default: prefills the panel's relay input, but never outranks the enrolled identity. Official installs set this so users can still edit it |
| `agentId` / `agentSecret` | from `agent.json` | Override the enrolled identity |
| `stateFile` | `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | Where the identity lives |
| `journalFile` | `~/.dsh/mobile-link/link-events.jsonl` | Lifecycle journal (rotated once at 256 KiB); `false` keeps it in memory only |
| `slowRequestMs` | `2000` | A slower single request gets its own `request.slow` entry; `0` disables those (per-attach `device.summary` is still written) |
| `diagnostics` | `true` | `false` refuses the phone's phase uploads; the phone ignores the refusal and stays connected |
| `dshUrl` | discovery | Explicit local DSH base URL (usually unnecessary — the host hands the connector its own address) |
| `heartbeatMs` | `20000` | DLP ping interval |

The connector does **not** read an endpoint handoff file any more: discovery happens inside
the host process (`ctx.inject(['webServer','connection'])`), which is what makes one npm
package work on both the desktop app and the command-line host. It **writes** one instead —
`$DSH_HOME/mobile-link/endpoint.json`, mode 0600 — for tools that run *outside* the host
(our dev/test scripts and the iOS integration helpers).

Address resolution order: this config block, then `DSH_RELAY_URL` (or
`DSH_MOBILE_LINK_RELAY`), then the enrolled identity file, then the repository
placeholder `wss://relay.example.com/dsh-link` — the placeholder being the
"nothing configured yet" sentinel rather than a real address.

## Design notes

- **No required services.** `inject` is empty and the routes are attached through
  `ctx.inject([...])`, so a future DSH that renames or drops `webServer` /
  `connection` cannot make the tunnel fatal on boot.
- **Protocol-transparent.** Nothing outside `lib/` is imported and no DSH
  business API is touched: the connector forwards frames, it does not interpret
  sessions. The relay has the same property.
- **Disable** by removing the row from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, or by
  setting `enabled: false`.

## Test

```bash
cd plugins/mobile-link && npm test    # zero dependencies
```

The wire protocol is specified in
[`docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md`](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/blob/main/docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md).

# DSH Mobile

**中文** · [English](README.en.md)

[![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![listed in awesome-deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--deepseek--harness-4D6BFE?logo=awesomelists&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness)
[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness)
[![iOS 17+](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-17%2B-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](docs/VERSIONING.md)
[![TestFlight](https://img.shields.io/badge/TestFlight-join-0D96F6?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk)
[![connector on npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-mobile-link?label=connector)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-mobile-link)
[![CI](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

把电脑上的 [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 会话接到 iPhone 与 iPad：原生 iOS
客户端、电脑侧连接器、可自建的公网中转。手机经中转连接电脑上的 DSH host，会话与消息流与电脑端
一致；任务在电脑锁屏后继续运行，挂起的提问可在手机上作答。电脑无需公网 IP，也无需 VPN。

![DSH Mobile 演示：电脑端登记、手机扫码配对，查看会话、远程文件、git 改动与提交历史](docs/artifacts/demo/dsh-mobile-demo.gif)

## 状态与兼容性

连接器与 iOS App 请保持最新版本：两者按同一份协议演进，跨版本的兼容窗口有限。版本组合与
兼容性约束见 [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](docs/VERSIONING.md)。

## 前提

- 电脑已安装并可运行 DSH（`dsh web`）；连接器需要 Node.js ≥ 22。
- 自建中转需一台有公网 IP 的主机（macOS 或 Linux）与 Caddy。
- 从源码构建 App 需 macOS + Xcode 16 以上；日常使用不需要。

## 快速开始

### A. 使用公共中转

1. 安装 App：加入 [TestFlight 公开测试](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk)（需先安装 TestFlight）。
2. 安装连接器，装进实际在用的宿主档案（装错不会报错，但连接器不会被加载）：
   - 命令行 web 版：`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mobile-link`
   - 官方桌面版：用应用内插件页，或应用自带的 `dsh` 命令装进 `desktop` 档案（普通 npm 版 `dsh`
     会拒绝该档案）。两种宿主的识别判据见 [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。
3. 登记：DSH 左下角「移动端连接」→ 确认中转地址 →「登记」。开放登记，无需邀请码，按来源限流；
   无头环境用 `dsh-mobile-link enroll --relay wss://<中转地址>/dsh-link`。
4. 生效：安装插件与面板登记均无需重启；仅命令行登记且宿主正在运行时需重启一次。
5. 配对：App「扫码配对」扫描面板中的二维码与配对码；配对码点「重新生成」才会更换。

顶部显示「已连接」即为成功；完整步骤与故障排查见 [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。

### B. 自建中转

自建使用仓库内 Go 实现（`relay-go/`）。构建与安装见
[`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md) §2–§4；Caddy 路由用
[`Caddyfile.snippet`](relay-go/deploy/Caddyfile.snippet) 配合
[`caddy_splice.py`](relay-go/deploy/caddy_splice.py) 插入站点块。

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now dsh-relay-go
```

实时负载与每设备用量：`curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/stats`（仅监听回环）。限额与运维细节见
[`relay-go/README.md`](relay-go/README.md) 与 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md)。

## 组件与数据流

```
┌──────────────┐   WSS    ┌────────────────────┐   WSS    ┌───────────────────┐
│  iOS App     ├─────────►│  Relay（公网主机）  │◄─────────┤ 电脑侧连接器       │
│  SwiftUI     │          │  鉴权 + 转发        │          │ (DSH 插件)        │
└──────────────┘          └────────────────────┘          └─────────┬─────────┘
                                                                     │ HTTP + WS
                                                           ┌─────────▼─────────┐
                                                           │ dsh web           │
                                                           │ 127.0.0.1:<port>  │
                                                           └───────────────────┘
```

| 组件 | 位置 | 职责 |
|---|---|---|
| iOS App | 手机 | 会话列表、转写、图片与文件、配对与设备管理 |
| 连接器 | 电脑（DSH 插件） | 以 `127.0.0.1` 访问本机 DSH，转成中转帧 |
| 中转 | 公网主机 | 鉴权与按 `agentId` 转发；**不解析会话内容** |
| DSH host | 电脑 | 会话、agent 与工具的真实执行方 |

产品上只提供经中转这一条连接方式；`dsh://direct` 是 DEBUG-only 的测试通道。选型与边界见
[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) 与 [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md)。

## 配置

仓库中的 `relay.example.com` 一律为占位符：中转地址由部署方决定，不属于仓库。真值只存在于本机并被
gitignore：

| 位置 | 用途 | 提供方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `.env.local` | 发布脚本、开发探针 | `cp .env.example .env.local`，按模板填站点与中转地址 |
| `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | 连接器的中转地址与身份 | 面板「登记」，或 `dsh-mobile-link enroll --relay <地址>` |
| `ios/DSHMobile/Config.local.xcconfig` | App 内预填的中转地址与更新源 | 从 `Config.xcconfig` 复制后填写 |

直接 clone 构建的 App 不含中转地址，属有意设计。

## 开发

```bash
cd ios/DSHMobile/DSHKit && swift test        # 协议层
cd plugins/mobile-link  && npm test          # 连接器
cd relay-go && make test                     # 中转（Go，生产实现）
cd mail && ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q   # 信件服务
npm run check:secrets                        # 本机真值没有进跟踪文件
npm run check:docs                           # 文档规范（结构、口吻、链接）

cd ios/DSHMobile && xcodebuild -scheme DSHMobile \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=DSH-Test' build
```

上述单测与一次不带本机配置的 Release 构建由 GitHub Actions 执行。需要仿真器、真实中转或开发者团队
ID 的验证不在 CI 内；CI 通过不等于可以发布。

界面测试为独立测试台：`./test/run.sh prepare` → `run <用例>` → `report --verdict …`；口径见
[`test/RULES.md`](test/RULES.md)，模板见 [`test/examples/`](test/examples)。

## 文档

| 文档 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md) | 两种部署路径的选择、操作步骤、故障排查 |

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-send-image

> 面向：使用者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20

**Lets the agent put a picture into the conversation.** A screenshot, the
clipboard, or a file — the host normalizes and persists the bytes, every DSH
client renders it inline, and the user can open it full screen.

Why a plugin is needed at all: DSH's model adapters declare **text-only output**,
so the agent cannot emit an image in its answer. The bytes reach the client
through the Host's attachment service (`ctx.attachments.saveImage`, which
normalizes and persists them) and the returned reference rides on this tool's
**result**, as an image content block — so every client draws the picture inside
the agent's own turn.

Submitting it as a prompt instead — which is what this plugin used to do — is
wrong twice over: a prompt is a **user message**, so the picture looked like
something the user had sent, and it **started a turn**, so the agent answered its
own screenshot. `send-image.mjs --via-prompt` keeps that path for a client that
cannot render tool-result images; nothing here uses it.

```
plugins/send-image/
├── package.json          # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle patch: the loader row
├── lib/index.js          # cordis plugin: registers the send_image tool
└── test/                 # node --test, 19 tests (no DSH, no network)
```

The tool is a thin shell around
[`skills/send-image/send-image.mjs`](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/blob/main/skills/send-image/send-image.mjs),
which owns the capture quirks (`screencapture`, `pngpaste`, the screen-recording
permission message) and prints one JSON descriptor. Standalone it only
*prepares* — the publishing half needs the Host context this plugin has:

```bash
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --screenshot        # prints the descriptor
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --file ./out/render.png
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --clipboard         # needs pngpaste
```

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-send-image
```

Then restart DSH (or reload the profile). From a checkout a relative spec works
too — the leading `./` matters, because DSH anchors it against your current
directory instead of resolving it inside the profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/send-image
```

## Use

The agent calls `send_image`. Exactly one source per call:

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Path to an image (absolute, or relative to the working directory) |
| `screenshot` | `true` captures the whole screen — the picture contains everything on it |
| `clipboard` | `true` sends the image on the clipboard (needs `pngpaste`) |
| `caption` | Text shown with the picture |

Passing none or several is a readable tool error rather than a schema failure:
source exclusivity is a runtime rule here, so the model is told what to fix.

### You can also take the screenshot yourself

Inside the DSH window, `⌥⌘S` (or the button at the left of the composer) starts a drag-select; the
selected rectangle is **attached to the current conversation as a draft** — you decide whether to send
it. The shortcut only works while the DSH window has focus (no system-wide hotkey), and it can be
rebound under Settings → Shortcuts. `Esc` cancels without leaving a file, and a missing Screen
Recording grant prints where to enable it and which program to restart.

Both supported hosts (the official desktop app and the command-line web host) run the same client
half, shipped in this package. The plugin is hot-pluggable: enabling or disabling it adds or removes
the shortcut, the composer button and its styles in place — no host restart, no page reload.

## Test

```bash
cd plugins/send-image && npm test    # 14 tests, zero dependencies
```

MIT.

# DSH Mobile

**中文** · [English](README.en.md)

[![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![listed in awesome-deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--deepseek--harness-4D6BFE?logo=awesomelists&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness)
[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness)
[![iOS 17+](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-17%2B-000000?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](docs/VERSIONING.md)
[![TestFlight](https://img.shields.io/badge/TestFlight-join-0D96F6?logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk)
[![connector on npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-mobile-link?label=connector)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-mobile-link)
[![CI](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

把电脑上的 [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 会话接到 iPhone 与 iPad：原生 iOS
客户端、电脑侧连接器、可自建的公网中转。手机经中转连接电脑上的 DSH host，会话与消息流与电脑端
一致；任务在电脑锁屏后继续运行，挂起的提问可在手机上作答。电脑无需公网 IP，也无需 VPN。

![DSH Mobile 演示：电脑端登记、手机扫码配对，查看会话、远程文件、git 改动与提交历史](docs/artifacts/demo/dsh-mobile-demo.gif)

## 状态与兼容性

连接器与 iOS App 请保持最新版本：两者按同一份协议演进，跨版本的兼容窗口有限。版本组合与
兼容性约束见 [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](docs/VERSIONING.md)。

## 前提

- 电脑已安装并可运行 DSH（`dsh web`）；连接器需要 Node.js ≥ 22。
- 自建中转需一台有公网 IP 的主机（macOS 或 Linux）与 Caddy。
- 从源码构建 App 需 macOS + Xcode 16 以上；日常使用不需要。

## 快速开始

### A. 使用公共中转

1. 安装 App：加入 [TestFlight 公开测试](https://testflight.apple.com/join/tHKQsbCk)（需先安装 TestFlight）。
2. 安装连接器，装进实际在用的宿主档案（装错不会报错，但连接器不会被加载）：
   - 命令行 web 版：`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mobile-link`
   - 官方桌面版：用应用内插件页，或应用自带的 `dsh` 命令装进 `desktop` 档案（普通 npm 版 `dsh`
     会拒绝该档案）。两种宿主的识别判据见 [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。
3. 登记：DSH 左下角「移动端连接」→ 确认中转地址 →「登记」。开放登记，无需邀请码，按来源限流；
   无头环境用 `dsh-mobile-link enroll --relay wss://<中转地址>/dsh-link`。
4. 生效：安装插件与面板登记均无需重启；仅命令行登记且宿主正在运行时需重启一次。
5. 配对：App「扫码配对」扫描面板中的二维码与配对码；配对码点「重新生成」才会更换。

顶部显示「已连接」即为成功；完整步骤与故障排查见 [`docs/ONBOARDING.md`](docs/ONBOARDING.md)。

### B. 自建中转

自建使用仓库内 Go 实现（`relay-go/`）。构建与安装见
[`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md) §2–§4；Caddy 路由用
[`Caddyfile.snippet`](relay-go/deploy/Caddyfile.snippet) 配合
[`caddy_splice.py`](relay-go/deploy/caddy_splice.py) 插入站点块。

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now dsh-relay-go
```

实时负载与每设备用量：`curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/stats`（仅监听回环）。限额与运维细节见
[`relay-go/README.md`](relay-go/README.md) 与 [`relay-go/deploy/README.md`](relay-go/deploy/README.md)。

## 组件与数据流

```
┌──────────────┐   WSS    ┌────────────────────┐   WSS    ┌───────────────────┐
│  iOS App     ├─────────►│  Relay（公网主机）  │◄─────────┤ 电脑侧连接器       │
│  SwiftUI     │          │  鉴权 + 转发        │          │ (DSH 插件)        │
└──────────────┘          └────────────────────┘          └─────────┬─────────┘
                                                                     │ HTTP + WS
                                                           ┌─────────▼─────────┐
                                                           │ dsh web           │
                                                           │ 127.0.0.1:<port>  │
                                                           └───────────────────┘
```

| 组件 | 位置 | 职责 |
|---|---|---|
| iOS App | 手机 | 会话列表、转写、图片与文件、配对与设备管理 |
| 连接器 | 电脑（DSH 插件） | 以 `127.0.0.1` 访问本机 DSH，转成中转帧 |
| 中转 | 公网主机 | 鉴权与按 `agentId` 转发；**不解析会话内容** |
| DSH host | 电脑 | 会话、agent 与工具的真实执行方 |

产品上只提供经中转这一条连接方式；`dsh://direct` 是 DEBUG-only 的测试通道。选型与边界见
[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) 与 [`docs/PAIRING.md`](docs/PAIRING.md)。

## 配置

仓库中的 `relay.example.com` 一律为占位符：中转地址由部署方决定，不属于仓库。真值只存在于本机并被
gitignore：

| 位置 | 用途 | 提供方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `.env.local` | 发布脚本、开发探针 | `cp .env.example .env.local`，按模板填站点与中转地址 |
| `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | 连接器的中转地址与身份 | 面板「登记」，或 `dsh-mobile-link enroll --relay <地址>` |
| `ios/DSHMobile/Config.local.xcconfig` | App 内预填的中转地址与更新源 | 从 `Config.xcconfig` 复制后填写 |

直接 clone 构建的 App 不含中转地址，属有意设计。

## 开发

```bash
cd ios/DSHMobile/DSHKit && swift test        # 协议层
cd plugins/mobile-link  && npm test          # 连接器
cd relay-go && make test                     # 中转（Go，生产实现）
cd mail && ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q   # 信件服务
npm run check:secrets                        # 本机真值没有进跟踪文件
npm run check:docs                           # 文档规范（结构、口吻、链接）

cd ios/DSHMobile && xcodebuild -scheme DSHMobile \
  -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=DSH-Test' build
```

上述单测与一次不带本机配置的 Release 构建由 GitHub Actions 执行。需要仿真器、真实中转或开发者团队
ID 的验证不在 CI 内；CI 通过不等于可以发布。

界面测试为独立测试台：`./test/run.sh prepare` → `run <用例>` → `report --verdict …`；口径见
[`test/RULES.md`](test/RULES.md)，模板见 [`test/examples/`](test/examples)。

dsh-scrapling

Scrapling web scraping for dsh: JavaScript rendering, structured extraction and a background crawler, behind one resident Python sidecar.

**A web-scraping extension for [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): [Scrapling](https://github.com/D4Vinci/Scrapling) as agent tools — JavaScript rendering, CSS/XPath extraction with self-healing selectors, sessions with login state, a background crawler and page Q&A. You supply the interpreter and the browser engine; everything runs in one resident Python process.** ## Contents - [What it does](#what-it-does) - [Install](#install) - [Runtime packs (macOS arm64)](#runtime-packs-macos-arm64) - [Verify it is live](#verify-it-is-live) - [What it does not provide](#what-it-does-not-provide) - [Enabling it in dsh](#enabling-it-in-dsh) - [The tools](#the-tools) - [Replacing the built-in fetch and search](#replacing-the-built-in-fetch-and-search) - [MCP mode](#mcp-mode) - [Settings](#settings) - [Proxies](#proxies) - [Security](#security) - [Data and privacy](#data-and-privacy) - [Known boundaries](#known-boundaries) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Development](#development) - [License](#license) ## What it does dsh ships `web_fetch` and `web_search`. The built-in `web_fetch` is deliberately honest and minimal: a plain HTTP(S) GET with no JavaScript execution and an honest User-Agent. That is a good default — and it means a single-page application yields only its loading shell, and there is no way to ask for "just the product table". Measured on a page whose content exists only after JavaScript runs: | Pipeline | Text obtained | |---|---| | raw HTML to text (no JS) | `SPA Shell / LOADING_PLACEHOLDER` | | `Fetcher` (curl_cffi, still no JS) | `SPA Shell / LOADING_PLACEHOLDER` | | browser render (patchright) | full rendered DOM, Markdown table, structured rows | This package adds what the built-ins structurally cannot do: - **Browser rendering** — JavaScript execution via patchright. - **Structured extraction** — CSS/XPath selection returning data, not a wall of Markdown. - **Self-healing selectors** — Scrapling's `adaptive` mode relocates an element after the site's markup changes; a selector that returns `None` after a class rename returns the relocated element with `adaptive` on. Everything runs against **one long-lived Python process**. That is not an optimisation: Scrapling's session classes keep cookies, the browser engines keep a page pool, and `adaptive` keeps a SQLite fingerprint database — a process per call would throw all of that away. Tools are registered **conditionally**: the plugin probes what the environment can actually do at startup and registers only what will work, so the model never burns a turn on a tool that was guaranteed to fail. Every tool renders its result row through the official tool-call view slot. `scrapling_answer` is the only tool that spends **another model call** — see [The tools](#the-tools). ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @jayyuen66/dsh-scrapling ``` Remove with `dsh plugin --profile web remove @jayyuen66/dsh-scrapling`. The package is on the public npm registry, so installation needs no credentials and no scoped-registry line. - **Requires Node.js `>= 24.9`.** This is an ESM-only package, and the build entry points (`build-client.ts`, `build-host.ts`, `build-cli.ts`) are executed by `node` directly, so the floor has to sit where TypeScript type stripping is on by default (Node 22.18 up). The number itself is the host floor: `0.2.2` hosts declare Node `>= 24.9.0`, and a host below it never starts. - **Requires host `dsh` at the `0.2.1-rc.5` or `0.2.2-alpha.3` line.** The requirement the host actually reads is `engines.dsh` (`^0.2.1-rc.5 || ^0.2.2-alpha.3`), and it decides alone; a host on a later line is refused and needs the explicit risk grant `dsh plugin --profile

allow-version @ --dsh-version --accept-risk`. The support window rolls: this package is verified against every released host version inside the window at publish time and re-verified once the window moves, so the version number in this bullet is not a standing promise. - **Requires Python 3.14+ with Scrapling installed** — named by `pythonBin`, or found by the fixed chain in `lib/runtime.ts` (managed runtime under `dataDir/runtime`, then the repository's `_env/.venv`, then `PATH`). In an installed package the `_env/.venv` leg does not exist, so after `setup --feature core --apply` the interpreter is that managed Python and otherwise the `python3` on your `PATH` (`python` on Windows); whichever one is chosen is logged at load time, and a missing Scrapling reports an error carrying the install line to copy. ```sh pip install "scrapling[rag]>=0.5,<0.6" python -m patchright install chromium ``` - **Why `rag` and not `fetchers`:** `rag` is `fetchers` plus `markdownify`, and the default `extractionType` is `markdown` — with plain `fetchers` the first fetch raises `ModuleNotFoundError` at the Markdown conversion. - **Version range:** developed and verified against Scrapling **0.5**, through interfaces that are not stable API surface (`Selector`, `Spider`, `SessionManager`, and the converter's noise-stripping helpers). The upper bound is pinned below `0.6`; outside the range the guards still run, but the anti-injection cleaning and the crawl path may not behave as documented. In 0.5 the browser backend is patchright only (the old standalone stealth fetch is gone; its anti-detection arguments live on `scrapling_render`), `capture_xhr` became session-level recording (hence `scrapling_session_network`), and `extra_flags` became additive — this package sends none, and WebRTC leak protection is carried by the `blockWebrtc` switch. - **Without the installer, the browser engine is yours.** The optional CLI can install the verified macOS arm64 set; the plugin itself downloads nothing at load time. Without a browser it simply does not register the browser-dependent tools, so the model never wastes a turn calling them. - **No `@deepseek-ai/*` under `dependencies`, by contract** (`test/publish-manifest.test.ts` enforces it). Consumer profiles install with `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, so a host package there becomes a real second copy whose module-level state splits from the running host's — every native tool call then throws while build and tests stay green. The host packages the artifact imports for value are required peers and stay externalized; the gate imports the built artifact and asserts that no host package body is inlined. - **The artifact is ESM-only and never committed** — `prepack` rebuilds it, so what ships is always what the current source produces. ### Shared version floor If your profile pins `@jayyuen66/dsh-plugin-shared` with a pnpm `overrides` entry, that pin must be at least the version this package declares. A lower pin installs a copy without the names the sources use, and the host then reports `N entries did not activate` together with `does not provide an export named ...` at boot - the package installs fine and never loads, and no per-repository CI run can see it. ## Runtime packs (macOS arm64) The package ships `bin/dsh-scrapling.mjs`. It installs the ability packs into `dataDir/runtime` (default `~/.dsh-scrapling`) — never into system Python and never into the user's Playwright cache. There is **no `postinstall`**; nothing is downloaded when the plugin loads. ```sh dsh-scrapling setup --feature core --apply dsh-scrapling setup --feature browser --apply dsh-scrapling setup --status ``` - `core` installs managed Python 3.14.9, Scrapling 0.5 and its pinned wheels; `browser` adds the full Chromium build (not the headless shell). - `search`, `media`, `mcp` and `adaptive-redis` all ride on `core`'s venv: `mcp` brings the official `scrapling-mcp` server (the pinned `mcp` package; its tool set is the upstream's, not this plugin's) that `official-mcp` mode needs, and `adaptive-redis` brings the `redis` client behind `adaptiveStorage: redis`. Every pack is installable; the settings card reports each as `ready`, `missing`, `corrupt` or `installing`. - `--feature` is a dry run by default; `--apply` writes. `--repair` re-installs without touching user data, and `--uninstall [--purge]` removes runtime files; only `--purge` removes `elements_storage.db` and `downloads/`. - `--offline

` installs with no network at all: `` must hold the Python archive named exactly as the manifest URL's last segment (browser and `curl -O` both keep `cpython-3.14.9+…-install_only.tar.gz`, and the percent-encoded spelling is accepted too) plus a `wheels/` directory with one wheel per pinned requirement - `pip download --only-binary=:all: --require-hashes -r py/runtime-requirements.txt -d /wheels` produces it. The hash check on the Python archive is the same one the networked path runs, and pip is invoked with `--no-index`; a missing archive or wheelhouse fails as `INSTALL_OFFLINE_ASSETS` instead of silently going online. - `setup --status` prints one JSON document: `dataDir`, `profile`, `runtime`, `packs` and `state`. With `--profile ` it reads that profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, resolves the interpreter from this package's `pythonBin` and the data directory from `dataDir` (the two settings the host actually uses); `packs` and `state` are then reported for that directory — when the entry carries no `dataDir`, both fall back to the CLI's own default. Without `--profile`, `profile.path` is `null`, a note says the profile was not read, and `runtime` falls back to the CLI's own chain (managed runtime → repo `_env/.venv` → PATH `python3`). Pass `--profile` whenever you compare the card's interpreter with what `--status` reports. - The settings card can start the same install/repair/cancel actions through the `scraplingRuntime` remote when the profile has both a remote surface and a jobs backend; otherwise it prints the CLI command. - `integrationMode` is deployment-only; `setup --mode` prints or writes the client entry for the two MCP shapes and `doctor` checks a profile against it — see [MCP mode](#mcp-mode). `official-mcp` starts `scrapling-mcp` from the managed venv, which the `mcp` pack provisions (`setup --feature mcp --apply`). - Only **macOS arm64** is verified. Windows, Linux and macOS x64 are blocked (B1/B2): every pack reports `blocked` and the installer refuses rather than guessing an asset path. ## Verify it is live 1. **The layer is mounted.** `dsh --profile web --dump-config` shows this package's layer line. - That command is the only accepted "it is in the layer stack" signal, and it is **not read-only** — it rewrites the profile's root assembly file. Read layer lines from stdout **and** check stderr separately: an unmatched patch target appears only on stderr, so the exit code alone proves nothing. Accept both `# == ` and `# == , patched by `. 2. **The startup log names the interpreter and the plan.** One line prints the probed capabilities and how many of the tools registered; the chosen interpreter path is logged at load. An interpreter that starts but lacks Scrapling is named in the log together with the pip line to copy. 3. **The settings card renders.** The plugin detail page carries the **scrapling** card with every user-editable field grouped by purpose; toggling a value enables Save, and the write returns 200. 4. **A tool round-trip.** Ask the model to fetch a JavaScript-heavy page: the result row renders in the chat through the official tool-call view. On a machine without a browser the render / capture_xhr tools are absent from the model's tool list and their prompt guidance is gone too — that absence is the conditional registration working, not a failure. ## What it does not provide - **It is not a search engine.** Discovery runs in the Python sidecar against one of six backends (`searchBackend`: `auto` / `tavily` / `bing` / `brave` / `serper` / `duckduckgo` / `searxng`); Scrapling's own `google_search` option only sets a referer header. Each backend needs its own setting (`tavilyApiKey`, `braveApiKey`, `serperApiKey`, `searxngEndpoint`) — a backend that is selected but not configured reports `SEARCH_AUTH` instead of silently switching to another one. - **The npm tarball bundles no interpreter or browser.** They come from your machine or from the optional CLI installer, which downloads the verified macOS arm64 set into `dataDir/runtime`; missing pieces remove the matching tools instead of being fetched at load time. - **It adds no HTTP route on the host side.** The settings card is a host config form and this package exposes no `/api` surface. The one socket that really listens is the MCP server under `integrationMode: mcp`, bound to `127.0.0.1` (`http://127.0.0.1:/mcp`): any other path gets 404, a declared body over 1 MiB gets 413, a request without `Content-Length` gets 411, and the bearer token is read only from `DSH_SCRAPLING_MCP_TOKEN` — with no token set, startup prints a stderr notice that the endpoint is unauthenticated and reachable from any local process. - **It adds no dsh subcommand.** The package's own `dsh-scrapling` CLI manages runtime packs, plus the two halves of the MCP hookup: `setup --mode native|mcp|official-mcp` generates the client entry and, with `--apply`, writes it to `/mcp/.patch.yml` (the profile itself is never touched), while `doctor --mode` compares that entry against the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` item by item. Given `--profile`, `setup --status` reads `pythonBin` and `dataDir` from that same file. ## Enabling it in dsh - `dsh.bundle.patch` points at `cordis.patch.yml`, which carries a single `- id: scrapling` entry with the **bare package name** — the host scans `dsh.client` on bare package-name entries only. The card components are bundled into `client.js` (only `react` / `zod` stay external to the host's module table), so the card does not depend on a second package being loaded. - The client half registers two surfaces: the settings card (on the `plugins.bundle.config` slot, keyed by the bundle package name — the host dispatches `entryKey: pkg.name`, so the card renders on this package's detail page) and one result row per tool on `tool.call.toolview`, drawn with the official tool-call view props. - The settings namespace is the entry id `scrapling`; precedence is settings-card value > registration-line `config:` > schema default. Setting a field back to its default saves a **clear-override**, not a write of the same value, so a later default change still reaches you. - Gate policy and the sidecar environment are snapshotted once when the plugin is applied — **settings changes take effect on the next start**. - Disabling a tool also removes its system-prompt guidance: the guidance is re-read at each prompt assembly against the tools that scope can actually see, so a machine without a browser loses the render / capture_xhr lines and a sidecar that never came up loses all of them. The section is placed next to the built-in `web_fetch` guidance. - `scrapling_crawl` registers its own job kind, so `job_list` labels its jobs as crawls rather than shell jobs. ## The tools Nineteen tools, behind fifteen settings switches (the seven session/state tools share switches), all exercised by the test suite: | Tool | Backend | Needs a browser | Concurrency | |---|---|---|---| | `scrapling_fetch` | `Fetcher` (curl_cffi) | no | concurrent; write verbs are serialised once `allowWriteMethods` is on | | `scrapling_extract` | `Selector` + CSS/XPath + `adaptive` | no | concurrent | | `scrapling_locate` | text / regex / similar-element lookup; returns generated selectors | no | concurrent | | `scrapling_links` | `LinkExtractor` plus next-page candidates | no | concurrent | | `scrapling_render` | `StealthySession` (patchright) | yes | serialised; the anti-detection switches (`solveCloudflare` / `hideCanvas` / `blockWebrtc`) live here | | `scrapling_capture_xhr` | one throwaway session, page-level recording | yes | serialised | | `scrapling_session_open` / `scrapling_session_fetch` / `scrapling_session_network` / `scrapling_session_state_save` / `scrapling_session_state_load` / `scrapling_session_list` / `scrapling_session_close` | Scrapling session classes | browser sessions only | serialised | | `scrapling_session_read` | current DOM of a browser session page | yes | serialised | | `scrapling_session_act` | structured actions on a session page (deployment gate) | yes | serialised | | `scrapling_download` | byte download into `dataDir/downloads` (deployment gate) | no | concurrent | | `scrapling_screenshot` | PNG/JPEG screenshot handed to the attachment service | yes | serialised | | `scrapling_crawl` | Scrapling Spider framework (`content` / `sitemap` / `feed` / `shopify`) as a job | no | serialised | | `scrapling_answer` | any fetch path plus `ctx.llm` | with `render: true` | serialised | - **Quotas.** At most 8 open sessions (3 of them browser sessions, each a real Chromium process), 2 crawls in flight, per-page bodies clipped by `*MaxOutputChars`, 8 MB per protocol frame, 16 queued frames. A ceiling answers with a specific code (`SESSION_LIMIT` / `CRAWL_BUSY` / `BAD_FRAME`) the model can back off from. - **`scrapling_crawl` returns a job id immediately** — a crawl takes minutes and a tool call has a timeout. Watch it with `job_list`, read it with `job_output`, stop it with `job_kill`; the tool needs a jobs registry that can attach a controller, and a profile without one simply does not register it (single-page fetching is unaffected). The crawl has a wall-clock ceiling (`crawlMaxRuntimeSeconds`) and never leaves the start domain. Politeness defaults follow Scrapling's spider defaults — robots.txt is **not** obeyed, per-domain delay is 0, up to 4 requests run in parallel — and is a deployment decision, not a per-call one (see [Settings](#settings)). - **`scrapling_answer` fetches the page first, then hands the text plus your question to a model** and returns the conclusion instead of the whole page. It follows the model the current session is already using by default (read from the session's live request header, so a mid-session model switch is picked up), which burns no separate quota; pin `answerProvider` / `answerModel` to route page-reading elsewhere. Page text is **untrusted input** — the prompt frames it explicitly as data, but that defence is prompt-level: it lowers the risk, it does not remove it. ### Render or static `scrapling_render` is much slower and heavier than `scrapling_fetch`, so start static. Two criteria: - **If the rendered result is shorter than the static fetch, go back to static.** Plenty of sites ship readable text from the server and then have their own script empty those containers and swap in canvas / Lottie animation — for those pages rendering can only lose content, and no wait setting brings it back. That is site behaviour, not a plugin defect. - **`waitSelector` waits for an element to appear, not for content to settle.** The element can be removed after it matched, so "the selector matched" does not mean the content is in the result. One thing that is not a criterion but worth knowing: axis ticks inside SVG **cannot be fetched at all** — the Markdown conversion emits no ` Replacing the built-in fetch and search The plugin registers itself as a **fetch provider** and a **search provider** on `ctx.web`, so the built-in `web_fetch` / `web_search` tools actually run on Scrapling instead of dsh's plain-HTTP implementation. The model still calls `web_fetch` / `web_search` — tool names cannot be swapped (same-name registration throws), the provider seam is the supported channel. Both providers are registered by default (`provideWebFetch` / `provideWebSearch`), but that alone displaces nothing: 1. leave `provideWebFetch` / `provideWebSearch` at their default (`true`); 2. set `fetchProvider` / `searchProvider` to `"scrapling"` in the **deployment** config. A configured id wins over auto-selection, which is why step 2 is required — and with two usable providers and no id named, `ctx.web` answers `WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS` and the tool becomes unavailable outright. Two consequences of pointing that line at this plugin: - **If the sidecar cannot start, the built-in `web_fetch` reports `WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_UNAVAILABLE`** rather than quietly falling back to plain HTTP. - **If you later remove the plugin but leave the line in**, the built-in tools report `WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_MISSING` — go back and remove `fetchProvider` / `searchProvider` too. - **The fetch provider really applies the output budget**: a body over `fetchMaxOutputChars` is cut to a head/tail window and flagged `truncated`, not passed through with a flag. Failures keep the sidecar code prefix (`URL_BLOCKED`, `SIDECAR_TIMEOUT`, `SIDECAR_UNAVAILABLE`), so a policy refusal is distinguishable from a crash or a timeout. Search is split in two, because Scrapling is not a search engine: **discovery** runs in the Python sidecar against the backend `searchBackend` names — Tavily, Bing HTML, Brave (API), Serper (API), DuckDuckGo HTML or SearXNG (JSON API); **reading** is this plugin's — the first `searchRenderTopN` results are actually fetched and, with a browser, rendered, so one `web_search` call returns both which pages matter and what they say. `auto` uses Tavily when `tavilyApiKey` is set, SearXNG when `searxngEndpoint` is set, and with neither configured it only goes to a public engine (Bing; DuckDuckGo when that backend is named explicitly) if `searchPublicFallback` is on — otherwise the provider is unavailable and `web_search` reports `SEARCH_BACKEND_MISSING` instead of querying anyone. Only Tavily and Bing have been exercised against the real endpoints here; Brave, Serper, DuckDuckGo and SearXNG are implemented to their documented request/response shapes and verified against local stubs, with real keys and real instances still unverified. Every returned URL goes through the same gate as a fetch; a page that fails to read is skipped alone, because search results routinely contain dead links. One consequence to know: `dsh-web`'s fetch body is a **closed** union of `html | text` with no `markdown` kind, and adding one is a cross-package change a plugin cannot make. The fetch provider therefore reports Scrapling's Markdown as `text`, which the built-in renderer displays normally. Use `scrapling_fetch` directly when you need `html` or a CSS selector. ## MCP mode `integrationMode` selects one of three mutually exclusive tool surfaces. It is deployment configuration (the `config:` block of `cordis.patch.yml`), it is read once when the plugin is assembled, and changing it requires a restart. | Mode | What it registers | |---|---| | `native` (default) | the `scrapling_*` tools listed above | | `mcp` | no native tools; the plugin serves the same tool table over MCP | | `official-mcp` | no native tools and no server from this plugin; `setup` only generates the `dsh-mcp-client` entry for the official `scrapling-mcp`, which runs in its own process, with its own sessions, and **without this plugin's URL guard** | In `mcp` mode the server runs inside the plugin's own host process and calls the same sidecar, so the URL guard, sessions, jobs and adaptive storage are the same ones the native tools use — there is no second implementation to drift. - **Endpoint** `http://127.0.0.1:/mcp` (`mcpPort`, default `39217`). Only loopback is bound; a request whose declared body exceeds 1 MiB is refused with `413`, and any other path gets `404`. The server is stateless: each request gets its own protocol instance, so nothing survives across them. - **Auth** off by default. Set the environment variable `DSH_SCRAPLING_MCP_TOKEN` and every request must then carry `Authorization: Bearer `. The token is only ever read from the environment, never from the profile, so it does not land in a config file. - **Tools** are the same `ToolDefinition` objects native registers: same JSON Schema, same argument validation, same renderers. `scrapling_answer` is not served — it routes through the model of the hosting session, which an external client does not have. `search` exists only on this surface, because an MCP client has no `ctx.web` seam. The gates are identical: with `allowBrowserActions=false` there is no `session_act`, with `allowFileDownloads=false` there is no `download`, and `search` is absent when no search backend is available. - **Results** are text content; a screenshot comes back as MCP image content instead of a host attachment. A failing tool returns `isError` with a readable message rather than dropping the connection. - **Names**: the MCP raw name is the tool name without the `scrapling_` prefix, and dsh's MCP client shows it as `mcp__scrapling__`. | Native tool | MCP raw name | |---|---| | `scrapling_fetch` | `fetch` | | `scrapling_extract` | `extract` | | `scrapling_locate` | `locate` | | `scrapling_links` | `links` | | `scrapling_render` | `render` | | `scrapling_capture_xhr` | `capture_xhr` | | `scrapling_session_open` | `session_open` | | `scrapling_session_fetch` | `session_fetch` | | `scrapling_session_network` | `session_network` | | `scrapling_session_state_save` | `session_state_save` | | `scrapling_session_state_load` | `session_state_load` | | `scrapling_session_list` | `session_list` | | `scrapling_session_close` | `session_close` | | `scrapling_crawl` | `crawl` | | `scrapling_session_read` | `session_read` | | `scrapling_session_act` | `session_act` | | `scrapling_download` | `download` | | `scrapling_screenshot` | `screenshot` | | — (`ctx.web` only) | `search` | Connecting dsh needs `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`, which this plugin deliberately does not depend on. Pin the build that matches the current host — npm `latest` is older than the host's own line and the host rejects the mismatch: ```bash dsh plugin --profile add @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.2.2-rc.1 # host on the 0.2.2-alpha.3 line: @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.2.2-alpha.3 # host on the 0.2.1-rc.5 line: @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.2.1-rc.5 ``` Then add one entry to that profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — this is exactly what `dsh-scrapling setup --mode mcp` prints, so you can als
