evidence.readmeExcerpt:
Oh My Claude

English | 中文

Claude Code, native inside dsh

Drive your logged-in Claude Code CLI as a first-class dsh provider: no API key, no extra services, no runtime dependencies.

Built with AI assistance, and open to more. Contributions from AI coding agents are welcome; start with CONTRIBUTING.md.

--- Claude Code CLI as an LLM provider for [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). Every request drives `claude -p` with stream-json in and out, so it uses whatever login, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, MCP servers and rate limits Claude Code already has. No API key needed. The plugin speaks the CLI's own protocol (the one the Agent SDK wraps) directly, so it has no runtime dependencies. ## Tour

The shield is dsh's own control. In a Claude session its rows become Claude's six permission modes, each labelled with the dsh access level it sets underneath.

One `✻` button beside the composer opens the whole plugin: Memory, Instructions, Skills, Rewind, Changes, MCP, Asides, Diagnostics, Tasks and Tune, plus a Restore tab while the session is still blank.

Cost and cached token count, two figures dsh cannot compute, join dsh's footer stats row. The pill turns orange once a session passes the spend line you set. The dollar figures are what the turns would cost at API rates; on a Claude subscription you are not billed them.

Plan usage and the CLI's own context breakdown live in dsh's context ring popover. On a phone the panel becomes a sheet.

Once an SSH box is saved, dsh's own Add workspace dialog gains a box dropdown: a folder on that box becomes a workspace here, and the session in it runs Claude Code there. Shots by tools/playwright/tour.ts. ## Install You need the Claude Code CLI on `PATH` and logged in (`claude --version` works, `claude` opens without asking you to sign in), and dsh 0.2 (0.2.2-alpha.2 or newer). On dsh 0.2.0 or 0.2.1, install 1.5.14; on dsh 0.1.x, install the npm tag for your line from the Compatibility table below. Nothing else: no API key, no Node build step. **From dsh's Plugins page**, in the web app or DSH Desktop: 1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar and press **Add plugin**. 2. Enter `dsh-oh-my-claude` and press **Install**. 3. Press **Enable now**, or turn on its switch later under **Installed plugins**. It loads without a restart. Reload the page and "Oh My Claude" appears in the model picker with the models your login can use. Pick one and chat. **From a terminal**, then restart dsh however you run it: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-oh-my-claude systemctl --user restart dsh-web.service ``` To install straight from the repository instead of npm, use `github:lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude` as the package name in either route. The plugin speaks English and Chinese and follows dsh's own language setting (Settings → General → Language), switching as soon as you change it. If the picker lists it as `Oh My Claude (not logged in)`, run `claude auth login` in a terminal on the box that runs dsh, or press Log in under Settings → Oh My Claude → Boxes. **DSH Desktop** (macOS and Windows) uses the Plugins page steps above. The plugin looks for `claude` in the usual install folders, since an app started from the Dock does not see your shell's PATH. On Windows it runs Claude as a plain child of dsh, so restarting the app ends a running turn, and the parts that need a Unix shell (Log in from Settings, SSH boxes) are not available. The server half has run under Electron on Linux the way Desktop runs it, and on Windows 11 with Claude Code installed from npm. When a newer version is on npm, an orange pill with the version number appears in Settings and on the panel's Runtime line; a click copies the update command for a terminal. On the Plugins page, dsh updates a third-party plugin by removing it and adding it again. Details, and the repairs the plugin makes on its own after a dsh upgrade, are under [Plugin updates](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#plugin-updates). Optional, in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`: ```yaml agent-default-model: # make Claude Code the default for new sessions provider: claude-code model: claude-fable-5-1 # any model id the picker lists subagent-model-selection: # let dsh subagents run on Claude Code too enabled: true allowedModels: - provider: claude-code model: claude-haiku-5-5 # any model id the picker lists ``` Working on the plugin itself? Start at [docs/developing.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/developing.md). ## Compatibility dsh ships prereleases only and moves client APIs between them, so every release of the plugin records the dsh line it was written for and the dsh it was driven on. "Runs on" is the range the code carries branches for; "tested on" is the dsh installed on the box when the release was cut. The update pill reads the floor off the registry: a box whose dsh is below it is never offered the update command, and the pill names the dsh that release needs instead. | Plugin | Runs on dsh | Tested on dsh | npm tag | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1.5.14 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-rc.1 | 0.2.2-rc.1 | `latest`, `dsh-0.2` | | 1.5.13 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-rc.1 | 0.2.2-rc.1 | none, superseded by 1.5.14 | | 1.5.12 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-alpha.2 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.13 | | 1.5.11 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-alpha.2 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.12 | | 1.5.10 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.2-alpha.2 | 0.2.2-alpha.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.11 | | 1.5.9 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.4 | 0.2.1-rc.4 | none, superseded by 1.5.10 | | 1.5.8 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.4 | 0.2.1-rc.4 | none, superseded by 1.5.9 | | 1.5.7 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.3 | 0.2.1-rc.3 | none, superseded by 1.5.8 | | 1.5.6 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.3 | 0.2.1-rc.3 | none, superseded by 1.5.7 | | 1.5.5 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.2 | 0.2.1-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.6 | | 1.5.4 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-rc.2 | 0.2.1-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.5 | | 1.5.3 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.1-alpha.1 | 0.2.1-alpha.1 | none, superseded by 1.5.4 | | 1.5.2 | 0.2.0-rc.1 through 0.2.0-rc.2 | 0.2.0-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.5.3 | | 1.4.2 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.7-rc.2 | 0.1.7-rc.2 | `dsh-0.1.7` | | 1.4.1 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.7-rc.2 | 0.1.7-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.4.2 | | 1.4.0 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.7-rc.2 | 0.1.7-rc.2 | none, superseded by 1.4.1 | | 1.3.1 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.6-alpha.2 | 0.1.6-alpha.2 | `dsh-0.1.6` | | 1.2.1 | 0.1.5-rc.1 through 0.1.6-alpha.2 | 0.1.6-alpha.2 | `dsh-0.1.5` | ## What you get 1. Any Claude model your login can use, in dsh's own picker. Hide the ones you don't use with a switch in Settings, or with `hiddenModels` in the plugin config. [Models](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#models) 2. Every dsh session resumes its Claude Code session, tool history included, and a terminal `claude /resume` sees the same one. [Sessions](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#sessions) 3. Restart dsh without killing a running Claude turn. [Restarts](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#restarts) 4. dsh's access shield sets Claude's six permission modes per session. [Permission mode](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#permission-mode-per-session) 5. Claude's permission prompts, questions and plan reviews become dsh dialogs, each option's preview under the question. [Approvals](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#approvals-and-questions) 6. One spark button opens Memory, Rewind, Changes, MCP and seven more tabs, all reachable from the keyboard. [The panel](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md) 7. Cost and cached tokens in dsh's footer, with a spend line that turns the pill orange. [Cost pill](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#cost-pill) 8. Plan usage (5-hour, weekly, extra usage) in dsh's context ring, which turns amber near a limit and red at one, with a notice above the composer. Only limits the session's model counts against, graded by Anthropic, so a new model needs no update. [Plan usage](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#plan-usage) 9. Restore or import any past Claude transcript, from dsh or from a terminal, and search inside them for what was said. [Session browser](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#session-browser) 10. Claude's slash commands and skills show up in dsh's slash menu under their own names, as `/claude-` where dsh already uses the name. A skill dsh also serves runs on any model, and so does one only Claude Code has: typed in a session on another model, it goes to that model with its instructions (switch it off in Settings). [Command bridge](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#command-bridge) 11. Claude gets dsh's subagents, jobs, goals and web search over MCP. [dsh tools over MCP](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#dsh-tools-over-mcp) 12. Edit CLAUDE.md, settings.json and MCP servers from the panel, on this box or a remote one, and sign in to an MCP server that needs it. [Instructions](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#instructions), [settings.json editor](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#settingsjson-editor), [MCP](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#mcp) 13. Run Claude on another box over SSH, or mount several accounts. [Remote boxes and accounts](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/remote.md) 14. Report a problem with a redacted box report, copied or filed as an issue. [Report a problem](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#report-a-problem) 15. All the orange is a switch, per group, any colour. [Claude look](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#claude-look) 16. Pick what dsh adds to your prompts, with the size of each block on the label. [dsh context](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#dsh-context) 17. A card offers each new Claude Code release for the box a session runs on, and installs it from dsh; a headless `claude -p` never updates itself. Channel, auto-install and history per box sit under the switch in Settings. [Claude Code updates](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#surviving-claude-code-updates) 18. What the last five versions changed, read from the plugin's own changelog, in Settings. [Changelog](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#changelog) 19. Every skill the CLI can reach, grouped by scope, with add, edit and remove for your own and the project's. What each costs, from the CLI's own `/skill-doctor`, is a table you can sort, beside what else drives your usage: the MCP servers behind the most requests, and how the work was shaped. [Skills](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#skills) 20. A mark on the browser tab and an optional desktop notice when a session you are not looking at finishes, or stops to ask you something. [Session notices](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#session-notices) 21. dsh's own goal and every earlier goal of the session, beside Claude Code's goal and its scheduled tasks. [Tasks](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#tasks) 22. Edit or remove a message you steered in while Claude works, or all of them as one, until Claude reads it. A file or image on the message stays on it; only the text changes. Nothing goes out while you edit. Send now stops Claude and sends one as the next turn. [Steering](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#dsh-tools-over-mcp) 23. Claude's working line (spinner, verb, figures) repeats above the composer once you scroll up past it, so reading back through a long turn never hides what Claude is doing. A switch in Settings turns it off. [Turn status](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#turn-status) 24. Select text in a reply and dsh's popover (dsh 0.2.2) shows Ask beside its Quote text, or on a phone a row above the composer does: ask Claude about the passage as a side question that leaves the conversation alone; ask with the question blank and Claude explains the passage. [Asides](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#asides) 25. A finished turn keeps a closing line where the working verb was, the way the terminal ends one: `✻ Crunched for 27s · done 3:21 AM`. A turn you stopped reads `Interrupted · What should Claude do instead?`. [Turn status](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#turn-status) 26. On dsh 0.1.7, Claude's tool calls show as dsh's own tool cards, the way every other provider's do, with the text streaming between them. Inline text is a switch away in Settings. [Tool rows](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) 27. A new session in a workspace opens on the Claude box, model and effort that workspace last ran, and a workspace with nothing remembered opens on a default model and effort you pick. [Remember model per workspace](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#remember-model-per-workspace) 28. After each reply, Claude's guess at your next prompt shows above the composer: Use writes it into the box, Send sends it as it is, and it folds away while you type something else. On by default, as in the terminal; a switch in Settings turns it off. [Suggested next prompt](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#suggested-next-prompt) 29. Claude's background shell tasks and subagents are listed on the Tasks tab while they run, each with Stop and, for a shell task, Output, plus Stop all once two or more run. A shell task that ended keeps its row and its Output for the last ten; the subagents a session already ran sit under Earlier subagents, each openable as Markdown. A subagent's row in the chat names each step as the CLI reports it. [Tasks](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#tasks) 30. If an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in dsh's environment is what Claude Code bills instead of your login, the session says so in one line at its start. [Where things live](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#where-things-live) 31. Each plan window says where it is heading at the current rate: the percent it ends at, or when the cap lands. [Plan usage](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#plan-usage) 32. Once the context window is 75% full (adjustable in Settings), a card above the composer says so and offers Compact, which sends Claude's own `/compact`. [Context nudge](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#context-nudge) 33. A Run button on every shell snippet Claude writes puts it in the composer as a prompt; Enter sends it, and it runs through Claude's Bash tool and dsh's approval. [Run a snippet](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/panel.md#run-a-snippet) 34. A session renamed in dsh keeps that name in `claude --resume`, and a name set on the Claude side renames the dsh session. [How it works](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md) 35. Switch a session between Claude and another model, such as DeepSeek or a local one, and back: Claude sees the prompts, replies and tool use the other model had in between. [Sessions](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md#sessions) 36. Up in an empty composer brings back your last prompt, Up again older ones, Down newer ones and back to empty, as in the Claude Code terminal; typing a character ends the walk. A new session recalls from the workspace's latest transcript. Switch it off under Settings ("Prompt recall"). 37. Ctrl+R in the composer searches the prompts typed before: this session, the workspace or everywhere on the box (Ctrl+S or Ctrl+Up/Down cycles). Enter sends the row, Tab writes it into the composer, Esc closes. Switch it off under Settings ("History search"). 38. Esc Esc in an empty composer while nothing runs opens the Rewind tab on the latest prompt, as the terminal's double Escape opens /rewind; after the rewind that prompt is back in the composer to edit and resend. Switch it off under Settings ("Edit last prompt"). The three composer gestures are listed in dsh's Keyboard shortcuts dialog too. Defaults you never have to touch, such as secret redaction in tool results and surviving the CLI's own updates, are on [How it works](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md). ## Configure Settings come in two kinds. The switches under Settings → Oh My Claude and in the panel's Tune tab apply at once and are kept on the box, so every browser sees the same ones. The keys below are install-time: they go as `config:` on the bundle row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and take effect when dsh next loads the plugin, which a dsh restart does. dsh's own Plugins page lists the plugin with an on/off switch but has no form for these keys. Three keys people change first: ```yaml permissionMode: dsh # follow the session's shield (default), or pin one of the CLI's six modes # spawn: node # unset: the Settings switch below decides; node or dsh here wins sshHost: "" # "[user@]host" drives a claude on another machine over ssh ``` Every key, with its default, is in [docs/configuration.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/configuration.md). ### Keep Claude running across dsh restarts This switch under Settings → Oh My Claude picks how Claude Code is started, and it is on unless you turn it off. `spawn: node` or `spawn: dsh` in the config overrides it and locks the switch; `spawn: keeper` leaves it free. A flip reaches each session on its next turn. | | On (`keeper`) | Off (`dsh`) | `node` (config only) | |---|---|---|---| | A turn running when dsh restarts | Keeps running; the new dsh reattaches and shows what it did | Ends; about ten seconds after the restart the session gets a "dsh restarted while this turn was in progress" prompt and carries on | Same as off | | Left running after dsh exits | Claude, until it has gone `processIdleMs` (30 min, never under 5 min) with no dsh attached and no output | Nothing after a normal shutdown: dsh ends Claude and everything it started | Claude ends when dsh does; what it started is not tracked | | dsh's environment | Passed whole | Passed whole except `DSH_*` names: dsh's seam drops names with KEY, TOKEN, SECRET or PASSWORD, and the plugin passes them back | Passed whole | | SSH boxes and remote workspaces | The far `claude` is held on the box and survives too; the idle limit above does not reach it, so it runs until a dsh reattaches or the box restarts | The far `claude` ends with the ssh connection | Same as off | | Platforms | Linux and macOS; Windows runs `node` | All; `node` when dsh mounts no subprocess seam | All | DSH Web and DSH Desktop run separate dsh profiles, so each reattaches only to the Claude processes it started. Two dsh started on the same profile directory still share them. ## Remote boxes and accounts Mount the plugin twice with different `configDir` values for two logins. List other boxes running dsh and this plugin under Settings → Oh My Claude → Boxes and jump between them. Or give a box a name and `user@host` and drive the `claude` there over SSH, with nothing on the far side but the CLI; Tailscale and WireGuard peers appear as hosts to pick from. All of it is on [docs/remote.md](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/blob/main/docs/remote.md). ## What it touches - **Runs** the `claude` binary you already have, on this box or on one you add over SSH. - **Reads** Claude Code's login (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, on macOS the `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain entry when that file has no live token, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when set) to fetch the model list and your plan usage. That token goes only to `api.anthropic.com`. - **Writes** its own state under `~/.local/state/dsh-oh-my-claude/`; login tokens for SSH boxes are files only you can read. CLAUDE.md, settings.json and MCP servers change only when you edit them from the panel. - **Listens** on a Unix socket for the keeper that holds Claude across a dsh restart. Its HTTP routes live inside dsh's own server, so on DSH Web it opens no TCP port. Under DSH Desktop, whose web server answers 403 to anything but its own window, the bridge that hands dsh's tools to Claude also listens on 127.0.0.1, behind the same key. - **Calls out** to `api.anthropic.com` (models, plan usage), `status.anthropic.com`, `downloads.claude.ai` (the CLI's release pointer), `registry.npmjs.org` (plugin update check) and `api.github.com` (the repo's star count). SSH goes only to boxes you add. ## Not covered - dsh's shell and file tools are not proxied (except `bash` for background jobs); Claude Code uses its own, under its own permission mode. - Claude Code sessions are not deleted when dsh sessions are. ## Bugs and feedback Found a bug, or something that reads wrong? Open an issue at [github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/issues](https://github.com/lcestou/dsh-oh-my-claude/issues) with the dsh and Claude Code versions (`dsh --version`, `claude --version`) and what you expected to see. Settings → Oh My Claude → Report a problem writes that report for you. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Claude, Claude Code and the Claude spark mark are trademarks of Anthropic, PBC. This project is an independent dsh plugin that drives the Claude Code CLI you already have; it is not made, endorsed or supported by Anthropic. The spark is drawn here only to say which sessions and controls belong to Claude Code, in the way the CLI itself draws it.

# dsh-web-search-pro [![CI](https://github.com/leiming2333/dsh-web-search-pro/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/leiming2333/dsh-web-search-pro/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) 给 DeepSeek Harness 装一套联网搜索：模型可以调用搜索引擎查当前信息，也可以打开搜索结果里的网页读正文。 装好就能用，不需要任何 API Key。默认同时查询 DuckDuckGo、Bing 网页、百度、360 搜索四家，再合并去重：单看一家的排序只是一种意见，而四家分歧最大的，恰好就是值得搜的那些查询。愿意配一家搜索 API 的话，可以单独选它，结果更稳更快。 它还能**接管内置的 `web_search`**：DSH 自带的 `web_search` 走 DeepSeek Messages 搜索，一次搜索是一次完整的模型请求，按生成计费。设置页里有一个开关，关掉官方路由后，同一个工具改由上面这些免密钥引擎提供结果——工具名、提示词、调用方式都不变，只是账单不再增长。**默认保持 DSH 原样（不接管）**，要不要省钱由你决定，详见[官方 Web 搜索开关](#官方-web-搜索开关)。 换引擎、填密钥、调条数、开关都在 **设置 → 网络搜索** 里，保存后下一条消息生效，不用重启。设置页还有一个**测试连接**按钮，用已保存的配置跑一次真实查询。 --- ## 它给模型什么 | 工具 | 作用 | |---|---| | `web_search_api` | 一次搜索，返回排序后的来源列表（标题、URL、摘要、发布时间）。默认走全部引擎聚合；支持临时指定 `provider`、`language`、`maxResults`，不写入设置。 | | `web_fetch_api` | 把一个 URL 读成纯文本（去掉标签、脚本和样式），用于打开搜索命中的网页。设置页有开关可以关掉它。 | 两个工具出错时都会说清下一步：抓取型被反爬会建议换引擎或配 API Key，解析不到结果会说明可能是引擎改了页面结构，401/403 提示密钥无效，429 提示限流或额度用尽，超时提示调大超时，而不是只抛一个状态码。 ## 支持的引擎 ### 免密钥（开箱即用） | `provider` | 引擎 | 怎么拿结果 | |---|---|---| | `all` | **全部引擎**（默认） | 四个一起查，轮转合并 + 按 URL 去重 | | `duckduckgo` | DuckDuckGo | 读 `html.duckduckgo.com` 结果页，`uddg` 参数还原真实链接 | | `bingweb` | Bing 网页 | 读 `bing.com/search` 结果页，`ck/a` 跳转里的 base64 还原真实链接 | | `baidu` | 百度 | 读 `baidu.com/s` 结果页，容器的 `mu` 属性取真实链接，过滤推广位 | | `so360` | 360 搜索 | 读 `so.com/s` 结果页，`data-mdurl` 取真实链接，过滤广告位 | | `searxng` | SearXNG（自建） | 调用实例的 `format=json` 接口，**必须填服务地址**；配了地址后也会加入 `all` | `provider` 默认 `all`。 ### `all` 是怎么合并的 ``` query ├─ DuckDuckGo ─┐ ├─ Bing 网页 ─┤ 并发，各自取 max(count,6) 条 ├─ 百度 ─┤ └─ 360 ─┘ ↓ 轮转交错（每个引擎轮流贡献一条） ↓ URL 去重（忽略 utm_* / spm / fbclid 等跟踪参数、末尾斜杠、#fragment） ↓ 截断到 maxResults ``` 几个刻意的选择： - **轮转，不拼接**。直接首尾相接的话，谁先返回、谁返回得多，谁就霸占列表前面。轮转让每家的最佳结果都进前几位。 - **去重保留先访问到的那一份**。四个引擎返回的热门页面大量重合，不去重的话列表会被同一批链接占满。 - **用 `allSettled`，不用 `all`**。一家被限流或改版是常态，不能让它拖垮整次搜索。成功的照常合并，失败的按引擎报告原因。 - **部分失败会写进结果**。工具输出里有 `来源：DuckDuckGo 8 · Bing 网页 8 · 百度 8` 和 `未返回：360 搜索（…）`，模型知道哪家没答，而不是以为结果本来就少。 一次实测（查「DeepSeek Harness 怎么安装」，`maxResults: 8`）： ``` 耗时 2685 ms · 合并后 8 条 引擎分布: DuckDuckGo 8 · Bing 网页 8 · 百度 8 · 360 搜索(失败) ``` 耗时接近最慢的那家，因为四家是并发查的。返回的 8 条覆盖了 runoob、CSDN、知乎、deepseek.com 等不同来源，单用一家通常拿不到这么分散。 ### 需要 API Key | `provider` | 服务 | 密钥申请 | 备注 | |---|---|---|---| | `tavily` | Tavily | https://app.tavily.com/home | 返回网页正文，可带生成式摘要 | | `serper` | Serper（Google 结果） | https://serper.dev/api-key | 结果最接近 Google，可带 answerBox | | `brave` | Brave Search | https://api.search.brave.com/app/keys | 独立索引 | | `exa` | Exa | https://dashboard.exa.ai/api-keys | 语义搜索，直接返回正文片段 | | `bing` | Bing Web Search API | https://portal.azure.com/ | 在 Azure 里创建 Bing Search 资源 | 加一家新的：在 `index.js` 的 `PROVIDERS` 加一条描述，在 `SEARCHERS` 加一个把该家响应映射成 `{ answer?, sources[] }` 的函数。去重、截断、错误文案、渲染都是共享的。 ## 关于「抓取型」引擎 免密钥引擎没有官方接口，插件读的是它们**公开的结果页**，和用浏览器打开那个页面看到的一样。这意味着： - **不用注册、不用付费、不会被额度卡住**，开箱即用。 - **页面结构属于引擎**。它们改版、加反爬，或者对自动化请求返回验证页时，解析就会失败。失败时工具会明确报告「没有解析出结果」或「被拒绝访问」，并建议换引擎，而不是假装「没有搜索结果」。 - 抓取时带上桌面浏览器的 User-Agent 和 `Accept-Language`，因为用插件自己的标识去请求会被直接挡掉；API 请求仍然如实标注身份。 - 向引擎要的结果数比实际需要的多（`count × 3`，至少 12 条），因为结果页里混着答案卡片、图片卡、推广位，能放进来源的通常不到一半。 实测这几个引擎在你当前网络下都可用（DuckDuckGo 约 2s，其余 0.4–1.5s）。**试过但没能用的**：Mojeek（直接返回验证码页）、搜狗（返回反爬验证页）、Ecosia（403 防火墙）、Brave 网页版（429）。这些没放进插件，免得选了就用不了。 有一个例外要说清楚：**360 搜索对密集请求很敏感**。正常使用（几分钟一次）没问题，但短时间内连续搜十几次会开始返回「访问异常页面」。这是 HTTP 200 的拦截页，不是搜索结果。插件会认出它并报「返回了验证/拦截页面，通常是请求过多」，而不是含糊地说「解析失败」。聚合模式下它挂了不影响其他三个，结果里会写 `未返回：360 搜索（…）`。 需要稳定、可预期的结果时（比如每天固定跑几十次查询），还是建议配一家 API。 ## 安装 仓库根目录就是插件包本身（`package.json` 里有 `dsh.bundle.patch` 与 `dsh.client`）；`_dev/` 只有开发与测试脚本，不会被装进 profile。 ```bash git clone https://github.com/leiming2333/dsh-web-search-pro.git cd dsh-web-search-pro node _dev/install.mjs --dry-run # 先看要改什么 node _dev/install.mjs # 备份后写入 desktop profile node _dev/install.mjs --profile web # 换一个 profile node _dev/install.mjs --uninstall # 回滚 ``` 脚本只做三件可回滚的事：把包复制到 `/plugins/` 与 `/node_modules/`，在 profile 的 `package.json` 里补 `dependencies`（`file:` 本地引用）与 `dsh.profile.bundles`，改写前备份为 `package.json.bak-<时间戳>`。它**不碰** `cordis.patch.yml`，那是你自己的层。 也可以在对话里让 DSH 自己装：「把 /path/to/dsh-web-search-pro 这个 bundle 装上」，它会用 `plugin_manager` 的 `install_bundle`。 装完要**重启 DeepSeek Harness**：宿主半身是 Node 模块，新包不会热加载；浏览器半身随页面刷新加载。 > **默认不改你现有的搜索选择。** 第一次启动只注册两个新工具（`web_search_api`、`web_fetch_api`）和一个设置页，内置 `web_search` 仍走你原来的提供方。想让它免费，去 **设置 → 网络搜索** 把「使用 DeepSeek 官方网页搜索」关掉——见下一节。 > 两者的加载时机不同，容易误导人：刷新页面就能让 **设置 → 网络搜索** 出现，但那条 `/api/web-search-pro/settings` 请求需要宿主进程里跑着插件。如果设置页出现了却报 `HTTP 404`，就是宿主没重启（要完全退出应用再启动，不是刷新页面）。重启后 `~/.dsh/web-search-pro/host-status.json` 会记录挂载到哪一步。 ## 官方 Web 搜索开关 DSH 原生有两个 web 工具：`web_search` 和 `web_fetch`。它们本身不含引擎，真正的检索由 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web` 选中的**搜索提供方**完成，而内置组合把选择固定成了： ```yaml - id: web name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-web' config: searchProvider: deepseek-official # DeepSeek Messages 搜索 fetchProvider: http # 本地 HTTP 抓取，免费 ``` `deepseek-official`（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-search-deepseek`）的做法是把搜索当成一次辅助模型请求：DeepSeek 在**完整的一轮 Messages 调用**里执行服务端检索，所以每次 `web_search` 都是延迟加生成 token。它不会报错，也不会提示你贵，只是账单会变。 插件在 `web` 服务里注册了自己的提供方 `web-search-pro`，设置页的**使用 DeepSeek 官方网页搜索**开关就是切这个选择： | 开关 | `web.searchProvider` | `web_search` 谁在答 | 费用 | |---|---|---|---| | **开（默认）** | `deepseek-official` | DeepSeek Messages 搜索 | 按模型轮次计费 | | 关 | `web-search-pro` | 本插件的免密钥引擎（与 `web_search_api` 同一套） | 免费 | 几个刻意的选择： - **默认开，是刻意的。** 装一个搜索插件就改掉别人 DSH 的搜索后端，不合适；默认保持 DSH 原样，谁想省钱谁自己关。关掉之后写进的是你的 profile，重启也还在。 - **不卸载官方 provider，只切选择。** 早期实现用 `- id: web-search-deepseek` + `disabled: true` 关掉它，结果内置的 **插件 → 网页搜索** 卡片整页消失——那个页面绑在提供方的命名空间上。现在 provider 一直挂着，卡片一直在。 - **写入走 `ctx.settings`，不直接改文件。** 那就是内置卡片自己的写入路径：同样校验 volatile 字段、同样带修订号拒绝陈旧写入、同样落到 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`。所以拖到卡片里手动改也认，两边看到的是同一个值。 - **不抢别人的选择。** 如果 DSH 选中的既不是 `deepseek-official` 也不是 `web-search-pro`（比如你在卡片里切到了新版 Search API），开关只报告 `foreign` 并保持不动——静默改写用户明确选过的提供方，比什么都不做更糟。 - **先挂后指、先指后卸。** 关官方时先注册自己的 provider 再把选择指过去，开官方时先把选择指回官方再注销自己：选择永远不指向一个不存在的提供方。 没有 `web` 或 `settings` 服务的组合里开关自动失效（`host-status.json` 会写明是哪一种），工具照常可用。 ## 配置 设置页里的每一项都存在 `/web-search-pro/settings.json`（默认 `~/.dsh/web-search-pro/settings.json`），改完即时生效，不用重启。 | 字段 | 默认 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `provider` | `all` | 用哪个引擎；默认全部聚合。 | | `apiKey` | 空 | 密钥。免密钥引擎与自建 SearXNG 留空即可。 | | `endpoint` | 空 | 自定义地址；留空用官方地址。SearXNG 必填。 | | `maxResults` | `8` | 每次结果条数（1–50，另受各家上限约束）。 | | `timeoutMs` | `20000` | 单次请求超时（1000–120000）。 | | `language` | 空 | 语言提示，如 `zh-CN`。 | | `includeAnswer` | `true` | 是否请求生成式摘要。传给 Tavily；Serper 的 answerBox 本来就随结果返回。 | | `enableFetch` | `true` | 是否注册 `web_fetch_api`。 | | `officialSearch` | `true` | 是否让内置 `web_search` 走 DeepSeek 官方搜索（计费）。`false` 表示由本插件的提供方作答。 | | `fetchMaxChars` | `20000` | 单页保留字符数（1000–200000）。 | 所有值在写入前都会做类型与范围归一化，手改 JSON 也不会把插件带进非法状态。 ## 验证 设置页底部有「测试连接」：用已保存的配置真跑一次搜索，显示提供方、结果条数、耗时和前三条来源；失败就把提供方返回的原因原样显示出来。 也可以回到对话说一句「搜索一下今天的科技新闻」。 ## 架构（以及为什么这么写） ``` ┌─ Host: index.js（零外部依赖，只用 node:fs/os/path）──────┐ │ settings.json ← 原子写入 │ │ ↓ │ │ web_search_api ─→ runSearch ─→ SEARCHERS[id] │ │ web_fetch_api ─→ runFetch ─→ htmlToText │ │ │ │ ctx.inject(['webServer'], …) │ │ └─ /api/web-search-pro/{settings,test} │ └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘ │ 同源 JSON ┌──────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┐ │ Client: client.js（只 require('react')） │ │ ctx.slots.register('settings.section', …) │ │ 设置 → 网络搜索（读 /settings，写 /settings，/test） │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **接管官方工具走的是两个服务，不是两个 import。** `ctx.web.registerSearchProvider({ id, available, ready, search })`（可选注入，disposer 随 fiber 释放）注册免密钥提供方；`ctx.settings.mutate('web', [{ op: 'set', path: ['searchProvider'], value }], revision)`（可选注入）切换选择。两者都是通过 `ctx` 拿到的服务，符合下面那条零依赖规则；缺任何一个，插件照常提供 `web_search_api`，只是开关失效并在 `host-status.json` 里说明。 **关键决定：这个插件不 import 任何 `@deepseek-ai/*` 包。** 这不是风格选择，是加载机制决定的。DSH 加载 profile 里的 bundle 时用「双锚点」解析名字（先 dsh 安装目录，再 profile 目录），但 **bundle 内部的 `import` 由 Node 自己从 bundle 所在位置向上找 `node_modules`**。从 `~/.dsh/profiles/

/node_modules/…` 出发，DSH 安装目录里的包不在解析链上： ```bash cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop node --input-type=module -e "console.log(import.meta.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'))" # ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND ``` 所以 `import { defineTool } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'` 会在加载期抛错，整个插件根本挂不上。本机那个第三方插件 `dsh-our-free-model` 也是同样的零依赖写法。 由此带来的两个替代： - `defineTool` 是对普通对象字面量的校验/包装。`localDefineTool` 复刻了这份契约：参数 DSL → 对象根 JSON Schema、必填与类型在执行前校验、`output.render` 负责呈现。注册表本身只把它当普通对象读。 - 配置不走 `settings`/`configForms` 那套 schema 投影（那需要 schemastery 的 `dict`/`meta` 结构），改由插件自己的 JSON 文件 + `/api/*` 路由承担。代价是密钥存在自己的状态文件里（见下），收益是设置页能真正做到「测试连接」这种需要在 Host 侧发网络请求的操作。 其他约束： - 不 `require('@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives')`（同样解析不到，且规范也禁止）。控件全部自己画，只用 `--dsw-alias-*` 主题变量并带 fallback，亮/暗主题都跟着宿主走。 - `web_fetch_api` 用 `when` 按模型步骤动态准入，而不是在 `apply` 时决定；否则关掉开关要重启才生效。 - 设置接口做同源校验（`Origin` 与 `Host` 比对），防止第三方页面改写「密钥发往哪个地址」。 ## 安全说明 - **密钥明文保存在 `~/.dsh/web-search-pro/settings.json`**，权限跟随用户目录。没有走 DSH 的 credentials 保管库：那个域只回答「是否存在」，而设置页需要回显掩码预览；更重要的是 credentials 服务不在零依赖可达范围内。密钥**不会**通过 `/api/settings` 回传给浏览器，页面只拿到 `hasApiKey` 和 `abcd…wxyz` 形式的掩码。 - 清除密钥只能显式点「清除密钥」；输入框留空表示保持原值，避免误清。 - `web_fetch_api` 只允许 `http`/`https`，跟随重定向，非 2xx 作为结果返回（附状态码），不执行页面脚本。 - 所有请求都由本地 Host 发起，浏览器不直连搜索 API，所以没有 CORS 问题，密钥也不出现在页面里。 ## 排错 | 现象 | 原因 / 处理 | |---|---| | 内置「插件 → 网页搜索」卡片不见了 | 有人给 `web-search-deepseek` 这一行写了 `disabled: true`。别那样关官方搜索：那个页面绑在这个提供方的命名空间上，行一卸载整页就没了。改用本插件的开关（`officialSearch`），它只切 `web.searchProvider`，provider 一直挂着。 | | 拨了开关，但「DSH 当前选中」没变 | 两种可能：选中值不是官方也不是本插件（`foreign`，按设计不抢）；或宿主没有 `web`/`settings` 服务，`host-status.json` 里的 `officialSearch`、`webSearchProvider` 字段会写明是哪一种。 | | 设置页里没有「网络搜索」这一栏 | 浏览器半身没加载。确认 profile `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 含 `dsh-web-search-pro`，重启并刷新页面。 | | 设置页显示「读取设置失败」 | 宿主没挂 `/api/web-search-pro`。先看 DSH 日志里以 `web-search-pro:` 开头的行，或 `~/.dsh/web-search-pro/host-status.json`（也可以跑 `node _dev/diagnose.mjs`），确认宿主半身跑到了哪一步；常见原因是 Web 服务未启动（该组合下工具仍可用，只是没有设置页）。 | | 工具报「未知的搜索提供方」 | `provider` 写了不支持的值，改成错误信息里列出的 id。 | | 401 / 403 | 密钥无效，或该密钥没有这个接口的权限。 | | 429 | 额度用尽，或被限流。 | | 一直超时 | 检查 `endpoint`；国内直连 Tavily/Brave 可能需要代理，可以把 `endpoint` 指向自己的转发地址。 | | 日志里出现 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` | 有人在插件里加了 `@deepseek-ai/*` 的 import，见上面的架构说明。 | ## 测试 ```bash node _dev/run-tests.mjs ``` 94 项检查，不需要任何桩包，因为插件本来就没有外部依赖： - **Host（68）**：清单与 patch 结构、只 import node 内置、两个工具的声明与准入、`localDefineTool` 的校验、五家 API 与四个抓取引擎的响应解析（含去重/截断/单次覆盖/跳转还原/推广位过滤/实体解码）、**聚合的轮转合并与 URL 去重、部分失败与全失败**、错误文案分级、HTML→文本、渲染输出、设置的归一化/原子读写/损坏降级、密钥掩码与不回传、挂载自诊断、**官方/免费接管（提供方注册、`settings.mutate` 的目标值与修订号、`foreign` 不抢、开关往返）**，以及 `/api` 的读写/测试/同源拒绝/坏 JSON/前缀剥离。 - **Client（26）**：字典键一致性、`settings.section` 注册、引擎分组、loading/error/ready 三态渲染、404 时的重启指引与手动配置兜底、免密钥引擎下密钥字段自动禁用、密钥徽标与清除按钮、脏检查与按钮启用、测试结果展示，以及 `pick`/`submitted`/`changesBetween`/`callApi`。 ## 文件 ``` dsh-web-search-pro/ # 仓库根目录就是这个包 ├── package.json # bundle 清单 + dsh.client 声明 ├── cordis.patch.yml # 插入 web-search-pro 这一行 ├── index.js # Host：设置存取、两个工具、provider 适配、官方/免费接管、HTTP API ├── client.js # Client：设置 → 网络搜索 ├── locale/{en,zh}.json # 插件清单里的标题与描述 ├── icon.svg # 原创图标 ├── LICENSE # MIT ├── CHANGELOG.md # 版本变更 ├── README.md # 本文件 ├── README.en.md # 英文说明 └── _dev/ # 开发与测试，不进 profile、不进 npm 包 ├── install.mjs # 安装 / 卸载 / 预演 ├── run-tests.mjs # 跑两个套件 ├── live-check.mjs # 对真实网络验证四个免密钥引擎 ├── diagnose.mjs # 诊断设置页为什么读不到数据 ├── smoke.mjs # Host 套件 └── client-smoke.mjs # 浏览器套件 ```

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-history-keeper

**Your DeepSeek Harness history comes back — and you can prove it.**

*Español: [README-es.md](README-es.md)*

> **Status: pre-alpha (0.1.0 in progress).** The engine works: `snapshot`, `verify` and
> `restore` run on real DSH logs, validated byte for byte on 8 sessions. Host plugin
> integration and live sync are the next milestones.

## The problem

Your conversations live in one place: `~/.dsh/sessions` on a single machine. If that
machine dies, they die with it. There is no copy of *why* it happened — and no way to
prove the copy you do have is intact.

`dsh-history-keeper` exists to fix that: capture the history, encrypt it, verify it, and
restore it — byte for byte.

That includes the **attachments**: a pasted image or file lives outside the session log, in
`~/.dsh/attachments`. When a captured session references one, the blob is captured with it,
verified against the hash its name claims, and restored next to the conversation. A history
without the images you pasted is an incomplete history.

## What it will do

| Milestone | Delivers |
|---|---|
| **0.1** | `snapshot`, `verify` and `restore` from a shared folder, with the CLI working without DSH running |
| **1.0** | live sync between machines, per-device manifests, explicit conflict handling, device pairing and revocation |

## Try it now (from a checkout)

The CLI needs nothing but Node — no DSH, no git, no external binaries.

```sh
export KEEPER_PASSPHRASE='a passphrase of at least 8 characters'

node bin/keeper.js init     --store ./vault
node bin/keeper.js snapshot --store ./vault --home ~/.dsh
node bin/keeper.js verify   --store ./vault
node bin/keeper.js restore  --store ./vault --home /tmp/restored-home
```

`restore` reproduces the host's own layout under `sessions/`, verifies every hash, and
never overwrites an existing log.

## Use it inside DSH

Install the bundle, then run `/keeper init` once in any conversation. That is the whole
setup: it creates the vault (default `~/.dsh/history-keeper`), generates a passphrase when
you have not chosen one, and writes it to `~/.dsh/history-keeper.key`.

No profile patch is required. The YAML below exists only to override the defaults:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: history-keeper
      name: dsh-history-keeper
      config:
        store: C:\Users\you\keeper-vault         # default: ~/.dsh/history-keeper
        sessionsRoot: C:\Users\you\.dsh\sessions # default: ~/.dsh/sessions
        autoSnapshotOnFlush: true                # capture after each closed turn
        debounceMs: 2000                         # settle time before a capture runs
        snapshotMinIntervalMs: 30000             # coalesce a burst of turns (0 disables)
        maxChunkBytes: 1048576                   # target chunk size; frames are never split
        secretScan: true                         # quarantine a session that looks like it holds a credential
        secretScanAllow: []                      # rule ids to ignore, e.g. [openai-key]
        secretScanEntropy: false                 # long high-entropy runs (noisy; off by default)
        captureAttachments: true                 # capture the blobs sessions reference
        autoCompact: true                        # checkpoint the chain when the policy approves
        compactMinManifests: 50                  # manifests since the last checkpoint before it acts
        keyFile: C:\Users\you\.dsh\history-keeper.key
        passphraseFile: null                     # wins over the key file and the env var
        passphraseEnv: KEEPER_PASSPHRASE
        deviceName: my-laptop
```

The passphrase is never written into the patch: it comes from `passphraseFile`, the key file
that `init` creates, or `KEEPER_PASSPHRASE`. Then, in a conversation:

```text
/keeper init       create the vault (generates a passphrase when none is configured)
/keeper status     what the vault holds, what is pending, what this machine is missing
/keeper snapshot   capture new session bytes now
/keeper verify     check every object, hash and chain
/keeper help
```

`restore` is deliberately **not** available from inside DSH: it writes the live session
store, and a running host would not notice. It stays a CLI operation, with DSH closed —
that is the whole point of a recovery tool.

### The secret gate

A capture never publishes a session whose new bytes look like a credential. The gate
**quarantines** instead of redacting, because rewriting bytes would break the byte-for-byte
promise: nothing is written for that session, and `/keeper snapshot` reports the rule and the
line — never the value. Publish anyway with `--force`, or silence one rule with
`--allow-rule <id>`.

It catches structured secrets (API keys, tokens, key assignments, private key blocks). A
password written in prose is **not** detectable by pattern: the gate is a safety net, not a
guarantee.

### Minimal setup

Every key is optional. With no `config` at all, the plugin looks for a store at
`~/.dsh/history-keeper`, reads sessions from `~/.dsh/sessions`, and tells you how to
create the store when it is missing.

Timestamps are stored in UTC (an instant must be unambiguous across machines) and
rendered in your local time zone next to the offset.

## Roadmap

The plan to 1.0 and to the vault as a standard product lives in
[docs/ROADMAP-1.0.md](docs/ROADMAP-1.0.md): six phases, a definition of done, and what is
explicitly out of scope. The format itself is the contract in [docs/SPEC-vault.md](docs/SPEC-vault.md).

## Design principles

1. **No external binaries.** `node:` only — no `git`, no `age`, nothing to install.
2. **Fail closed.** No key, no sync. A conflict never writes. Encryption never degrades to plaintext.
3. **Never overwrite, never delete.** Restore only creates; anything that already exists and differs is set aside.
4. **Append-only and verifiable.** Every object is immutable and named by content; the chunk chain lets anyone audit integrity, even without the key.
5. **Copies per device, never a shared mutable file.**
6. **The transport is dumb.** A folder (or any provider) only moves blobs: it never parses, orders or merges.
7. **Auditable by you.** `verify` and a readable report — you do not have to trust us.

## Privacy

History is encrypted before it leaves the machine, and metadata is encrypted too: file
names and sizes do not reveal which projects you work on. Without the key, the store is
opaque. There is no server and no account.

## Install

Not published yet. When 0.1 ships:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-history-keeper
```

## Compatibility

Developed against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`. The bundle declares
`engines.dsh` so an incompatible host refuses it instead of misbehaving.

## Development

```sh
node --test "test/*.test.mjs"   # unit tests, no dependencies to install
npm run guard                   # refuses committed session logs
```

Moving your history to another machine today, without sync:
[`docs/TRANSFER.md`](docs/TRANSFER.md).
Design notes and roadmap: [`docs/`](docs/). Release history, including versions that were
never published and why: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## Licensing

This repository uses a split licensing model:

- **Source code** (`bin/`, `lib/`, `scripts/`, `test/`, `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`): licensed under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**. See [`LICENSE-CODE`](LICENSE-CODE).
- **Documentation** (`README.md`, `README-es.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/`): licensed under **CC BY-NC 4.0**. See [`LICENSE-DOCS`](LICENSE-DOCS).

Commercial use of the source code is not permitted without explicit permission from the author.

### License history

Versions `0.1.0-rc.1` through `0.1.0-rc.7` were published under **MIT** and remain available
under MIT for whoever obtained them. The split model above applies from `0.1.0-rc.9` onward;
`0.1.0-rc.8` was published with MIT metadata by mistake and is deprecated. There are no forks
of this project as of 2026-10-24. Full timeline, fork status and contribution terms:
[`LICENSING-HISTORY.md`](LICENSING-HISTORY.md).

---

## The contract

The vault format is specified in [`docs/SPEC-vault.md`](docs/SPEC-vault.md) and enforced by
`npm run conformance` against a committed reference vault: any implementation —a policy package, a
fork, a rewrite— that passes it can read the same vault. What may differ between products is the
*philosophy* ([`docs/PHILOSOPHIES.md`](docs/PHILOSOPHIES.md)): which lineage is visible, when the
vault travels, what is retained. The one this version ships is the conservative philosophy
([`docs/adr/0001-filosofia-conservadora.md`](docs/adr/0001-filosofia-conservadora.md)).
## What it covers

The situations the plugin covers today, by role and with the gaps named: [docs/CASES.md](docs/CASES.md).

# dsh-plugin-moss-tts

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · Version **0.1.1** · Apache-2.0 · [Engine repo](https://github.com/litterbit/dsh-moss-tts)

Local text-to-speech for DeepSeek Harness, powered by the MOSS-TTS-Nano-100M C++ CPU engine.
Everything is synthesized on this machine; text never leaves it, and the weights are installed
once and shared with the CLI and the web playground.

![Settings → Moss Speech](assets/screenshot-settings.png)

```
Harness assistant reply ──► auto-read / per-message read button
                                 │
                     POST /moss-tts/stream (same origin, no CORS)
                                 │
        host plugin: engine lifecycle + verified download + paced proxy
                                 │  stdin/stdout JSON
                 moss_tts.exe --stdio (resident, weights loaded once)
                                 │
            browser AudioWorklet ring buffer ──► speakers
```

## Requirements

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek Harness | 0.2.1-rc or newer (client slot contract) |
| OS | Windows x64 (the engine ships for that platform only) |
| Disk | ~170 MB (engine + weights), installed once |

## Install

**Desktop app**: sidebar **Plugins** → **Add plugin** → paste

```
github:litterbit/dsh-plugin-moss-tts#main
```

**CLI profile** (a profile the desktop app does not own):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:litterbit/dsh-plugin-moss-tts#main
```

**Restart DSH** afterwards. You get a "Moss Speech" settings page, a speaker toggle at the left
of the composer, a read button on every assistant reply, and five `moss_tts_*` tools.

> Installing from a local checkout: `dsh plugin --profile <name> add D:\path\to\dsh-plugin-moss-tts`
> (an absolute path is required).

## First run: install the engine

Open **Settings → Moss Speech → Download engine**. The plugin fetches
`MossTTS-win-x64-full.zip` (~160 MB) from the
[engine releases](https://github.com/litterbit/dsh-moss-tts/releases), verifies it against the
release's `sha256sums.txt`, and extracts it into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MossTTS`.

- Already installed via the CLI or the web playground? It is reused; nothing is downloaded twice.
- Downloads resume after an interruption; cancel removes only the partial file.
- **Follows your system proxy**: `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` first, then the Windows Internet
  settings (`ProxyEnable` + `ProxyServer`, via a CONNECT tunnel). A machine whose browser can open
  GitHub needs no extra configuration; set `NO_PROXY=*` to force direct connections.
- Behind a blocked network, point `engineUrl` + `engineSha256` at a mirror in the plugin config,
  or set `autoDownload: false` and manage the install yourself.

## Usage

| Entry point | What it does |
|---|---|
| 🔊 left of the composer | Auto-read. Reads each reply when it settles; while speaking the same button is ⏹ and stops it |
| 🔊 on a reply | Reads that reply only (whole text, ignores the auto-read limit) |
| Settings → Moss Speech | Voice, auto-read limit, skip code blocks, preview, engine state and paths |
| `moss_tts_say` | Agent-initiated speech (plays locally, or `save_to` writes a WAV) |
| `moss_tts_voices` / `moss_tts_stop` / `moss_tts_clone` / `moss_tts_engine` | Voices / stop / clone a voice / engine status and install |

Markdown is cleaned before speaking: fenced code and tables are skipped, links keep their text,
heading and list markers are stripped, and long replies are cut on a sentence boundary at the
auto-read limit (default 1500 characters, 0 = unlimited).

## Privacy

- Synthesis is fully local: no network, no uploaded text, no telemetry.
- The only outbound traffic is the engine download you trigger from the settings page.
- Cloned voices live under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MossTTS\userdata\voices\user\`.

## How it relates to the CLI and the web playground

All three run the same `moss_tts.exe`, the same weights and the same data directory:

- CLI: `moss_tts.exe --text "hello" --out hello.wav`
- Web playground: double-click `moss_tts.exe` → `http://127.0.0.1:8759/`
- This plugin: no port; it spawns the resident engine over `--stdio`

Engine and plugin version independently: `engine.json` pins a release, falls back to the latest
one when that tag is gone, and always verifies the release's `sha256sums.txt`.

## Uninstall

In the desktop app, remove it from the sidebar **Plugins** page. For a CLI-managed profile:
`dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-plugin-moss-tts`.

The weights are left in place (the CLI and the web playground still use them). Delete
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\MossTTS` to remove them too.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Settings keeps showing "not installed" | Press "Re-check"; verify `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MossTTS\moss_tts.exe` and `models\` exist |
| Download fails / hash mismatch | Usually a proxy rewriting the body. Retry once; if it persists, set `engineUrl` + `engineSha256` in the plugin config |
| "Ready" but silent | The tab is muted, or the output device is wrong; click anywhere in the page once so the browser allows playback |
| Long replies are cut short | The auto-read limit (1500 chars) — raise it in settings, or use the reply's own read button |
| Plugin does not appear | DSH must be restarted; `dsh --profile desktop --dump-config` should contain a row `id: moss-tts` |

## Development

```bash
node tools/build-client.mjs          # regenerate lib/client.js (committed; installs run no build)
node tools/build-client.mjs --check  # what CI uses to catch a stale bundle
node --test tests/*.test.mjs         # no DSH required; engine tests skip without an engine
```

Host contract (verified against DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 on the development machine): `dsh.bundle.patch`
inserts one loader row for the host half; `dsh.client.platform = "web"` plus
`exports["./client"]` load the browser half; the host registers routes through
`ctx.get('webServer').register` and the client registers slots through `ctx.slots.inject`.
Nothing is imported from the host packages — tool definitions are plain objects with standard
JSON Schema.

## License

Apache-2.0. Model weights come from MOSS-TTS-Nano-100M (Apache-2.0) and are converted to the
engine's container format by the engine repo; this package ships **no** weights or binaries and
downloads them at runtime. See [NOTICE](NOTICE.md).

# @lmzhen/dsh-evolution-all

`DEFAULT install` is the full installation bundle. It mounts the host automation and the profile-root memory/skill model rows so every session receives the family model tools and prompt guidance without selecting a separate preset.

The full form also includes the unified skill-history workbench page (history / pending / merge / health views), while editable parameters live on the platform plugin-config cards. The health view ships but is disabled by default.

Use this form for the normal full installation. To shrink the installation, uninstall it before installing `host`, the one-click `preset`, or the layered `host + Evolution preset` form; these forms are mutually exclusive because their shared rows must not mount twice.

Ordinary memory/skill approval is disabled by default. Merge has its own approval and platform-write controls.

# dsh-evolution

## What is this plugin for?

The plugin is designed to generate skills automatically and manage their full lifecycle, with an emphasis on retaining capabilities that are specific to a user and a project. It is task-oriented: the model builds and maintains a private set of skills for the user's environment, preferences and working procedures, improving its fit for those tasks.

That lifecycle includes creation, discovery, use, revision after review, restructuring, merging, archiving and restoration. These are independent capabilities rather than stages every skill must pass through. The plugin also provides budgeted memory for project facts and user preferences across sessions.

It does not modify or train the model, and it does not provide a hosted model service. DSH's configured model performs the semantic work, while the plugin's write gates, snapshots, history and approval mechanisms constrain changes and recovery.

## Platform line

The family targets DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` only. Published packages declare the `^0.2.2-rc.0` peer range and the `>=0.2.2-rc.0 <0.2.3-0` engine range. The single host edge is the `evolutionPlatform` service; features reach it through the family's platform ports, never by importing host internals.

## What is a skill?

Early language models generated text autoregressively. Questions, instructions and answers were linked statistically, so prompts that described the domain, task and constraints precisely usually improved the result. That relationship was a foundation of early prompt engineering.

Chain-of-thought and stronger model capabilities reduced the need for exhaustive prompts in some single-step tasks: the model could recall terminology and conventions during reasoning. Tool calling then changed the objective again. Instead of producing one piece of content, the model had to complete a sequence of operations. Execution order, tool constraints, completion criteria and failure recovery still needed explicit instructions. The prompt increasingly resembled an operating manual rather than a complete description of one desired answer.

Different tasks need different manuals, and they cannot all remain in context. One approach is to connect step-specific prompts and inputs and outputs into a fixed workflow. Another is to package a manual as a module that the model can discover by name and description and load when relevant. That module is a skill. In DSH, a skill normally consists of a `SKILL.md` body and optional scripts, templates and reference files, loaded through the native `skill` tool.

Skills and MCP belong to different layers. MCP is a protocol for connecting tools and resources; a skill describes when to use those capabilities, in what order, and what counts as done. The plugin manages procedural knowledge, not tool connectivity itself.

## Why build this plugin?

Two related changes are taking place:

1. **The marginal value of some general-purpose skills is falling.** Public, common operating procedures are increasingly being absorbed into model capability through training. Maintaining a separate manual for those tasks yields less benefit, although this does not make every general-purpose skill obsolete.
2. **Models are becoming capable of extracting operating procedures from execution traces.** With real trajectories and clear feedback, a model can organize the steps, constraints and corrections from a task into a reusable skill. This plugin uses that capability during review and skill writing. The output still passes structural checks and may require human approval; it is not assumed to be correct merely because a model produced it.

At the same time, every user's machine, project conventions, preferences and complex task details remain different. Once general capability is sufficient, the decisive knowledge is often valid only for one person or one project. A private skill set grows with task variety and complexity, and it also develops duplication, staleness and structural problems. Maintaining all of that manually does not scale.

The plugin therefore uses the model's semantic ability to automate the generation and maintenance work that is suitable for automation, while retaining human control and recovery paths. Its objective is not unrestricted skill accumulation, but a useful, inspectable and maintainable private skill set built from real work.

## How does it relate to memory plugins?

The two are largely complementary. A typical memory plugin manages facts: who the user is, what the project is, and what was decided. This plugin is more concerned with process: how a class of task should be performed, in what order, and to what standard. It is intended primarily for people who use Harness to get work done.

The plugin also contains a memory module, but its design differs from the familiar retrieve-on-demand, continuously growing model:

- **Memory has a hard character budget.** The default budgets for project memory in `MEMORY.md` and the user profile in `USER.md` are 2200 and 1375 characters. If a batch would exceed the budget, it is refused rather than silently truncated. The model must delete or compact existing entries before adding new ones. After the budget is lowered, replacement can also be refused when an existing entry exceeds the new limit; deletion is then the recovery path.
- **Memory is supplied as a snapshot instead of relying only on deliberate retrieval.** This keeps critical project facts visible during a task instead of depending on the model to search for them.

Snapshot injection does not mean that every persisted byte necessarily reaches the model context. Entries matched by threat scanning are filtered, and abnormally large files are skipped. The character budget bounds injection size; it is not a guarantee that every task avoids performance loss or additional context cost. The design keeps critical facts within a bounded context while using skills to maintain procedural knowledge.

## What capabilities does it provide?

Each capability below has a corresponding code entry point. They have different triggers and should not be read as a pipeline that runs for every task.

| Capability | Current behavior and defaults |
|---|---|
| Skill generation and updates | The agent can create and patch skills through `skill_manage`. By default, review prompts ask the model to generate or update skills at an interval of ten weighted tool calls after substantive cadence signals, delivered at a task boundary; a review does not have to produce a new skill |
| Skill catalog and search | The full catalog is published by default and loaded through the native `skill` tool; `skill_search` provides local retrieval, while discovery domain cards and catalog trimming are off by default |
| Library curation | Curator performs deterministic lifecycle maintenance on interval and idle conditions, marking stale skills and archiving them; LLM-nominated consolidation is a separate option |
| Skill merge | Started with `/evolution merge scan` or `pair`. Scan requires local potion models and can fall back to stub without an LLM; ordinary pair does not require potion, but round 1/authoring requires a child-session model. Initiated runs are auto-approved by default, with `mergeApproval` available for manual approval |
| Memory | Available in `all`, `preset` and selected layered-preset sessions. Project memory and user-profile budgets default to 2200 and 1375 characters; new writes are refused at the limit rather than silently truncated |
| Write approval and recovery | Ordinary write approval is off by default and stages memory and skill writes when enabled; curator and merge use their own controls. Skill history, body undo, unit undo and archive restore have different scopes, and execution-time failures do not guarantee complete rollback |
| Diagnostics and UI | `/evolution doctor`, curation reports, skill health and a knowledge graph are available; `all` provides settings, skill history and a merge panel on Web/desktop GUI, while the health panel is disabled by default |

See [Feature reference](docs/features.md) for triggers, failure behavior and limits.

## Install

See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for prerequisites, all four installation forms and upgrades. Install the full form by default:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @lmzhen/dsh-evolution-all
# Restart DSH, then run in a session:
/evolution doctor
```

For the desktop GUI, replace `--profile web` with `--profile desktop`. After installation, ask the agent to remember a project fact and open a new session to verify that it is injected. `doctor` checks the installation form and service state; it does not replace an actual read/write check.

The full source layout reports<!-- gen:install-counts --> 35 packages installed (the published list is 36; the agent preset is separate)<!-- /gen:install-counts -->.

## Installation forms

| Form | Use case | Capabilities and UI |
|---|---|---|
| `all` | Default full installation | Memory and skill tools in every session; evolution workbench (history/pending/merge/health) and the diagnostics card on Web/desktop GUI |
| `host` | No memory/skill write tools for the model | Explicit merge, background curation, manual maintenance and diagnostics remain; automatic review and usage accounting do not run; no evolution workbench or diagnostics |
| `preset` | Migration from an older configuration | Similar tool coverage to `all`, without settings or sidebar panels |
| Layered preset | Tools only in selected sessions | `host` plus the Evolution preset; other sessions do not enable automatic plugin behavior; no settings or sidebar panels |

Use only one form per profile. See [packages/INSTALL.md](packages/INSTALL.md) for exact session behavior and [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for commands.

## Common commands

| Command | When to use it |
|---|---|
| `/evolution doctor` | Check installation form, versions and service state |
| `/evolution pending` | List ordinary writes waiting for approval |
| `/evolution skill history <name>` | Inspect body and support-file history |
| `/evolution skill undo <name>` | Revert the skill body; support files are not restored |
| `/evolution curator status` | Inspect automatic curation state |
| `/evolution merge status <runId>` | Inspect an initiated merge run |
| `/graph` | Browse or edit the skill and memory graph |

See [docs/commands.md](docs/commands.md) for the command reference and [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) for common settings.

## Data and safety

- In the default assembly, plugin data is stored under `$DSH_HOME` and does not depend on a family-hosted service. See [Operations](docs/operations.md) for backup and restore scope.
- Controlled memory/skill model tools scan call arguments, and the corresponding write paths apply structural checks and policy protection. Approval is an optional additional control; it neither replaces those checks nor covers curator or merge internal writes.
- Skill deletion archives the skill. Body history is recorded best-effort; verify an available version before undo, and note that body undo does not restore support files. Pre-curation snapshots can be restored, and merge runs retain records used for undo.
- Local storage does not mean that content never leaves the machine. Review, LLM curation and discovery domain generation send the relevant task or skill content to the configured model provider; branch review also copies session events into a child session.
- API keys are managed by DSH model and credential configuration. Do not place them in skills, memories or plugin configuration. See [Models and API keys](docs/api-keys.md).

## Compatibility

| Item | Current requirement |
|---|---|
| Validated platform line | **`0.2.1-rc.3`** |
| Published dependency window | `^0.2.1-rc.2` |
| Family version | `0.37.1` |
| Node | `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0` |

Published packages do not cross older prerelease platform lines. See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for installation and upgrade order.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): installation, first memory write and first skill operation.
- [Feature reference](docs/features.md): actual capabilities, defaults and limits.
- [Commands](docs/commands.md): everyday, curation, merge and maintenance commands.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): approval, budgets, intervals and model-related settings.
- [Models and API keys](docs/api-keys.md): model dependencies and credential configuration.
- [Operations](docs/operations.md): backup, upgrade, uninstall and verification.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): symptom-based diagnosis.
- Maintainer references: [package map and canonical facts](packages/README.md) and [development guide](docs/developer/development.md).

# @lmzhen/dsh-evolution-host

Infrastructure-only installation bundle for background automation and management without the general memory/skill-authoring model rows.

It mounts review, curator, approval/state, activity, replay, merge, maintenance, graph, and command infrastructure, but not `memory`, `skill_manage`, or the evolution skill catalog used by the full model-tool forms.

Host-only still exposes the read-only `maintenance_probe` and the merge-child-only `merge_stage` model tools. During the author phase, `merge_stage` supports staging writes and copies; it is not a read-only or generally available user tool. The host distinction is the absence of the general memory/skill-authoring model rows, not the absence of every model tool.

Use `all` or the layered Evolution preset when sessions need memory and skill authoring. `host` is mutually exclusive with `all`, `preset`, and a layered host-plus-preset installation.

# dsh-evolution

## What is this plugin for?

The plugin is designed to generate skills automatically and manage their full lifecycle, with an emphasis on retaining capabilities that are specific to a user and a project. It is task-oriented: the model builds and maintains a private set of skills for the user's environment, preferences and working procedures, improving its fit for those tasks.

That lifecycle includes creation, discovery, use, revision after review, restructuring, merging, archiving and restoration. These are independent capabilities rather than stages every skill must pass through. The plugin also provides budgeted memory for project facts and user preferences across sessions.

It does not modify or train the model, and it does not provide a hosted model service. DSH's configured model performs the semantic work, while the plugin's write gates, snapshots, history and approval mechanisms constrain changes and recovery.

## Platform line

The family targets DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` only. Published packages declare the `^0.2.2-rc.0` peer range and the `>=0.2.2-rc.0 <0.2.3-0` engine range. The single host edge is the `evolutionPlatform` service; features reach it through the family's platform ports, never by importing host internals.

## What is a skill?

Early language models generated text autoregressively. Questions, instructions and answers were linked statistically, so prompts that described the domain, task and constraints precisely usually improved the result. That relationship was a foundation of early prompt engineering.

Chain-of-thought and stronger model capabilities reduced the need for exhaustive prompts in some single-step tasks: the model could recall terminology and conventions during reasoning. Tool calling then changed the objective again. Instead of producing one piece of content, the model had to complete a sequence of operations. Execution order, tool constraints, completion criteria and failure recovery still needed explicit instructions. The prompt increasingly resembled an operating manual rather than a complete description of one desired answer.

Different tasks need different manuals, and they cannot all remain in context. One approach is to connect step-specific prompts and inputs and outputs into a fixed workflow. Another is to package a manual as a module that the model can discover by name and description and load when relevant. That module is a skill. In DSH, a skill normally consists of a `SKILL.md` body and optional scripts, templates and reference files, loaded through the native `skill` tool.

Skills and MCP belong to different layers. MCP is a protocol for connecting tools and resources; a skill describes when to use those capabilities, in what order, and what counts as done. The plugin manages procedural knowledge, not tool connectivity itself.

## Why build this plugin?

Two related changes are taking place:

1. **The marginal value of some general-purpose skills is falling.** Public, common operating procedures are increasingly being absorbed into model capability through training. Maintaining a separate manual for those tasks yields less benefit, although this does not make every general-purpose skill obsolete.
2. **Models are becoming capable of extracting operating procedures from execution traces.** With real trajectories and clear feedback, a model can organize the steps, constraints and corrections from a task into a reusable skill. This plugin uses that capability during review and skill writing. The output still passes structural checks and may require human approval; it is not assumed to be correct merely because a model produced it.

At the same time, every user's machine, project conventions, preferences and complex task details remain different. Once general capability is sufficient, the decisive knowledge is often valid only for one person or one project. A private skill set grows with task variety and complexity, and it also develops duplication, staleness and structural problems. Maintaining all of that manually does not scale.

The plugin therefore uses the model's semantic ability to automate the generation and maintenance work that is suitable for automation, while retaining human control and recovery paths. Its objective is not unrestricted skill accumulation, but a useful, inspectable and maintainable private skill set built from real work.

## How does it relate to memory plugins?

The two are largely complementary. A typical memory plugin manages facts: who the user is, what the project is, and what was decided. This plugin is more concerned with process: how a class of task should be performed, in what order, and to what standard. It is intended primarily for people who use Harness to get work done.

The plugin also contains a memory module, but its design differs from the familiar retrieve-on-demand, continuously growing model:

- **Memory has a hard character budget.** The default budgets for project memory in `MEMORY.md` and the user profile in `USER.md` are 2200 and 1375 characters. If a batch would exceed the budget, it is refused rather than silently truncated. The model must delete or compact existing entries before adding new ones. After the budget is lowered, replacement can also be refused when an existing entry exceeds the new limit; deletion is then the recovery path.
- **Memory is supplied as a snapshot instead of relying only on deliberate retrieval.** This keeps critical project facts visible during a task instead of depending on the model to search for them.

Snapshot injection does not mean that every persisted byte necessarily reaches the model context. Entries matched by threat scanning are filtered, and abnormally large files are skipped. The character budget bounds injection size; it is not a guarantee that every task avoids performance loss or additional context cost. The design keeps critical facts within a bounded context while using skills to maintain procedural knowledge.

## What capabilities does it provide?

Each capability below has a corresponding code entry point. They have different triggers and should not be read as a pipeline that runs for every task.

| Capability | Current behavior and defaults |
|---|---|
| Skill generation and updates | The agent can create and patch skills through `skill_manage`. By default, review prompts ask the model to generate or update skills at an interval of ten weighted tool calls after substantive cadence signals, delivered at a task boundary; a review does not have to produce a new skill |
| Skill catalog and search | The full catalog is published by default and loaded through the native `skill` tool; `skill_search` provides local retrieval, while discovery domain cards and catalog trimming are off by default |
| Library curation | Curator performs deterministic lifecycle maintenance on interval and idle conditions, marking stale skills and archiving them; LLM-nominated consolidation is a separate option |
| Skill merge | Started with `/evolution merge scan` or `pair`. Scan requires local potion models and can fall back to stub without an LLM; ordinary pair does not require potion, but round 1/authoring requires a child-session model. Initiated runs are auto-approved by default, with `mergeApproval` available for manual approval |
| Memory | Available in `all`, `preset` and selected layered-preset sessions. Project memory and user-profile budgets default to 2200 and 1375 characters; new writes are refused at the limit rather than silently truncated |
| Write approval and recovery | Ordinary write approval is off by default and stages memory and skill writes when enabled; curator and merge use their own controls. Skill history, body undo, unit undo and archive restore have different scopes, and execution-time failures do not guarantee complete rollback |
| Diagnostics and UI | `/evolution doctor`, curation reports, skill health and a knowledge graph are available; `all` provides settings, skill history and a merge panel on Web/desktop GUI, while the health panel is disabled by default |

See [Feature reference](docs/features.md) for triggers, failure behavior and limits.

## Install

See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for prerequisites, all four installation forms and upgrades. Install the full form by default:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @lmzhen/dsh-evolution-all
# Restart DSH, then run in a session:
/evolution doctor
```

For the desktop GUI, replace `--profile web` with `--profile desktop`. After installation, ask the agent to remember a project fact and open a new session to verify that it is injected. `doctor` checks the installation form and service state; it does not replace an actual read/write check.

The full source layout reports<!-- gen:install-counts --> 35 packages installed (the published list is 36; the agent preset is separate)<!-- /gen:install-counts -->.

## Installation forms

| Form | Use case | Capabilities and UI |
|---|---|---|
| `all` | Default full installation | Memory and skill tools in every session; evolution workbench (history/pending/merge/health) and the diagnostics card on Web/desktop GUI |
| `host` | No memory/skill write tools for the model | Explicit merge, background curation, manual maintenance and diagnostics remain; automatic review and usage accounting do not run; no evolution workbench or diagnostics |
| `preset` | Migration from an older configuration | Similar tool coverage to `all`, without settings or sidebar panels |
| Layered preset | Tools only in selected sessions | `host` plus the Evolution preset; other sessions do not enable automatic plugin behavior; no settings or sidebar panels |

Use only one form per profile. See [packages/INSTALL.md](packages/INSTALL.md) for exact session behavior and [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for commands.

## Common commands

| Command | When to use it |
|---|---|
| `/evolution doctor` | Check installation form, versions and service state |
| `/evolution pending` | List ordinary writes waiting for approval |
| `/evolution skill history <name>` | Inspect body and support-file history |
| `/evolution skill undo <name>` | Revert the skill body; support files are not restored |
| `/evolution curator status` | Inspect automatic curation state |
| `/evolution merge status <runId>` | Inspect an initiated merge run |
| `/graph` | Browse or edit the skill and memory graph |

See [docs/commands.md](docs/commands.md) for the command reference and [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) for common settings.

## Data and safety

- In the default assembly, plugin data is stored under `$DSH_HOME` and does not depend on a family-hosted service. See [Operations](docs/operations.md) for backup and restore scope.
- Controlled memory/skill model tools scan call arguments, and the corresponding write paths apply structural checks and policy protection. Approval is an optional additional control; it neither replaces those checks nor covers curator or merge internal writes.
- Skill deletion archives the skill. Body history is recorded best-effort; verify an available version before undo, and note that body undo does not restore support files. Pre-curation snapshots can be restored, and merge runs retain records used for undo.
- Local storage does not mean that content never leaves the machine. Review, LLM curation and discovery domain generation send the relevant task or skill content to the configured model provider; branch review also copies session events into a child session.
- API keys are managed by DSH model and credential configuration. Do not place them in skills, memories or plugin configuration. See [Models and API keys](docs/api-keys.md).

## Compatibility

| Item | Current requirement |
|---|---|
| Validated platform line | **`0.2.1-rc.3`** |
| Published dependency window | `^0.2.1-rc.2` |
| Family version | `0.37.1` |
| Node | `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0` |

Published packages do not cross older prerelease platform lines. See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for installation and upgrade order.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): installation, first memory write and first skill operation.
- [Feature reference](docs/features.md): actual capabilities, defaults and limits.
- [Commands](docs/commands.md): everyday, curation, merge and maintenance commands.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): approval, budgets, intervals and model-related settings.
- [Models and API keys](docs/api-keys.md): model dependencies and credential configuration.
- [Operations](docs/operations.md): backup, upgrade, uninstall and verification.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): symptom-based diagnosis.
- Maintainer references: [package map and canonical facts](packages/README.md) and [development guide](docs/developer/development.md).

Like `all`, it mounts model tools at profile root so every session receives them. It does not include the settings/skill-history UI umbrella, merge sidebar, or skill-health panel.
