# LoopX for DeepSeek Harness

`dsh-loopx-plugin` is one independently versioned DSH package with three
separate Loader rows:

- the init row automatically installs or upgrades the LoopX CLI, installs the
  packaged workflow skills into `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills` (default
  `~/.agents/skills`), and verifies the DSH-native `loopx` entry before DSH
  finishes loading it. `/loopx-init` remains the explicit repair command.
- a passive same-session Driver becomes eligible only after the exact current
  Session successfully invokes the exact `loopx` skill. It then asks LoopX
  whether another turn may run and queues the authoritative heartbeat task
  into that live DSH Agent.
- the package-root Host registers GoalBar at the authenticated
  `/api/loopx.goalbar` route required by DSH 0.1.5. Its web Client adds a compact
  GoalBar between DSH's native GoalBar and Queue dock rows, visible only for one
  exact live `(goalId, loopxAgentId)` binding.

Installing the plugin and starting DSH load and prepare these capabilities;
neither creates a binding nor activates the Driver. The GoalBar
does one bounded read when a browser row mounts, then watches exact-Session
`step/end` and `turn/end` boundaries. It rereads LoopX only when the opaque
revision of the authoritative binding or active Goal state changes; a watch
lease also detects changes written outside that Session. DSH Agent-status
events update an existing row without a LoopX business read. Until one exact
Session contains valid typed `loopx` invocation evidence, its Driver makes no
LoopX CLI, binding, quota, or heartbeat call, creates no timer, and queues no
followup.

The package does not expose LoopX model tools, a binding sidecar, or its own
Goal/Todo state. Models use the installed LoopX skills and call the LoopX CLI
directly. LoopX remains the only authority for Goal, Agent, Todo, quota,
activation, and durable thread-binding data. The GoalBar protocol and its
deferred atomicity limit are specified in the versioned
[DSH native LoopX design](../../docs/plans/2026-08-20-dsh-native-skill-driver.md).

## Install

Requirements are stable Node.js 22.22.3+ (excluding Node.js 23), `pnpm`,
Python 3.11+ with `pip`, and network access for the first DSH start when no
compatible LoopX CLI is already installed. LoopX itself is deliberately not a
prerequisite. The initializer
honors an explicit `PYTHON_BIN`; otherwise it tries `python3`, then discovers
`python3.<minor>` executables on the supplied `PATH` in descending numeric
order, then tries the bare name `python`. The last name is what a python.org
Windows install registers, so it keeps that host reachable when `python3` is
absent or is the `WindowsApps` App Execution Alias that never starts Python.
Unlike the versioned names it is not a `PATH` scan result; it is resolved when
the candidate runs. Installation still checks the Python version and pip;
reopening the managed runtime uses the same discovery and validates the LoopX
CLI. No hard-coded minor-version list is maintained. When selecting Python for
installation, an invalid explicit interpreter fails instead of falling back.
Managed-runtime readback keeps the existing CLI fallback behavior. If the
plugin must install or upgrade LoopX, it writes an isolated
copy under `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/runtime/dsh-loopx-plugin` (default
`~/.agents/runtime/dsh-loopx-plugin`) and never mutates the system Python
environment. This works with externally managed Python distributions that
enforce PEP 668; the plugin does not use `--break-system-packages`.
This version requires LoopX 1.2.4 or newer, the published release that
includes the Windows peer-file fix. Bootstrap, Driver and GoalBar use the same
version floor; an older global or managed CLI is upgraded or rejected before
business commands run. An explicit outdated `LOOPX_BIN` must be upgraded by its
owner. Older plugin releases retain their original CLI requirements.
Install the prebuilt release into the web profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add \
  "https://github.com/loopx-project/loopx/releases/download/dsh-loopx-plugin-v0.1.1-beta.6/dsh-loopx-plugin-0.1.1-beta.6.tgz"
```

The beta.6 package targets the qualified DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 API and retains the
qualified frozen 0.1.5 and 0.1.7-rc.2 compatibility ranges. The exported legacy
RPC registration remains available to explicit callers, but plugin startup
always uses the shared API.

The source candidate additionally qualifies DSH 0.2.1-rc.2. Its frozen source
host uses MCP client 2.3.0 and SDK 1.32.0 to address
[GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw).
These dependency overrides do not patch an independently installed DSH binary;
that host's owner must update its affected MCP dependencies separately.

For a compatible DSH source build, use:

```bash
cd packages/dsh-loopx-plugin
./install.sh
```

Start DSH on loopback (port `0` asks the OS for a free port) and open the
printed URL. The plugin finishes its idempotent LoopX CLI and skill bootstrap
before DSH publishes the Web URL through its native Loader readiness boundary.
The source candidate gates only LoopX's Host and Driver on `loopxBootstrap`,
so disabling or uninstalling it keeps the shared Web server and runtime alive.
The published beta.6 limitation is described under automatic initialization:

```bash
dsh --profile web --port 0
```

Use `/loopx <task>` immediately. If automatic initialization reports a safe
failure in the DSH log, fix the named Python or package-manager problem and run
`/loopx-init` once to retry; normal installation does not require that command.

Installation is the GoalBar opt-in: there is no separate remote endpoint or
per-session grant. A row remains hidden until the exact DSH Session has one
unique LoopX binding. After invoking the installed `loopx` skill for that
Session, run the minimum authority readback inside that Session's DSH shell
(or replace `$DSH_SESSION_ID` with the exact Session id):

```bash
loopx --registry .loopx/registry.json --format json \
  resolve-agent-thread \
  --host-surface deepseek-harness-native \
  --thread-id "$DSH_SESSION_ID"
```

`status=bound` with one exact pair admits the row; missing or ambiguous results
fail closed and render nothing. `Start` resumes a stopped Goal and asks the
Driver to evaluate only when that exact live Session already contains typed
`loopx` skill activation evidence. It never activates an inactive Session.
`Pause` stops the Goal and retires only future queued/scheduled continuation;
it does not abort a claimed or running turn.

To start DSH from a terminal with this machine's stored LoopX provider
credential without placing the value in argv, shell history, or output:

```bash
loopx dsh-launch web
```

The launcher uses `DSH_HOME` when set, otherwise
`~/.local/state/loopx/dsh-home`. Ordinary DSH installation defaults to `~/.dsh`;
launching the isolated home does not reuse that home's installed plugins. To
reuse an ordinary installation, select its actual home explicitly:

```bash
loopx dsh-launch --dsh-home "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}" web
```

For a new isolated source installation, use the same home and package-local
host for installation, readback, launch, and removal:

```bash
cd packages/dsh-loopx-plugin
export DSH_HOME="$HOME/.local/state/loopx/dsh-home"
./install.sh
export DSH_BIN="$PWD/node_modules/.bin/dsh"
"$DSH_BIN" --profile web --dump-config
loopx dsh-launch --dsh-bin "$DSH_BIN" web
# When removing this installation:
"$DSH_BIN" plugin --profile web remove dsh-loopx-plugin
```

Use `--dsh-home <path>` to select profile and Session state,
`--dsh-agents-home <path>` to isolate installed skills, and `--dsh-bin <path>`
when `dsh` is not on `PATH`. Arguments after `--` are passed to DSH unchanged.
The launcher resolves the same write-only machine credential used by the
managed executor, then replaces itself with DSH so the credential exists only
in the child process environment.

Maintainers can validate the built and packed surfaces with:

```bash
pnpm build
pnpm smoke:mcp-transport
pnpm smoke:artifact
pnpm smoke:profile
pnpm smoke:runtime
pnpm smoke:docker
```

The runtime smoke creates an isolated temporary DSH profile. Its real web
process proves profile composition, automatic initialization before readiness,
immediate skill-catalog visibility, boot-manifest discovery, bundle serving,
Client materialization, and the loopback Connection fence. A
live-disable probe withdraws the bootstrap provider and all package rows while
checking that DSH stays available and LoopX's route retires; a fresh process
also boots with the whole package disabled. Separately, a
packed supported-DSH Context, Connection, and WebServer with a live Host Session fixture
cover same-turn binding discovery, lease-time source reconciliation,
status-only updates, pending-watch cancellation, successful actions, and
handler disposal through the real HTTP carrier. The served Client is then
applied in DSH's real ClientModuleSystem with a VM document harness; that layer
covers slot order and coexistence, Session injection, and ordinary-unload/HMR
style cleanup, but it is not a browser-mounted React interaction. These layers
do not replace the owner-reviewed packed-browser gate: that separate manual
layer mounts the served Client at a real DSH URL and exercises Client-to-carrier
Start/Pause. Focused Client tests cover Session-generation replacement and old
request cancellation without duplicating that matrix in the packed smoke.
The Docker smoke packs the current plugin and builds the current LoopX
release-candidate wheel, then starts both in a clean Debian container with the
DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 release candidate. It proves PEP 668-compatible private installation,
the managed launcher, startup readiness, installed `loopx` skill files, launch-
token authentication, and an authenticated GoalBar read through DSH's shared
API carrier. It requires Docker, `uv`, and network access for base images and
never opens a browser or configures a model provider.

## Maintainer release and marketplace handoff

A DSH plugin release needs an immutable prebuilt GitHub asset and a qualified
install channel in each marketplace named in its closeout. The
[`awesome-dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin)
directory and [DSH Plugin Hub](https://github.com/dshplugin/dsh-plugin-hub)
have distinct published catalogs. Current Hub releases read
`https://api.dsh-plugin.org/plugins.en.json` and `plugins.zh.json`; updating
the awesome directory does not update those consumers. Marketplace maintainers
retain authority over their own catalogs.

Pinned GitHub release installation does not require publishing LoopX on npm.
Release-URL installed-state matching shipped in
[Hub 1.5.0](https://github.com/dshplugin/dsh-plugin-hub/releases/tag/v1.5.0).
Qualification must read the actual marketplace's catalog back, select the
pinned package, install it, recognize the installed row, update it and remove
it successfully. The optional npm channel retains its separate account and
trusted-publisher requirements.

For every DSH plugin release:

1. Update the package version and this README's pinned install URL. Run the
   typecheck, tests, and the built, packed, runtime, profile, and Docker smokes
   listed above, plus `pnpm smoke:registry --tarball <packed-package.tgz>`.
   The registry smoke serves the real packed bytes on loopback and invokes
   DSH's unversioned package-name installer; it publishes nothing. CI repeats
   this installation and removal on Linux and Windows.
   Qualification uses pnpm 10.33.0; use that version for reproducible source
   and isolated-registry checks.
2. Prepare complete bilingual GitHub release notes. Run
   `examples/release/release-readiness-doc-smoke.py` with one `--surface` for
   every optional capability changed by the release.
3. Merge the exact reviewed commit, pack from that immutable tag target, and
   publish both the version tag and `dsh-loopx-plugin-<version>.tgz` asset.
4. Read the remote release body back and rerun the release-readiness smoke.
   Download the remote asset and verify that its SHA-256 matches the local
   package before advertising it. For the npm channel, publish that **same
   tarball**, including its compiled Host, Client, Driver and initializer:

   ```bash
   npm whoami
   npm publish ./dsh-loopx-plugin-VERSION.tgz --access public --tag latest
   node scripts/verify-distribution.mjs --tarball ./dsh-loopx-plugin-VERSION.tgz
   ```

   `latest` intentionally names the qualified plugin candidate, because the
   marketplace installs its unversioned npm name. Do not substitute a
   beta-only tag or publish the monorepo root. The readback checks metadata,
   tag, downloaded bytes and the repository search used by DSH Hub. A missing
   package, wrong artifact or search-index delay fails verification; publishing
   alone does not complete marketplace recovery. npm account authentication
   or configured trusted publishing belongs to the release operator.

   For token-free CI publication, configure the package's npm Trusted Publisher
   with organization `loopx-project`, repository `loopx`, and workflow filename
   `dsh-plugin-publish.yml`, permitting `npm publish`. Then dispatch **Publish
   DSH Plugin to npm** on the existing published plugin tag, using that same tag
   for the `release_tag` input. This keeps npm provenance on the artifact's commit.
   The workflow requires a merged tag, consumes its GitHub asset without
   rebuilding, and verifies npm bytes and discovery. It neither creates a
   GitHub release nor replaces npm account ownership or the release guide gate.
5. For the awesome directory, in a clean fork branch of `awesome-dsh-plugin`, update only
   `data/plugins/loopx-project__loopx--packages-dsh-loopx-plugin.yml` to the new
   immutable asset URL. Confirm the URL resolves, then run
   `node scripts/generate-readme.mjs --check` and `git diff --check`.
6. Open the upstream directory pull request and link it from the release
   closeout. Separately verify the installed Hub's catalog source at the
   released Hub revision. Read both language feeds and the website's install
   command; for the LoopX row, check the `ic` and `igc` targets against the
   immutable release URL. Route stale Hub metadata to its existing
   [data-correction issue channel](https://github.com/dshplugin/dsh-plugin-hub/issues).
   Keep that marketplace's adoption open until its actual consumer resolves
   and installs the released package. A merged directory PR, another catalog's
   listing, or an upgraded Hub cannot establish that postcondition.

## Shadow observer (default off)

`src/observer.ts`, exported as `dsh-loopx-plugin/observer`, is the
`dsh-session-events` provider for the LoopX
[Reliability Diagnostics](../../loopx/capabilities/reliability_diagnostics/README.md)
capability: an L1 shadow observer that consumes read-only harness events and
appends compact, public-safe envelopes plus an observer stats record to
`<loopx-runtime-root>/reliability_diagnostics/by-goal/<sha256>.ndjson`, where
`sha256` is the lowercase digest of the exact UTF-8 Goal id. Upgrade the CLI and
plugin together. An existing legacy filename blocks flushes with
`LegacyDiagnosticLedgerError` until the
[offline upgrade](../../loopx/capabilities/reliability_diagnostics/docs/local-retention-v0.md#upgrading-a-legacy-ledger-offline)
preserves its history; readback never silently migrates it. It is a
separate Cordis row and bundle from the Driver, with no Driver or Agent
injection and no shared send path. It never calls `agent.send`, touches the
inbox, invokes the LoopX CLI, schedules, retries, stops, or resumes anything.
Every hook body and every flush is isolated, so an observer failure is counted
into the receipt instead of reaching DSH. This is module and hook isolation,
not an OS-process-isolation claim.

Before its first append, the producer applies the same recursive local-path,
credential-like value, and credential-field guard as the Python contract.
Unsafe event tokens or ids are counted as `public_safety_violation` and never
reach ledger bytes; CLI ingest independently re-validates persisted records.

It is off unless one exact goal, DSH session, and complete run identity are
declared before DSH starts:

```bash
export LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_GOAL_ID=<goal-id>
export LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_SESSION_ID=<session-id>
export LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_RUN_IDENTITY_JSON='{"worker_id":"<worker>","model_id":"<model>","task_id":"<task>","environment_id":"<environment>","tools_id":"<tools>","budget_id":"<budget>","adapter_revision":"<adapter-revision>","observer_revision":"<observer-revision>"}'
# optional: LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_LEDGER_DIR, LOOPX_DSH_SHADOW_OBSERVER_BUFFER_BOUND (default 256)
loopx reliability-diagnostics receipt --goal-id <goal-id> --format json
loopx reliability-diagnostics status  --goal-id <goal-id> --format json
```

Unless all required variables are valid, the independent observer row
registers no hook and writes no file. When enabled, it consumes only
`session/created`, `session/event`, and `session/disposed`; it skips the retired
token-level `assistant/chunk` rows older logs still replay, and records tool
names, turn and step numbers, typed end reasons, and ids only, never arguments,
outputs, prompts, or paths. Events for
any session other than the exact configured session are rejected as
`identity_invalid`. The stats record pins worker/model/task/environment/tools/
budget plus adapter and observer revisions, declares source coverage, and
proves count conservation. Sequence gaps, bounded-buffer drops, flush attempts,
declared clock uncertainty, and the empty outbound and influence fields make
the run's admissibility auditable from the receipt.

This is an experimental adapter implementing the RFC's P0 prototype
components. It does not establish the RFC's P0 exit: C0 fidelity, a qualifying
C1 run, and measured observer overhead remain separate evidence gates.

## Optional native operation context (SDK prerequisite)

The independently loaded `dsh-loopx-plugin/native-operation-context` subpath
registers one read-only model tool, `loopx_operation_context`. It is absent from
the default plugin tree and `cordis.patch.yml`; installing the package does not
activate it. An explicit SDK Loader patch can load the built module:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: loopx-native-operation-context
      name: file:///absolute/path/to/dsh-loopx-plugin/lib/native-operation-context.js
```

The tool accepts `{}` only. It derives the calling live session and open Turn
from DSH's agent and session-projection services; caller-supplied identities,
closed Turns, cancelled calls and disposed or shadowed tool registrations fail.
Only provider, model and reasoning-effort options are returned. Other agent
options, including credentials, are excluded. Profile options are observations,
not HTTP wire attestation; `wire_profile_verified` and `execution_allowed` are
always `false`. This module creates no Core actor, grant, binding, approval or
account access, and consumes no approval.

The initial runtime qualification uses the Python SDK and bundled DSH
`0.1.5rc1`: a real native tool call returned the matching SDK session and open
Turn. This does not qualify other DSH versions or the complete managed operation
journey. From a source checkout, build and verify registration using an
interpreter with the selected `deepseek-harness` SDK installed:

```bash
pnpm --dir packages/dsh-loopx-plugin build
"$SDK_PYTHON" packages/dsh-loopx-plugin/smoke/dsh-native-context-sdk-smoke.py \
  --module packages/dsh-loopx-plugin/lib/native-operation-context.js \
  --provider deepseek-official --model deepseek-flash
```

This smoke initializes the real SDK with an isolated temporary home and dummy
credentials, checks the runtime's schema registration, and makes zero model
requests. It does not execute a Turn or test financial operations. Remove the
explicit Loader row to disable the module, then restart the owning SDK runtime;
the default plugin tree remains unchanged. Existing active sessions must be
closed by their owner rather than treated as revoked by editing a patch file.

The read-only module alone delivers no frontend or Lark operation path.

## Optional owned SDK operation connection

`dsh-loopx-plugin/native-operation` is a separate, explicit Loader module for
the internal `OwnedDshOperationHost`. It registers `loopx_operation` with an
absolute, parent-owned Unix socket supplied by the host; it is absent from the
default exports and patch. Installing the package grants no execution access.

The host retains the original SDK stdio connection across separately admitted
Turns. Kernel peer PID, native session/Turn/call ID, exact native arguments and
the observed provider/model/effort must match before dispatch to the existing
Core operation handler. The existing Turn session file and typed operation
store own profile binding, revocation, approval, first consumption and outcome;
there is no second approval store or public actor/proof/consume endpoint.
Changing the module/package JS, model profile or session requires fresh
admission and approval. Transport loss never permits an automatic effect retry.

The real SDK/bundled runtime `0.1.5rc1` qualifies two Turns on one retained
connection with a scripted loopback provider: prepare, reject before approval,
fixture confirmation, inspect, one permitted consumption, rejected repeat and
canonical `not_executed` outcome. Synthetic confirmation is not human approval;
no venue/account effect or paid model call is involved. The read-only real-model
probe above and this integrated synthetic-provider test prove different stages.

SDK `0.1.5rc1` cannot reload persisted sessions (`session already exists`);
a new host still refuses that version's resume before runtime launch.
An isolated candidate uses Python SDK `0.2.1a3`, built with the official wheel
script from [upstream source `2fbf4359`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/2fbf4359b82fb94c03dcce0b831660d87f12ea5c),
and an explicit `runtime_bin` pointing to npm `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-alpha.3`.
The SDK's public `resume_session` restores the same persisted identity without
sending input. The host pins SDK files, the executable/Node and complete npm
closure into the immutable profile; changes require fresh admission/approval.
File/SQLite tests close the first process, restore the original session and
repeat the operation sequence. Missing or unreadable history refuses without
a provider call, replacement binding or reusable failed client. This candidate
does not qualify the default plugin's peer range or a published Python release.

Public CLI/delegation activation, frontend/Lark original-card return and actual
financial execution remain unqualified. The public managed-operation preflight
remains Codex-only until those entry points are integrated. Disable by omitting this explicit
module and closing its owned host; do not interpret patch removal as revoking
an already running process.

## GoalBar authority and privacy boundary

The GoalBar carrier uses Connection's authenticated `/api/loopx.goalbar`
Fetch route. Explicit callers of the deprecated RPC registration can still
register `/loopx`; plugin startup does not select it automatically. Both pass
Connection's Host/Origin trust fence and browser authentication, and this
package adds no second credential of its own. The deployment's reachability
policy — loopback by default, or declared `trustedHosts` — decides which
browsers can reach the host at all; Phase 1 does not support LAN or remote
browsers. The browser supplies only its injected DSH Session id and, for an
action, the last validated Goal/Agent pair. The Host re-derives cwd and thread
identity from the live DSH Agent, freshly resolves the binding, and executes
only fixed LoopX argv.

The wire allowlist contains ids, activation, live Agent status, full-lane
counts, cursors, opaque source revisions, and fixed error codes. It excludes
Todo text, Goal objective, quota, evidence, CLI output, exception messages,
registry paths, credentials, and binding candidates. A source revision is only
a change token, not authorization or a compare-and-swap guard. Installing the
package grants no model tool authority, does not create or repair bindings, and
does not change LoopX core state by itself.

## Automatic initialization and `/loopx-init` repair

When DSH loads the plugin, the init row runs the same typed initialization
routine and publishes the `loopxBootstrap` readiness service only after it
settles. DSH's native Loader wait keeps the printed URL behind initialization;
the service is a dependency only of LoopX's Host and Driver. A safe failure is
logged without raw subprocess output or local paths and leaves `/loopx-init`
registered for an explicit retry. Disabling the package leaves LoopX's
rows unavailable while DSH remains usable. Removing the package's
rows releases its routes without stopping the shared Web server or runtime.
Automatic startup does not create Agent followups or model calls.

The host-isolation repair in this source is pending a new plugin release.
Published beta.6 still adds the shared Web dependency and can disconnect DSH
during hot uninstall, including with Hub 1.6.4. For that published package,
close DSH, remove it with the native plugin CLI, then restart DSH.

The repair command has no arguments. Extra input returns a usage error before any
model work or CLI probe. A valid invocation queues a bounded start followup on
the exact receiving Agent, then probes the current LoopX installation. When the
CLI is missing or lacks the DSH-native skill contract, it runs exactly one
fixed-argv `pip install --upgrade --target <plugin-runtime> 'loopx>=1.2.4'`, writes a
small managed Python launcher beside that target, then uses that same
interpreter and launcher to install and read back the skills. Driver and
GoalBar resolve this same managed runtime, including after an explicit repair.
It never constructs a shell command, mutates the system Python environment,
edits a registry, or retries the install mutation.

Unless the command is cancelled, it queues a second bounded followup for the
typed success or failure result. These are ordinary Agent turns, so a valid,
uncancelled invocation normally adds two model calls; cancellation leaves only
the already queued start turn, while invalid input adds none. The prompts do
not authorize tools, commands, or another installation. Followup delivery is
best effort and is not retried. The native `CommandResult` rendered by the
command UI remains authoritative: a followup failure or model reply cannot
change the installation result or repeat its mutation.

On success, DSH's filesystem skill provider invalidates its catalog and loads
created or updated skills without a restart. Missing or unknown skill status
still fails initialization instead of being guessed as unchanged.

After initialization, invoke the `loopx` skill with the task text. The skill
uses the exact DSH-managed `$DSH_SESSION_ID`, passes
`--host-surface deepseek-harness-native`, and follows the typed commands
returned by LoopX. The historical external connector remains the distinct
`deepseek-harness` / `dsh` surface.

## Driver activation boundary

Activation is per Session, not per plugin, process, Agent, Goal, or project.
The Driver accepts only either of these durable typed Session facts:

- a `user/message` whose source is exactly `skill-invocation`, whose name is
  exactly `loopx`, and whose form is exactly `instructions`;
- a model `tool/call` named exactly `skill`, with JSON object arguments whose
  `name` is exactly `loopx`, paired by call id with a subsequent successful
  `tool/result`.

A skill catalog, ordinary prose, shell text, `/loopx-init`, plugin-authored
init or heartbeat messages, a failed, malformed, unmatched, or superseded
model call, and the presence of a CLI, registry, Goal, binding, or project file
do not activate the Driver. Recovery folds only the current Session's existing
typed event history in memory and performs no external probe. Replacing or
clearing a Session recomputes from the replacement history; activation never
inherits across that boundary and has no plugin-owned durable store.

Existing Sessions upgraded from an older plugin version remain inactive when
their retained history has no recognizable invocation evidence. Invoke the
installed `loopx` skill once in every Session that should continue
automatically. Activation records intent only: it does not create a binding,
select a Goal or Agent, spend quota, or grant tool authority. After activation,
the existing exact binding, fresh quota, scheduler/heartbeat, reservation, and
pre-step revalidation order remains authoritative.

## Driver retry boundary

DSH's LLM retry plugin owns provider-request retries. This Driver retries only
safe fixed-argv LoopX reads and an idempotent `quota should-run` receipt, at
most twice beyond the first attempt. Every retry uses the same
`--turn-instance-id`. Typed authority denials, incompatible schemas,
cancellation, and human input are never retried. There is no cumulative
eight-failure breaker or plugin-owned durable activation state. The small
process-local activation projection is bound to one exact Session and is
reconstructed only from its typed event history. Exhausting the three attempts
stops that evaluation; it does not create a periodic error-retry loop. Only a
typed LoopX local-scheduler plan can schedule another wakeup, and its limit on
unchanged polls is enforced.

For an admitted automatic continuation, that exact turn id is also carried in
the LoopX-owned canonical heartbeat body and the typed DSH continuation source.
The source is attribution for reservation matching, not authority. Before work
enters a model step, the Driver replays the same receipt and the LoopX guard
returns the typed settlement plan for that exact id. Accountable

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-loyalchiiina-plugin-pack

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）**插件聚合 bundle 包**：一条安装命令把 14 个独立插件一起挂上，也可以只挑其中一个单独装。

- 本包**自身不含任何行为**：`lib/index.js` 只有 `export {}`，不注册服务 / 工具 / 路由 / UI。
- 全部功能来自 `cordis.patch.yml`（`dsh.bundle.patch`）里 `insert:` 的 14 个独立 npm 子包。
- 适配 DSH 内核 `0.2.2-rc.1`。

> 形态参考：官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile`（同样是「bundle 包 = 一份 patch + 一份 dependencies」，`lib/index.js` 只有 `export {}`）。

---

## 一、包含的 14 个组件

| # | 包名 | 作用（简述） | 聚合条目 id |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `dsh-artifact-linker` | 产物路径联动：常驻注入「产物路径铁律」+ 正文文件名渲染成可点芯片（侧栏预览 / 系统默认程序打开 / 复制绝对路径） | `suite-artifact-linker` |
| 2 | `dsh-browser-hub` | 侧边栏浏览器增强：搜索引擎选择、书签收藏、多级文件夹、导入 360/Chrome 书签 | `suite-browser-hub` |
| 3 | `dsh-chat-image-lightbox` | 对话图片灯箱：全屏缩放/平移/下载/翻页、缩略图网格、TIFF·HEIC 转码、防盗链自动转存，并注入「图片投递铁律」 | `suite-chat-image-lightbox` |
| 4 | `dsh-console-sentinel` | 控制台哨兵（Windows）：一键清理任务栏控制台窗口与空壳，预览后执行、持久白名单、DSH 宿主与 Fluent/MPI 求解器硬保护 | `suite-console-sentinel` |
| 5 | `dsh-deepseek-web-free` | 非官方 DeepSeek 网页端提供方：把网页端当模型用 + 内嵌网页面板（侧栏标签 / 鲸鱼悬浮球） | `suite-deepseek-web-free` |
| 6 | `dsh-font-enhancer` | 字体 DIY：「字」悬浮球 + 分区独立调字体/颜色/字号/行高，方案管理、8 款字体、130 款皮肤 | `suite-font-enhancer` |
| 7 | `dsh-lit-fetch` | 学术文献检索与 PDF 下载：DOI(Crossref)·关键词(OpenAlex) 检索，8 个 Sci-Hub 镜像 + Unpaywall 兜底，生成批量获取清单 HTML | `suite-lit-fetch` |
| 8 | `dsh-skill-browser` | 技能浏览器：把技能库变成可浏览/检索/治理的资产（浏览、调用台账、MCP 管理、快速上手 + 130 款皮肤） | `suite-skill-browser` |
| 9 | `dsh-agent-team-auto-orchestrator` | 智能体团队自动编排：每轮常驻注入团队编排铁律 + 工具层硬门（只认真派活） | `suite-agent-team-auto-orchestrator` |
| 10 | `dsh-todo-float-ball` | Todo 悬浮球：实时显示当前会话 `todo_write` 进度环与清单，可多会话并排、130 款共享皮肤 | `suite-todo-float-ball` |
| 11 | `dsh-voice-alert` | 语音提醒：回合结束自动播报「完成 / 失败」，内置 20 个音效（零配置），可克隆音色 | `suite-voice-alert` |
| 12 | `dsh-archive-favorites-forge` | 对话收藏与归档工坊：收藏任意会话、复制 session id 与 transcript 绝对路径、单条永久删除（带守卫）、按闲置 N 小时批量归档、过滤/导出清单 | `suite-archive-favorites-forge` |
| 13 | `dsh-model-fold` | 三级级联模型面板：来源 / 模型 / 强度三列并排，识图与思考开关，逐模型真实测活 | `suite-model-fold` |
| 14 | `dsh-schedule-calendar` | 日程中心：侧边栏日程表、多城市天气、节假日、提醒、工作待办、休息日与上下班倒计时 | `suite-schedule-calendar` |

> 版本口径以 `package.json` 的 `dependencies` 为准：14 个子包全部取自 **npm 已发布版本**（caret 范围），不含任何 `link:` / `file:` 本地路径依赖。

---

## 二、怎么装

### 方式 A · 装整包（14 个一起）

```powershell
# 只做依赖安装（不改任何 profile 配置）
pnpm add dsh-loyalchiiina-plugin-pack
```

要真正挂进 DSH，还需要把聚合包列进 **profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`**（它的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 才会被合并）：

```json
// ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json
"dsh": {
  "profile": {
    "bundles": ["dsh-loyalchiiina-plugin-pack"]
  }
}
```

> 桌面端（desktop profile）由 Electron 独占管理，CLI 直接拒绝 `dsh plugin --profile desktop`，只能手改 `profiles/desktop/package.json` 后用 pnpm 安装。

### 方式 B · 只装其中一个

聚合包不是必需的中间层。想只要某几个能力，直接单独装对应子包：

```powershell
pnpm add dsh-todo-float-ball
```

然后把**该子包自己的包名**（不是 `suite-*`）列进 `dsh.profile.bundles` —— 因为每个子包自带 `dsh.bundle.patch`，可以独立安装、独立启用。

### 🔴 不要同时启用两者

同一个 profile 里**不要**把 `dsh-loyalchiiina-plugin-pack` 和它包含的某个子包**同时**列进 `dsh.profile.bundles`：那样同一个插件会被两个 bundle 层各挂一次，插件会注册两遍。
（entry id 因为统一加了 `suite-` 前缀而不会撞 `duplicate loader entry id`，但重复注册本身仍然是错的。）

### 改完怎么生效

| 改动位置 | 生效方式 |
|---|---|
| `package.json` / `cordis.patch.yml` / profile 的 bundles 与 node_modules / 预设 | **彻底退出 DSH 客户端再启动**（宿主是 Node 进程，没有热重载） |
| 子包的 `lib/client.js`（客户端 bundle） | 装好后 **Ctrl+Shift+R 硬刷新**（Ctrl+R 只从内存缓存重载，会让人误判「改了没用」） |

---

## 三、组件开关（可开关）

层顺序为 `bundle:*` → `user-patch` → `home-patch`，后层按 id **last-wins** 覆盖。因此关掉单个组件有两条路：

**① 在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里按 entry id 关掉（推荐，改动可逆、不进包）**

```yaml
- id: suite-voice-alert
  disabled: true
```

**② 直接改本包 `cordis.patch.yml`** 给对应条目加 `disabled: true`（等价于「插件默认关闭」）。

**调参**：本包**不写任何 `config:` 覆盖**，14 个组件一律跑各自默认值。要调参数，在 profile 层按 entry id 追加 `config:`，字段名参考各子包自己的 `cordis.patch.yml` / README。

---

## 四、目录结构

```
dsh-loyalchiiina-plugin-pack/
├── package.json          # dsh.bundle.patch + 14 个 dependencies
├── cordis.patch.yml      # dsh.bundle.patch 指向它：- insert: 14 条 entry
├── lib/
│   └── index.js          # export {} —— 聚合包不是插件
├── locale/
│   ├── zh.json
│   └── en.json
├── icon.svg
├── README.md
└── README_EN.md
```

---

## 五、bundle 规范要点（为什么长这样）

1. **聚合包声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`**：`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向 `cordis.patch.yml`，DSH 依据它把 entry 插进 loader。缺这一项会被判 `declares no dsh.bundle`。
2. **聚合包自己不是插件**：没有 `apply` / `inject`，`lib/index.js` 只有 `export {}`；聚合包本身不会被当成 entry 加载（它不出现在自己的 `insert:` 列表里）。
3. **子包各自独立可装**：14 个子包都各自声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`（这是它们能单独安装的前提）。所以「聚合」不等于「子包不能单独用」，也不等于要删掉子包的 bundle 声明。
4. **entry id 唯一且不与子包冲突**：子包自带 patch 的 id 就是**自己的包名**，所以本包统一用 `suite-<短名>`，任何情况下都不会与子包 id 相同，从根上避免 `duplicate loader entry id`。
5. **一个组件一条 entry**：14 条 entry ↔ 14 个组件，`name` 一律写子包名（不写路径、不写版本号）。
6. **无 BOM**：`package.json` / `cordis.patch.yml` / `lib/index.js` / locale 全部 UTF-8 **无 BOM**（BOM 会让 JSON/YAML 解析当场失败）。

---

## 六、版本策略

- 聚合包自身版本 `0.1.0`；子包用 **caret 范围**（`^x.y.z`），允许补丁级更新。
- 聚合包**不锁死**子包版本：修 bug 直接 `pnpm update` 即可，不必等聚合包发版。
- 子包出现 breaking change 时，聚合包升 **minor** 并在 CHANGELOG 写清影响。

## 七、状态与许可

- 当前版本 `0.1.0`：已发布到 npm 与 GitHub。
- License: MIT。

---

## English

`dsh-loyalchiiina-plugin-pack` is an **aggregate bundle package** for DSH (DeepSeek Harness): install 14 standalone DSH plugins with one command, or pick any single one on its own.

- The bundle itself ships **no behaviour**: `lib/index.js` is only `export {}` — no services, tools, routes or UI.
- All functionality comes from the 14 child packages inserted by `cordis.patch.yml` (declared as `dsh.bundle.patch`).
- The bundle declares `dependencies` on published npm versions only (caret ranges), never `link:` / `file:` paths.
- Every child package carries its own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so each one can still be installed and enabled independently.
- Bundle entry ids use the `suite-<short-name>` prefix so they can never collide with a child package's own entry id (`duplicate loader entry id`).
- No `config:` overrides are set here: all 14 components run their default configuration. Disable one by its entry id in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.
- Adapts DSH kernel `0.2.2-rc.1`.

**Install**

```powershell
pnpm add dsh-loyalchiiina-plugin-pack
```

Then list it in the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` array so its `dsh.bundle.patch` gets merged. Changes to `package.json` / `cordis.patch.yml` / profile bundles take effect after a **full DSH client restart**; a child package's client bundle only needs a **Ctrl+Shift+R** hard refresh.

| # | Package | What it does | Bundle entry id |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `dsh-artifact-linker` | Turns declared artifact paths into one-click chips; resident absolute-path rules | `suite-artifact-linker` |
| 2 | `dsh-browser-hub` | Sidebar browser upgrade: search engines, bookmarks, folders, 360/Chrome bookmark import | `suite-browser-hub` |
| 3 | `dsh-chat-image-lightbox` | Full-screen image lightbox, thumbnail grid, TIFF/HEIC transcoding, delivery rule | `suite-chat-image-lightbox` |
| 4 | `dsh-console-sentinel` | Windows console-window sentinel: preview-then-close, whitelist, solver protection | `suite-console-sentinel` |
| 5 | `dsh-deepseek-web-free` | Unofficial DeepSeek Web provider + embedded web panel | `suite-deepseek-web-free` |
| 6 | `dsh-font-enhancer` | Per-region font/colour/line-height DIY with presets and themes | `suite-font-enhancer` |
| 7 | `dsh-lit-fetch` | Literature search + PDF download (Crossref/OpenAlex/Sci-Hub/Unpaywall) | `suite-lit-fetch` |
| 8 | `dsh-skill-browser` | Browse, search and govern the local skill library | `suite-skill-browser` |
| 9 | `dsh-agent-team-auto-orchestrator` | Team-orchestration law injection plus a tool-level gate | `suite-agent-team-auto-orchestrator` |

# dsh-schedule-calendar · 日程助手

> **功能描述**：日程助手一个面板搞定：今日安排、日历、待办、天气，可开关的黄历与星座运势，每日签到攒运气，并按实际完成情况自动生成日报与周报。适配 DSH 内核 0.2.2-rc.1。
>
> **English**: Schedule assistant in one panel: today plan, calendar, to-dos, weather, an almanac and horoscope block you can switch off, a daily check-in, and automatic daily and weekly reports built from what you actually finished. Adapts DSH kernel 0.2.2-rc.1.


DSH 桌面端的侧边栏「日程助手」插件：多城市天气、黄历宜忌、农历日历、日程与提醒、工作待办、日报周报、星座运势与配对、好运签到，以及按人设置的休息日（双休 / 大小周 / 单休 / 自定义）与上下班倒计时，全部收进一个侧边栏标签页。

> 依赖宿主插件 `dsh-better-sidebar`（提供侧边栏标签页能力）。

## 效果图

| 今日（天气 + 日程 + 星座运势） | 日历（农历 / 假期 / 休息日配色） |
| --- | --- |
| ![今日](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/loyalchiiina/dsh-schedule-calendar/main/docs/screenshots/1-today.png) | ![日历](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/loyalchiiina/dsh-schedule-calendar/main/docs/screenshots/3-calendar.png) |

| 日程（重复 / 未来高亮） | 待办（截止日期 / 逾期） |
| --- | --- |
| ![日程](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/loyalchiiina/dsh-schedule-calendar/main/docs/screenshots/4-events.png) | ![待办](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/loyalchiiina/dsh-schedule-calendar/main/docs/screenshots/5-todos.png) |

| 报告（日报 / 周报 / 批量） | 设置（人员班制 / 城市 / 配色 / 关于） |
| --- | --- |
| ![报告](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/loyalchiiina/dsh-schedule-calendar/main/docs/screenshots/6-reports.png) | ![设置](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/loyalchiiina/dsh-schedule-calendar/main/docs/screenshots/7-settings.png) |

## 功能

- **多城市天气**：按「省 / 市 / 区」级联或关键字搜索添加城市（区级用 Nominatim 地理编码，回退 Open-Meteo），横向表格显示今天 / 明天 / 后天 / 大后天 4 天预报；支持「🔄 刷新」与失败自动重试。
- **黄历（宜 / 忌）**：今日头部在星期右侧显示农历与当日宜忌（本地黄历算法，按日固定）。
- **农历日历**：显示农历与节气、法定节假日；周末 / 个人休息日 / 法定假期 / 补班上班 四类背景色可区分，且可在设置里自定义颜色；日历右侧分栏点日期看/加当天日程，支持右键加日程。
- **日程**：标题、日期、时间、备注、提前提醒；支持**不重复 / 每日 / 每周 / 每月 / 每年 / 农历每年（生日纪念）**；记录创建时间；列表按下次发生排序，**本周期已过发灰、未到的高亮**。
- **工作待办**：可设**截止日期**，未完成按截止日排序、逾期红色「⚠ 逾期」，已完成显示完成时间。
- **日报 / 周报**：日报可「一键生成（自动统计当日日程 / 未完成任务 / 已完成）」，支持按日期区间**批量一键生成**；周报自动汇总本周日报与完成情况，也可手动修改并保存。
- **星座运势**：在「设置」里为每人填写生日（可选**阳历 / 农历 + 年份**，自动识别星座）；「今日」底部显示星座图案与每日气运（综合 / 恋爱 / 事业 / 财运 / 幸运色 / 幸运数字），并给出**星座配对**（最配 TOP3 + 与其余 11 星座的相处评分）。
- **好运签到**：今日顶部 Buff 条，每日签到随机抽取「鸿运当头 / 日进斗金 / 暴富」等好运词并附健康提醒，连续签到累计天数。
- **人员与班制**：多人管理；每人在「双休 / 大小周 / 单休 / 自定义星期」间切换。**大小周**语义：大周周六周日都休（双休），小周周六上班、周日休；可指定本周大 / 小周并自动交替。
- **上下班倒计时**：按当前人员班制实时倒计时（距上班 / 距下班），上下班到点提醒。
- **左侧栏入口**：在原生左侧栏脚部注入「日程助手」按钮，一键打开右侧面板；也可从右侧「新建标签页」选择「日程助手」。
- **数据随包走**：数据存在插件包内 `data/store.json`，便于整包打包 / 备份。

## 安装（桌面端 · desktop profile）

> 桌面端 profile 由 Electron 独占，`dsh plugin --profile desktop` 会被拒绝，需手改 profile。

1. 把本包放到 `~/.dsh/local-plugins/dsh-schedule-calendar`（或 `npm i dsh-schedule-calendar`）。
2. 编辑 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`：
   - `dependencies` 增加：`"dsh-schedule-calendar": "link:<本包绝对路径>"`（npm 安装则写版本号）
   - `dsh.profile.bundles` 增加：`"dsh-schedule-calendar"`
3. 在该 profile 目录执行 `pnpm install`。
4. **完全退出 DSH 再启动**（宿主端无热重载）。左侧栏脚部出现「日程助手」按钮，点击打开右侧面板。

## 数据与隐私

- 数据只写本机插件包内 `data/store.json`，不上传任何服务器。
- 天气 / 城市 / 节假日 / 黄历 / 星座运势由宿主端代理转发或本地生成；失败时界面降级提示，不影响日程与待办。

## 开发

- 宿主端：`lib/index.js`（`ctx.webServer.register` 前缀路由：`/ping` `/data` `/geocode` `/weather` `/holidays` `/lunar` `/divisions` `/resolve` `/almanac` `/horoscope` `/lunar2solar`）。
- 客户端：`lib/client.js`（`__ModuleLoader__.load` 手写 bundle，`ctx.betterSidebar.registerTab` + 左侧栏槽位）。
- 契约：`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client.platform: web`；bundle id / package name / patch name 三处一致。
- 本地探针：`scripts/probe.cjs`（迷你 React 运行时渲染七视图）、`scripts/probe-host.mjs`（假 req/res 跑宿主全路由）。

MIT License.

Malo Browser

A browser for scripted demos. It is built on Electron + Chromium and splits a web demo into a Stage (what the audience sees) and a Recorder (fixed-spec capture) without forking the browser engine; demo flows are written as scene scripts, with a Director console and a loopback control API on top. This repository is a working prototype (0.1.x): hidden recording, physical CDP input, an overlay, 1080p30 output, evidence files and a minimal `.app`. It is also the `malo-browser` agent runtime: a background daemon hands out port leases so several agents can drive isolated browser sessions at the same time. ## Install ### Requirements - Node 22.12+ on the 22 line, 24.x, or 26+ (`engines` is `^22.12.0 || ^24.0.0 || >=26.0.0`; the 23 and 25 lines are excluded). The range is declared in `package.json`, so a mismatch surfaces during install (yarn fails; npm/pnpm print an EBADENGINE warning and fail under `engine-strict`) instead of deep inside vite/vitest. - ffmpeg and ffprobe on `PATH` (resolved from `PATH` first, then the Homebrew/local fallback directories); missing binaries exit with code 3. - macOS for the verified path: window modes and recording are tested there, and hidden mode uses the accessory activation policy. - Python 3 only for the bundled fixture static server (`python3 -m http.server`). - git. ### From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/Lumos-789/malo-browser.git cd malo-browser npm install npm run build ``` `npm run build` compiles the main process with tsc and bundles the fixture and the director console with vite. `npm run typecheck` type-checks the main and renderer projects without emitting, and `npm test` runs the vitest unit suite. ### Plugin packaging The repository is both the app and the plugin carrier; there is no second copy of the source. - ZCode plugin: `.zcode-plugin/plugin.json` (name `malo-browser`, version kept in sync with the repo), skill `skills/malo-browser/SKILL.md` (install / configure / troubleshoot; it does not reimplement the product), icon `assets/malo-browser/icon.png` (512x512). With the `dev-oss-projects` marketplace registered: `zcode plugins install malo-browser@dev-oss-projects -s user`. - DSH bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` (patch -> repo-root `cordis.patch.yml`) and `index.js` mounts `skills/` through `bundledSkillDir`. `engines.dsh` and the optional `@deepseek-ai/*` peerDependencies are in `package.json`; because the peer is optional, it does not affect `npm install` for the Electron app. ## Run Serve the fixture page first (the default demo target), in another terminal: ```bash python3 -m http.server 4788 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory out/fixture ``` Default: hidden background recording for 10 seconds. ```bash npx electron . --mode=record --seconds=10 --out=evidence --label=hidden ``` The default recording shows no window, takes no focus and claims no Dock icon on macOS (`setActivationPolicy('accessory')`), so you can keep using the machine while it records. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `npm run build` | main process (tsc), fixture and director (vite) | | `npm run typecheck` | type-check main + renderer projects, no emit | | `npm test` | vitest unit suite | | `npm start` | Director console + Stage; the Stage shows as `inactive` and does not steal focus | | `npm run start:control` | same, plus the loopback control API on `http://127.0.0.1:7317` | | `npx electron . --mode=record --seconds=10` | hidden recording (default) | | `npx electron . --mode=record --window-mode=inactive --seconds=10` | visible but unfocused recording | | `npx electron . --mode=record --plain --seconds=10` | no interaction, static page only (control run) | | `npx electron . --mode=app --autorun=report-review --scenes=fixtures/scenes` | run a whole scene headless and produce a take | | `npx electron . --mode=app --director-check` | invisible check of the Director and the preload bridge | | `npx electron . --mode=app --headless=true --control-api=true` | windowless background instance with only the control API and recording | | `npx electron . --mode=stage --window-mode=inactive` | visible Stage for manual browsing | | `npm run daemon` | malo-browser broker daemon handing out leases to agents | | `npm run smoke:malo -- ` | real multi-agent / multi-session path | | `npm run smoke:toolbar` | hidden check of the handoff toolbar (preload, Enter navigation, address sync, back, page viewport) | | `npm run smoke:control -- report-review` | against a running control API: load scene -> record -> verify evidence | | `npm run package` | package an unpacked app under `dist/` (Apple Silicon: `dist/mac-arm64/Malo Browser.app`) | | `./scripts/run-phase0.sh` | Phase 0 primary evidence run (hidden + inactive) | `--mode=stage` follows `--window-mode`, and its default is `hidden`; pass `--window-mode=inactive` (or `focused`) to actually see the Stage. Common flags: `--url`, `--width`, `--height`, `--out`, `--label`, `--keep-frames`, `--window-mode=hidden|inactive|offscreen|ghost|focused`, `--focus-emulation=false`, `--control-api=true`, `--control-port`, `--headless=true`, `--scenes`, `--autorun`, `--plain`. A misspelled flag fails fast; `--help` prints the full reference and `--version` prints the version. The app control API binds only to loopback, generates a random token at startup and writes it to `/control.json` (0600). Routes and curl examples are in the [App control API](#app-control-api) section below. ### Window and focus modes Measured in Phase 0: | Mode | Behaviour | Recordable | Interactive | |---|---|---|---| | `hidden` (default) | window is never shown | yes | yes with focus emulation | | `hidden` + `--focus-emulation=false` | window is never shown | yes | no, clicks are dropped | | `inactive` | window is shown without taking focus | yes | yes | | `offscreen` | window is shown at (-12000, -12000) | yes | yes | | `ghost` | window is shown with opacity 0 | yes | yes | | `focused` | window is shown and takes focus | yes | yes | Headless mode requires `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled` (on by default), otherwise CDP physical clicks do not take effect. ### malo-browser agent runtime `malo-browser` is the background web-execution layer for agents: one long-lived daemon manages port leases, every agent gets a stable port, and one port can host several isolated sessions. There is no visible window by default; it does not take focus, does not cover the screen and does not switch Spaces. Screenshots are produced only on explicit request or as failure evidence. ```bash npm run daemon # in another terminal curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7410/health cat ~/.malo-browser/broker.json ``` Defaults: broker `127.0.0.1:7410`, lease port pool `7411-7499`, data directory `~/.malo-browser`. A successful start prints one JSON line and writes `~/.malo-browser/broker.json` (0600) with `{endpoint, token, pid}`. Only one daemon may use a data directory: a healthy running instance makes the new process fail loudly, and a stale `broker.json` left by a stopped instance is overwritten. Daemon flags: `--daemon-port=7410`, `--port-min=7411`, `--port-max=7499`, `--lease-ttl-seconds=300`, `--session-idle-seconds=300`, `--max-sessions=4`, `--data-dir=~/.malo-browser`. A new session needs both the lease token and its own session token; a session token from session A cannot read session B (401). `width` / `height` are the page viewport, and the handoff toolbar does not consume them. Sessions without a `profile` are anonymous and are wiped on close; sessions created with `{"profile":"work"}` share that profile's cookies and storage across sessions and daemon restarts. Profile names allow lowercase letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen (max 64 chars). Data lives under `/leases//sessions//{downloads,artifacts}`, profile data under `/chromium`. `delivery-video` is only a visual-output adapter; it does not define the malo-browser kernel boundary. ### Verification scripts - `npm run smoke:malo -- ~/.malo-browser/broker.json http://127.0.0.1:4788` runs the real daemon chain (see also [docs/malo-browser.md](docs/malo-browser.md)). - `npm run smoke:toolbar` builds and drives the handoff toolbar in a hidden window. - `npm run smoke:control -- report-review` talks to an already running control API; set `DEMO_CONTROL_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:7317`) and `DEMO_CONTROL_TOKEN` from `/control.json`. ## Scene scripts Scenes are YAML files at `fixtures/scenes//scene.yaml`, loaded through the `demo://scene//...` protocol, which only serves files inside the scene directory. The field contract is [schemas/scene.schema.json](schemas/scene.schema.json). ### Bundled scenes - `report-review`: the currently usable demo, 7 steps `wait_for -> highlight -> click -> fill -> assert -> spotlight -> annotate`. The page loads as `demo://scene/report-review/index.html`. - `multi-a -> multi-b`: verifies multi-scene switching: 1280x720 switches to 1600x900 through one continuous screencast, and evidence records `run.scene_ids`. - `login-demo`: the full account-login path (see below). Scene actions: `goto`, `login`, `wait`, `wait_for`, `wait_for_presenter`, `click`, `fill`, `press`, `scroll`, `highlight`, `spotlight`, `annotate`, `mask`, `blackout`, `assert`, `scene`, `set`, `note`, `screenshot` (19 actions). ### Target resolution Targeted actions resolve in a fixed order, first match wins: | Priority | Form | Resolved to | |---|---|---| | 1 | `data_demo_id: increment` | `[data-demo-id="increment"]` | | 2 | `selector: ".btn-primary"` | raw CSS selector | | 3 | `text: 金额异常` | text match (rules below) | | 4 | `x: 640` + `y: 360` | viewport point (no selector, last resort) | Text matching picks the smallest **visible** element (not hidden, has size) whose text **contains** the target string, and marks it with a runtime attribute for later commands in the same step. No match, or no target at all, reports `E_SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND` (the message distinguishes "no element contains this text" from "the step has no resolvable click or visual target"). Three special cases do not use `text` as the target: - `fill`: `text` is the input content; the target is `selector` / `data_demo_id` / coordinates, or `target_text` names the element to click. - `annotate`: `text` is the annotation copy; the target must be `selector` / `data_demo_id` / coordinates. - `wait_for`: `text` is the wait condition (wait for text to appear), not a click target. ### Account login The `login` action uses a `0600` account file outside the repository; a scene stores only `account_id`, the password is read from `password_env` at runtime, and the action opens the login page, fills, submits and waits for a success condition. `fixtures/scenes/login-demo` verifies the whole path. The default account file is `~/.config/malo-browser/accounts.json`, overridable with `MALO_BROWSER_ACCOUNTS`. The file must live outside a git worktree, be a regular `0600` file, keep `origin` and `login_url` same-origin, and define `success_selector` or `success_url`; a plaintext `password` field is rejected. Format, security boundary, examples and failure troubleshooting: [docs/accounts.md](docs/accounts.md). ### Scene variables `vars` holds scene-local strings; `${name}` interpolates them into action fields, and `${env:SCENE_NAME}` reads an environment variable from the `SCENE_` namespace only — any other name is rejected, so a third-party scene cannot pull cloud keys or tokens into a URL or form field. ### Validation Scene validation reports every error at once; unknown fields, out-of-range times and missing targets fail before the scene loads. ## Recording and evidence ### Output files A `--mode=record` run writes, per take: ```text evidence/ hidden.mp4 hidden.evidence.json # version, viewport, DPR, frames, duration, SHA256, steps, self-checks hidden.overlay-frame.png # overlay check frame (not written with --plain) hidden.overlay-before.png # same moment before the overlay (not written with --plain) ``` An app-mode take (autorun or control API) writes `/recordings/_/take-01.mp4` plus `take-01.evidence.json`; a failed `assert` step also writes `/errors//step-.png` (other failing actions carry the error, not a screenshot). App-mode evidence and the encoded mp4 are written with mode 0600. The document records `status`, `app`, `scene`, `run` (including `run.scene_ids` for multi-scene takes), `capture`, `video`, `steps`, `checks`, `warnings` and `error` when the take failed. ### Self-checks A `--mode=record` take exits 0 only when every self-check passes: no Node in the window, frames arrived, duration within ±0.5s, 30fps, 1920x1080, black-frame ratio <50%, and the overlay really ended up in the video (skipped for `--plain`). App-mode takes check `frames_arrived`, `steps_completed` and `steps_within_take`; a failed step or a failed check marks the evidence `failed` and the take carries `video.partial`. Failed self-checks raise `E_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH` with the failing check ids. In the autorun path a failed step still stops the recorder first, so the take keeps its video and its failed evidence. ### Failed takes "Failure also has evidence" holds for every entry point: - `--mode=record` writes `/

# DSH ChatGPT Direct

DSH plugin for in-process ChatGPT Codex authorization, model discovery, and account quota. It uses the built-in `llm-pi-ai/openai-codex` transport and DSH credential store. No CLIProxyAPI process is needed for direct sessions.

Install the release package through DSH plugin manager. In Settings → CPA, choose **Add ChatGPT account** to authorize. The plugin adds account-listed models while retaining existing models and the default selection. Select an `openai-codex` model for a conversation to use direct transport. Existing `chatgpt-cpa` sessions remain on their original route until switched.

Quota is an account-level observation, refreshed while the settings page or a direct conversation is visible; it is not a per-model guarantee. Credentials never leave DSH’s credential store except in authorized calls to ChatGPT.

The interface uses layout patterns from the MIT-licensed DSH OpenCode Go plugin; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Model discovery uses the account endpoint with a minimum tested Codex catalog compatibility version of `0.165.0`. When a local Codex model cache is available, only its newer stable `client_version` is used; no cached models, identity or credentials are imported. Machines without Codex use the bundled compatibility baseline.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-choice

A single-choice board inside the DeepSeek Harness chat, next to the built-in `ask_user_question`.

```
ask_user_choice({ title, subtitle?, options, noneLabel? })
```

Every option is **text**, an **image** or a **sound**. The card is posted as a normal chat
row, the user presses the check icon on one row, and the choice comes back as an ordinary
chat message that starts the next turn.

## Behaviour

- **one pick per board** — the check button on the chosen row; other rows become inert;
- **«none of these»** — a trailing row with its label from `noneLabel`;
- sounds and image previews stay usable after the pick;
- **non-blocking** — the tool returns immediately, unlike `ask_user_question`, which waits
  for the answer inside the turn;
- **subagents are refused** — only the main agent can show a board:
  `human interaction is unavailable while the calling agent is owned by another live agent…`.

All visible text (title, subtitle, option titles and descriptions, `noneLabel`) comes from
the agent, in the language of the conversation.

## Card

Rows: a 52 px preview (image thumbnail or ▶ button), the title and description, and the
round check button on the right. Clicking an image opens a lightbox; pressing ▶ plays the
sound with a plain `Audio` object, so there is no extra UI. A pick replaces the drafts
carefully: the composer keeps its text, the choice is sent as its own message.

## Options

```jsonc
{
  "kind": "text",              // required: text | image | audio
  "title": "Keep as is",       // row label
  "description": "…",          // optional second line
  "value": "…",                // text sent to the chat (defaults to title)
  "src": "C:\\sounds\\a.wav"   // image/audio: http(s) URL or absolute local path
}
```

Local files are copied into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-choice\media` and served over loopback.

## Bridge

`127.0.0.1:49236`:

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/status` | port and media counter |
| `GET` | `/media/<file>` | served image or audio |
| `POST` | `/attach` | copy a local file and return its URL |
| `GET` | `/settings` | stored settings (`language`) |
| `POST` | `/settings` | save `language`: `ru`, `en`, `zh` or `auto` |

## Settings

The plugin row config (`plugins.row.config`) holds one control: the interface language —
Русский, English, 中文 or Авто. It is stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-choice\settings.json`
and applies to the card and the form without a restart.

The language is resolved in this order:

1. the saved `language`, when it is `ru`, `en` or `zh`;
2. `auto` — the application language: `document.documentElement.lang`, then
   `navigator.language`; `ru*` → ru, `zh*` → zh, anything else → en;
3. nothing stored — `ru`.

All card text (title, subtitle, option titles and descriptions, `noneLabel`) comes from the
agent, in the language of the conversation; only the plugin's own labels — the pick, play
and open buttons and the settings row — follow the language above.

## Languages

The interface speaks Russian, English and Chinese. The language comes from the
extension setting when it is `ru`, `en` or `zh`; `auto` follows the application
language (`document.documentElement.lang`, then `navigator.language`; `ru*` → ru,
`zh*` → zh, anything else → en); with nothing stored it is `ru`. Change it in
**Plugins → Choice**; the value lives in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-choice\settings.json`
and applies without a restart.

## Screenshots

![Plugin settings](docs/img/settings.jpg)

## Install

```json
"dsh-choice": "github:machine202502/dsh-choice#main"
```

and add `dsh-choice` to `dsh.profile.bundles`. A restart is required for the host half to
load; the client half reloads with the page.

## License

MIT.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-restart

Restart DeepSeek Harness from the interface or with an agent tool — with the option to
continue the same session after the start.

## What it does

| Capability | Where |
|---|---|
| "Restart" button | sidebar footer, next to the account (power icon) |
| Confirmation | a modal with two buttons, no extra options |
| Agent tool | `dsh_restart({ fake })` — for extension development only |
| Session continuation | a restart via the tool opens the session and writes `[auto.continue]` |

## How the restart works

The restarting process cannot be a child of the application: `taskkill /T` kills the whole
tree together with it. So the plugin:

1. writes the marker `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-restart\pending.json`;
2. creates a one-shot scheduler task `DSH-Restart` (Windows) with a helper script;
3. the helper waits 1.5 s, closes the application's process tree, waits 1.8 s, launches the
   `.exe` and deletes the task.

On macOS/Linux a separate `sh` process is used (`kill` + `open`/launch).

## Auto-continue

After the start the client reads the marker through the local bridge `127.0.0.1:49233`:

```
GET  /claim      → { marker } — atomic: only one client receives the marker
POST /restart    → write the marker and restart
GET  /health     → a live-host signal for the watchdog
GET  /settings   → current overrides
POST /settings   → save overrides (no restart)
```

Exactly one page load claims the marker, so double initialization does not produce two
messages. A restart via the tool returns the session with an `[auto.continue]` message: the
client opens the same session, waits for the composer to be ready, inserts the text and
sends it with the send button (Enter is the fallback). The sidebar footer button does not
create a marker and does not continue the session.

The user's draft is not lost: if the field already contains text, it is temporarily stashed
in `localStorage`, `[auto.continue]` is sent, and then the text is returned to the input
field (without being sent). The message queue is session state — the plugin neither reads
nor changes it.

## The tool

The tool exists for developing and debugging DSH itself: a plugin, `cordis.patch.yml`, the
profile. It is not intended for ordinary work, for "refreshing state", or for calls without
a code/config change that needs a fresh process.

```text
dsh_restart { fake: true }
→ Preflight passed; fake restart requested, nothing was restarted.
```

Without `fake` the tool restarts the application and returns the session with an
`[auto.continue]` message. The `fake` flag runs every check but restarts nothing — for
tests. If the tool is disabled, a call from old memory fails with
`unknown tool "dsh_restart"`.

## Plugin settings

On the Plugins → Restart → Configure page:

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Language | Russian | language of the button and the form: Russian, English, Chinese, or "Auto" (follows the application language) |
| The `dsh_restart` command is available to the agent | enabled | when disabled the tool disappears; a call from old memory fails with `unknown tool "dsh_restart"` |
| Watchdog active | enabled | when disabled a restart just closes and opens the application, with no profile rollback |
| Watchdog wait, sec | 10 | how long to wait for a live-start signal before rolling back (1–120) |

Overrides are stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-restart\settings.json`; the values from
`cordis.patch.yml` remain the defaults. Saving settings needs no restart: the tool is
registered and unregistered on the fly, and the interface language is applied immediately.

## Languages

Interface languages: **Russian, English, Chinese**.

- The language comes from the extension setting `language` when it is `ru` / `en` / `zh`.
- `auto` follows the application language: `document.documentElement.lang` first, then
  `navigator.language`; `ru*` → `ru`, `zh*` → `zh`, otherwise `en`.
- The default is `ru`.
- It is changed in the settings form: Plugins → Restart → Configure.
- Overrides are stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-restart\settings.json`.

## When the tool refuses

`dsh_restart` is available to the agent only in "quiet" mode — when a restart will not
disturb anyone:

| Check | Refusal |
|---|---|
| Call from a subagent | `dsh_restart is only available to the main agent: a subagent cannot restart the app; do not retry, report the need to the parent agent instead` |
| Access mode is not Full access | `dsh_restart requires the Full access permission preset (current: …)` |
| Another session or subagent is still working | `dsh_restart refused: N other session(s) or subagent(s) are still working (…)` |
| A background job is still running | `dsh_restart refused: N background job(s) are still running (…)` |

The checks go through `ctx.permissionPresets.current(agent.session)`, `ctx.agents.list()`
and `ctx.jobs.list(agentId)`; a "working" status is `running` or a non-empty agent input
queue. A subagent is detected by `exec.agent.options.subagentDepth` (plus `exec.parent`).

The button in the interface performs none of these checks: the user decides when to restart.

## Limitations

- a **tray** item and an entry in the native **Application** menu cannot be added by the
  plugin: the tray and the menu live in the Electron main process, while the plugin lives
  in a child host process;
- the restart is performed through the Windows Task Scheduler; if policy forbids creating
  tasks, the restart will not work;
- workspace sessions that are executing a turn at that moment will be interrupted (as the
  modal warns).

### The button and the tool behave differently

- **`dsh_restart` (agent)** — always opens the session and writes `[auto.continue]`
  (or `[auto.continue.failed]` if the watchdog rolled the profile back).
- **The "Restart DeepSeek Harness" button in the sidebar** — simply restarts the
  application: no marker is created, the session is not continued, no auto-message is sent.

### Cookies and "Web authentication failed"

Every launch of Desktop Host takes a new port and sets a `dsh-auth-<random>` cookie for
`127.0.0.1`. Chromium stores cookies per host, not per port, so old cookies are not replaced
and accumulate. Measured on a live installation: about 122 such cookies produce a `Cookie`
header of roughly 17.5 KB, it stops fitting into the limit (16 KB), the welcome request
receives `431`, and the application fails with
`desktop welcome: Web authentication failed`. In addition, the lifetime of these cookies is
capped in the profile: `connection.cookieMaxAgeDays: 7`.

Before every launch (after the application is killed, before `Start-Process`) the helper
runs `src/cookie-clean.py` and deletes only the `dsh-auth-*` lines for
`127.0.0.1`/`localhost`. Other cookies are left alone.

If the application did crash on the welcome step (the crash log contains
`Web authentication failed`), the watchdog does not roll the profile back and does not
disable plugins: it cleans the cookies, launches the application once more and waits for a
healthy start.

### Binding the watchdog to a restart

Every restart gets a token:

```
dsh_restart → marker { token, sessionId } + watchdog.json { token }
watchdog  → compares the token in watchdog.json before rolling back
start     → the host deletes watchdog.json (the token is voided)
```

So the watchdog triggers only for the restart that started it, and cannot touch an
application raised later or by another restart.

Before rolling back, the watchdog compares the SHA-256 of `package.json`,
`cordis.patch.yml`, `cordis.yml` with the ones saved at request time. If the files were
changed by hand, no rollback is performed — the human is assumed to have taken over the
edits.

Profile files are written without a BOM (`WriteAllText` + `UTF8Encoding(false)`), otherwise
the host cannot read `package.json`.

### Known limitation: a subagent's job after its completion

If a subagent started a background job and finished its turn, DSH deletes the record of
that job together with the agent, although the job itself keeps running. The pre-restart
check **will not see** such a job and will not refuse the restart.

What is covered:

| Owner of the work | Refusal |
|---|---|
| Own background job | yes |
| A subagent or another session is still working | yes |
| Their jobs, while the owner is alive | yes |
| A subagent's job after its turn finished | no |

Why: the job registry `ctx.jobs` is keyed by agent id and is cleared when the agent is
destroyed; the `jobs.start` wrapper sees only jobs started through that path, while a
subagent starts them differently. Detection by child processes is unreliable: the
application's service processes constantly appear and disappear nearby. The solution is
deferred.

## Screenshots

![Restart dialog](docs/img/settings.jpg)

## Installation

```bash
npx --yes github:machine202502/dsh-restart
```

Or manually:

```json
"dsh-restart": "github:machine202502/dsh-restart#main"
```

and add `dsh-restart` to `dsh.profile.bundles`.

After installation the application needs a restart (you can use the button once it appears).

## Verification

```bash
node tests/smoke.mjs                   # tool, checks, fake, bridge
node tests/load-client.mjs client.js   # the client module loads and returns apply
```

## License

MIT

# dsh-voice-ext

Local **Russian** speech recognition for DeepSeek Harness.

The plugin does not replace the built-in Voice input: it adds a provider to the shared
`ctx.speechToText` service, so the microphone button, recording and text insertion stay stock.

```
microphone button → ctx.speechToText → provider dsh-voice-ext → GigaAM v3 (sherpa-onnx)
```

## Model

[GigaAM v3 CTC](https://github.com/salute-developers/GigaAM) (MIT), ONNX conversion
[sherpa-onnx-nemo-ctc-giga-am-v3-russian](https://huggingface.co/csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-nemo-ctc-giga-am-v3-russian-2025-12-16).

- `model.int8.onnx` — 224,721,476 bytes, SHA-256 is verified after download;
- `tokens.txt` — the model vocabulary;
- default directory: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-voice-ext\models\gigaam-v3`;
- CPU, ~1.1 s for a 5.5-second phrase, no Python and no GPU.

## Settings

Page **Plugins → Voice ext**:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Model directory | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-voice-ext\models\gigaam-v3` | any directory with `model.int8.onnx` and `tokens.txt` |
| CPU threads | 2 | recognizer `numThreads` |
| Download automatically | on | fetch the model at start if it is missing |

Provider and language selection live in Voice input itself (the `speechToText` service);
this plugin declares the languages `ru` and `auto`.

Bridge for the form: `127.0.0.1:49234` — `GET /status`, `POST /settings`, `POST /prepare`.

## Languages

Interface languages: Russian, English, Chinese.

The interface language comes from the `language` extension setting when it is `ru`, `en` or
`zh`. The value `auto` follows the application language: `document.documentElement.lang`, then
`navigator.language`; `ru*` → `ru`, `zh*` → `zh`, otherwise `en`. With no setting at all the
default is `ru`.

The setting is changed in the plugin form **Plugins → Voice ext** and stored in the file
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-voice-ext\settings.json`.

## Profile configuration

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: voice-ext
      name: 'dsh-voice-ext'
      config:
        providerId: dsh-voice-ext
        language: ru
        threads: 2
        autoDownload: true
```

To make the plugin the default provider, name it in the `speech-to-text` entry:

```yaml
- id: speech-to-text
  config:
    defaultProvider: dsh-voice-ext
    language: ru
```

## Screenshots

![Plugin settings](docs/img/settings.jpg)

## Installation

```json
"dsh-voice-ext": "github:machine202502/dsh-voice-ext#main"
```

and add `dsh-voice-ext` to `dsh.profile.bundles`. Installation pulls in
`sherpa-onnx-node@1.13.8` and the platform binary (`sherpa-onnx-win-x64` on Windows).
After a restart the provider is registered; if the model is not found and `autoDownload` is on,
it is downloaded at start (224 MB).

## Testing

```bash
node tests/probe.mjs      # recognizes tests/fixtures/sample-ru-16k.wav directly
node tests/provider.mjs   # registers the provider and recognizes through its API
```

Reference: «Вот мой голос, меня же слышно хорошо» — “Here is my voice, I can be heard well”.

A diagnostic run through the shared service is enabled with `selfTest: <path to wav>`;
the result is written to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-voice-ext\selftest.json`.

## Dependencies

`sherpa-onnx-node@1.13.8` and the platform binary (`sherpa-onnx-win-x64` etc.).

## License

MIT. The GigaAM model is distributed under MIT; the conversion is under the sherpa-onnx
license (Apache-2.0).

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
