# Entire for DeepSeek Harness

A Host-only DSH plugin that exposes the [Entire](https://docs.entire.com/) CLI's feature surface to the agent: sessions, checkpoints, hybrid search, code history, trails, reviews, the `entire-graph` code graph, and a classified passthrough for setup, plugins, accounts, repositories, and the authenticated API.

The plugin reads Entire's data. It also closes the capture loop: in a repository that carries `.entire/dsh-hooks.json`, it forwards DSH session lifecycle events to `entire-agent-dsh`, an external agent binary implementing the [Agent Integration Protocol](https://docs.entire.com/agents/agent-integration-protocol/overview). DSH session start, turns, compaction and session end then become Entire sessions and checkpoints, and commits carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.

## Install

Install from this repository (the release tag is immutable, so the command reproduces the same package contents):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#entire-v0.2.0&path:/plugins/entire"
```

Or install from the repository's plugin index, which the Web **Plugins → Discover** tab
reads; add `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins/main/index.json`
as an index source, then install the version from the card. See
[`docs/plugin-index.md`](../../docs/plugin-index.md).

Or install the local checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin add ./plugins/entire
```

Either way the package is linked from the profile; there is no build step and no runtime dependency. The same address works with the `plugin_manager` tool's `install_bundle`.

Entire must be installed and on `PATH` (`entire --version` should print a version), or set `binary` to its absolute path. Session capture additionally needs `entire-agent-dsh` on `PATH` and `entire agent add dsh` in the target repository.

## Configuration

The bundle patch inserts one row, `entire`. Override its `config` in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `binary` | `entire` | CLI executable name or absolute path. |
| `repoPath` | `""` | Pin a repository/worktree. Empty uses the Session's current directory. |
| `allowWrites` | `false` | Permit repository-scoped mutations after approval. |
| `allowAdmin` | `false` | Permit machine/account/control-plane commands after approval; implies `allowWrites`. |
| `timeoutMs` | `600000` | Default per-call budget. Reads cap lower; review runs cap at 30 minutes. |
| `maxOutputChars` | `24000` | Head/tail truncation budget. |
| `promptSection` | `true` | Add the Entire guidance section to the system prompt. |

A malformed value falls back to its default instead of failing activation.

## Tools

| Tool | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `entire_status` | `status`, `version`, `doctor`, `activity`, `agent-help` |
| `entire_sessions` | `session list/current/info/tokens/stop/attach/adopt/resume` |
| `entire_checkpoints` | `checkpoint list/explain/tokens/delete`, `tokens profile` |
| `entire_search` | `search` work and `--code` search |
| `entire_history` | `blame`, `why`, `experts`, `recap`, `dispatch` |
| `entire_trails` | trail list/show/approvals/findings/create/update/comment/approve/link/unlink/checkout/resume/merge |
| `entire_review` | `review` run/list/agents/models/findings/configure |
| `entire_graph` | graph query/neighbors/impact/def/explain/context/commit/diff/checkpoint/capabilities/health/agent-guide/setup/index/verify |
| `entire_run` | Remaining CLI commands and `entire api`, with read/write/admin classification |

Every command also accepts `--help` through `entire_run`.

## Permissions

Reads never prompt. Two gates control everything else:

- `allowWrites` — `session stop/attach/adopt/resume`, `checkpoint delete` (when `dryRun:false`), trail writes, `review run/configure`, `graph setup/index/verify`, and task-driven `entire_run` commands.
- `allowAdmin` — `enable`/`disable`/`configure`/`clean`, agent/plugin/auth/org/project/repo/cluster commands, non-GET API calls, and unrecognized commands. It implies writes.

Enabled actions still ask through the Harness approval pipeline. When approval support is absent, the ask becomes a denial. A disabled gate returns a message naming the exact config key.

Dangerous defaults are deliberate: `checkpoint delete` and `trail merge` run as dry runs until the caller passes `dryRun: false`. `graph verify` executes the test command it is given and is treated as a write. `entire_run` refuses interactive logins, `entire mcp`, and shell completion.

The executor uses `execFile` with an explicit argv — never a shell — closes stdin so prompts cannot hang, kills on timeout/cancellation, and truncates large output with an explicit marker.

## Examples

```json
{"action": "status"}
{"action": "info", "sessionId": "019ed5fe-ec49-7a72-89fd-f38e323f5448"}
{"action": "explain", "target": "a1b2c3d4e5f6", "short": true}
{"action": "blame", "file": "src/auth.go", "line": "42"}
{"action": "query", "query": "where is the token refresh implemented?"}
{"action": "list", "project": "gh/acme"}
```

```json
{"argv": ["plugin", "list"]}
{"argv": ["api", "/api/v1/clusters"]}
```

## Limitations

- Web-only Entire surfaces (CI checks, gates, mirrors, Brain) are reachable only through their REST endpoints via `entire_run` + `entire api`; they are not modeled as typed actions.
- Entire's keyring and network access must be available to the Host process. A sandboxed environment can block both; the plugin reports that rather than treating it as a logout.
- JSON payloads are passed through, not modeled, so a changed Entire response shape is visible to the agent instead of breaking the plugin.
- No Web UI panel: capability is model-facing only.

## Capture (DSH sessions into Entire)

Entire cannot see DSH sessions on its own. This plugin closes the loop: in a
repository that carries \`.entire/dsh-hooks.json\` (written by
\`entire-agent-dsh install-hooks\`, which \`entire agent add dsh\` runs), the
plugin forwards session-start, turn, compaction and session-end events to
\`entire hooks dsh <hook>\`. The external agent binary \`entire-agent-dsh\` on
\`PATH\` normalizes each payload through the Entire Agent Integration Protocol.

The effect: DSH sessions show up in \`entire session list\`, each turn produces a
checkpoint, and commits carry an \`Entire-Checkpoint\` trailer, so
\`entire checkpoint list/explain\`, \`blame\`, \`why\` and \`search\` work.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| \`capture\` | \`true\` | Forward DSH session lifecycle events to \`entire hooks dsh\`. |
| \`captureMarker\` | \`.entire/dsh-hooks.json\` | Repository marker that scopes capture; empty means every repository. |
| \`captureTimeoutMs\` | \`10000\` | Timeout for one forwarded hook call. |

Capture is inert where the marker is missing, and it needs \`entire-agent-dsh\`
on \`PATH\` (install it, then \`entire agent add dsh\` per repository).

## Tests

```sh
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

# DSH Plugins

Custom **skills and plugins** for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/sredevopsorg), maintained by [sredevopsorg](https://github.com/sredevopsorg).

The repository publishes two things:

- **Skills** — `SKILL.md` instruction bundles packaged by the **skills plugin** under [`plugins/skills/skills/`](plugins/skills/skills/). Install that one plugin and every skill is registered; [`install.sh`](install.sh) remains a legacy/manual symlink alternative.
- **DSH plugins** — self-contained bundles under [`plugins/`](plugins/), installed from this repository's release tags **or** browsed from the repository's [plugin market index](#the-plugin-index-discover).

| Kind | What it is | Where it lives here |
|---|---|---|
| **Skill** | A `SKILL.md` (or flat `<name>.md`) instruction bundle loaded on demand by the model or with `/name`. Skills are packaged and served by a DSH skill-provider plugin. | [`plugins/skills/skills/`](plugins/skills/skills/) |
| **Plugin** | A Cordis plugin package loaded into a DSH profile (`dsh plugin …`). | [`plugins/`](plugins/) |
| **Tool** | A model-facing tool registered by a plugin via `ctx.tools`, shipped inside a plugin package. | [`plugins/entire/`](plugins/entire/) |

The repository also publishes [`index.json`](index.json), a **format-1 plugin market index** that [@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) reads in the Web **Plugins → Discover** tab.

> Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` **0.2.x**, currently **`0.2.2-rc.1`**. The CLI version gate is strict, so check `dsh --version` before reporting plugin issues. Bundle patches are checked against the installed DSH by `scripts/validate-bundles.mjs`.

---

## Contents

### Skills

All nine skills ship in the single [`skills`](plugins/skills/README.md) plugin. Install it
(see [Installing the skills](#installing-the-skills)) and the catalog lists every row below.

| Skill | Surface | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| [`software-architecture`](plugins/skills/skills/software-architecture/SKILL.md) | model + user | Choosing the simplest sufficient design, patterns to apply or skip, engineering practices, tool/skill selection |
| [`fullstack-development`](plugins/skills/skills/fullstack-development/SKILL.md) | model + user | Container-based Python and Node.js/TypeScript backends, frontends, monorepos, Docker, e2e testing |
| [`supabase`](plugins/skills/skills/supabase/SKILL.md) | model + user | Anything touching Supabase: DB, Auth, Edge Functions, Realtime, Storage, CLI, MCP, logs, debugging |
| [`supabase-postgres-best-practices`](plugins/skills/skills/supabase-postgres-best-practices/SKILL.md) | model + user | Postgres schema, migrations, RLS, indexes, locking, query plans — load *before* touching a database |
| [`ghost-theme-development`](plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-development/SKILL.md) | model + user | Authoring Ghost Handlebars themes: templates, contexts, helpers, settings, routing, GScan |
| [`ghost-theme-modern-frontend`](plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/SKILL.md) | model + user | Wiring a Ghost theme to Vite, Tailwind CSS, and React/Vue/Svelte islands |
| [`helm-chart-development`](plugins/skills/skills/helm-chart-development/SKILL.md) | model + user | Creating, editing and improving Helm charts: templates, values.yaml, helpers, hooks, CRDs, subcharts |
| [`kubernetes-kubectl-operations`](plugins/skills/skills/kubernetes-kubectl-operations/SKILL.md) | model + user | Safe kubectl operations, cluster triage, and opt-in Kubernetes MCP inspection |
| [`github-actions-security-audit`](plugins/skills/skills/github-actions-security-audit/SKILL.md) | model + user | Auditing and hardening GitHub Actions workflows: token permissions, script injection, `pull_request_target`, action pinning, runners, supply chain |

### Plugins and tools

| Plugin | Kind | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| [`code-editor`](plugins/code-editor/README.md) | bundle + web editor | Browsing a Session's workspace and editing UTF-8 files from a right-sidebar tab, with sandbox-aware saves and optimistic conflict detection |
| [`entire`](plugins/entire/README.md) | bundle + tool | Reading Entire sessions, checkpoints, search, trails, and code history, plus capturing DSH sessions as Entire checkpoints |
| [`peak-rate-footer`](plugins/peak-rate-footer/README.md) | bundle + web footer | A green/orange footer showing whether DeepSeek API usage is currently billed at peak or off-peak rates, with a local clock, next-change countdown, and in-footer time-zone picker |
| [`skills`](plugins/skills/README.md) | bundle + 9 skills | Installing every skill in this repository as one plugin: a packaged skill provider serving the architecture, fullstack, Supabase/Postgres, Ghost theme, Helm, Kubernetes, and GitHub Actions skills |
| [`superagent`](plugins/superagent/README.md) | bundle + web panel | A vendored fork of DeepSeek Harness's `dsh-superagent` research prototype: a proactive agent for one GitHub repository (optionally Feishu) that runs tickets in their own DSH sessions and answers in the original conversation |

```
    │   ├── lib/                           # committed build output — what a Git install ships
    │   ├── prompts/, skills/, docs/       # executor prompts, its own two skills, numbered docs
    │   ├── locale/en.json, icon.svg, NOTICE.md, LICENSE
    │   └── README.md
    └── skills/
        ├── package.json                   # name, license, exports, dsh.bundle.patch, files: skills
        ├── cordis.patch.yml               # inserts the host-wide skill-provider row
        ├── index.js                       # provider: discovers/parses/serves packaged skills
        ├── test/skills.test.mjs           # provider + frontmatter tests (node --test)
        ├── locale/en.json
        ├── icon.svg
        ├── README.md
        └── skills/                        # the 9 packaged skills — add new skills here
            ├── software-architecture/SKILL.md
            ├── fullstack-development/SKILL.md
            ├── supabase/{SKILL.md,references/,assets/}
            ├── supabase-postgres-best-practices/{SKILL.md,references/}
            ├── ghost-theme-development/{SKILL.md,references/}
            ├── ghost-theme-modern-frontend/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/}
            ├── kubernetes-kubectl-operations/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/}
            ├── helm-chart-development/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/}
            └── github-actions-security-audit/SKILL.md
```

A skill directory may carry any supporting files — `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` — because the whole directory is the skill's resource base. That directory is also what `npm pack` ships: a repository skill outside `plugins/skills/skills` is not installable and fails [`scripts/validate-skills.mjs`](scripts/validate-skills.mjs).

---

## Requirements

- **DSH** — `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh …`, or a global `dsh` install (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`). The Discover flow additionally needs the experimental **Custom plugin indexes** bundle (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle`), enabled from the Web Plugins page.
- **Node.js ≥ 18** and **npm/npx** — for the Ghost and Helm toolchain scripts, `npx gscan`, and the optional Kubernetes MCP server (`npx -y kubernetes-mcp-server@latest`).
- **Ghost 6.x + `gscan`** — only for the two Ghost theme skills.
- **Helm 3+** — only for `helm-chart-development`. No cluster or network needed;
  `scripts/verify-chart.mjs` shells out to `helm lint` and `helm template`.
- **`kubectl` + a kubeconfig** — only for `kubernetes-kubectl-operations`. The skill
  inspects and, with explicit confirmation, changes a cluster;
  `scripts/verify-kube-access.sh` is a read-only preflight and accepts
  `--kubeconfig <path>`. Set `KUBERNETES_MCP_KUBECONFIG` to an absolute path for a
  dedicated, preferably read-only kubeconfig; when the optional Kubernetes MCP row is
  enabled, it passes that value to the server as `KUBECONFIG`. Without it, the server
  uses `KUBECONFIG` or `~/.kube/config`.
- **Entire CLI** (`entire`) on `PATH` — only for the `entire` plugin. It records agent sessions and
  checkpoints and backs every tool; session capture additionally needs the `entire-agent-dsh`
  binary and `entire agent add dsh` in the target repository. Search, trails, and recap also need
  an authenticated login and OS keyring access.
- **`git`** and **`pnpm` 9 or newer** — only when installing DSH plugin packages from this
  repository (`dsh plugin …` forwards to pnpm; `path:` subdirectory installs need pnpm 9).
  No npm publish is involved. `superagent` also fetches its two runtime dependencies
  (`zod`, `proper-lockfile`) from the npm registry.
- **A DSH Web profile** — only for the Web plugins: the built-in right Sidebar for
  `code-editor`, whose browser bundle contributes a right-sidebar tab and whose Host half
  serves the browser-only workspace write endpoint, and the built-in bottom frame seat for
  `peak-rate-footer`, whose Client module contributes the rate-status footer.
- **Node.js 22.19+ or 24+, `git`, GitHub CLI 2.48+, `tmux`, and Python 3.8+** — only for the
  [`superagent`](plugins/superagent/README.md) fork, whose managed-service script and
  executor sessions need them. It requires a Web profile (the management panel is a web
  plugin) and its own `stateDir` configuration; `SETUP.md` in the plugin drives the
  deployment. Its optional session capture additionally needs the `entire` plugin in the
  same profile and `entire agent add dsh` in the target repository — see
  [`docs/entire-dsh-audit.md`](docs/entire-dsh-audit.md) for the current root causes.

---

## Installing the skills

Every skill is packaged in one plugin, [`plugins/skills`](plugins/skills/README.md). Its
bundle patch inserts one host-wide row, and that row registers a skill provider on
`ctx.skills` that discovers and serves the packaged `plugins/skills/skills/` directory.
Installing the plugin is the supported path: no filesystem root to configure and no
per-skill symlink to maintain.

### Option A — install the skills plugin (recommended)

From this local checkout:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/skills
```

Or from the pinned GitHub release (the tag is immutable, so the contents are reproducible;
quote the `&` or the shell will split it):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#skills-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/skills"
```

Or add the repository's [plugin index](#the-plugin-index-discover) source once and install
the version from the **Discover** card. `dsh --profile web list` shows the installed
package and `dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes the tree without booting. Restart a
running DSH after installing; the skill catalog is built at startup.

The packaged provider uses the standard bundled rank `600` and `source: bundled`. A
project-local or user filesystem root still wins duplicate-name precedence (ranks 100–500),
so a project can override a packaged skill of the same name.

### Option B — `install.sh` (legacy/manual alternative)

For setups that cannot install a plugin, [`install.sh`](install.sh) links the same packaged
skills from `plugins/skills/skills/` into a DSH filesystem root:

```bash
./install.sh                                   # all skills -> ~/.dsh/skills
./install.sh --project /path/to/your/project   # -> <project>/.dsh/skills (rank 100)
./install.sh ghost-theme-development \         # only a subset
             ghost-theme-modern-frontend
./install.sh --dry-run                         # show what would change
./install.sh --uninstall                       # detach again
```

It links each skill by symlink, skips anything that is not a managed link, and refuses to
overwrite real files. After installing into the user root, restart DSH so the catalog is
rebuilt. A user-root link has rank 400, which beats the packaged provider's rank 600, so
`--uninstall` hands a skill back to the plugin.

### Option C — manual symlinks

```bash
# into a project (rank 100)
PROJECT=/path/to/your/project
mkdir -p "$PROJECT/.dsh/skills"
for d in plugins/skills/skills/*/; do
  [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] || continue
  ln -sfn "$PWD/${d%/}" "$PROJECT/.dsh/skills/$(basename "$d")"
done

# or into the user root (rank 400), available from every project
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/skills
for d in "$PWD"/plugins/skills/skills/*/; do
  [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] || continue
  ln -sfn "${d%/}" ~/.dsh/skills/
done
```

### Option D — configure `customSkillDirs`

Point the filesystem provider at the packaged skills directory in your profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
  config:
    customSkillDirs:
      - /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugins/plugins/skills/skills
```

The provider watches roots, so new, renamed, or deleted skills appear without restarting
DSH. **Restart DSH** after changing `customSkillDirs` itself, since that is plugin
configuration.

### Using a skill

- **Model-invoked** — skills with `modelInvocable` appear in the session catalog; the agent calls the `skill` tool with the exact kebab-case name before acting.
- **User-invoked** — type `/` in the composer and pick a skill, or type `/software-architecture` directly.

`install.sh` deliberately skips `docs/ghost-themes.md` and any `_`- or `.`-prefixed entry, so repository documentation is never registered as a skill.

---

## Installing plugins

Every plugin under [`plugins/`](plugins/) ships as a self-contained DSH bundle (two are
no-toolchain plain ESM; the forked `superagent` commits its build output). Two install paths
resolve to the same package:

### From Discover (plugin index)

Add the repository's index once; **Discover** then lists every published plugin version and
installs it after confirmation:

1. Open **Plugins** in the Web sidebar and switch on **Custom plugin indexes** under
   **Experimental plugins**.
2. Select **Discover → Add index source** and enter:

   ```
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins/main/index.json
   ```

3. Pick a plugin and version and confirm the install. Each entry pins its exact Git commit.

The index and its maintenance are documented in [`docs/plugin-index.md`](docs/plugin-index.md).

### From a pinned GitHub release tag

The same package installs with pnpm's Git subdirectory parameter, pinned to an immutable
release tag:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#entire-v0.2.0&path:/plugins/entire"
```

Quote the spec: the shell must not interpret `&`. Replace `web` with your profile.
`dsh --profile web list` shows the installed package, and
`dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes the tree without booting.

Requirements, full-URL and commit-pinned variants, update/uninstall commands,
and troubleshooting are in
[`docs/installing-plugins-from-github.md`](docs/installing-plugins-from-github.md).
For local development, install a checkout instead:
`dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/entire`.

---

## Quick start — Ghost theme toolchain

`scaffold-theme.mjs` generates a GScan-clean theme wired for Vite, optional Tailwind, and optional React islands. It needs only plain Node ≥ 18.

```bash
# Scaffold a Vite + Tailwind + React-islands theme
node plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/scaffold-theme.mjs \
  --name my-theme --out ./themes --react

cd themes/my-theme
npm install
npm run build
npm test          # build + GScan

# Fuller pre-flight: build → GScan → zip → archive assertions
bash "$OLDPWD/plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/verify-theme.sh" .
```

```bash
node plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/scaffold-theme.mjs --help
```

Flags: `--name`, `--out`, `--react`, `--no-tailwind`, `--force`.

---

## Authoring a skill

Create `plugins/skills/skills/<kebab-case-name>/SKILL.md` (directory bundle) or `plugins/skills/skills/<kebab-case-name>.md` (flat file). A directory bundle may include any supporting files; nested `**/SKILL.md` files are **not** discovered.

Skills **must** live inside the packaged plugin. `scripts/validate-skills.mjs` fails when a
`SKILL.md` exists anywhere outside `plugins/skills/skills` (including a resurrected
top-level `skills/`), when the package manifest does not ship the skills directory, when
`npm pack --dry-run` would omit a packaged skill file, or when two skills share a name.
That is what keeps "every new or edited skill" inside the single installable plugin.

Frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill                     # required — must match the kebab-case directory/file name
description: >-                    # required — shown in the catalog, capped (~500 chars)
  One paragraph on what the skill does and when it should trigger.
whenToUse: >-                      # optional — extra routing guidance
  Use when …
metadata:                          # optional, free-form
  author: sredevopsorg
  version: "1.0.0"
disable-model-invocation: false    # optional — keep out of model-facing catalogs
user-invocable: true               # optional — keep out of `/` commands
---
# Skill title

Instructions…
```

Rules the skill provider enforces (identical to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` and the packaged provider in `plugins/skills/index.js`):

- `name` and `description` are mandatory; a skill missing either is dropped.
- `*invocable` keys accept YAML booleans and `true/false`, `yes/no`, `on/off`, `1/0`. A rejected spelling drops the **whole skill** with a warning.
- Prefer `disable-model-invocation: true` for human-only workflows and `user-invocable: false` for model-only ones.
- Keep `description` trigger-focused — it is the only thing the model sees before loading the body.

Conventions used in this repo:

- One skill per concern; put long material in `references/` and load it from `SKILL.md`.
- Frontmatter first line, fenced by `---`; no BOM, no leading blank line.
- The `name` must match its directory (or flat-file) name exactly — `scripts/validate-skills.mjs` enforces this.
- Skills live only in `plugins/skills/skills/`; the packaged provider serves them, so there is nothing to copy or symlink.
- Scripts live in `scripts/`, are dependency-light, and document `--help`.
- Cite upstream sources in the body when guidance is derived from official docs.

After adding or editing a skill, run `node scripts/validate-skills.mjs` and
`cd plugins/skills && npm test` before committing; see [Verifying](#verifying).

---

## Plugins and tools

A DSH plugin is an npm package that Cordis loads; a **bundle** additionally declares its patch layer:

```json
{
  "name": "@sredevopsorg/dsh-<name>",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": { ".": "./index.js" },
  "engines": { "dsh": "^0.2.1-rc.2" },
  "dsh": {
    "manifestVersion": 1,
    "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" }
  }
}
```

`engines.dsh` is the compatibility gate the installer, the market index, and the launcher enforce; omit it and an unsupported DSH version installs silently and fails later at activation. A bundle that only adds configuration needs no `index.js` or `.` export — declare the patch, plus `./package.json`, `./locale/*.json`, and `./icon.svg` for management and market display.

Install and select it into a profile — from Discover, from GitHub with a pi

# DeepSeek rate footer

A DSH Web profile bundle that adds a slim footer to the bottom of the Web GUI
showing whether DeepSeek API usage is billed at **peak** or **off-peak** rates.
The footer is green for off-peak and orange for peak.

It also shows the current local time and the next rate change, and lets you pick
the clock's time zone directly in the footer.

## What it does

- Evaluates DeepSeek's UTC schedule on every tick:
  - peak: `01:00-04:00` and `06:00-10:00` UTC, Monday through Friday,
    excluding Chinese public holidays;
  - off-peak: every other hour, including weekends and Chinese public holidays
    in full.
- Shows a green **Off-peak rates** bar or an orange **Peak rates** bar.
- Labels an off-peak weekend or Chinese public holiday, so an off-peak result
  inside a peak window is easy to understand.
- Shows the current time in the selected zone and a countdown to the next rate
  change (`Peak in 2h 14m`, `Off-peak in 3d 6h`, and similar).
- Lets you change the clock's IANA time zone from the selector beside the clock.
  The choice is stored in this browser's `localStorage`; the default follows the
  browser's local zone. The rate calculation itself always uses UTC.
- Follows the light/dark theme with DSH theme tokens and registers no Host route,
  tool, prompt section, or session event.

## Install

From a pinned release:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#peak-rate-footer-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/peak-rate-footer"
```

Or from a local checkout:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/peak-rate-footer
```

Refresh the Web GUI after installing. The plugin occupies the built-in
`shell.bottom` seat and appears immediately.

## Configuration

The clock's time zone is selected in the footer itself. Use the browser's local
zone (the default), UTC, or any IANA zone supported by the browser. The footer
stores the choice under `dsh-peak-rate-footer.timeZone` in `localStorage`.

The rate schedule is not configurable: it follows DeepSeek's published rule at
<https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/>.

### Holiday data

The bundle includes Chinese public holiday ranges for 2025, 2026, and 2027 from
the State Council notices:

- 2025: [国务院办公厅关于2025年部分节假日安排的通知](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202411/content_6986383.htm)
- 2026: [国务院办公厅关于2026年部分节假日安排的通知](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/202511/content_7047090.htm)
- 2027: [国务院办公厅关于2027年部分节假日安排的通知](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/202611/content_7085101.htm)

Adjusted make-up workdays are irrelevant to the rate schedule: those dates are
weekends, and weekends are already off-peak. After 2027, update `HOLIDAY_RANGES`
in [`client.js`](client.js) when the next State Council notice is published.

## Development

```sh
npm test        # schedule, holiday, transition, and time-zone tests
npm run check   # node --check on the package entry points and tests
```

The package is authored in this directory and installed with
`dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/peak-rate-footer`; the profile patch is
never edited by hand.

# DSH Plugins

Custom **skills and plugins** for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/sredevopsorg), maintained by [sredevopsorg](https://github.com/sredevopsorg).

The repository publishes two things:

- **Skills** — `SKILL.md` instruction bundles packaged by the **skills plugin** under [`plugins/skills/skills/`](plugins/skills/skills/). Install that one plugin and every skill is registered; [`install.sh`](install.sh) remains a legacy/manual symlink alternative.
- **DSH plugins** — self-contained bundles under [`plugins/`](plugins/), installed from this repository's release tags **or** browsed from the repository's [plugin market index](#the-plugin-index-discover).

| Kind | What it is | Where it lives here |
|---|---|---|
| **Skill** | A `SKILL.md` (or flat `<name>.md`) instruction bundle loaded on demand by the model or with `/name`. Skills are packaged and served by a DSH skill-provider plugin. | [`plugins/skills/skills/`](plugins/skills/skills/) |
| **Plugin** | A Cordis plugin package loaded into a DSH profile (`dsh plugin …`). | [`plugins/`](plugins/) |
| **Tool** | A model-facing tool registered by a plugin via `ctx.tools`, shipped inside a plugin package. | [`plugins/entire/`](plugins/entire/) |

The repository also publishes [`index.json`](index.json), a **format-1 plugin market index** that [@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) reads in the Web **Plugins → Discover** tab.

> Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` **0.2.x**, currently **`0.2.2-rc.1`**. The CLI version gate is strict, so check `dsh --version` before reporting plugin issues. Bundle patches are checked against the installed DSH by `scripts/validate-bundles.mjs`.

---

### Plugins and tools

```
    │   ├── package.json                   # name, license, exports, dsh.bundle.patch, dsh.client
    │   ├── cordis.patch.yml               # inserts the Host row whose Client half fills shell.bottom
    │   ├── index.js                       # empty Host half; the Client module owns rendering
    │   ├── client.js                      # schedule, holiday data, local clock, time-zone picker
    │   ├── test/schedule.test.mjs         # peak/holiday/transition/time-zone tests (node --test)
    │   ├── locale/en.json, locale/es.json, locale/zh.json
    │   ├── icon.svg
    │   └── README.md
    ├── superagent/                        # vendored fork of deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype
    │   ├── package.json                   # @sredevopsorg/dsh-superagent, build + bundle patch
    │   ├── cordis.patch.yml               # plugin rows and worker/router agent presets
    │   ├── src/                           # TypeScript source (91 modules)
    │   ├── tests/                         # vitest suites
    │   ├── lib/                           # committed build output — what a Git install ships
    │   ├── prompts/, skills/, docs/       # executor prompts, its own two skills, numbered docs
    │   ├── locale/en.json, icon.svg, NOTICE.md, LICENSE
    │   └── README.md
    └── skills/
        ├── package.json                   # name, license, exports, dsh.bundle.patch, files: skills
        ├── cordis.patch.yml               # inserts the host-wide skill-provider row
        ├── index.js                       # provider: discovers/parses/serves packaged skills
        ├── test/skills.test.mjs           # provider + frontmatter tests (node --test)
        ├── locale/en.json
        ├── icon.svg
        ├── README.md
        └── skills/                        # the 9 packaged skills — add new skills here
            ├── software-architecture/SKILL.md
            ├── fullstack-development/SKILL.md
            ├── supabase/{SKILL.md,references/,assets/}
            ├── supabase-postgres-best-practices/{SKILL.md,references/}
            ├── ghost-theme-development/{SKILL.md,references/}
            ├── ghost-theme-modern-frontend/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/}
            ├── kubernetes-kubectl-operations/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/}
            ├── helm-chart-development/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/}
            └── github-actions-security-audit/SKILL.md
```

A skill directory may carry any supporting files — `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` — because the whole directory is the skill's resource base. That directory is also what `npm pack` ships: a repository skill outside `plugins/skills/skills` is not installable and fails [`scripts/validate-skills.mjs`](scripts/validate-skills.mjs).

---

## Requirements

- **DSH** — `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh …`, or a global `dsh` install (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`). The Discover flow additionally needs the experimental **Custom plugin indexes** bundle (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle`), enabled from the Web Plugins page.
- **Node.js ≥ 18** and **npm/npx** — for the Ghost and Helm toolchain scripts, `npx gscan`, and the optional Kubernetes MCP server (`npx -y kubernetes-mcp-server@latest`).
- **Ghost 6.x + `gscan`** — only for the two Ghost theme skills.
- **Helm 3+** — only for `helm-chart-development`. No cluster or network needed;
  `scripts/verify-chart.mjs` shells out to `helm lint` and `helm template`.
- **`kubectl` + a kubeconfig** — only for `kubernetes-kubectl-operations`. The skill
  inspects and, with explicit confirmation, changes a cluster;
  `scripts/verify-kube-access.sh` is a read-only preflight and accepts
  `--kubeconfig <path>`. Set `KUBERNETES_MCP_KUBECONFIG` to an absolute path for a
  dedicated, preferably read-only kubeconfig; when the optional Kubernetes MCP row is
  enabled, it passes that value to the server as `KUBECONFIG`. Without it, the server
  uses `KUBECONFIG` or `~/.kube/config`.
- **Entire CLI** (`entire`) on `PATH` — only for the `entire` plugin. It records agent sessions and
  checkpoints and backs every tool; session capture additionally needs the `entire-agent-dsh`
  binary and `entire agent add dsh` in the target repository. Search, trails, and recap also need
  an authenticated login and OS keyring access.
- **`git`** and **`pnpm` 9 or newer** — only when installing DSH plugin packages from this
  repository (`dsh plugin …` forwards to pnpm; `path:` subdirectory installs need pnpm 9).
  No npm publish is involved. `superagent` also fetches its two runtime dependencies
  (`zod`, `proper-lockfile`) from the npm registry.
- **A DSH Web profile** — only for the Web plugins: the built-in right Sidebar for
  `code-editor`, whose browser bundle contributes a right-sidebar tab and whose Host half
  serves the browser-only workspace write endpoint, and the built-in bottom frame seat for
  `peak-rate-footer`, whose Client module contributes the rate-status footer.
- **Node.js 22.19+ or 24+, `git`, GitHub CLI 2.48+, `tmux`, and Python 3.8+** — only for the
  [`superagent`](plugins/superagent/README.md) fork, whose managed-service script and
  executor sessions need them. It requires a Web profile (the management panel is a web
  plugin) and its own `stateDir` configuration; `SETUP.md` in the plugin drives the
  deployment. Its optional session capture additionally needs the `entire` plugin in the
  same profile and `entire agent add dsh` in the target repository — see
  [`docs/entire-dsh-audit.md`](docs/entire-dsh-audit.md) for the current root causes.

---

## Installing the skills

Every skill is packaged in one plugin, [`plugins/skills`](plugins/skills/README.md). Its
bundle patch inserts one host-wide row, and that row registers a skill provider on
`ctx.skills` that discovers and serves the packaged `plugins/skills/skills/` directory.
Installing the plugin is the supported path: no filesystem root to configure and no
per-skill symlink to maintain.

### Option A — install the skills plugin (recommended)

From this local checkout:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/skills
```

Or from the pinned GitHub release (the tag is immutable, so the contents are reproducible;
quote the `&` or the shell will split it):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#skills-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/skills"
```

Or add the repository's [plugin index](#the-plugin-index-discover) source once and install
the version from the **Discover** card. `dsh --profile web list` shows the installed
package and `dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes the tree without booting. Restart a
running DSH after installing; the skill catalog is built at startup.

The packaged provider uses the standard bundled rank `600` and `source: bundled`. A
project-local or user filesystem root still wins duplicate-name precedence (ranks 100–500),
so a project can override a packaged skill of the same name.

### Option B — `install.sh` (legacy/manual alternative)

For setups that cannot install a plugin, [`install.sh`](install.sh) links the same packaged
skills from `plugins/skills/skills/` into a DSH filesystem root:

```bash
./install.sh                                   # all skills -> ~/.dsh/skills
./install.sh --project /path/to/your/project   # -> <project>/.dsh/skills (rank 100)
./install.sh ghost-theme-development \         # only a subset
             ghost-theme-modern-frontend
./install.sh --dry-run                         # show what would change
./install.sh --uninstall                       # detach again
```

It links each skill by symlink, skips anything that is not a managed link, and refuses to
overwrite real files. After installing into the user root, restart DSH so the catalog is
rebuilt. A user-root link has rank 400, which beats the packaged provider's rank 600, so
`--uninstall` hands a skill back to the plugin.

### Option C — manual symlinks

```bash
# into a project (rank 100)
PROJECT=/path/to/your/project
mkdir -p "$PROJECT/.dsh/skills"
for d in plugins/skills/skills/*/; do
  [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] || continue
  ln -sfn "$PWD/${d%/}" "$PROJECT/.dsh/skills/$(basename "$d")"
done

# or into the user root (rank 400), available from every project
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/skills
for d in "$PWD"/plugins/skills/skills/*/; do
  [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] || continue
  ln -sfn "${d%/}" ~/.dsh/skills/
done
```

### Option D — configure `customSkillDirs`

Point the filesystem provider at the packaged skills directory in your profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
  config:
    customSkillDirs:
      - /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugins/plugins/skills/skills
```

The provider watches roots, so new, renamed, or deleted skills appear without restarting
DSH. **Restart DSH** after changing `customSkillDirs` itself, since that is plugin
configuration.

### Using a skill

- **Model-invoked** — skills with `modelInvocable` appear in the session catalog; the agent calls the `skill` tool with the exact kebab-case name before acting.
- **User-invoked** — type `/` in the composer and pick a skill, or type `/software-architecture` directly.

`install.sh` deliberately skips `docs/ghost-themes.md` and any `_`- or `.`-prefixed entry, so repository documentation is never registered as a skill.

---

## Installing plugins

Every plugin under [`plugins/`](plugins/) ships as a self-contained DSH bundle (two are
no-toolchain plain ESM; the forked `superagent` commits its build output). Two install paths
resolve to the same package:

### From Discover (plugin index)

Add the repository's index once; **Discover** then lists every published plugin version and
installs it after confirmation:

1. Open **Plugins** in the Web sidebar and switch on **Custom plugin indexes** under
   **Experimental plugins**.
2. Select **Discover → Add index source** and enter:

   ```
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins/main/index.json
   ```

3. Pick a plugin and version and confirm the install. Each entry pins its exact Git commit.

The index and its maintenance are documented in [`docs/plugin-index.md`](docs/plugin-index.md).

### From a pinned GitHub release tag

The same package installs with pnpm's Git subdirectory parameter, pinned to an immutable
release tag:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#entire-v0.2.0&path:/plugins/entire"
```

Quote the spec: the shell must not interpret `&`. Replace `web` with your profile.
`dsh --profile web list` shows the installed package, and
`dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes the tree without booting.

Requirements, full-URL and commit-pinned variants, update/uninstall commands,
and troubleshooting are in
[`docs/installing-plugins-from-github.md`](docs/installing-plugins-from-github.md).
For local development, install a checkout instead:
`dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/entire`.

---

## Quick start — Ghost theme toolchain

`scaffold-theme.mjs` generates a GScan-clean theme wired for Vite, optional Tailwind, and optional React islands. It needs only plain Node ≥ 18.

```bash
# Scaffold a Vite + Tailwind + React-islands theme
node plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/scaffold-theme.mjs \
  --name my-theme --out ./themes --react

cd themes/my-theme
npm install
npm run build
npm test          # build + GScan

# Fuller pre-flight: build → GScan → zip → archive assertions
bash "$OLDPWD/plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/verify-theme.sh" .
```

```bash
node plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/scaffold-theme.mjs --help
```

Flags: `--name`, `--out`, `--react`, `--no-tailwind`, `--force`.

---

## Authoring a skill

Create `plugins/skills/skills/<kebab-case-name>/SKILL.md` (directory bundle) or `plugins/skills/skills/<kebab-case-name>.md` (flat file). A directory bundle may include any supporting files; nested `**/SKILL.md` files are **not** discovered.

Skills **must** live inside the packaged plugin. `scripts/validate-skills.mjs` fails when a
`SKILL.md` exists anywhere outside `plugins/skills/skills` (including a resurrected
top-level `skills/`), when the package manifest does not ship the skills directory, when
`npm pack --dry-run` would omit a packaged skill file, or when two skills share a name.
That is what keeps "every new or edited skill" inside the single installable plugin.

Frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill                     # required — must match the kebab-case directory/file name
description: >-                    # required — shown in the catalog, capped (~500 chars)
  One paragraph on what the skill does and when it should trigger.
whenToUse: >-                      # optional — extra routing guidance
  Use when …
metadata:                          # optional, free-form
  author: sredevopsorg
  version: "1.0.0"
disable-model-invocation: false    # optional — keep out of model-facing catalogs
user-invocable: true               # optional — keep out of `/` commands
---
# Skill title

Instructions…
```

Rules the skill provider enforces (identical to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` and the packaged provider in `plugins/skills/index.js`):

- `name` and `description` are mandatory; a skill missing either is dropped.
- `*invocable` keys accept YAML booleans and `true/false`, `yes/no`, `on/off`, `1/0`. A rejected spelling drops the **whole skill** with a warning.
- Prefer `disable-model-invocation: true` for human-only workflows and `user-invocable: false` for model-only ones.
- Keep `description` trigger-focused — it is the only thing the model sees before loading the body.

Conventions used in this repo:

- One skill per concern; put long material in `references/` and load it from `SKILL.md`.
- Frontmatter first line, fenced by `---`; no BOM, no leading blank line.
- The `name` must match its directory (or flat-file) name exactly — `scripts/validate-skills.mjs` enforces this.
- Skills live only in `plugins/skills/skills/`; the packaged provider serves them, so there is nothing to copy or symlink.
- Scripts live in `scripts/`, are dependency-light, and document `--help`.
- Cite upstream sources in the body when guidance is derived from official docs.

After adding or editing a skill, run `node scripts/validate-skills.mjs` and
`cd plugins/skills && npm test` before committing; see [Verifying](#verifying).

---

## Plugins and tools

A DSH plugin is an npm package that Cordis loads; a **bundle** additionally declares its patch layer:

```json
{
  "name": "@sredevopsorg/dsh-<name>",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": { ".": "./index.js" },
  "engines": { "dsh": "^0.2.1-rc.2" },
  "dsh": {
    "manifestVersion": 1,
    "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" }
  }
}
```

`engines.dsh` is the compatibility gate the installer, the market index, and the launcher enforce; omit it and an unsupported DSH version installs silently and fails later at activation. A bundle that only adds configuration needs no `index.js` or `.` export — declare the patch, plus `./package.json`, `./locale/*.json`, and `./icon.svg` for management and market display.

Install and select it into a profile — from Discover, from GitHub with a pinned release tag, or from a local checkout while developing:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#code-editor-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/code-editor"
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#entire-v0.2.0&path:/plugins/entire"
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#peak-rate-footer-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/peak-rate-footer"
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#skills-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/skills"
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#superagent-v0.1.2&path:/plugins/superagent"
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/code-editor # local checkout
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/entire   # local checkout
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/peak-rate-footer # local checkout
dsh plugin --profile web list
dsh --profile web --dump-config                 # inspect the composed tree, no boot
```

`dsh plugin` forwards its arguments to pnpm. See
[Installing plugins from GitHub](docs/installing-plugins-from-github.md) for the
tag scheme, pinning, and troubleshooting, and [Publishing the plugin index](docs/plugin-index.md)
for how a released version reaches Discover.

Conventions this repository follows:

```
plugins/<name>/
├── package.json          # name, license, engines.dsh, exports, dsh.bundle.patch
├── cordis.patch.yml      # plugin rows / config
├── index.js              # plugin entry: export apply() / inject / (optional) Config
├── <support>.js          # plain-ESM support modules, imported relatively
├── locale/en.json        # display title + description for management and market surfaces
├── icon.svg              # optional, referenced by package.json "icon"
├── test/                 # unit tests where the plugin has logic to test
└── README.md             # configuration table + observable behavior
```

[`entire`](plugins/entire/README.md) and [`skills`](plugins/skills/README.md) ship plain ESM
with **no dependencies and no build step**. That is deliberate: a workspace-linked plugin
cannot resolve bare `@deepseek-ai/*` specifiers unless its manifest declares them as
`peerDependencies`, so a dependency-free package keeps `dsh plugin add` free of both a
toolchain and install-script approval.

[`superagent`](plugins/superagent/README.md) is the deliberate exception: it is a vendored
fork of an upstream TypeScript project, so it keeps that project's `tsdown` build and
`vitest` suites for development. Its **built `lib/` is committed**, which keeps the Git
install toolchain-free (no build or lifecycle script runs when pnpm fetches it); CI
rebuilds it and fails when the committed output drifts from the source. Its importable
surfaces resolve inside its own package, and its bundle rows name the package itself, so
the plugin loads from a profile like any other bundle.

The [`skills`](plugins/skills/README.md) bundle is the packaging pattern for skills: its
`cordis.patch.yml` inserts one host-wide row, `index.js` registers a provider via
`ctx.skills.registerProvider`, and the Markdown skill bundles ship inside the npm package
unchanged. The provider uses the literal bundled rank `600` (`BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK`) instead
of importing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill`, precisely so the package stays dependency-free; see
the plugin README for the trade-off.

Model-facing tools are registered from a plugin via `ctx.tools`; they should declare a JSON-schema input, fail with actionable messages, and never leak stack traces.

---

## The plugin index (Discover)

[`index.json`](index.json) is a **format-1 plugin market index**. It lists each published

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Skills for DeepSeek Harness

One DSH plugin that installs **every skill maintained in this repository** into a profile
at once. It packages the Markdown skill bundles and registers a host-wide skill provider,
so `dsh plugin add` is the only install step — no symlinks, no `customSkillDirs`, no
copying `SKILL.md` files around.

The plugin is dependency-free plain ESM with no build step and no install scripts: the
files under `skills/` are the exact skills the provider serves.

## Install

Install from this repository (the release tag is immutable, so the command reproduces the
same package contents):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#skills-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/skills"
```

Or install from the repository's plugin index, which the Web **Plugins → Discover** tab
reads; add `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins/main/index.json`
as an index source, then install the version from the card. See
[`docs/plugin-index.md`](../../docs/plugin-index.md).

Or install the local checkout while developing:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/skills
```

Quote the spec: the shell must not interpret `&`. `dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm; a Git
install needs `git` and pnpm 9 or newer. Restart a running DSH after installing; the skill
catalog is rebuilt at startup.

## What it provides

| Skill | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [`software-architecture`](skills/software-architecture/SKILL.md) | Choosing the simplest sufficient design, patterns to apply or skip, engineering practices, tool/skill selection |
| [`fullstack-development`](skills/fullstack-development/SKILL.md) | Container-based Python and Node.js/TypeScript backends, frontends, monorepos, Docker, e2e testing |
| [`supabase`](skills/supabase/SKILL.md) | Anything touching Supabase: DB, Auth, Edge Functions, Realtime, Storage, CLI, MCP, logs, debugging |
| [`supabase-postgres-best-practices`](skills/supabase-postgres-best-practices/SKILL.md) | Postgres schema, migrations, RLS, indexes, locking, query plans — load *before* touching a database |
| [`ghost-theme-development`](skills/ghost-theme-development/SKILL.md) | Authoring Ghost Handlebars themes: templates, contexts, helpers, settings, routing, GScan |
| [`ghost-theme-modern-frontend`](skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/SKILL.md) | Wiring a Ghost theme to Vite, Tailwind CSS, and React/Vue/Svelte islands |
| [`helm-chart-development`](skills/helm-chart-development/SKILL.md) | Creating, editing and improving Helm charts: templates, values.yaml, helpers, hooks, CRDs, subcharts |
| [`kubernetes-kubectl-operations`](skills/kubernetes-kubectl-operations/SKILL.md) | Safe kubectl operations, cluster triage, and opt-in Kubernetes MCP inspection |
| [`github-actions-security-audit`](skills/github-actions-security-audit/SKILL.md) | Auditing and hardening GitHub Actions workflows: token permissions, script injection, `pull_request_target`, action pinning, runners, supply chain |

Every skill is model- and user-invocable (no `disable-model-invocation` /
`user-invocable: false` in the current frontmatter), so each appears in the session
catalog and under `/` in the composer.

## How it works

`cordis.patch.yml` inserts one host-wide row:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: skills
      name: '@sredevopsorg/dsh-skills'
```

`index.js` is that row's plugin. Its `apply(ctx)` calls
`ctx.skills.registerProvider(...)`, and the provider:

1. discovers top-level directory bundles (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) and flat files
   (`skills/<name>.md`) in the packaged `skills/` directory;
2. parses each frontmatter block with the same contract as
   `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` — `name` (kebab-case, matching the directory or
   file), `description`, optional `whenToUse`, optional `disable-model-invocation` /
   `user-invocable`, optional `metadata`; invalid files are dropped with a warning;
3. lists candidates with `source: "bundled"`, the packaged directory as `resourceBase`,
   and the standard bundled-provider rank `600`, so a project-local skill root (rank
   100/200) still overrides a packaged skill of the same name;
4. loads the body from disk on demand. The body keeps its resource base, so
   `references/`, `scripts/`, and `assets/` paths written in `SKILL.md` resolve as
   written.

### Why no peerDependencies

The official bundled badge skill imports `BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK` from
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill` and declares that package as a peer dependency. That works for a
package shipped inside the DSH installation. This plugin is installed from Git into a
profile, where a workspace-linked package cannot resolve bare `@deepseek-ai/*` specifiers
unless its manifest declares them — and declaring them would make `dsh plugin add`
depend on resolving the host's internal packages at install time.

Instead the rank is the documented literal `600` (`BUNDLED_SKILL_RANK`) with this comment
and note. The plugin has **no runtime or peer dependencies at all**, which matches the
repository convention for installable bundles. If DSH ever changes the bundled rank, the
only effect is duplicate-name precedence against other packaged providers; update the
constant in `index.js` with the DSH release.

## Adding or editing a skill

Skills live **inside this package** so that editing one is automatically part of the
installable plugin. Create `plugins/skills/skills/<kebab-case-name>/SKILL.md` (directory
bundle; supporting files welcome) or `plugins/skills/skills/<kebab-case-name>.md` (flat
file). Do not create a `SKILL.md` anywhere else in the repository —
`scripts/validate-skills.mjs` fails when one is outside this package.

Frontmatter rules and conventions are documented in the
[root README](../../README.md#authoring-a-skill). After adding or editing a skill, run:

```sh
node scripts/validate-skills.mjs   # frontmatter + packaging + npm pack contents
cd plugins/skills && npm test      # provider test: every packaged skill parses and lists
```

`plugins/skills/README.md` and the root README must carry the pinned install command for
the current version; `scripts/validate-github-install.mjs` enforces it on release.

## Migrating from `install.sh`

`install.sh` at the repository root is kept as a legacy/manual alternative; it now links
from `plugins/skills/skills/`. If you previously linked the skills into `~/.dsh/skills`
or a project root, remove those links once so the plugin's copy is the one in use:

```sh
./install.sh --uninstall
```

A per-skill symlink at the user root has rank 400 and would otherwise win duplicate-name
precedence over the packaged provider at rank 600. Leaving it works, but a later package
update would not be reflected until the link is removed or its target updated.

## Configuration

The bundle adds no configuration. The provider always scans the packaged `skills/`
directory; disable the `skills` row in a profile's `cordis.patch.yml` to remove the
packaged skills from that profile. The plugin does not watch files: skills are static
package contents, so restart DSH after installing an updated version.

## Verification

```sh
node scripts/validate-skills.mjs                     # repository contract + npm pack
cd plugins/skills && npm test                        # provider and frontmatter tests
npm pack --dry-run --json                            # all SKILL.md + references shipped
dsh --profile web --dump-config                      # composes without booting
```

The provider test asserts the package lists all 9 skills, that each parsed name matches
its directory, that each body loads, and that referenced resources are packaged.

# DSH Plugins

Custom **skills and plugins** for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/sredevopsorg), maintained by [sredevopsorg](https://github.com/sredevopsorg).

The repository publishes two things:

- **Skills** — `SKILL.md` instruction bundles packaged by the **skills plugin** under [`plugins/skills/skills/`](plugins/skills/skills/). Install that one plugin and every skill is registered; [`install.sh`](install.sh) remains a legacy/manual symlink alternative.
- **DSH plugins** — self-contained bundles under [`plugins/`](plugins/), installed from this repository's release tags **or** browsed from the repository's [plugin market index](#the-plugin-index-discover).

| Kind | What it is | Where it lives here |
|---|---|---|
| **Skill** | A `SKILL.md` (or flat `<name>.md`) instruction bundle loaded on demand by the model or with `/name`. Skills are packaged and served by a DSH skill-provider plugin. | [`plugins/skills/skills/`](plugins/skills/skills/) |
| **Plugin** | A Cordis plugin package loaded into a DSH profile (`dsh plugin …`). | [`plugins/`](plugins/) |
| **Tool** | A model-facing tool registered by a plugin via `ctx.tools`, shipped inside a plugin package. | [`plugins/entire/`](plugins/entire/) |

The repository also publishes [`index.json`](index.json), a **format-1 plugin market index** that [@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) reads in the Web **Plugins → Discover** tab.

> Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` **0.2.x**, currently **`0.2.2-rc.1`**. The CLI version gate is strict, so check `dsh --version` before reporting plugin issues. Bundle patches are checked against the installed DSH by `scripts/validate-bundles.mjs`.

## Requirements

- **DSH** — `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh …`, or a global `dsh` install (`@deepseek-ai/dsh`). The Discover flow additionally needs the experimental **Custom plugin indexes** bundle (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle`), enabled from the Web Plugins page.
- **Node.js ≥ 18** and **npm/npx** — for the Ghost and Helm toolchain scripts, `npx gscan`, and the optional Kubernetes MCP server (`npx -y kubernetes-mcp-server@latest`).
- **Ghost 6.x + `gscan`** — only for the two Ghost theme skills.
- **Helm 3+** — only for `helm-chart-development`. No cluster or network needed;
  `scripts/verify-chart.mjs` shells out to `helm lint` and `helm template`.
- **`kubectl` + a kubeconfig** — only for `kubernetes-kubectl-operations`. The skill
  inspects and, with explicit confirmation, changes a cluster;
  `scripts/verify-kube-access.sh` is a read-only preflight and accepts
  `--kubeconfig <path>`. Set `KUBERNETES_MCP_KUBECONFIG` to an absolute path for a
  dedicated, preferably read-only kubeconfig; when the optional Kubernetes MCP row is
  enabled, it passes that value to the server as `KUBECONFIG`. Without it, the server
  uses `KUBECONFIG` or `~/.kube/config`.
- **Entire CLI** (`entire`) on `PATH` — only for the `entire` plugin. It records agent sessions and
  checkpoints and backs every tool; session capture additionally needs the `entire-agent-dsh`
  binary and `entire agent add dsh` in the target repository. Search, trails, and recap also need
  an authenticated login and OS keyring access.
- **`git`** and **`pnpm` 9 or newer** — only when installing DSH plugin packages from this
  repository (`dsh plugin …` forwards to pnpm; `path:` subdirectory installs need pnpm 9).
  No npm publish is involved. `superagent` also fetches its two runtime dependencies
  (`zod`, `proper-lockfile`) from the npm registry.
- **A DSH Web profile** — only for the Web plugins: the built-in right Sidebar for
  `code-editor`, whose browser bundle contributes a right-sidebar tab and whose Host half
  serves the browser-only workspace write endpoint, and the built-in bottom frame seat for
  `peak-rate-footer`, whose Client module contributes the rate-status footer.
- **Node.js 22.19+ or 24+, `git`, GitHub CLI 2.48+, `tmux`, and Python 3.8+** — only for the
  [`superagent`](plugins/superagent/README.md) fork, whose managed-service script and
  executor sessions need them. It requires a Web profile (the management panel is a web
  plugin) and its own `stateDir` configuration; `SETUP.md` in the plugin drives the
  deployment. Its optional session capture additionally needs the `entire` plugin in the
  same profile and `entire agent add dsh` in the target repository — see
  [`docs/entire-dsh-audit.md`](docs/entire-dsh-audit.md) for the current root causes.

---

## Installing the skills

Every skill is packaged in one plugin, [`plugins/skills`](plugins/skills/README.md). Its
bundle patch inserts one host-wide row, and that row registers a skill provider on
`ctx.skills` that discovers and serves the packaged `plugins/skills/skills/` directory.
Installing the plugin is the supported path: no filesystem root to configure and no
per-skill symlink to maintain.

### Option A — install the skills plugin (recommended)

From this local checkout:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/skills
```

Or from the pinned GitHub release (the tag is immutable, so the contents are reproducible;
quote the `&` or the shell will split it):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#skills-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/skills"
```

Or add the repository's [plugin index](#the-plugin-index-discover) source once and install
the version from the **Discover** card. `dsh --profile web list` shows the installed
package and `dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes the tree without booting. Restart a
running DSH after installing; the skill catalog is built at startup.

The packaged provider uses the standard bundled rank `600` and `source: bundled`. A
project-local or user filesystem root still wins duplicate-name precedence (ranks 100–500),
so a project can override a packaged skill of the same name.

### Option B — `install.sh` (legacy/manual alternative)

For setups that cannot install a plugin, [`install.sh`](install.sh) links the same packaged
skills from `plugins/skills/skills/` into a DSH filesystem root:

```bash
./install.sh                                   # all skills -> ~/.dsh/skills
./install.sh --project /path/to/your/project   # -> <project>/.dsh/skills (rank 100)
./install.sh ghost-theme-development \         # only a subset
             ghost-theme-modern-frontend
./install.sh --dry-run                         # show what would change
./install.sh --uninstall                       # detach again
```

It links each skill by symlink, skips anything that is not a managed link, and refuses to
overwrite real files. After installing into the user root, restart DSH so the catalog is
rebuilt. A user-root link has rank 400, which beats the packaged provider's rank 600, so
`--uninstall` hands a skill back to the plugin.

### Option C — manual symlinks

```bash
# into a project (rank 100)
PROJECT=/path/to/your/project
mkdir -p "$PROJECT/.dsh/skills"
for d in plugins/skills/skills/*/; do
  [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] || continue
  ln -sfn "$PWD/${d%/}" "$PROJECT/.dsh/skills/$(basename "$d")"
done

# or into the user root (rank 400), available from every project
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/skills
for d in "$PWD"/plugins/skills/skills/*/; do
  [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] || continue
  ln -sfn "${d%/}" ~/.dsh/skills/
done
```

### Option D — configure `customSkillDirs`

Point the filesystem provider at the packaged skills directory in your profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
  config:
    customSkillDirs:
      - /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugins/plugins/skills/skills
```

The provider watches roots, so new, renamed, or deleted skills appear without restarting
DSH. **Restart DSH** after changing `customSkillDirs` itself, since that is plugin
configuration.

### Using a skill

- **Model-invoked** — skills with `modelInvocable` appear in the session catalog; the agent calls the `skill` tool with the exact kebab-case name before acting.
- **User-invoked** — type `/` in the composer and pick a skill, or type `/software-architecture` directly.

`install.sh` deliberately skips `docs/ghost-themes.md` and any `_`- or `.`-prefixed entry, so repository documentation is never registered as a skill.

---

## Installing plugins

Every plugin under [`plugins/`](plugins/) ships as a self-contained DSH bundle (two are
no-toolchain plain ESM; the forked `superagent` commits its build output). Two install paths
resolve to the same package:

### From Discover (plugin index)

Add the repository's index once; **Discover** then lists every published plugin version and
installs it after confirmation:

1. Open **Plugins** in the Web sidebar and switch on **Custom plugin indexes** under
   **Experimental plugins**.
2. Select **Discover → Add index source** and enter:

   ```
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins/main/index.json
   ```

3. Pick a plugin and version and confirm the install. Each entry pins its exact Git commit.

The index and its maintenance are documented in [`docs/plugin-index.md`](docs/plugin-index.md).

### From a pinned GitHub release tag

The same package installs with pnpm's Git subdirectory parameter, pinned to an immutable
release tag:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#entire-v0.2.0&path:/plugins/entire"
```

Quote the spec: the shell must not interpret `&`. Replace `web` with your profile.
`dsh --profile web list` shows the installed package, and
`dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes the tree without booting.

Requirements, full-URL and commit-pinned variants, update/uninstall commands,
and troubleshooting are in
[`docs/installing-plugins-from-github.md`](docs/installing-plugins-from-github.md).
For local development, install a checkout instead:
`dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/entire`.

## Quick start — Ghost theme toolchain

`scaffold-theme.mjs` generates a GScan-clean theme wired for Vite, optional Tailwind, and optional React islands. It needs only plain Node ≥ 18.

```bash
# Scaffold a Vite + Tailwind + React-islands theme
node plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/scaffold-theme.mjs \
  --name my-theme --out ./themes --react

cd themes/my-theme
npm install
npm run build
npm test          # build + GScan

# Fuller pre-flight: build → GScan → zip → archive assertions
bash "$OLDPWD/plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/verify-theme.sh" .
```

```bash
node plugins/skills/skills/ghost-theme-modern-frontend/scripts/scaffold-theme.mjs --help
```

Flags: `--name`, `--out`, `--react`, `--no-tailwind`, `--force`.

---

## Authoring a skill

Create `plugins/skills/skills/<kebab-case-name>/SKILL.md` (directory bundle) or `plugins/skills/skills/<kebab-case-name>.md` (flat file). A directory bundle may include any supporting files; nested `**/SKILL.md` files are **not** discovered.

Skills **must** live inside the packaged plugin. `scripts/validate-skills.mjs` fails when a
`SKILL.md` exists anywhere outside `plugins/skills/skills` (including a resurrected
top-level `skills/`), when the package manifest does not ship the skills directory, when
`npm pack --dry-run` would omit a packaged skill file, or when two skills share a name.
That is what keeps "every new or edited skill" inside the single installable plugin.

Frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill                     # required — must match the kebab-case directory/file name
description: >-                    # required — shown in the catalog, capped (~500 chars)
  One paragraph on what the skill does and when it should trigger.
whenToUse: >-                      # optional — extra routing guidance
  Use when …
metadata:                          # optional, free-form
  author: sredevopsorg
  version: "1.0.0"
disable-model-invocation: false    # optional — keep out of model-facing catalogs
user-invocable: true               # optional — keep out of `/` commands
---
# Skill title

Instructions…
```

Rules the skill provider enforces (identical to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` and the packaged provider in `plugins/skills/index.js`):

- `name` and `description` are mandatory; a skill missing either is dropped.
- `*invocable` keys accept YAML booleans and `true/false`, `yes/no`, `on/off`, `1/0`. A rejected spelling drops the **whole skill** with a warning.
- Prefer `disable-model-invocation: true` for human-only workflows and `user-invocable: false` for model-only ones.
- Keep `description` trigger-focused — it is the only thing the model sees before loading the body.

Conventions used in this repo:

- One skill per concern; put long material in `references/` and load it from `SKILL.md`.
- Frontmatter first line, fenced by `---`; no BOM, no leading blank line.
- The `name` must match its directory (or flat-file) name exactly — `scripts/validate-skills.mjs` enforces this.
- Skills live only in `plugins/skills/skills/`; the packaged provider serves them, so there is nothing to copy or symlink.
- Scripts live in `scripts/`, are dependency-light, and document `--help`.
- Cite upstream sources in the body when guidance is derived from official docs.

After adding or editing a skill, run `node scripts/validate-skills.mjs` and
`cd plugins/skills && npm test` before committing; see [Verifying](#verifying).

---

## Plugins and tools

A DSH plugin is an npm package that Cordis loads; a **bundle** additionally declares its patch layer:

  "name": "@sredevopsorg/dsh-<name>",

# Superagent for DeepSeek Harness

A proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a DSH bundle: it listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu, evaluates requests under a Policy, turns authorized ones into Tickets, and executes each in its own DSH Session. A web panel shows what needs a person.

This is a **fork** of the DeepSeek Harness research prototype [`deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype) (MIT), vendored from upstream commit [`8c32a9d`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype/commit/8c32a9dc5d72c033816c6a8110b37f40cf94fba4) and republished here as `@sredevopsorg/dsh-superagent` so it can be installed and versioned like the other bundles in this repository. The upstream project calls itself a research prototype for reference only; that caveat applies to this fork too. See [Fork provenance](#fork-provenance) and [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

> This code grew out of the DeepSeek Harness team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.

The upstream prototype was adapted for publication and is not identical to the internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are future directions and are not implemented here.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Install

Install from this repository, pinned to the release tag (the tag is immutable, so the command reproduces the same package contents):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#superagent-v0.1.2&path:/plugins/superagent"
```

The package ships its built `lib/` directory, so **no build step runs at install time** and the Git dependency needs no toolchain beyond Node and pnpm. The same spec works with the `plugin_manager` tool's `install_bundle` and from the repository's plugin index (Discover).

pnpm may report unmet `@deepseek-ai/*` peer dependencies after the install. That is expected: those packages are supplied by the running DSH installation through its own module resolution, not by the profile; the peer ranges document the DSH versions the code was built and tested against.

Or install a local checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile superagent add "link:$PWD"
```

The bundle then activates automatically in the profile (`dsh plugin add` reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles`).

### Requirements

- DSH satisfying this package's `engines.dsh` (`^0.2.1-rc.2`); the fork was smoke-tested against DSH `0.2.2-alpha.3`.
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` and pnpm 9 or newer (for installation; the plugin itself runs under DSH).
- Git 2.32+, GitHub CLI 2.48+, tmux, and Python 3.8+ for the managed-service script and for the agent's work.
- A DSH model provider configured for the profile.
- A `stateDir` configuration is optional: each profile that does not set one gets `<DSH home>/state/superagent/<profile>`, so an install starts and serves its panel before setup (see [Configuration](#configuration)).

### Configuration

The bundle inserts the `dsh-superagent` row, the `dsh-superagent-github` Source, a disabled `dsh-superagent-feishu` Source, and the worker/router agent presets. Installation is enough to start the plugin and open its panel: when the profile does not configure `stateDir`, it defaults to `<DSH home>/state/superagent/<profile>`, scoped so two profiles can load the bundle without contending for one state lock. A dedicated profile should pin its directory explicitly in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, using the row id from the bundle patch (ids are unchanged from upstream):

```yaml
- id: dsh-superagent
  config:
    stateDir: /absolute/path/to/state/superagent
# Feishu is optional; enable its Source after configuring the bot's lark-cli.
- id: dsh-superagent-feishu
  disabled: false
```

An explicit `stateDir` always wins over the default and cannot be changed from the panel, so choose a stable path a dedicated deployment can back up.

See [examples/profile.cordis.patch.yml](examples/profile.cordis.patch.yml) and [docs/006-deployment.md](docs/006-deployment.md) for every configuration key, account setup, upgrades, and troubleshooting.

## Development and verification

The fork is a normal pnpm TypeScript project. `pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile   # dev dependencies (DSH 0.2.1-alpha.2 packages, vitest, tsdown)
pnpm typecheck                   # tsc --noEmit
pnpm test                        # vitest run
pnpm build                       # tsdown: writes the committed lib/
git status --short lib           # must be clean: the committed lib/ is reproduced by the build
```

Verify that the published package is complete and installable before tagging:

```sh
npm pack --dry-run --json        # tarball must contain lib/, cordis.patch.yml, locale/, prompts/, skills/, README.md
node --check lib/index.js && node -e "import('./lib/index.js').then(m => console.log(m.name, typeof m.apply))"
```

Optional end-to-end install check into a scratch DSH profile, from the packed tarball:

```sh
npm pack --pack-destination /tmp
DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-scratch dsh plugin --profile scratch add /tmp/sredevopsorg-dsh-superagent-0.1.2.tgz
DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-scratch dsh --profile scratch --dump-config
```

The install path is covered by hand: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, a rebuild-vs-committed-`lib/` diff, `npm pack --dry-run`, and a scratch-profile install from the packed tarball — `dsh plugin add`, `dsh --profile scratch --dump-config`, then booting a Web profile where the plugin serves its management API (`/orchestrator/api/state`) and reports the expected setup problem. The unit suite has one upstream test that is timing-sensitive under load and fails the same way in an unmodified checkout of the upstream tree; it is unrelated to the fork.

## Limitations

- Upstream describes this as a research prototype, not production software; the fork does not change that.
- The vendored code was written against DSH `0.2.1-alpha.2` and this fork declares `^0.2.1-rc.2`. It was smoke-tested on DSH `0.2.2-alpha.3`: installed from the packed tarball into a fresh Web profile, booted, and its management API answered with the expected `repositoryUnset` setup problem. A full end-to-end run of the agent needs GitHub/Feishu accounts, a model provider and a repository, so it is the operator's setup step. DSH `0.2.2-alpha.3` also cannot dump a JSON Schema for preset rows that are custom Loader carriers (`unrecognized Loader tree carrier`); that diagnostic appears for the shipped presets too and does not affect booting.
- The management panel is Web-only. Feishu support is optional and inert until its Source is enabled and a bot `lark-cli` is configured.
- Ticket execution shells out to `git`, `gh`, `tmux`, `python3` and `lark-cli` as configured; DSH's sandbox/permission settings for the profile still apply.
- Committed `lib/` means the fork must rebuild and commit it on every source change; CI should assert the build reproduces it.
