# DSH Plugins

Custom **skills and plugins** for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/sredevopsorg), maintained by [sredevopsorg](https://github.com/sredevopsorg).

The repository publishes two things:

- **Skills** — `SKILL.md` instruction bundles packaged by the **skills plugin** under [`plugins/skills/skills/`](plugins/skills/skills/). Install that one plugin and every skill is registered; [`install.sh`](install.sh) remains a legacy/manual symlink alternative.
- **DSH plugins** — self-contained bundles under [`plugins/`](plugins/), installed from this repository's release tags **or** browsed from the repository's [plugin market index](#the-plugin-index-discover).

| Kind | What it is | Where it lives here |
|---|---|---|
| **Skill** | A `SKILL.md` (or flat `<name>.md`) instruction bundle loaded on demand by the model or with `/name`. Skills are packaged and served by a DSH skill-provider plugin. | [`plugins/skills/skills/`](plugins/skills/skills/) |
| **Plugin** | A Cordis plugin package loaded into a DSH profile (`dsh plugin …`). | [`plugins/`](plugins/) |
| **Tool** | A model-facing tool registered by a plugin via `ctx.tools`, shipped inside a plugin package. | [`plugins/entire/`](plugins/entire/) |

The repository also publishes [`index.json`](index.json), a **format-1 plugin market index** that [@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) reads in the Web **Plugins → Discover** tab.

> Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` **0.2.x**, currently **`0.2.2-rc.1`**. The CLI version gate is strict, so check `dsh --version` before reporting plugin issues. Bundle patches are checked against the installed DSH by `scripts/validate-bundles.mjs`.

## Installing the skills

Every skill is packaged in one plugin, [`plugins/skills`](plugins/skills/README.md). Its
bundle patch inserts one host-wide row, and that row registers a skill provider on
`ctx.skills` that discovers and serves the packaged `plugins/skills/skills/` directory.
Installing the plugin is the supported path: no filesystem root to configure and no
per-skill symlink to maintain.

### Option A — install the skills plugin (recommended)

From this local checkout:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/skills
```

Or from the pinned GitHub release (the tag is immutable, so the contents are reproducible;
quote the `&` or the shell will split it):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins#skills-v0.1.0&path:/plugins/skills"
```

Or add the repository's [plugin index](#the-plugin-index-discover) source once and install
the version from the **Discover** card. `dsh --profile web list` shows the installed
package and `dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes the tree without booting. Restart a
running DSH after installing; the skill catalog is built at startup.

The packaged provider uses the standard bundled rank `600` and `source: bundled`. A
project-local or user filesystem root still wins duplicate-name precedence (ranks 100–500),
so a project can override a packaged skill of the same name.

### Option B — `install.sh` (legacy/manual alternative)

For setups that cannot install a plugin, [`install.sh`](install.sh) links the same packaged
skills from `plugins/skills/skills/` into a DSH filesystem root:

```bash
./install.sh                                   # all skills -> ~/.dsh/skills
./install.sh --project /path/to/your/project   # -> <project>/.dsh/skills (rank 100)
./install.sh ghost-theme-development \         # only a subset
             ghost-theme-modern-frontend
./install.sh --dry-run                         # show what would change
./install.sh --uninstall                       # detach again
```

It links each skill by symlink, skips anything that is not a managed link, and refuses to
overwrite real files. After installing into the user root, restart DSH so the catalog is
rebuilt. A user-root link has rank 400, which beats the packaged provider's rank 600, so
`--uninstall` hands a skill back to the plugin.

### Option C — manual symlinks

```bash
# into a project (rank 100)
PROJECT=/path/to/your/project
mkdir -p "$PROJECT/.dsh/skills"
for d in plugins/skills/skills/*/; do
  [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] || continue
  ln -sfn "$PWD/${d%/}" "$PROJECT/.dsh/skills/$(basename "$d")"
done

# or into the user root (rank 400), available from every project
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/skills
for d in "$PWD"/plugins/skills/skills/*/; do
  [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] || continue
  ln -sfn "${d%/}" ~/.dsh/skills/
done
```

### Option D — configure `customSkillDirs`

Point the filesystem provider at the packaged skills directory in your profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
  config:
    customSkillDirs:
      - /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugins/plugins/skills/skills
```

The provider watches roots, so new, renamed, or deleted skills appear without restarting
DSH. **Restart DSH** after changing `customSkillDirs` itself, since that is plugin
configuration.

### Using a skill

- **Model-invoked** — skills with `modelInvocable` appear in the session catalog; the agent calls the `skill` tool with the exact kebab-case name before acting.
- **User-invoked** — type `/` in the composer and pick a skill, or type `/software-architecture` directly.

`install.sh` deliberately skips `docs/ghost-themes.md` and any `_`- or `.`-prefixed entry, so repository documentation is never registered as a skill.

---

## Installing plugins

Every plugin under [`plugins/`](plugins/) ships as a self-contained DSH bundle (two are
no-toolchain plain ESM; the forked `superagent` commits its build output). Two install paths
resolve to the same package:

### From Discover (plugin index)

Add the repository's index once; **Discover** then lists every published plugin version and
installs it after confirmation:

1. Open **Plugins** in the Web sidebar and switch on **Custom plugin indexes** under
   **Experimental plugins**.
2. Select **Discover → Add index source** and enter:

   ```
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sredevopsorg/dsh-plugins/main/index.json
   ```

3. Pick a plugin and version and confirm the install. Each entry pins its exact Git commit.

# dsh-local-api

给 DeepSeek Harness 侧栏加两个开关，用来管理本机的**独立 API 守护进程**：一个对应 GPT/Codex 风格的服务，一个对应 GLM/ZCode 风格的服务。每行都显示真实状态，可以一键启停，关掉 Harness 之后服务照常运行。

```
● GPT 本地 API
● GLM 本地 API
CHEN-SM
```

![侧栏底部两个开关](docs/preview.png)

两行都固定在侧栏底部、账户行（头像）上方。插件只管理进程生命周期：它不读取、不写入、也不显示你的 API Key，也不会改动任一服务自己的配置文件。

## 功能

| | |
| --- | --- |
| 实时状态 | 每 30 秒请求一次 `GET /healthz`（启停进行中改为 1 秒），并配合查询真实进程表。守护进程被外部杀掉后，下一次轮询就会把开关弹回「已停止」。 |
| 启动 | GLM：执行 `glm-api-server-via-zcode.exe start`。GPT：隐藏执行服务自带的 `Start-Server.ps1`（`-WindowStyle Hidden`），原样调用，代理、凭据、配置仍由脚本自己处理。 |
| 停止 | 只结束**可执行文件完整路径**与配置一致的那些进程，其他服务、代理程序与 Harness 本身都不受影响。 |
| 防重复启动 | 永不启动第二份：如果进程已经存在，就改为等待 `/healthz`，等不到则报 `unhealthy`，不会重复 spawn。 |
| 不弹窗 | 启动器以 `windowsHide` 方式运行，状态以 `/healthz` 为准，不依赖可见窗口。 |
| 退出 Harness | 卸载插件只注销本地 HTTP 路由，正在运行的服务不会被杀掉。 |
| 设置 | 每个服务的可执行文件/脚本路径与端口，可在侧栏面板里改，持久化到 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\dsh-local-api\settings.json`。 |
| 登录过期（GLM） | ZCode 凭据失效时，服务返回的 `401` / `login token rejected` 会显示成琥珀色的「登录过期」并给出重试提示，而不是笼统的报错。 |

插件加载时**不会**自动启动或停止任何服务，首次渲染只查询状态。

## 环境要求

- 支持第三方插件（Cordis bundle）的 DeepSeek Harness。
- Windows（进程发现用 CIM，GPT 的启动器是 PowerShell）。
- 两个服务各自另行安装。本仓库**不带**任何二进制、也不带服务配置，路径由使用者自己填。

## 安装

在本地检出后：

```powershell
# 指向本目录的绝对路径
plugin_manager install_bundle C:\path\to\dsh-local-api
```

安装后刷新一次 Harness 页面，然后在侧栏任一行打开面板填写路径：

| 设置项 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| `exePath` | GLM 服务可执行文件（`glm-api-server-via-zcode.exe`） |
| `port` | GLM 端口，默认 `18081` |
| `gptExePath` | GPT 服务可执行文件（`openai-api-server-via-codex.exe`） |
| `gptScriptPath` | 它的启动脚本（`Start-Server.ps1`） |
| `gptPort` | GPT 端口，默认 `18080`，需与该服务 `config.toml` 中的端口一致 |

这五个键同时也存在于插件配置（`cordis.patch.yml`）里，可以在安装时直接给出；面板里填的值优先，并保存在 `~/.dsh/dsh-local-api/` 下。

## 目录结构

```
dsh-local-api/
├─ package.json        # dsh.client（web）与 dsh.bundle（patch）
├─ cordis.patch.yml    # bundle 入口；路径默认全部留空
├─ lib/index.js        # Host 半：探活、启停、设置、同源路由
├─ lib/client.js       # Web 半：sidebar.footer.action 里的两个开关
├─ locale/{en,zh}.json # 插件列表里的元数据
├─ docs/preview.png    # 侧栏底部的实际渲染
├─ icon.svg
├─ LICENSE
└─ README.md
```

## 实现说明

Host 半在 Harness 的 Web 服务上挂 `/api/dsh-local-api/*`，所有请求都必须带 `x-dsh-local-api: 1` 头，避免被跨站请求触发启停。所有进程操作都在 Host 进程里完成（`execFile` / `spawn`），渲染进程只发同源 `fetch`。

Web 半是一个普通的 `__ModuleLoader__` bundle，只注册**一个** `sidebar.footer.action` 条目，内部用 `flex-direction: column` 渲染两行——因为该槽位默认把条目横向排列，注册两项会左右并排而不是上下叠放。

## 注意事项

- 面板里显示的端口是插件用来探活的端口。改服务真实端口要改服务自己的配置（`config.toml` 或启动参数），两边保持一致。
- 停止使用 `Stop-Process -Force`，且只针对路径匹配到的进程。若服务以其他账户运行，需要给插件同等权限，或手动停止。
- 只在上面的两个服务上测试过；界面只使用 `--dsw-alias-*` 主题变量，因此跟随明暗主题。

## 许可证

MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

# dsh-l2d — DSH 插件 在 DeepSeek Harness 界面之上叠加一层透明 Live2D 角色。**真实 Cubism 5 渲染**（官方 Web SDK 5-r.5）， 支持表情/动作/四肢姿势、API 关键帧动作链、分区互动、余额峰谷价、体型校正、右键菜单、自发聊天和工作区会话状态联动。 > 拖拽惯性已恢复为“安全惯性”：临界阻尼弹簧收敛到松手点，不追加甩出初速度，不会飞走。 ## 交互 | 操作 | 行为 | |---|---| | 单击头部 | 亲和反应（兔牙 / 爱心眼 + 视线） | | 单击胸部 | 害羞反应（脸红 / ＞＜） | | 上/下拖拽裙摆 | 连续调整裙摆形态（Clothes1） | | 单击足部 | 穿/脱鞋切换（Clothes4） | | 单击其他身体区域 | 戳一戳动作链（随机或 DeepSeek 决定） | | 右键角色 | 菜单：设置 / 对话 / 随机动作 / 切换体型 / 余额价格 | | 悬停角色 | 底部价格条更新；不占用对话气泡 | | 拖动角色 | 带安全惯性，位置持久化 | ## 体型与缩放 - 基础画布从 240×300 提升到 320×400，整体视觉更大。 - 缩放范围 `0.6 ~ 2.0`。 - 体型切换使用 `Clothes2`： - 默认体型：0 - 体型1：0.4 - 体型2：1.0 - 三个体型有统一视觉校正系数，避免换体型后看起来忽大忽小。 ## API 关键帧动作链 除了预设动作组，DeepSeek 可以返回 `keyframes` 步骤，直接编排眼、嘴、头、身体的微动作： ```json { "chain": [ { "kind": "expression", "name": "兔牙" }, { "kind": "keyframes", "duration": 1600, "tracks": [ { "param": "ParamEyeLOpen", "keys": [[0, 1], [140, 0.25], [360, 1]] }, { "param": "AngleZ", "keys": [[0, 0], [220, 7], [620, -4], [1000, 0]] } ] } ], "bubble": "看我一下" } ``` 安全限制： - 参数只能来自前端上报的 `safeParams` - 最多 5 条轨道、每轨 2~10 个关键帧、总时长 0.5~8 秒 - 物理输出参数仍被注入层拒绝 - 开启 `API 自主动作` 后，空闲状态会定期让 API 编排一次小动作 动作链字段： ```json { "chain": [ { "kind": "expression", "name": "兔牙", "delayMs": 0 }, { "kind": "motion", "name": "竖手指打开", "closeMotion": "竖手指关闭", "closeAfterMs": 6000 }, { "kind": "pose", "pose": { "right": "grass", "left": "chest" } }, { "kind": "look", "x": 0.2, "y": 0.1 } ], "bubble": "来啦，别戳啦" } ``` 后一次戳会生成新 `runId`，打断上一次动作链的延时步骤。 ## 峰谷价 按 DeepSeek 公告规则： - 工作日 `09:00-12:00`、`14:00-18:00` 为峰价 - 其余工作日时段与周末全天为谷价 - 气泡用红色显示峰价、绿色显示谷价 - 展示 V4-Pro / V4-Flash 的输入/输出与缓存命中价 ## UI - 设置面板独立于角色主体，挂在屏幕右上侧，不遮住模型预览 - 状态徽标与设置齿轮移到角色外侧 - 价格条显示在角色下方，不占用对话气泡 - 右键菜单提供设置、对话、随机动作、切换体型、余额价格 ## 自发聊天 - 可开关；开启后： - 工作区回到 `attention` 时，把最新助手回复截短后回流成气泡 - 长时间 `idle` 时按 8~18 秒随机间隔说一句短台词 - 有 8 秒最小间隔，避免刷屏 ## 组成 | 文件 | 作用 | |---|---| | `lib/index.js` | 宿主侧：注入行、13 条路由、设置持久化、AI 指令队列 | | `lib/overlay.js` | 浏览器侧：透明叠加层、拖拽物理、设置面板、AI 执行桥 | | `assets/renderer.js` | 渲染内核（由 `packages/renderer` 构建，含 Cubism Framework + 内联 shader） | | `cordis.patch.yml` | bundle patch，把本插件作为 loader entry 插入 profile | ## 安装 ``` # 1) 目录链接到 profile（Windows 用 Junction，避免 mklink 权限问题） # 链接目标：D:\Desktop\DSH-L2D\packages\dsh-l2d-plugin # 链接位置：%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-l2d # 2) profile 的 package.json 增加依赖与 bundle "dsh-l2d": "link:D:/Desktop/DSH-L2D/packages/dsh-l2d-plugin" // dependencies "dsh-l2d" // dsh.profile.bundles # 3) profile 的 cordis.patch.yml 追加 - insert: - id: dsh-l2d name: dsh-l2d config: {} ``` 改完**重启 DSH**（注入表在宿主启动时收集一次，热加载收不到）。 `schemastery` 通过 `node_modules/@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 目录链接复用 profile 共享依赖。 ## 路由 | 路径 | 说明 | |---|---| | `/dsh-l2d/core.js` | Cubism Core | | `/dsh-l2d/renderer.js` | 渲染内核 | | `/dsh-l2d/overlay.js` | 叠加层脚本 | | `/dsh-l2d/model/*` | 模型静态资源（扩展名白名单 + 防穿越） | | `/dsh-l2d/settings.json` | GET 读取 / PUT 保存（仅回环可写） | | `/dsh-l2d/config.json` | 前端所需的非敏感配置（不含 apiKey） | | `/dsh-l2d/balance.json` | 余额查询（用户自填 Key） | | `/dsh-l2d/ai-action.json` | 戳一戳 API 动作链（用户自填 Key） | | `/dsh-l2d/agent-state.json` | 读取最新 DSH 会话状态并聚合成 thinking/working/attention/error/idle | | `/dsh-l2d/audio/*` | 自定义音效 | | `/dsh-l2d/ai/call` | POST 下发 AI 指令 | | `/dsh-l2d/ai/poll` | GET 取走待执行队列 | | `/dsh-l2d/status.json` | 健康检查 | ## 拖拽 - 容器用 `transform: translate3d()` 定位，逻辑位置与渲染位置分离 - 拖拽目标 1:1 跟手，渲染位置用临界阻尼弹簧收敛 - 松手不追加甩出初速度，因此有惯性滞后但不会飞走 > 参数写入走 `setPreUpdate` 钩子；实际执行点在 Cubism 的 > `saveParameters` 之后、`onLateUpdate` 之前，这是外部参数唯一不会被覆盖的正确窗口。 ## AI 工具 宿主侧收到 `POST /dsh-l2d/ai/call` 后入队，浏览器侧 400ms 轮询执行。 ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:/dsh-l2d/ai/call \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"name":"l2d_set_expression","args":{"name":"兔牙"}}' ``` 可用工具（白名单，其余一律拒绝）： ``` l2d_set_expression l2d_play_motion l2d_look_at l2d_set_pose l2d_set_parameters l2d_play_keyframes l2d_stop_keyframes l2d_reset_pose l2d_emote l2d_gaze l2d_say l2d_act l2d_get_state l2d_reset ``` MCP 只转发高层那一组（`l2d_emote` / `l2d_gaze` / `l2d_say` / `l2d_act` / `l2d_get_state` / `l2d_reset`，外加表情、动作、姿势），不转发 `l2d_set_parameters` 和 `l2d_play_keyframes`。 动作返回 `skipped` 或 `conflict` 时不要当故障重试。 `l2d_act` 走原来的 `executePokeAction`。`priority` 为 `BACKGROUND` | `NORMAL` | `FORCE`：低优先级不能打断高优先级，同级可以。对话演出和邪神是 `FORCE`，待机视线是 `BACKGROUND`。`POST /ai/result` 的 `result` 只表示受理；`event` 才是 `action-done`（`phase` 为 `start`、`end` 或 `interrupted`）。被挡住时 `reason` 是 `priority-blocked`。 工具定义见仓库 `dist/ai-tools.json`，提示词见 `docs/AI-模型控制提示词.md`。 ## 性能 - 目标 30fps（静止 6 秒降 15fps，20 秒降 10fps） - 窗口失焦 10fps，页面隐藏完全暂停 - 拖拽走合成层，不触发重排 - 静止时不写任何参数、不调 lookAt ## 调试 不启动 DSH 也能测： ```bash pnpm dev:server # 127.0.0.1:5300 ``` - `/` 渲染调试台（模型/画布/XY 轴眼神控制/能力清单） - `/overlay-test.html` 原样加载 `lib/overlay.js`，验证拖拽、物理、设置面板 本地服务器会把 `/dsh-l2d/*` 前缀剥离后复用同一套路由，等于复刻了插件环境。 ## DSH Workspace Agent 当 DSH profile 同时加载 Workspace Registry 和 Session Controller 时，插件会创建或复用独立的 `Live2D Agent` 工作区： - 默认目录：`$DSH_HOME/workspaces/live2d-agent`。 - `AGENTS.md`：由 DSH Agent Instructions 加载，定义桌宠 Agent 的职责、MCP 使用方式和只读边界。 - `agent.md`：由插件定期更新的状态快照，只包含其他工作区标题、会话状态与活动时长，不包含聊天文本、文件路径或错误详情。 - 专属 Session 通过 DSH 原生 `sessionController.create({ workspaceId })` 创建，并通过 `sessionController.prompt()` 启动初始化对话。 - 状态变化通过队列消息通知专属 Session；其他工作区不会被写入或控制。 - 新增路由：`POST /dsh-l2d/workspace/ensure`、`GET /dsh-l2d/workspace/status.json`。 MCP Server 新增 `l2d_workspace_ensure` 和 `l2d_workspace_status`。要让专属 Agent 自己调用 Live2D 控制工具，需要按下方配置 DSH MCP Client；本插件不会擅自启动独立 MCP 子进程。 ### 专属 MCP 工具作用域 本仓库的 `cordis.patch.yml` 会声明一个独立的 `dsh-l2d` Agent preset，并在该 preset 内加载 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`。因此 `dsh_l2d` MCP 工具只对选择该 preset 的 Live2D Session 可见，不会放进 profile 全局工具集合。 - MCP Server 名称：`dsh_l2d` - DSH 实际工具名：`mcp__dsh_l2d__l2d_act`、`mcp__dsh_l2d__l2d_get_state`、`mcp__dsh_l2d__l2d_workspace_status` 等。 - 默认仓库路径：`D:/Desktop/DSH-L2D`。如果仓库放在其他位置，请在启动 DSH 的环境中设置 `DSH_L2D_ROOT`。 - MCP Client 设置了 `failOnStartupError: true`，服务器无法启动时不会悄悄创建一个缺少 Live2D 工具的专属 Agent。
# DSH-L2D ### Give your DSH workspace a little life. **面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 Live2D 桌宠、具身行为运行时与 Agent 控制桥** 让 AI 不只通过文字回应，也能通过视线、表情、姿态和连续动作表达状态。

项目简介 · 能力状态 · 架构 · 快速开始 · 开发验证 · 文档

--- ## 🐟 项目是什么 DSH-L2D 是运行在 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）** 中的 Live2D 角色系统。它把 Live2D 渲染、模型无关的动作运行时、工作区上下文和 MCP Agent 工具连接起来，让角色能够对用户交互与 Agent 工作状态作出可观察的反馈。 项目关注的不只是“播放一个动作”，而是建立一条可检查、可仲裁、可追踪的执行链： **工作区状态 / 用户意图 → 语义行为 → 模型能力解析 → 动作队列与轨迹 → 参数所有权仲裁 → Cubism 渲染。** Agent 描述“看向用户”“进入思考状态”或“一段连续动作”等语义目标；本地运行时负责能力检查、动作调度和参数写入。Agent 不应直接绕过运行时操纵每一帧的 Cubism 参数。 > **状态口径：** 本仓库同时包含已实现代码、局部接线、实验性模块和后续架构计划。单元测试通过不等于真实 DSH 宿主、所有模型或所有展示容器均已验收。本文会把实现状态与验证状态分开说明。 ## ✨ 能力与实现状态
### 🎭 Live2D 角色呈现 - Live2D Cubism / WebGL 渲染器 - 表情、动作组、姿态与视线控制 - 呼吸、眨眼和待机微动作 - 角色拖拽及展示层交互 - DSH 页面 Overlay 接入路径 ### 🧠 具身行为与动作编排 - 语义动作意图与 Cue 行为循环 - BACKGROUND / NORMAL / FORCE 优先级 - FIFO 动作队列与连续动作链 - 动作时长声明、回执与中断语义 - 模型能力画像与参数适配基础
### 🔌 Agent 与 MCP Bridge - stdio MCP Server 与本机插件桥接 - Live2D 专属 Workspace / Session 接入 - 工作区状态快照与状态报告 - 动作 enqueue / status / cancel 桥接能力 - 工具按运行时注册结果暴露 ### 🗃️ 动作知识库与模型注册 - SQLite 模型、参数和动作注册表 - Actions Lib 与 G0–G4 入库校验 - GIF 帧提取与动作时序分析 - Model Adapter 与参数边界校验 - 人工审核闸门和执行记录
### 当前实现状态 | 子系统 | 状态 | 当前边界 | |---|---|---| | Live2D Renderer | **已实现，持续回归** | 模型加载、渲染、参数注入和更新调度已有实现；具体模型仍需独立验收 | | ParamInjector / 参数仲裁 | **已实现，持续完善** | 统一写入路径、托管参数策略和所有权约束；未知或未托管参数不能被默认放行 | | 动作链与 FIFO 调度 | **已实现** | 支持最多 15 个输入段；相邻兼容段可合批，每个 Renderer 批次最多 8 步 | | Actions Lib / SQLite | **已实现，持续扩展** | 有动作链仓储、版本和校验管线；动作入库通过不代表已获真实模型运行时验证或人工批准 | | MCP Server | **已实现** | stdio 服务通过本机回环接口连接插件；可用工具以当前运行时 tools/list 为准 | | MCP Bridge / Workspace | **已接入，持续验收** | 已有 WorkspaceManager、StatusReporter、动作队列和工具注册接线；当前本地 Agent Client 是降级实现，不应描述为已接通真实 A2A 后端 | | Overlay 展示 | **已有实现** | 页面悬浮层是当前主要接入路径；其他容器需要按 Host API 和实际宿主逐项验收 | | Sidebar / 独立桌宠窗口 | **部分实现 / 待验收** | 有扩展点或窗口通道设计；不能据此推断所有容器已完成无缝切换 | | 自动肢体分配 / 多肢协调 | **规划与前置验证中** | M1 语义 Cue 路径不等于自动肢体分配完成；需先完成参数域证据和真实模型 acquire/release 验证 | | Workspace 双视图 UI | **实验性** | Whale Workspace 有双视图和会话连续性实现；当前 InMemoryConversationService 是 mock，不是生产 AI 后端 | ### 最近的工程进展 以下是近期代码与验证方向的摘要，详细实现以提交和专项文档为准： - **动作链可靠性：** FIFO 队列对短暂的 conflict / priority-blocked 进行有限重试；已受理但仍为 pending 的动作不会被重复提交。动作链输入上限提升到 15 段，并对相邻兼容段进行合批。 - **动作时长契约：** Actions Lib 的每个 motion step 必须声明 duration_ms，链级总时长会汇总持久化。 - **MCP Bridge：** 插件宿主挂载 WorkspaceManager、Live2DMCPBridge 和 StatusReporter；工具在 Bridge 初始化就绪后注册，避免未就绪时伪报工具可用。 - **模型与参数写入：** Renderer 修复了 Angle 短名托管白名单和 AngleZ 总线限幅问题，并补充目标动作的有界预载等待。 - **动作知识库：** SQLite 注册表、GIF 时序分析、Model Adapter、审核流程和 E2E 管线已建立；validated、runtime_verified 与人工 approved 是不同状态，不能互相替代。 相关追踪：[PR #27 · FIFO 动作链](https://github.com/tequed232/DSH-L2D/pull/27) · [PR #26 · MCP Bridge](https://github.com/tequed232/DSH-L2D/pull/26) · [PR #25 · 动作知识库](https://github.com/tequed232/DSH-L2D/pull/25) · [PR #19 · M1 行为循环](https://github.com/tequed232/DSH-L2D/pull/19) ## 🏗️ 系统架构 ~~~mermaid flowchart TB A["DSH Workspace / Agent"] --> B["Workspace Context & Persona"] B --> C["Semantic Behavior Intent"] C --> D["Capability Profile / Model Adapter"] D --> E["Action Queue / Motion Track"] E --> F["WriteIntent"] F --> G["Ownership & Priority Arbitration"] G --> H["ParamInjector"] H --> I["Cubism / Physics / WebGL Renderer"] J["MCP Client"] --> K["stdio MCP Server"] K --> L["Loopback HTTP / Host Bridge"] L --> C L --> M["Workspace / Session / Status"] N["DSH Plugin Host"] --> O["Presentation Adapter"] O --> I P["SQLite Registry / Actions Lib"] --> D P --> E ~~~ > 上图是模块关系示意。不同入口和容器的接线状态并不相同；图示不代表所有宿主扩展点均已完成端到端验收。 ### 模块职责 | 模块 | 路径 | 职责 | |---|---|---| | Core | packages/core | 语义动作、轨迹、优先级和模型无关的行为逻辑 | | Renderer | packages/renderer | Cubism 模型生命周期、WebGL、帧调度与参数注入 | | DSH Plugin | packages/dsh-l2d-plugin | 插件生命周期、Overlay、宿主服务和客户端接入 | | MCP Server | packages/dsh-l2d-mcp | stdio MCP 工具、参数校验和本机调用转发 | | MCP Bridge | packages/mcp-bridge | Workspace、状态报告、动作队列和宿主侧工具注册 | | Database | packages/dsh-l2d-db | SQLite Schema、模型注册、Actions Lib 和审核数据 | | Tools | tools/ | 能力扫描、GIF 分析、运行时探针、验收和开发工具 | | Docs | docs/ | 架构决策、接口约束、审计和 Agent 使用指南 | ### 核心执行约束 1. **单一权威 Avatar Runtime：** 角色行为状态不属于某个 UI 容器。切换 Presentation 不应创建第二套权威动作状态。 2. **统一参数写入：** 动作源必须经过受控的参数写入与仲裁路径，不得创建并行 Cubism Writer。 3. **能力先于执行：** supported、approximate、unsupported 和 unknown 必须区分；未知能力不能按支持处理。 4. **优先级与所有权：** 冲突动作按优先级和参数所有权处理；被打断的动作需要明确终态并释放资源。 5. **宿主边界：** 独立 Electron WebContents 不能假设与 iframe 共享内存状态；跨窗口同步必须经过宿主侧通道。 ## 🧠 动作系统与回执语义 ### 动作优先级 | 优先级 | 用途 | 行为 | |---|---|---| | BACKGROUND | 呼吸、待机和环境微动作 | 不应抢占更高优先级动作 | | NORMAL | 普通情绪表达和交互反馈 | 可按调度规则替换低优先级动作 | | FORCE | 需要立即响应的交互或演出 | 可抢占较低优先级动作 | ### 连续动作链 - 输入动作链最多 15 个 segment。 - Renderer 单次批次最多 8 个 step。 - 相邻且优先级、气泡等边界兼容的 segment 可以合批，但不能跨越优先级边界。 - 遇到短暂冲突时，队头按策略有限等待；超时后应明确返回原因。 - accepted 表示请求已受理，不等于动作已经播放完成。 - pending 表示动作仍在执行或等待，不应将其重复提交。 动作完成、被打断或仍在等待，应依据实际回执和事件判断。不要仅凭工具调用成功、请求被接受或预计时长推断角色动作已完成。 ### 模型能力画像 | 状态 | 含义 | 处理方式 | |---|---|---| | supported | 有证据确认可用 | 正常执行 | | approximate | 可通过近似映射表达 | 降级执行并保留标记 | | unsupported | 已确认不支持 | 跳过或返回明确原因 | | unknown | 尚未验证 | 不得假定支持 | ## 🧩 DSH 集成与 MCP ### DSH 展示容器 当前宿主扩展点以 [Host API 审计](docs/Host-API-Audit.md) 和对应代码为准： | 宿主位置 | 扩展点 / 入口 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | 页面悬浮层 | shell.overlay | 当前主要角色展示接入路径 | | 右侧面板 | sidebar.right.pane.tab | keyed tab 扩展点；需独立完成宿主验收 | | 设置面板 | settings.section | 设置分区，不等同于独立设置窗口 | | 桌面独立窗口 | pet-window.mjs | 需处理独立 WebContents 和状态同步边界 | ### MCP 接入 packages/dsh-l2d-mcp 提供 stdio MCP Server；Bridge 通过本机回环 HTTP 与插件宿主通信。MCP Server 不负责渲染 Live2D，也不应把密钥或本机服务暴露到公网。 **工具清单以运行时 MCP tools/list 返回的 schema 为准。** README 中的工具名和示例只用于解释调用模式，不是永久 API 保证。可从 [MCP 包说明](packages/dsh-l2d-mcp/README.md) 查看安装方式、工具语义和回执示例。 ### Workspace 与隐私边界 - 专属 Live2D Workspace / Session 与其他会话隔离。 - 工作区状态快照只提供必要的状态元数据，不应被解释为聊天正文、文件路径或详细错误信息。 - 其他 Session 应保持只读，不因 Live2D 状态通知而被提示、修改或停止。 - Bridge 当前本地降级 Agent Client 不代表真实 A2A 后端已经接入。 - 系统与媒体传感器默认关闭；启用前应由用户明确选择。 - 本机控制服务只应监听 loopback，不应直接暴露到公网。 ## 🚀 快速开始 ### 环境要求 - Node.js 22 或更高版本 - pnpm 12.5.1（以根目录 package.json 的 packageManager 字段为准） - 已安装并可运行的 DeepSeek Harness 环境 - 用户自行准备的 Live2D 模型与 Cubism Core ### 1. 获取代码并安装依赖 ~~~bash git clone https://github.com/tequed232/DSH-L2D.git cd DSH-L2D pnpm install ~~~ ### 2. 构建 Renderer ~~~bash pnpm build:renderer ~~~ ### 3. 打包 DSH 插件 ~~~bash npm pack ./packages/dsh-l2d-plugin ~~~ 将生成的插件包按当前 DSH profile 的插件安装方式部署。插件注册、profile 路径和 Cordis patch 机制可能随宿主版本变化，请以当前 DSH 版本和插件包说明为准。安装或更新插件后，按宿主要求重启 DSH。 ### 4. 配置 Live2D 模型与 Cubism Core 模型文件与 Cubism Core 不随仓库分发。请准备具有合法使用授权的模型资源，并按照插件设置及当前模型目录约定完成配置。 - 不要把模型文件、纹理或 Cubism Core 二进制提交到仓库。 - 不要将第三方模型资源上传到未经授权的 CDN。 - 模型加载成功不代表该模型的所有动作、参数和物理效果均已验证。 ### 5. 配置 MCP（可选） 在仓库根目录安装依赖后，可按 MCP 客户端配置启动： ~~~bash node packages/dsh-l2d-mcp/src/server.mjs ~~~ MCP 客户端配置示例（请将路径替换为本机仓库绝对路径）： ~~~json { "mcpServers": { "dsh-l2d": { "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/DSH-L2D/packages/dsh-l2d-mcp/src/server.mjs"] } } } ~~~ 先确保 DSH 插件已加载，或启动本地调试服务。MCP Server 默认只连接本机回环地址；如需指定服务地址，可参考 [MCP 包说明](packages/dsh-l2d-mcp/README.md) 中的 DSH_L2D_URL 配置。 ## # 07 · 上下文观察与受控维护（只读首版实现）

状态：**只读观察已实现并自测；G0–G4 验收门禁已补齐（OS/Electron 级出口认证平台阻断、真实面板绑定读数未执行）；手动压缩（T5）按设计后置、未实现**。更新：2026-11-08。主形态为 DeepSeek Harness Host/client plugin；本目录同时是该插件仓库（`dsh-context-mng`）。

本插件在原生“上下文”面板里回答“这个会话目前保留了哪些内容、来源是什么、估算用量与 provider 实报各是多少”，并且**不修改**会话、prompt 或模型请求。观察、维护、05 长期记忆是三个独立概念；面板显示隐藏不代表模型遗忘。

实施路线、来源与边界见[实施路线](docs/implementation-route.md)；Host 兼容性以[兼容性说明](docs/compatibility.md)的实际字节为准；机制说明见[机制说明](docs/mechanisms.md)；验收门禁对照见[验收门禁补齐记录](docs/acceptance-gates.md)。

## 首版范围

已实现：

- 来源组成分类（system / developer / user / assistant / tools / tool_result / memory / unknown），未知保持 unknown，不从正文猜来源；
- 估算（`utf8_bytes_estimate_v1`，标签“UTF-8 字节估算”）与 provider 实报 usage 分列，不互相分摊；
- 有界内存观测快照（单会话 8 份 / 2MiB，总计 32MiB，LRU）、revision、去重、订阅与切会话失效；
- 只读采样：Session surface 投影、`llm/stream` 透明观测（不改 chunk、不缓存整条流）、`agent/pre-step` 只标阶段；
- 原生 client main 面板 + 只读 Connection RPC（`/local-context`）；
- 经授权的本地过滤报告导出（原子写、路径/符号链接防护、脱敏后内容）。

明确不做（首版）：自动压缩、自动 omit、维护写入、prompt 前后缀、Provider 切换、长期记忆写入、日志删除、跨会话搜索/聚合、成本账单、telemetry、网络出口。

## 配置（唯一授权来源）

`cordis.patch.yml` 的 `config.access.registry` 是唯一范围来源。必须显式登记才会采样/显示：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: context-mng
      name: dsh-context-mng
      config:
        maintenance: { enabled: false }
        access:
          registry:
            schema_version: 1
            revision: 1
            bindings:
              - context_ref: my-project
                session_ref: session-1
                scope:
                  scope_id: my-project
                  generation: 1
                  identity_digest: "<64 位小写 hex>"
                read: true
                export_root_refs: [reports]
                active: true
            export_roots:
              - root_ref: reports
                path: "C:/Users/me/Documents/context-reports"
```

- `context_ref`/`session_ref` 是登记标识；`scope.identity_digest` 由登记方提供（任意稳定 64 hex），运行时不从正文/cwd 推断。
- `export_roots` 是 `export_root_refs` 到真实目录的内部映射；面板只看到 ref，不看到路径。
- 空 registry 是合法状态：面板显示“未登记/无权限”，不生成假数据。

## 浏览器传输（Host ↔ Client，本包自有合同）

实现期实测：rc.5 `connection.rpc.handle` 对 profile 插件不可用（详见[CTX-RPC-03 变更单](docs/design-change-ctx-rpc-03.md)）。
因此使用 rc.5 支持的 `connection.fetch.register` exact Fetch 路由；请求外壳与 BusinessResponse 语义不变，
响应体直接是 BusinessResponse（HTTP 200，业务拒绝也在 200 内），未认证 401、非 owner 403 由 Host 先行拒绝。

| endpoint | 路由 | data |
|---|---|---|
| `context.list` | `POST /api/context-mng/context.list` | `{contexts:[{context_ref,session_ref,scope_id,generation,read,export_root_refs}]}` |
| `observation.get` | `POST /api/context-mng/observation.get` | `{changed,observation?,current_revision}` |
| `group.read` | `POST /api/context-mng/group.read` | `{text,next_offset,revision}` |
| `report.export` | `POST /api/context-mng/report.export` | `{status:"saved"\|"conflict",report_ref,digest}` |

每个请求外壳：`{schema_version:1, operation_id, context_ref, expected_scope_generation, view_epoch, input}`；
`context.list` 使用同一外壳但不需要 context_ref/expected_scope_generation。请求体中的任何 caller/principal/grant
字段都会被严格 schema 拒绝；owner 门禁由 Host 在调用插件路由前完成，registry 是唯一的范围权威。

## 自测

```powershell
node --test --test-isolation=none tests/   # 178 组件/合同测试（Node 26；默认 node --test 在本机沙箱受 spawn 限制）
node tools/context-report.mjs --fixture    # 双合成会话只读报告
node tools/observe-smoke.mjs --fixture --network-evidence   # 缓存/切会话/取消/导出 + 出站 0
node tools/probe-host.mjs --asar "E:/dsh/resources/app.asar"  # rc.5 安装字节探针（28 checks）
```

门禁级验证（隔离 Host、真实 Chromium、真实已注册 Provider、安装/卸载、Node 24）见
[docs/acceptance-gates.md](docs/acceptance-gates.md) 与 `evidence/task5-*`；其中 OS/Electron 级包捕获出口认证
因当前会话未提权被平台阻断，真实面板绑定数据读数一致性未执行——均如实标注，不以组件测试替代。

## 安全边界

- 观察路径零网络、零子进程、零自动更新；正文不落盘（用户主动导出除外）。
- scope/正文先授权后读取；秘密过滤在投影与导出出口都执行。
- 不修改 prompt、不 append 会话、不取消主模型请求；`llm/stream` 包装透明 passthrough。
- 维护默认关闭；没有 Host 共享运行租约证据前不开启任何写路径。

## 开发入口

- [产品形态与首版范围](docs/product-form.md)：已确认方向、用户旅程与可修改设计默认。
- [编码级软件设计](docs/software-design.md)：首版只读观察、手动压缩后续增量；含 schema、Host 接缝、状态和需求变更地图。
- [实施路线与来源](docs/implementation-route.md)：开工说明、采用级别、隔离/出口边界与首个验收动作。
- [兼容性与已核接口](docs/compatibility.md)：rc.5 实际字节、哈希与接缝事实。
- [验收门禁补齐记录](docs/acceptance-gates.md)：G0–G5 对照、真实 AgentLoop/Chromium/Provider/安装卸载证据与阻断项。
- [机制说明](docs/mechanisms.md)：场景→触发→判断→状态→证据→失败恢复，供后续 skill 改进引用。
- [实现独立复审](docs/implementation-review.md)：无 Critical；2 Important/3 Minor 已修复并回归，列残余未验证层。
- [独立开发计划](PLAN.md)：分阶段任务索引与原始验收口径。
- [共同开发约束](../docs/development-contract.md)、[形态决策](../docs/capability-forms.md)、[详细设计](../docs/ecosystem-learning-design.md)。

## 许可

本项目代码 MIT（见 `LICENSE`）；来源与第三方说明见 `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`。本项目不随附 DeepSeek Harness 源码。

Public package repository metadata is absent and npm version returns 404; local acceptance logs describe isolated installs but do not establish a public package-to-repository installation mapping. The owner fallback relies on a specific host contract and is not portable evidence. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# dsh-dump-manager

Sidebar entry, session table, the entry-stream viewer with two exports, plus the
newest-turn export and its `LLM Dump` conversation tab, for dumps captured by
[dsh-llm-dump](https://github.com/wannaknowhys/dsh-llm-dump).

## Install / remove

```powershell
# install: point the plugin manager at this directory
plugin_manager install_bundle target = <path to this directory>

# or from the CLI
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:<path to this directory>

# remove
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-dump-manager
```

The bundle has a host half (routes, exports) and a browser half (sidebar card,
panel, tab, settings page). Host modules do not hot-reload: after editing one,
toggle the bundle so the Host re-imports the module.

## Levels

```
panel   (sidebar button)   sessions only: view / folder / delete
viewer  (查看)             one session's entries: select, export
tab     (LLM Dump)         the same stream, mounted beside 轨迹 / 统计
header  (导出本轮 ▾)       export the newest turn with three filters
settings (Plugins tab)     the same options, shared storage
```

### Panel

- **LLM Dumps <size> · Exports <size>** beside Settings in the sidebar foot.
- Header repeats both sizes plus session/request counts.
- Table: session/workspace, requests, size, last write, actions.
- Row actions: view, folder (open the dump directory), delete (two-step).
- Session dumps live in `<outputDir>` (by default `%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps`, one
  directory per session); exports live beside it in `exports\`.

### Viewer

The viewer never shows request numbers as a dimension. It shows **entries** —
the typed units of the conversation:

| type | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | the assembled system prompt |
| `tools` | the tool definitions block |
| `user` / `assistant` | conversation messages (tool calls included in assistant) |
| `tool` | a tool result message |

The last row may be the **tail entry** — the answer to the newest request, read
from `responses.jsonl` rather than from a request snapshot. It is the only reply
that has not yet been resent as history, and it carries a `最新回复` badge
(`最新·中断` when the stream was cut short).

- One continuous list per session. Each row: checkbox, type badge, one-line
  summary, expand toggle.
- **缩略** renders the expanded entry as readable text (tool calls as
  `→ name(args)`); **详细** renders its complete JSON.
- Entries load 100 at a time: reaching the bottom loads the next page, and the
  footer reports `已渲染/总数`. `⤓ 到底部` renders every remaining entry of the
  segment in one commit and jumps to the end.
- The type row above the list selects or hides whole types: the checkbox
  selects every entry of that type in the current segment, clicking the name
  hides or shows the type (hidden types stay selected; nothing is hidden by
  default).
- A row's content is fetched only when it is expanded.
- `全选本段` selects every entry of the current segment.
- `Shift+点击选区间`: a plain click on a checkbox sets the anchor; Shift+clicking
  a checkbox or a row adds the whole span between the anchor and that row, in the
  current visible order, so a hidden type is never swept in. Shift+clicking a
  span that is already fully selected removes it. The anchor stays at the last
  plain click and resets when the segment or the hidden types change.

**Segments (tabs).** The stream is one segment while each request only appends
messages. When a request rewrites history (compaction, rebuild) the stream
breaks; each segment gets a tab. With a single segment no tab bar is shown.

## Newest-turn export

`导出本轮 ▾` beside the session title exports the newest turn from the last
conversation request's snapshot (not from the entry stream):

- The turn starts at the last message whose `source.kind === 'user'`. Injected
  user-role messages (`time-context`, `runtime-context`, `agent-instructions`,
  `skill-catalog`, `compact-checkpoint`, notices, `agent-message`, …) never
  start a turn.
- The reply to that request comes from `responses.jsonl`; it is not in any
  snapshot yet.
- One-shot calls (session title, …) are skipped: a request with neither an
  assistant message nor a user message is not a conversation call.

Three persisted filters live in `%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps\ui.json`:

| Option | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| include user input | on | keep the `kind === 'user'` message |
| include tools | on | keep tool-call blocks and tool results |
| include injected context | off | keep the other user-role messages |

When the user's prompt was compacted away, the turn spans segments: each crossed
boundary must look like a compaction (`messages[1].source.kind ===
'compact-checkpoint'`), retained messages are deduplicated, and the file carries
a note (Markdown) / `joinedCompaction: true` (JSON). Anything else is refused
with `409` and a code the UI turns into a dialog: `NO_DUMP`, `NO_USER`, `FORK`.
The dialog offers the viewer for manual segment export.

Files: `<title>_latest_<stamp>.md|.json` in the exports folder.

## Strings

All UI and export text comes from `lib/strings.js` (en + zh, English fallback).
The browser half cannot import it (plain script, no bundler), so
`tools/sync-strings.mjs` regenerates its inline copy and
`tools/check-strings.mjs` asserts the two copies and both languages agree.

## Export kinds

Both write into the exports folder (`<outputDir>\..\exports`), never overwrite
(`-1`, `-2`, …).

| Kind | Content | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **transcript** | The selected entries only, rendered as Markdown, segments separated by `## 段 N · seq a–b`; a tail entry adds a note saying it came from the response stream | `.md` |
| **payload** | For each segment represented in the selection, the complete request snapshot that last contained those entries (`lastSeq`): unfolded messages + tools + tool history + sampling, one compact JSON line | `.json`, one per segment |

Selecting every entry of a 132-request session produces a ~1.2 MB transcript
instead of the ~162 MB the snapshot-per-request model produced.

## Settings page

`Settings → Plugins → LLM Dump Settings` owns two groups:

- **Newest-turn export** — the same three filters and format the header menu
  writes, backed by `%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps\ui.json`.
- **Capture (dsh-llm-dump)** — edits `%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps\config.json` on
  llm-dump's behalf: the output directory, with a two-step confirm since
  existing dumps are not moved. Unknown keys survive the rewrite; the file is
  replaced atomically. A directory browser covers drives (Windows) or `/`, with
  Home / parent / an editable path for UNC targets, a per-host share list for a
  bare `\\server\`, and a New folder action wherever a real directory is open.

## Data format

The reader understands **dsh-llm-dump data format version 1**: one timestamped,
append-only `requests.jsonl` per session plus `objects.jsonl` for content
deduplication, and `responses.jsonl` for the reply to the newest request.
Unknown fields are ignored, so a newer llm-dump may add fields without breaking
this reader. The format itself is documented in the llm-dump README.

At startup, and again on every overview request, the host side resolves
`dsh-llm-dump/package.json` and compares its `dsh.formatVersion` with the range
this build reads (`1`). A newer writer is reported once in the Host log and as a
warning row at the top of the panel; reading is never blocked.
`DSH_LLM_DUMP_PACKAGE` points the check at another copy of that file, for a
side-by-side install.

## Host routes (loopback only)

| Method | Path | Body / query |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/dsh-dumps/overview` | — |
| GET | `/api/dsh-dumps/stream` | `?id=` |
| GET | `/api/dsh-dumps/entry` | `?id=&i=` |
| GET/POST | `/api/dsh-dumps/prefs` | `{ export: { … } }` (GET returns `{ prefs, defaults }`) |
| GET/POST | `/api/dsh-dumps/capture` | `{ outputDir? }` → `{ capture, defaults, exportsDir }` |
| GET | `/api/dsh-dumps/roots` | `{ roots, home, platform, stale, probedAt, durationMs }` |
| GET | `/api/dsh-dumps/shares` | `?host=` → `{ shares: [{ name, path }] }` (`net view`) |
| POST | `/api/dsh-dumps/latest` | `{ id, lang }` → `{ file, bytes, messages, joinedCompaction }` or `409 { code }` |
| POST | `/api/dsh-dumps/export` | `{ kind, id, entries: [i], lang }` |
| POST | `/api/dsh-dumps/reveal` | `{ which: 'root' \| 'exports' }` or `{ id }` |
| POST | `/api/dsh-dumps/delete` | `{ id }` |

Ids are restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, deletions only touch a direct child of
the output directory, and every route refuses non-loopback callers.

## Tests

```powershell
npm test
```

Runs on synthetic folded dumps in a throwaway `DSH_HOME` under the system temp
directory; the real profile is never touched:

- `tools/check-strings.mjs` — both string copies are in sync and complete.
- `test/smoke-compat.mjs` — the startup warning, the compatibility block in
  `/overview`, and the pure version comparison.
- `test/smoke-latest.mjs` — newest-turn export: filters, fork refusal, prefs,
  capture config, directory roots.
- `test/smoke-tail.mjs` — the tail entry: flagged from `responses.jsonl`,
  exported with its note in both languages, interrupted streams included.

## Caveat

`payload` is semantically complete, not byte-identical to the wire body: the
folded store keeps values, not the adapter's final serialization, so key order
can differ. Token counts match closely; exact wire capture needs a fetch hook.

No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-llm-dump

Captures **every complete LLM request** and stores it folded: repeated message
prefixes and large repeated fields are stored once and referenced by hash.

- Hook: the `llm/stream` waterfall. The listener observes `GenerateOptions` and
  never modifies it, so capture cannot change what the model receives.
- No `fetch` interception is involved: the full request object is available at
  this seam, so prefix matching is a local computation over captured payloads.

This is a host-side bundle with no browser half. It needs a DeepSeek Harness
build that provides the `llm` service.

## Install / remove

```powershell
# install: point the plugin manager at this directory
plugin_manager install_bundle target = <path to this directory>

# or from the CLI
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:<path to this directory>

# remove
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-llm-dump
```

Host modules do not hot-reload. After editing one, toggle its bundle so the Host
re-imports the module.

## What is captured

`GenerateOptions` at the provider boundary:

- `messages` — the full model-visible conversation, including the assembled
  system prompt
- `tools` — active tool definitions
- `model`, `provider`, `sessionId`, sampling fields
- `toolHistory` and other large top-level fields (stored once, referenced)

Adapters may still transform the request afterwards (image projection, tool
updates, deferred loading); this is the last public state before that step.

## Storage

```
<outputDir>/<sessionId>/
  objects.jsonl    {"h": sha1, "v": <content>}   unique content, written once
  requests.jsonl   {"prefixLen": n, "suffix": [hash...], ...}
  responses.jsonl  {"seq": n, "blocks": [...], ...}   the answer to request n
```

A request reuses the first `prefixLen` messages of the previous request in the
same session and lists only the new suffix. An identical retry becomes a record
with `prefixLen == messageCount` and an empty suffix. A compaction or rewrite
shows up as a shorter `prefixLen` plus a larger suffix — nothing is lost.

Each record also carries `sha1`, the hash of the whole request's canonical JSON,
so a replay can prove it reconstructed the exact content.

## Data format (version 1)

`requests.jsonl` and `responses.jsonl` are an append-only contract shared with
[dsh-dump-manager](https://github.com/wannaknowhys/dsh-dump-manager). Readers
must ignore unknown fields so a later minor version can add them.

The format number is advertised as `dsh.formatVersion` in this package's
`package.json` (currently `1`), independently of the package's semver — a
UI-only release does not look like a format change. `dsh-dump-manager` reads it
at startup and warns when it cannot read what this writer produces.

| File | One line per | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `objects.jsonl` | unique content | `h` (SHA-1 of canonical JSON), `v` (the value) |
| `requests.jsonl` | request | `at`, `seq`, `sessionId`, `provider`, `model`, `messageCount`, `toolCount`, `prefixLen`, `suffix`, `tools`, `top`, `sha1` |
| `responses.jsonl` | finished stream | `seq`, `request` (the request `sha1`), `at`, `ms`, `reason`, `usage`, `blocks`, `interrupted` |

- `messages` is stored only through `suffix`; `prefixLen` says how much of the
  previous request's message list is reused.
- `top` holds every other top-level field. A value larger than 1 KB is replaced
  by `{"$dshRef": "<hash>"}` and stored once in `objects.jsonl`; `tools` uses the
  same indirection (or `null` when the request had no tools).
- Hashes are SHA-1 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace), the same
  computation `tools/unfold-dump.mjs --verify` repeats.

## Response capture

Requests alone cannot show the newest answer: the reply to request *n* only
enters the dump when request *n+1* resends it as an `assistant` message. The
listener therefore also reads the stream it is forwarding and appends one line to
`responses.jsonl` when the stream ends:

```json
{"seq": 12, "request": "<sha1>", "at": "…", "ms": 3412,
 "reason": {"kind": "stop"}, "usage": {...},
 "blocks": [{"type": "text", "text": "…"}], "interrupted": false}
```

- Blocks are assembled with the harness's own rules, duplicated here because a
  plugin cannot import the internal package: deltas per index, `block-end`
  overrides, `max-tokens` drops tool calls, an interrupted stream keeps only
  closed text/reasoning.
- `interrupted` is true when no `finish` chunk arrived (consumer cancelled) or
  the finish kind is `error` / `aborted`; the record then holds exactly what was
  delivered before the cut.
- Capture is observation only: every chunk is forwarded unchanged, the upstream
  iterator is closed when a consumer stops early, and no error can escape into
  the response path.

Every response is stored, but they are mostly redundant — all except the newest
one reappear inside the next request. `dsh-dump-manager` shows only the newest,
which is the one the request snapshots can never contain.

## Config

`%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps\config.json` — re-read when its mtime changes:

```json
{
  "outputDir": "D:/llm-dumps"
}
```

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `outputDir` | `%DSH_HOME%\llm-dumps` | Where session directories are written |

`DSH_LLM_DUMP_CONFIG` overrides the config path.

`dsh-dump-manager` can edit this file from its settings page; unknown keys are
preserved and the write is atomic.

## Replay

```powershell
node tools/unfold-dump.mjs <sessionId> --summary
node tools/unfold-dump.mjs <sessionId> --verify
node tools/unfold-dump.mjs <sessionId> --seq 3 --out req.json
```

`--verify` recomputes the canonical hash of every replayed request and fails on
any mismatch. The tool reads `outputDir` from the same config file, so it works
against any capture directory.

## Tests

```powershell
npm test
```

Both tests run in a throwaway `DSH_HOME` under the system temp directory and
never touch the real profile:

- `test/smoke-fold.mjs` — prefix reuse, one object per unique value, and a replay
  whose canonical hash matches every record.
- `test/smoke-response.mjs` — chunk forwarding, block assembly, the `seq` /
  `sha1` link back to the request, and an aborted stream.

## Privacy

The dump holds the entire model-visible conversation, including file contents,
tool output, and the system prompt. Keep it out of repositories and delete it
when the investigation ends.

# dsh-resume

This folder is a frozen snapshot of the files the compatibility sample audits.
Its `engines.dsh` range is the real one from `L3n3L/dsh-resume@0.1.3`:

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0`

```json
"engines": {
  "dsh": ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"
}
```

The heading is here on purpose: the sample isolates the host-range verdict, and
the remote audit still checks README requirements. Upstream's localized README
does not use a `## Requirements` heading, so a live audit of the repository can
also add a `readme` failure to the same row.

# dsh-plugin-toolkit

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dw/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
[![CI](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-toolkit)](LICENSE)


![dsh-plugin-toolkit](docs/card.png)

English · [中文](./README.zh.md)

Everything a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin needs between `init` and a version the market index accepts: scaffolding, a test harness for the client bundle, a way to see a change without restarting the app, and a release that does not depend on remembering fourteen steps.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel   # a plugin that already passes the checks
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .                          # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release --pr --merge              # tag, wait for npm, update the index, open and merge the PR
```

## The panel

![The Plugin doctor tab, on a plugin that fails two checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/panel.png)

The same checks, in the right sidebar: type a folder, an `owner/repo`, or a GitHub link, and it says which one would fail and why. Nothing is installed and nothing is written.

## Three paths

| You are… | Start with | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| writing your first plugin | [`init`](#1-write-a-plugin) | `doctor`, `fix`, `verify` |
| changing a panel that is already installed | [`dev`](#2-develop-a-panel) | `mount`, the testkit, `audit` |
| shipping a version | [`verify`](#3-ship-a-version) | `release`, `index` |

It also installs as a plugin. `dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit` puts a
**插件体检 / Plugin doctor** panel under the conversation and a tab in the right
sidebar. Give it a folder that holds a plugin's `package.json`, or just
`owner/repo` — or a repository name, which it searches GitHub for and lists the
candidates to pick from. It then runs the same checks `verify` runs and says
which one would break the install, with the reason on the line — the same
answers as the CLI, without leaving the app.

```
$ dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit
```

### 1. Write a plugin

[`init`](#start-from-a-plugin-that-already-passes) writes the files whose absence shows up as a failed first publish — `engines.dsh`, the patch file, a `files` list that ships the code, a client bundle, a test for it, and the CI that runs both. `doctor` then checks the same things without writing anything, and [`verify`](#prove-the-tarball-works-not-just-the-repository) checks the tarball instead of the working copy.

If a plugin already exists, `doctor --fix` turns the failing checks into a
repair plan. It names the file and the edit for every problem, writes nothing
until you add `--write`, and then runs the checks again. `fix --engines` is
still there when the host range is the only thing you need to change.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel
cd my-panel && npm install && npm test && npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest doctor .
```

### 2. Develop a panel

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) supplies the missing half, and [`dev`](#edit-a-plugin-that-is-already-installed) pushes a rebuilt bundle into the running app.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest mount ./client.js     # what a user would see, without the app
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

### 3. Ship a version

`verify` first (it is the only check that reads the tarball), then `release`, which tags, waits for the registry, writes the index entry with the publish time the registry reports, and — with `--pr --merge` — opens and merges the pull request.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release . --pr --merge
```

## What `verify` actually does

![Five steps, and the failure each one catches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/pipeline.svg)

The order matters. Packing first means the check reads the file list npm will publish, not the folder you have. Installing the tarball means the root export is imported the way the loader imports it. Mounting means the client bundle is actually executed, in jsdom, with a host that records what it registered.

Each step exists because a plugin once got past the step before it and still installed into nothing.

## Why this exists

Releasing one plugin fifteen times taught me three things the ecosystem's tooling does not cover:

1. **A version is not shipped when npm accepts it.** Registry propagation took two to eight minutes every time. `npm view` answered from a stale local cache, so I repeatedly believed a release had failed when it had not — and once believed it had succeeded when the market still could not see it.
2. **The market index is a second release, done by hand.** Each version needs an entry carrying `publishTimestamp` from the registry and `engines.dsh` from the manifest. Forget the range and the index validator rejects the PR with `Engines mismatch` — after the tag is already public.
3. **Reading a manifest is not the same as checking it.** A plugin can have a valid `package.json` and still be uninstallable: `files` that omit the entry the manifest points at, a bundle patch that does not exist, a README that never states the host range it declares.

The five failures behind these checks — a red dot with no panel, a row the host drops, an app that disables every plugin after one unguarded `apply()`, a tab nothing can open, and a checker that was wrong — are written up with their exact error text and how to reproduce each one: [Five plugins that installed and did nothing](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/blob/main/docs/why-it-exists.md).

### Four ways a plugin installs and still does nothing

Each of these shipped in a real version of this toolkit before the check below existed. A manifest check passes on all four.

| What you see | What it was | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The tab is a red dot and the panel never opens | `exports["."]` pointed at the CLI, so the loader's row had no plugin to apply | `root export` |
| The plugin is installed, the app never serves it | `dsh.client` declared, `exports["./client"]` missing — the host drops the row | `client declaration` |
| The app says the third-party plugin is unsupported and disables all of them | `apply()` read `ctx.webServer` without declaring it; cordis throws instead of returning `undefined` | `verify` (calls `apply` on a context that has no services) |
| The tab registers, and nothing in the UI opens it | `sidebarRightTabs.register()` registers a *type*; the sidebar lists what `tabs.guide()` returns | a testkit test, not `doctor` |

The first three are static: `doctor` and `verify` catch them without the app running. The fourth is a UI contract, so it needs the panel mounted and the registration inspected — that is what [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) is for.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer (the registry is read with `fetch`; no runtime dependencies)
- Git and `gh` on `PATH` for the steps that touch GitHub
- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0` — the version whose market index carries `engines.dsh`, which is what makes the range check meaningful
- For `testkit`: `jsdom`, `react` and `react-dom` as dev dependencies (`npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom`)

## Start from a plugin that already passes

```sh
$ npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel --title "My panel"
created 8 file(s) in /Users/you/my-panel
  .github/workflows/ci.yml
  .gitignore
  README.md
  client.js
  cordis.patch.yml
  index.js
  package.json
  test/panel.test.mjs

next: npm install && npm test && npm run doctor
```

What you get is not a snippet: it is a plugin whose `doctor` already passes (`engines.dsh`, the patch file, the `files` list), with a client bundle that registers a sidebar tab, a testkit test for it, and a CI workflow that runs both. `init` refuses a directory that is not empty unless you pass `--force`, and refuses a name npm would refuse — those are the two mistakes that cost the most time later.

Every command that takes a path expands a leading `~` before touching the filesystem. The tool, not the shell, expands `~` for these arguments: `cmd` and PowerShell pass `"~/my-panel"` through literally, while a POSIX shell usually expands it first. `init '~/my-panel' --name my-panel` writes into your home directory (the same files `init ~/my-panel` writes on a POSIX shell), and `doctor '~/my-panel'` reads it back. The Windows spelling `~\my-panel` works too; a directory literally named `~` is never created.

## Where it lives

The checker is docked **under the conversation**, above the input bar: a single
row, collapsed by default. Open it and it carries the whole guide — who it is
for, how to use it, what each check means, and what it cannot tell you — plus
the folder field and the results. The same panel is also a **Plugin doctor** tab
in the right sidebar, for when the conversation is busy.

The panel speaks both languages and opens in Chinese; the 中文 / EN switch sits
in the dock's header row (and in the sidebar tab) and the choice is remembered.

Look at it without the app:

```sh
node scripts/preview.mjs /tmp/panel.html   # collapsed, open, with a result, and the tab
```

## Test a panel without a browser

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. `testkit` supplies the missing half: a DOM, the real React, and a host context that records what the panel registers.

```sh
npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom
```

```js
import { mountClient, createFetch } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({
  file: 'client.js',
  copy: { 'my-plugin': { title: 'My panel' } },
  fetch: createFetch({
    '/my-plugin/report': { body: { score: 71, noise: 3 } },
    '/my-plugin/apply': () => ({ status: 201, body: { score: 92 } }),
  }),
});

await panel.click('[data-testid="optimize"]');
console.assert(panel.text().includes('92'), 'the score on screen did not move');
console.assert(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent.includes('92'));
await panel.unmount();
```

`unmount()` is async: it lets React finish the work its own unmount schedules before the DOM goes away. Skipping the `await` surfaces as `ReferenceError: window is not defined` *after* the test has already passed, which is a confusing way to learn it.

What you get back: `text()`, `html()`, `query(selector)`, `must(selector)` (throws with the rendered HTML when it misses), `click(selector)`, `type(selector, value)`, `press(selector, key)`, `focus`, `attributes(selector)`, `snapshot(dir, name)` for a normalised DOM baseline, and `host` for assertions about what the bundle registered.

### Keep a visual baseline

The DOM is the baseline: normalising class order and whitespace gives a file that fails for the reasons a screenshot would — a lost label, a control that stopped rendering — and can be reviewed in a diff instead of by eye.

```js
import { expectSnapshot } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({ file: 'client.js' });
expectSnapshot(panel.html(), '__snapshots__', 'panel');   // throws with the element that moved
await panel.unmount();
```

First run writes nothing: it tells you to re-run with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, so a baseline is always a decision, never a side effect. That rerun writes the normalised HTML and returns `{ status: 'written' }`; later runs return `same` or fail with the element that moved.

### Check what assistive tech sees

```js
panel.expectAria('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]', { label: 'Protection', selected: 'true' });
assert.match(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent, /Score moved 71 → 77/);
```

`expectAria()` compares the attributes a screen reader actually reads — `role`,
`label`, `live`, `selected`, `expanded`, `checked`, `pressed`, `disabled` — and
names the one that differs:

```
[aria-live="polite"]: expected aria text to be "9", but it is "0"
```

A missing attribute is reported as `nothing`, not as an empty string, because
those are different bugs. `panel.aria(selector)` returns the same object when you
want to assert on it yourself.

`must()` throws with the rendered markup when the selector misses, which is the difference between "the assertion failed" and "here is what the user actually got".

Every example below is a file in this repository, run by CI, and the output shown is the output it prints:

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs` | mount a real bundle, read the text, click, read it again |
| `node examples/route-stubs.mjs` | answer the routes a panel asks for, and assert on the requests |
| `node examples/baseline.mjs` | a DOM baseline compared on every run |
| `node examples/aria.mjs` | what assistive tech sees |

```sh
$ node examples/mount-a-bundle.mjs
Demo panel Count 0 0
Demo panel Count 1 1
```

```sh
$ node examples/route-stubs.mjs
Score 71
asked for: 1 route(s), undeclared route answers 404
```

To look at a bundle by hand:

```sh
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js            # print the text a user would see
npx dsh-plugin mount ./client.js --html     # print the markup
```

That is how the AIignore panel was checked before release: the real bundle, mounted in Node, against a stubbed `/aiignore/*`:

```
$ npx dsh-plugin mount ../ai-context-doctor/plugin/client.js
AIignore No workspace yet Could not read the report …
```

## Put the badge on a plugin that passes

If `verify` passes on your plugin, this badge says so and links back here:

```md
[![checked with dsh-plugin-toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit)
```

It is a claim, not a decoration: add it only when `dsh-plugin verify .` exits 0.

## Start from the example

[`dsh-plugin-example`](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-example) is a ~70-line plugin: one sidebar tab, two languages, one behaviour test, CI that runs `verify` through the composite action. It is the shape this toolkit expects, so it is also the fastest way to see whether the toolkit fits your plugin. It is a GitHub template too: **Use this template** starts you on a plugin whose first publish already passes.

```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-example
```

## See what is installed, and what the app loaded

`doctor` checks one folder you name. The question that actually gets asked is
"why is my plugin not in the sidebar?", and the answer needs three things at once:
what is installed, whether each installed copy is valid, and which of them the
running app actually loaded.

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
dsh-aiignore           0.37.1    loaded       ok
demo-panel             0.3.0     not loaded   ok  — dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json does not list it, and the loader mounts only listed bundles
                                            fix: add "demo-panel" to dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json (or run `dsh plugin add demo-panel`), then restart the app

1 installed plugin(s) are not in the running app:
```

"Not loaded" has three different causes, and `audit` names the one that applies
instead of offering a blanket restart:

- **Not in `dsh.profile.bundles`.** `pnpm add` (or `npm install`) installs the
  package but does not tell the loader to mount it. Add the package name to
  `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`, or run
  `dsh plugin add <name>`, then restart the app.
- **No `dsh.bundle`.** The package declares `dsh` but no patch file to mount.
  Add `dsh.bundle.patch` to its `package.json` and ship the patch file, then
  reinstall.
- **Listed, but the app predates the install.** The profile is already correct;
  restart the app once to read the new list.

Advisories (`engines.dsh`, README Requirements) are counted apart from problems:
the market index needs them, the loader does not, so they should not bury a plugin
that is actually broken.

`audit` exits `1` when an installed plugin has a hard failure **or** when the
running app did not load at least one installed plugin, so CI can gate on a
profile where the app silently skipped a plugin. It exits `0` when every
installed plugin is loaded and valid. If no graph was read (`--host` omitted),
the loaded column is `?` and only hard failures change the exit code.

Without `--host` the loaded column is `?`, because guessing would be worse than
saying nothing. Only packages that declare a `dsh` field are audited — the rest of
`node_modules` is ordinary dependencies, and auditing those is noise.

An installed package whose `package.json` cannot be read is the exception: the
`dsh` field that would mark it as a plugin is in the file that failed to parse.
If its name is still in `dsh.profile.bundles`, `audit` reports a `manifest`
failure naming the unreadable `package.json` and exits `1` instead of treating
the folder as an ordinary dependency. A truncated manifest from an interrupted
install therefore cannot make the plugin disappear from the report, and a valid
sibling plugin is still listed on the same run. The exception stays narrow: a
damaged `package.json` in a package that is neither in `dsh.profile.bundles` nor
readable enough to expose a `dsh` field is still an ordinary dependency and is
skipped, so one broken transitive install does not fail every audit.

## Edit a plugin that is already installed

The host already swaps a rebuilt bundle without a page reload: it watches each plugin's entry artifact and reports a `rebuilt` frame on `/plugins/events`. `dev` puts the new file where the host is looking, then **proves** the frame arrived instead of asking you to check by eye.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

![dsh-plugin dev printing the revision the app reported](docs/dev.gif)

*Recorded from a real run against the running app: the last line is the revision the app sent back on `/plugins/events`, not a message the tool printed on faith.*

```
demo-aiignore: /work/plugin/client.js -> ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-aiignore/client.js
initial: copied 163647 bytes at 1:18:43 AM
reloaded dsh-aiignore (rev e0c0230c4fc9)
watching /work/plugin
```

That last line is the whole point: the revision came back from the app's own event stream, so "it reloaded" is a fact, not a hope.

A plugin the running app never loaded cannot be reloaded, and the app says so by leaving it out of the graph it sends first. `dev` reads that graph, so a freshly installed plugin gets the sentence that fixes it instead of a timeout:

```
copied, but not confirmed: the running app has not loaded demo-panel, so it will not report a reload; restart the app once after installing it
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dest <dir>` | write into this installed copy instead of searching `~/.dsh/profiles/*/node_modules/<name>` |
| `--entry <file>` | copy this file instead of `dsh.client.entry`, `client.js`, `lib/client.js` |
| `--build <command>` | run this before each copy (a failed build copies nothing) |
| `--host <url>` | confirm the reload against the app at this URL; without it the copy still happens and the tool says it is unconfirmed |
| `--once` | copy once and exit, for scripts |

Two things it does not do, because the host does not: React state inside the reloaded plugin is lost, and a failed swap does not roll back to the previous bundle.

## Use it in CI

The same checks run as a GitHub Action, so a tag cannot go out on a plugin that would not install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit@v1
  with:
    dir: plugin        # the folder holding the plugin's package.json
    command: verify    # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
```

`verify` is the default because it is the only check that reads what a user
actually installs: `doctor` reads the working copy, so a `files` list that
forgets `client.js` passes it and fails only after `npm i`.

`command: doctor` stops at the manifest checks (fast, no install), and
`command: index` audits `market/index.json` instead, failing on any version whose
`engines.dsh` is missing or is not a semver range (a malformed value such as
`>=banana`, or a single pinned version such as `0.2.0`, both fail). Pin
`version:` if you would rather not track the latest release.

## Check a plugin you have not cloned

The panel takes three kinds of input: a folder, `owner/repo`, or a GitHub URL.
A bare name is a search, not a guess — it asks GitHub, lists the matches with
their stars, and checks the one you pick. A repository is downloaded once as a
tarball into a temp folder, so nothing is cloned into your workspace and
nothing is installed.

The CLI reads a repository straight from the GitHub API:

```bash
dsh-plugin doctor --remote V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
```

```text
dsh-plugin doctor: 1 problem(s) in V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
  ⨯ engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"; declare the range you support, e.g. "engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.0" }
```

That is the whole reason this mode exists: the plugin hub files failed installs
back into plugin repositories, and the report is a sentence — `plugin install
failed`, `plugin does not support the DSH version in use` — that never names a
file. Reading `package.json` over the API is enough to name it.

What it can see, and what it cannot:

- Manifest checks (`engines.dsh`, `dsh field`, `files`, `dsh.client`,
  `exports`) run on the real `package.json`.
- README checks (`readme`) run on the text GitHub serves: the README must have
  a `Requirements` heading and must state the host range `package.json`
  declares. A repository whose checkout fails `readme` fails the remote check
  too, with the same sentence.
- File checks (does `exports["./client"]` point at a file that exists, does the
  root export `apply`) need the tree. A package that runs `prepack`,
  `prepublishOnly`, `prepare` or `build` publishes files it does not commit, so
  those checks are **skipped with a note** instead of calling a working plugin
  broken.
- Public repositories work anonymously, but GitHub allows 60 requests an hour.
  Export `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) to audit more than one or two.

To check a whole list in one pass, put one `owner/repo` per line in a file and
pass it with `--from` (`-` reads standard input):

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt
```

Repositories are read four at a time by default. `--jobs N` changes that width;
values above `8` are capped at `8`, and `--jobs 1` walks the list one repository
at a time, the timing the command had before batching. The output — and the
`--json` array — still follows the input list, and every verdict is the one the
sequential run produced, so a diff between two runs compares repositories rather
than scheduling.

When GitHub answers `403` or `429`, the shared quota is gone, so the batch stops
starting new repositories and marks every entry it could not read as
`rate-limited` instead of `clean` or `unreadable`. If the response carries
`x-ratelimit-reset` (or `retry-after`), the reset time is printed with the
verdict, and the remaining entries are reported without another request.

### Will this plugin install on my DSH?

The eight compatibility reports, from four repositories, all end with the same
question. Add `--host <version>` to a remote audit and it answers that question
for one repository. This is the output for `L3n3L/dsh-resume`, a real plugin
whose declared range stops before DSH 0.2.0, checked against the
`0.2.2-alpha.3` canary from the reports. The checked-in sample is a frozen 0.1.3
snapshot, so the line stays true as the upstream repository changes:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
incompatible  L3n3L/dsh-resume  0.1.3 (host >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0) [incompatible with dsh 0.2.2-alpha.3; declares ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"]

summary: 1 repository — 0 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 0 rate-limited
```

The verdict comes first: `incompatible` means the range in `package.json` does
not accept the host, so the installer rejects the plugin before it unpacks it.
This run exits `1`. The same answer is reproducible without a GitHub request:
the checked-in snapshot under `examples/compatibility-sample/` keeps the 0.1.3
manifest fields that decide compatibility, and its `## Requirements` heading
isolates the host-range answer. This command feeds that snapshot through the
real CLI path:

```sh
$ node scripts/compatibility-sample.mjs
```

(`npm run compatibility` runs the same script.) The test suite runs that
command and compares its output with the block above, so the sample cannot
drift from the formatter or from the README. Running
`dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3` without the
sample audits the repository's current default branch instead; a README or
manifest change since 0.1.3 can add another `readme` or manifest failure to the
same row.

The line carries the range `package.json` declares and one of `compatible`,
`incompatible`, or `unknown` against that host version. `unknown` is the honest
answer for a missing or malformed range — there is nothing to compare — while a
range that excludes the host is `incompatible`, counted as failing, and exits
`1`. npm's pre-release rule is part of the answer: `>=0.2.0` does not accept
`0.2.2-alpha.3`, because a range only opts into a pre-release when it names one
of the same `major.minor.patch`. A canary host can therefore be `incompatible`
with a range that will accept the final release. The same flag works in the
batch mode, so one `--from` run answers the whole list:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
```

The compatibility flags are `--remote <owner/repo>` for one repository,
`--from <file>` for a list (`-` reads standard input), `--host <version>` for
the DSH version to compare against, and `--json` for the machine-readable
finding. `--jobs <n>` sets the batch width, and `--patch-dir <dir>` writes the
host-targeted repair for each repository that needs one. The help text lists
the same flags; a test fails if this section names a flag the CLI does not have.

`--host` still names the running app URL for a local `audit`; on `--remote` it
is the DSH version to compare against. With `--json`, each finding gains
`host` and `compatibility` beside `hostRange`.

Each repository gets one line with its verdict — `clean`, `failing`,
`unreadable`, or `rate-limited` — and the run ends with a counted summary:

```text
clean         demo/plugin  1.2.3 (host >=0.2.0)
failing       demo/broken  — engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"
rate-limited  demo/blocked — GitHub rate-limited this request (403) for package.json; set GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN to raise the limit; the limit resets at 2026-11-04T20:00:00.000Z
rate-limited  demo/next    — GitHub rate-limited the batch before this repository was read, so it was not requested; the limit resets at 2026-11-04T20:00:00.000Z

summary: 4 repositories — 1 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 2 rate-limited
```

The parenthesised count is the number of failed checks, not the number of failing
repositories: one repository that fails both `engines.dsh` and its client
declaration prints `1 failing (2 problems)`. A repository whose `package.json`
has an empty `dsh` field and no `dsh.bundle.patch` is `failing` here too: the
batch runs the same `dsh field` check as `doctor`, and the `--json` finding
carries that failure even though no patch path was declared to check. A README
with no `Requirements` heading is treated the same way: the batch asks the same
`readme` question as a checkout, so the row is `failing`, the `--json` finding
names `readme`, and the run exits `1` instead of reporting the repository clean.

The command exits `1` when any repository is failing, unreadable, or
rate-limited, and `0` only when every repository in the list is clean. `--from`
also accepts the JSON evidence shape (an array, or an object with `rows`) that
the old shell loop printed, so an existing audit file can be replayed without
rewriting it.

### Measured throughput

The measurement uses the first eight repositories from the 3 November
install-failure list — `610la/dsh-notification-center`,
`Anionex/dsh-vision-toolkit`, `ChongCyrus/Vibe-Mathematics`,
`CrazyShout/dsh-ssh-remote`, `Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model`,
`FSMargoo/dsh-at-file`, `FylarOpen/dsh-fylar-office-editor` and
`GraySilver/dsh-evolve-modes` — served from memory with a fixed 500 ms delay on
every API request. That makes the number r
